words.ex: The landlord will evict the tenant for not paying rent.
words.ex_cn: 房东会因为租客不付房租而将他驱逐。
words.en: To evict someone means to force them to leave a house or piece of land, usually because they have not paid the rent or have broken the law.

words.ex: He exhale slowly after running.
words.ex_cn: 他跑步后慢慢呼出气。
words.en: To exhale means to breathe out air from your lungs.

words.tr: n. 喜爱；类同；密切关系；亲和力
words.ex: She has an affinity for painting.
words.ex_cn: 她喜爱绘画。
words.en: A natural liking for or attraction to someone or something.

words.tr: adj. 无法改变的；不能变更的
words.ex: His decision is inalterable.
words.ex_cn: 他的决定是不可改变的。
words.en: not able to be changed

words.ex: He tried to debase the coin with cheap metal.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用廉价金属贬低硬币的价值。
words.en: To debase something means to reduce its value or quality.

words.tr:
n. 回想
v. 回想
words.ex: In retrospect, I should have studied harder.
words.ex_cn: 回顾过去，我本该更努力学习的。
words.en: When you consider something in retrospect, you think about it afterwards, and often have a different opinion about it from the one that you had at the time.

words.ex: He needs time to acclimate to the new climate.
words.ex_cn: 他需要时间来适应新气候。
words.en: When you acclimate or are acclimated to a new situation, place, or climate, you become used to it.

words.tr: v. 嫉妒；羡慕；不乐意地做（或付出）
words.ex: He begrudges his friend's success.
words.ex_cn: 他嫉妒朋友的成功。
words.en: If you begrudge something, you feel unhappy or resentful about having to give it, do it, or allow it.

words.ex: The earthquake was a terrible calamity.
words.ex_cn: 这场地震是一场巨大的灾难。
words.en: A calamity is an event that causes great harm or damage, such as a flood or a fire.

words.ex: He gave his last dollar to the homeless man, showing an altruistic heart.
words.ex_cn: 他把最后一美元给了那个无家可归的人，表现出一颗无私的心。
words.en: If you describe someone as altruistic, you mean that they show unselfish concern for the welfare of others.

words.ex: The movie had a banal plot that everyone had seen before.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影的剧情平庸得让人看过了无数次。
words.en: If you describe something as banal, you do not like it because you think that it is so ordinary that it is not at all effective or interesting.

words.ex: The treacherous road made driving very scary.
words.ex_cn: 这条危险的道路让驾驶非常可怕。
words.en: If you describe someone as treacherous, you mean that they are likely to betray you and cannot be trusted. If you say that something is treacherous, you mean that it is very dangerous and unpredictable.

words.ex: The cat got entangled in the string.
words.ex_cn: 猫被绳子缠住了。
words.en: If something is entangled in something else, it is caught or twisted around it, or mixed with it so that it is difficult to separate the two things.

words.ex: The car stopped at the junction.
words.ex_cn: 汽车在交叉路口停了下来。
words.en: A junction is a place where two or more things, especially roads or railways, come together.

words.ex: The manager will empower the team to make decisions.
words.ex_cn: 经理将授权团队做决定。
words.en: To give someone the authority or power to do something.

words.ex: He tried to dissuade her from quitting her job.
words.ex_cn: 他试图劝她不要辞掉工作。
words.en: If you dissuade someone from doing something, you persuade them not to do it.

words.ex: The latent talent in the child became clear after years of practice.
words.ex_cn: 孩子潜在的才能在多年练习后显现出来。
words.en: Latent is used to describe something which is hidden and not obvious at the moment, but which may develop further in the future.

words.tr: adj. 衰老的；老朽的；破旧的
words.ex: The old house is decrepit and needs repair.
words.ex_cn: 这栋老房子破旧不堪，需要修理。
words.en: Something that is decrepit is old and in poor condition.

words.ex: The judge will summon him tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 法官明天将传唤他。
words.en: If you summon someone, you order them to come to you.

words.tr: adj. 扭曲的；弯曲的；复杂的
words.ex: The twistful road made driving difficult.
words.ex_cn: 这条弯曲的道路让驾驶变得困难。
words.en: Characterized by twists or turns; winding.

words.tr: adj. 有浮力的；心情愉快的；
words.ex: The buoyant life jacket keeps you on the water.
words.ex_cn: 有浮力的救生衣让你浮在水面上。
words.en: A buoyant object floats on a liquid or in the air. A buoyant economy, market, or industry is successful because a lot of money is being spent or invested in it.

words.tr:
v. 完成；使完美；圆房
adj. 完美的；至上的；圆满的
words.ex: He consummated the deal with a handshake.
words.ex_cn: 他用握手完成了这笔交易。
words.en: To consummate means to make something complete or perfect, often used in the context of a marriage or an agreement. It can also describe someone who is extremely skilled in a particular area.

words.ex: The irate customer shouted at the clerk.
words.ex_cn: 这位愤怒的顾客对店员大喊大叫。
words.en: If someone is irate, they are very angry about something.

words.tr:
n. 通勤；
v. 通勤；
words.ex: His daily commute takes an hour by train.
words.ex_cn: 他每天的通勤坐火车要一个小时。
words.en: If you commute, you travel a long distance every day between your home and your place of work.

words.ex: He can descry a ship on the horizon.
words.ex_cn: 他能看见地平线上的一艘船。
words.en: To catch sight of something or someone that is difficult to see or that is far away.

words.tr: v. 诱骗；消遣；迷住；消磨
words.ex: He beguiles her with sweet words.
words.ex_cn: 他用甜言蜜语哄骗她。
words.en: If someone beguiles you, they charm you in a way that makes you trust them or like them, often so that they can deceive you.

words.tr: n. 解说词；评论；实况报道；
words.ex: The commentator gave live commentary during the soccer match.
words.ex_cn: 解说员在足球比赛期间进行了现场解说。
words.en: A commentary is a spoken or written description of an event or situation that is broadcast or published as it occurs.

words.ex: He tried to pacify the crying baby with a toy.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用一个玩具让哭闹的婴儿安静下来。
words.en: If you pacify someone who is angry, upset, or not pleased, you make them calm or content.

words.tr: adj. 有资格的；合格的；合意的；
words.ex: He is eligible to vote because he is 18 years old.
words.ex_cn: 他年满18岁，有资格投票。
words.en: Someone who is eligible for something is qualified or allowed to do it.

words.tr: adj. 不合时宜的；过早发生的
words.ex: His untimely death shocked everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他突如其来的去世让所有人都感到震惊。
words.en: If you describe an event as untimely, you mean that it happened earlier than it should, or sooner than you expected.

words.ex: He felt chagrin when he lost the game.
words.ex_cn: 他输掉比赛时感到懊恼。
words.en: Chagrin is a feeling of disappointment, upset, or annoyance, perhaps because of your own failure.

words.tr: adj. 压迫的；沉重的；难以忍受的；闷热的
words.ex: The oppressive heat made it hard to breathe.
words.ex_cn: 令人窒息的炎热让人难以呼吸。
words.en: If you describe a society, its laws, or customs as oppressive, you think they treat people in an unfair and cruel way and prevent them from having opportunities and freedom.

words.ex: The doctor wrote a prescription for medicine.
words.ex_cn: 医生开了一张药方。
words.en: A prescription is a written order from a physician for the preparation and administration of a drug or device for a patient.

words.ex: The benign teacher always helped students after class.
words.ex_cn: 这位仁慈的老师总是在课后帮助学生。
words.en: A benign substance or process does not have any harmful effects.

words.ex: His speech was full of bombast and little truth.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲充满空洞的豪言壮语，却缺乏真实内容。
words.en: Bombast is speech or writing that sounds grand or important but has little meaning.

words.ex: The broken bridge is a menace to drivers.
words.ex_cn: 这座破桥对司机来说是个危险物。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is a menace, you mean that they are likely to cause serious harm.

words.ex: He fabricates excuses to avoid work.
words.ex_cn: 他编造借口来逃避工作。
words.en: To fabricate means to invent or produce something false in order to deceive someone.

words.tr: adj. 不恰当的；不得体的；无吸引力的
words.ex: It is unbecoming to shout at teachers.
words.ex_cn: 对老师大喊大叫是不合适的。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour or remarks as unbecoming, you mean that they are shocking and unsuitable for that person.

words.tr:
n. 探测器；
v. 探查；
words.ex: The probe sent back photos from Mars.
words.ex_cn: 探测器从火星传回了照片。
words.en: If you probe into something, you ask questions or try to discover facts about it. A probe is also a long thin instrument that doctors and dentists use to examine parts of the body.

words.tr: adj. 沮丧的；泄气的；失望的
words.ex: He became despondent after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后变得沮丧。
words.en: If you are despondent, you are very unhappy because you have been experiencing difficulties that you think you will not be able to overcome.

words.ex: He got a penalty for breaking the rules.
words.ex_cn: 他因违反规则而受到惩罚。
words.en: A penalty is a punishment that is imposed on someone for doing something that is against the rules or the law.

words.ex: The study found a causal link between smoking and lung cancer.
words.ex_cn: 这项研究发现了吸烟与肺癌之间的因果关系。
words.en: A causal factor or event is one that causes or leads to something else.

words.tr:
n. 烈火；火焰；闪耀
v. 闪耀；熊熊燃烧；发亮光
words.ex: The fire began to blaze in the woods.
words.ex_cn: 火在森林里开始猛烈燃烧。
words.en: A blaze is a very large or fiercely burning fire that is difficult to control.

words.tr: adj. 对（享乐）感到厌倦的；（因司空见惯而）无动于衷的
words.ex: He is blase about the new phone because he has one every year.
words.ex_cn: 他对新手机无动于衷，因为他每年都换一部。
words.en: If you describe someone as blasé, you mean that they are not easily impressed, excited, or worried by things, usually because they have seen or experienced them before.

words.tr: adj. 无望的；凄凉的；荒凉的；
words.ex: The future looks bleak without a job.
words.ex_cn: 没有工作，未来看起来毫无希望。
words.en: If you describe a situation as bleak, you mean that it seems unlikely to improve or get better.

words.tr:
v. 臆测；猜想
n. 臆测；猜度
words.ex: He surmises that it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他推测明天会下雨。
words.en: If you surmise that something is true, you guess it from the available evidence, although you do not know for certain.

words.tr:
adj. 道德败坏的；堕落的；腐化的
v. 使堕落；使腐化；使败坏；“deprave”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The movie showed a depraved man who hurt others.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影展示了一个堕落的人，他伤害了别人。
words.en: If you describe someone as depraved, you mean that they are morally very bad or evil.

words.ex: The words on the sign are indistinct.
words.ex_cn: 标志上的字模糊不清。
words.en: not clear or sharply defined

words.tr:
n. 精巧动作；军事演习；花招
v. （熟练地）移动；操控；算计
words.ex: The dancer's maneuver was breathtaking.
words.ex_cn: 舞者的精巧动作令人叹为观止。
words.en: A maneuver is a movement or series of movements requiring skill and care.

words.ex: The company will withhold his salary until he signs the contract.
words.ex_cn: 公司会扣留他的工资，直到他签署合同。
words.en: If you withhold something that someone wants, you refuse to let them have it.

words.ex: They ascribe his success to hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他们把他的成功归因于努力工作。
words.en: If you ascribe an event or condition to a particular cause, you say or consider that it was caused by that thing.

words.ex: The genesis of the story is a simple dream.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事的起源是一个简单的梦。
words.en: The origin or mode of formation of something.

words.ex: The teacher will revoke his privilege to use the computer.
words.ex_cn: 老师将撤销他使用电脑的权限。
words.en: If someone in authority revokes something such as a law, license, or agreement, they cancel it.

words.ex: He tried to defraud the bank with a fake check.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用一张假支票诈骗银行。
words.en: If someone defrauds you, they take something away from you or stop you from getting what is rightfully yours by deceiving you.

words.tr: v. 连根拔起；迁离；根除；
words.ex: The storm uprooted the old tree.
words.ex_cn: 风暴把那棵老树连根拔起了。
words.en: If you uproot yourself or if you are uprooted, you leave a place where you have lived for a long time and go to live somewhere else.

words.ex: The quiet music was a prelude to the loud concert.
words.ex_cn: 轻柔的音乐是盛大音乐会的前奏。
words.en: A prelude is an introductory piece of music, event, or action that comes before a more important one.

words.tr: adj. 可压缩的；可压榨的
words.ex: The gas is compressible under high pressure.
words.ex_cn: 这种气体在高压下可以被压缩。
words.en: Capable of being compressed or made more compact.

words.ex: The confrontation between the two teams was intense.
words.ex_cn: 两队之间的对抗非常激烈。
words.en: A confrontation is a situation in which there is a lot of disagreement or argument about something important.

words.tr: v. 弥补；兑换；付清；赎回；履行
words.ex: He worked hard to redeem his mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作来弥补自己的错误。
words.en: To redeem something means to get it back by paying a sum of money or by doing something to compensate for a fault or mistake.

words.ex: He loves the bucolic life in the countryside.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢乡村的田园生活。
words.en: Relating to the pleasant aspects of the countryside and country life.

words.ex: The company is a legal entity.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司是一个法律实体。
words.en: An entity is something that exists separately from other things and has a clear identity of its own.

words.tr: v. （贸然）上前搭讪；（唐突地）走近谈话
words.ex: He accosted a stranger on the street.
words.ex_cn: 他在街上拦住了一位陌生人。
words.en: If someone accosts another person, they go up to them and speak to them, especially in a way that seems rude or threatening.

words.tr: adj. 散漫的；不连贯的；断续的
words.ex: He gave a desultory answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个漫无目的的回答。
words.en: Something that is desultory is done in an unplanned and disorganized way, and without enthusiasm.

words.ex: The puzzle was perplexing and hard to solve.
words.ex_cn: 这个谜题令人困惑，很难解决。
words.en: If you find something perplexing, you find it confusing or difficult to understand.

words.ex: He tried to persuade her to stay.
words.ex_cn: 他试图说服她留下。
words.en: If you persuade someone to do something, you cause them to do it by giving them good reasons for doing it.

words.ex: It's a coincidence that we both wore blue today.
words.ex_cn: 我们今天都穿了蓝色，真是巧合。
words.en: A coincidence is when two or more similar or related events occur at the same time by chance and without any planning.

words.ex: He made a hypothesis that plants grow faster in light.
words.ex_cn: 他提出一个假设，认为植物在光照下长得更快。
words.en: A hypothesis is an idea which is suggested as a possible explanation for a particular situation or condition, but which has not yet been proved to be correct.

words.ex: The defiant child refused to clean his room.
words.ex_cn: 这个不顺从的孩子拒绝打扫房间。
words.en: If you say that someone is defiant, you mean they show aggression or independence by refusing to obey someone.

words.ex: The cloth shows shrinkage after washing.
words.ex_cn: 这块布在洗涤后出现了缩水。
words.en: The process, fact, or amount of shrinking.

words.tr:
adj. 据说的；号称的；有名气的
v. 认为；以为；“repute”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He is a reputed doctor in this city.
words.ex_cn: 他是这座城市里有名的医生。
words.en: Generally believed to be a particular thing, although this might not be true.

words.tr: v. 暗指；（间接）提到；影射
words.ex: He alluded to the problem without naming it.
words.ex_cn: 他暗示了这个问题，但没有点明。
words.en: To allude to something means to mention it in an indirect way.

words.ex: He is apprehensive about the test.
words.ex_cn: 他对考试感到担忧。
words.en: Anxious or fearful that something bad or unpleasant will happen.

words.tr:
n. 不信任；名誉丧失；信誉丧失
v. 不信；败坏名声；使丢脸
words.ex: His lies brought discredit to the company.
words.ex_cn: 他的谎言使公司失去了信任。
words.en: To discredit someone or something means to cause them to lose people's respect or trust.

words.ex: His discourse on climate change was clear and logical.
words.ex_cn: 他关于气候变化的论述清晰而有逻辑。
words.en: Discourse is spoken or written communication between people, especially serious discussion of a particular subject.

words.tr: adj. 不礼貌的；失礼的；粗鲁的
words.ex: He was discourteous to the waiter.
words.ex_cn: 他对服务员无礼。
words.en: If you say that someone is discourteous, you mean that they are rude and have no consideration for the feelings of other people.

words.ex: Her kindness emanates from her smile.
words.ex_cn: 她的善良表现在她的微笑中。
words.en: To emanate means to come out from a source.

words.tr: adj. 意志坚强的；有目的的；有意图的
words.ex: He is purposeful in achieving his goals.
words.ex_cn: 他在实现目标时意志坚强。
words.en: If someone is purposeful, they show that they have a definite aim and a strong desire to achieve it.

words.ex: The fallen tree obstructs the road.
words.ex_cn: 倒下的树挡住了道路。
words.en: If something obstructs a road or path, it blocks it, stopping people or vehicles from getting past.

words.tr: adj. 有资格的；合格的； v. 取得资格；“qualify”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He is a qualified teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位有资格的老师。
words.en: Having the necessary qualifications for a particular job or task.

words.ex: The blighted tree lost all its leaves.
words.ex_cn: 这棵枯萎的树掉光了所有的叶子。
words.en: If something is blighted, it is affected by a condition that causes it to wither or deteriorate, often used to describe plants or areas.

words.tr: adj. 教皇的；武断的；傲慢的
words.ex: He wore a pontifical robe during the ceremony.
words.ex_cn: 他在仪式上穿了一件教皇式的长袍。
words.en: Relating to the Pope or to the office or authority of the Pope; having the pomp or dignity associated with high ecclesiastical office.

words.tr: adj. 贪心的；贪婪的；渴望的
words.ex: He is covetous of his neighbor's new car.
words.ex_cn: 他垂涎邻居的新车。
words.en: If you are covetous, you have a strong desire to possess something, especially something that belongs to someone else.

words.tr:
n. 小提琴；骗局
v. 摆弄；虚度时光；拉小提琴；篡改
words.ex: He bought a fiddle at the music shop.
words.ex_cn: 他在音乐店买了一把小提琴。
words.en: A fiddle is a musical instrument with strings that you play with a bow. It is the same as a violin.

words.ex: The cat likes to roam around the garden.
words.ex_cn: 这只猫喜欢在花园里游荡。
words.en: To roam means to move about or travel without any definite purpose or destination.

words.ex: His crabbed handwriting made it hard to read the note.
words.ex_cn: 他难辨认的笔迹让这张便条很难阅读。
words.en: If you describe someone's writing or behavior as crabbed, you mean that it is small and difficult to read or understand, often because it is written in a very small space.

words.ex: There is a correlation between exercise and good health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼与健康之间存在相关性。
words.en: A correlation between things is a connection or link between them.

words.tr:
v. 把…联系在一起；
adj. 副的；
n. 同事；伙伴；
words.ex: He associates happiness with family time.
words.ex_cn: 他把幸福与家庭时光联系在一起。
words.en: If you associate someone or something with a particular quality or idea, or if they are associated with it, you connect them in your mind with that quality or idea.

words.ex: The mysterious box appeared on his doorstep.
words.ex_cn: 那个神秘的盒子出现在他的门口。
words.en: If someone or something is mysterious, it is not fully understood or explained and seems interesting or puzzling.

words.tr:
adj. 惹人喜爱的
v. 使受喜爱；“endear”的现在分词
words.ex: Her smile is endearing.
words.ex_cn: 她的微笑很可爱。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as endearing, you mean that it causes you to feel very fond of them.

words.ex: The two lawyers gave adversarial arguments in court.
words.ex_cn: 两位律师在法庭上提出了对抗性的论点。
words.en: Involving or characterized by conflict or opposition.

words.ex: He has a masculine voice and strong build.
words.ex_cn: 他声音低沉，身材强壮。
words.en: Having qualities or appearance traditionally associated with men.

words.ex: The teacher will critique the student's essay tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 老师明天会对学生的作文发表评论。
words.en: A critique is a detailed analysis and assessment of something, especially a literary, philosophical, or political theory.

words.tr: n. 往返移动之物；航天飞机；
words.ex: The bus is a shuttle between the hotel and the airport.
words.ex_cn: 这辆巴士是酒店和机场之间的往返交通工具。
words.en: A shuttle is a vehicle that travels frequently between two places. In weaving, a shuttle is a device used to carry the weft thread back and forth across the loom.

words.ex: She wore a necklace made of jade.
words.ex_cn: 她戴着一条玉制的项链。
words.en: A hard, typically green stone used for ornaments and implements and consisting of the minerals jadeite or nephrite.

words.ex: The teacher spoke in a comprehensible way.
words.ex_cn: 老师用容易理解的方式讲话。
words.en: If something is comprehensible, you can understand it.

words.tr: n. 宣告无罪；无罪的判决
words.ex: The court gave him an acquittal after the trial.
words.ex_cn: 审判后，法院宣布他无罪。
words.en: An acquittal is a formal declaration in a court of law that someone who has been accused of a crime is not guilty.

words.ex: The charity aims to alleviate destitution among the elderly.
words.ex_cn: 该慈善机构旨在减轻老年人的贫困。
words.en: Destitution is the state of having no money or possessions.

words.tr: adj. 包容的；包含全部费用的；
words.ex: The school is inclusive and welcomes all students.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校是包容的，欢迎所有学生。
words.en: Inclusive is used to describe something that is designed to include all types of people, things, or ideas, and to treat them all fairly and equally.

words.ex: The character is fictitious and does not exist in real life.
words.ex_cn: 这个角色是虚构的，现实中不存在。
words.en: Fictitious means invented and not true or not existing.

words.ex: The teacher berated the student for being late.
words.ex_cn: 老师因为学生迟到而责备了他。
words.en: To scold or criticize someone angrily.

words.ex: The error is negligible.
words.ex_cn: 这个误差可以忽略。
words.en: If you describe something as negligible, you mean that it is so small or unimportant that it is not worth considering or worrying about.

words.ex: He is adept at solving math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他擅长解决数学问题。
words.en: Someone who is adept at something is very skilled at it.

words.ex: The inert gas does not react with other elements.
words.ex_cn: 这种惰性气体不与其他元素发生反应。
words.en: If someone or something is inert, they are not moving or reacting in any way.

words.ex: Salt is soluble in water.
words.ex_cn: 盐可以溶于水。
words.en: A substance that is soluble can be dissolved in a liquid.

words.ex: He talked with bravado, but he was scared.
words.ex_cn: 他装出勇敢的样子说话，但他其实很害怕。
words.en: A bold manner or a show of boldness intended to impress or intimidate.

words.tr: n. 鼎盛时期；（人生或事业的)巅峰；册封为神
words.ex: The artist's work reached apotheosis in his final masterpiece.
words.ex_cn: 这位艺术家的作品在他的最终杰作中达到了神化。
words.en: The highest point in the development of something; culmination or climax.

words.tr: v. 使有尊严；使崇高；使显贵
words.ex: He tried to dignify his actions with excuses.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用借口来美化自己的行为。
words.en: To dignify something means to make it seem important and worthy of respect, often by treating it in a serious or formal way.

words.tr: v. 体现；使具体化；包含
words.ex: He embodies kindness and patience.
words.ex_cn: 他体现了善良和耐心。
words.en: To embody means to represent a quality or an idea exactly; to include or contain something.

words.ex: The small town has a maritime history.
words.ex_cn: 这个小镇有着海洋历史。
words.en: Relating to the sea, especially in relation to seaborne trade or naval matters.

words.ex: An apparition appeared in the dark hallway.
words.ex_cn: 一个幽灵出现在黑暗的走廊里。
words.en: An apparition is a ghost or ghostlike image of a person.

words.ex: The fallen tree impeded the car's path.
words.ex_cn: 倒下的树阻碍了汽车的前进。
words.en: To impede something means to make its movement, development, or progress difficult.

words.ex: The accident caused many casualties.
words.ex_cn: 这场事故造成了许多伤亡人员。
words.en: A casualty is a person who is killed or injured in a war or in an accident.

words.tr: n. 自我主义；利己主义
words.ex: He acts out of egoism, not kindness.
words.ex_cn: 他出于利己主义行事，而不是善意。
words.en: Egoism is the belief that you should think about your own interests and needs rather than those of other people.

words.ex: The recessive gene is often masked by a dominant gene.
words.ex_cn: 隐性基因常常被显性基因所掩盖。
words.en: In genetics, a recessive gene is one that is expressed only when there is no dominant gene present.

words.tr: v. 同意；继承；即位；加入
words.ex: He acceded to their request.
words.ex_cn: 他同意了他们的请求。
words.en: If you accede to someone's request, you do what they ask.

words.tr: adj. 有免疫力的；免疫的；不受影响的；
words.ex: Children are immune to this disease after vaccination.
words.ex_cn: 儿童接种疫苗后对这种疾病有免疫力。
words.en: If you are immune to a particular disease, you cannot be affected by it. If you are immune to something such as criticism, it does not affect you.

words.ex: He tries to aggrandize himself by lying about his achievements.
words.ex_cn: 他通过吹嘘自己的成就来抬高自己。
words.en: To increase the power, status, or wealth of someone or something.

words.ex: He has a habit of waking up early.
words.ex_cn: 他有早起的习惯。
words.en: A habit is something that you do often or regularly.

words.ex: We walked through the arboretum to see different trees.
words.ex_cn: 我们穿过植物园，看各种树木。
words.en: An arboretum is a place where many different types of trees are grown for scientific and educational purposes.

words.tr: adj. 可笑的；荒谬的；滑稽的
words.ex: It is ludicrous to wear a coat in summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天穿外套真是荒谬。
words.en: If you describe something as ludicrous, you are emphasizing that you think it is foolish, unreasonable, or unsuitable.

words.ex: He amended the letter before sending it.
words.ex_cn: 他在发送信件之前修正了它。
words.en: To amend something means to make changes to it in order to improve it or make it more accurate.

words.tr: v. 沉思；冥想；考虑；仔细计划
words.ex: He meditates every morning to feel calm.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上冥想以保持平静。
words.en: To meditate means to spend time in quiet thought for religious purposes or relaxation.

words.ex: The diver submerge to explore the coral reef.
words.ex_cn: 潜水员潜水去探索珊瑚礁。
words.en: To submerge something means to put it below the surface of a liquid, especially water. If something submerges, it goes below the surface of a liquid.

words.ex: He made an adjuration to tell the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他恳切地要求说实话。
words.en: An adjuration is a solemn urging or a formal command, often invoking a sacred or authoritative source to compel someone to act or to refrain from acting.

words.tr: adj. 饮食的；营养的；与消化有关的
words.ex: The alimentary canal helps digest food.
words.ex_cn: 消化道帮助消化食物。
words.en: Relating to nourishment or sustenance.

words.tr: adj. 不相似的；不一样的；不同的
words.ex: The two apples are dissimilar in color.
words.ex_cn: 这两个苹果颜色不同。
words.en: If one thing is dissimilar to another, or if two things are dissimilar, they are very different from each other.

words.ex: They will renovate the old house next month.
words.ex_cn: 他们下个月将翻新那栋老房子。
words.en: To renovate means to restore something to a good state of repair or to make it as good as new.

words.ex: The artist lived in obscurity for most of his life.
words.ex_cn: 这位艺术家一生大部分时间都默默无闻。
words.en: The state of being unknown, inconspicuous, or unimportant.

words.ex: The queen's reign lasted 70 years.
words.ex_cn: 女王的统治持续了70年。
words.en: The period during which a sovereign rules; to hold royal office; to prevail

words.tr: adj. 无价的；无法估计的
words.ex: Her kindness is inestimable.
words.ex_cn: 她的善良是无法估量的。
words.en: If you describe the value, benefit, or importance of something as inestimable, you mean that it is extremely great and cannot be calculated.

words.ex: The ad induced him to buy the product.
words.ex_cn: 这则广告诱使他购买了该产品。
words.en: To induce a state or condition means to cause it.

words.ex: There is a disparity in pay between men and women.
words.ex_cn: 男女之间的工资存在差异。
words.en: A disparity between two or more things is a noticeable difference between them.

words.ex: He condescended to explain the simple math to his little brother.
words.ex_cn: 他屈尊向弟弟解释了简单的数学。
words.en: If someone condescends to do something, they agree to do it in a way which shows that they think they are superior to the people they are doing it for.

words.ex: He is a scientist of great renown.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位享有盛誉的科学家。
words.en: Renown is the state of being known and talked about by many people because of your achievements, qualities, or actions.

words.tr: adj. 乡巴佬的；粗野的；粗鄙的
words.ex: His boorish behavior made everyone uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 他粗俗的行为让所有人都感到不舒服。
words.en: If you describe someone as boorish, you mean their behavior is unrefined, insensitive, or rude.

words.tr:
adj. 通便的；导泻的；宣泄感情的
n. 泻药
words.ex: The doctor prescribed a cathartic to help with his constipation.
words.ex_cn: 医生开了一种泻药来帮助他缓解便秘。
words.en: If you describe something as cathartic, you mean that it causes you to release strong feelings that you have been keeping inside, especially feelings of sadness or anger.

words.ex: The new law gave impetus to environmental protection.
words.ex_cn: 新法律为环境保护提供了推动力。
words.en: Something that gives a process impetus or an impetus makes it happen or progress more quickly.

words.tr: adj. 肥沃的；有繁殖力的；多产的；富饶的；
words.ex: The fertile land grows many crops.
words.ex_cn: 这片肥沃的土地长满了各种作物。
words.en: Land or soil that is fertile is able to support the growth of a large number of strong healthy plants.

words.ex: He adulterates milk with water to make more money.
words.ex_cn: 他往牛奶里加水以赚更多钱。
words.en: To make something poorer in quality by adding another substance to it.

words.ex: He had no recourse but to ask for help.
words.ex_cn: 他别无依靠，只能求助。
words.en: If you have recourse to a particular course of action, you use it when you are in a difficult situation or when you need to achieve something.

words.ex: He was hesitant to answer the question.
words.ex_cn: 他犹豫着不敢回答这个问题。
words.en: If you are hesitant about doing something, you are slow to do it, usually because you are uncertain, worried, or nervous about it.

words.ex: I acquaint him with the new rules.
words.ex_cn: 我让他熟悉新规则。
words.en: If you acquaint someone with something, you tell them about it so that they know it.

words.tr: adj. 没注意到的；未觉察的；忘却的；
words.ex: He was oblivious to the noise around him.
words.ex_cn: 他对周围的噪音毫无察觉。
words.en: If you are oblivious to something or oblivious of it, you are not aware of it.

words.ex: He acted out of malice, not mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他是出于恶意，而不是错误。
words.en: Malice is behavior that is intended to harm people or their reputations, or cause them embarrassment and upset.

words.ex: She sang softly to allay his fears.
words.ex_cn: 她轻声唱歌以缓解他的恐惧。
words.en: If you allay someone's fears or doubts, you stop them feeling afraid or doubtful.

words.ex: The bank will disburse the loan next week.
words.ex_cn: 银行将在下周发放贷款。
words.en: To disburse means to pay out money from a fund or account.

words.ex: The fairy tale features a dwarf who lives in a small house.
words.ex_cn: 这个童话故事中有一个住在小房子里的侏儒。
words.en: A dwarf is a person, animal, or plant that is much smaller than the usual size of its species. As a verb, to dwarf means to make someone or something seem small or insignificant in comparison.

words.tr: adj. 严格的；缜密的；严密的；
words.ex: The teacher is rigorous about homework deadlines.
words.ex_cn: 老师对作业截止日期要求严格。
words.en: If you are rigorous in something, you are very thorough and strict in the way you do it.

words.tr: adj. 超越的；杰出的；卓越的
words.ex: The beauty of the sunset was transcendent.
words.ex_cn: 日落的美是超凡的。
words.en: If you describe something as transcendent, you mean that it is extremely good or impressive, often in a way that goes beyond the ordinary.

words.ex: He gave a conciliatory smile to calm the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他露出和解的微笑来平息争执。
words.en: If you are conciliatory, you show that you are willing to end a disagreement with someone by doing or saying things that will please them.

words.tr: n. 良心的责备；后悔；悔恨
words.ex: He felt no compunction about lying to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他撒谎骗朋友时毫无愧疚。
words.en: A feeling of guilt or moral scruple that prevents or follows the doing of something bad.

words.tr: adj. 婚姻的；夫妻（关系）的
words.ex: They live a conjugal life with their children.
words.ex_cn: 他们与孩子一起过着夫妻生活。
words.en: Conjugal means relating to marriage or the relationship between husband and wife.

words.ex: He outdid his brother in the math competition.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学竞赛中胜过了他的哥哥。
words.en: To outdo someone means to be more successful than them in a particular activity.

words.ex: He wants to emigrate to Canada for a better life.
words.ex_cn: 他想移民到加拿大过更好的生活。
words.en: To leave one's own country in order to settle permanently in another.

words.ex: He added the bibliography at the end of his report.
words.ex_cn: 他在报告末尾添加了参考书目。
words.en: A bibliography is a list of the books and articles that have been used by someone when writing a particular book or article.

words.ex: The mushroom is comestible and safe to eat.
words.ex_cn: 这种蘑菇可食用且安全。
words.en: Something that is comestible is suitable or safe for eating.

words.tr: adj. 典范的；可做模范的；惩戒性的
words.ex: He is an exemplary student who always finishes his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名模范学生，总是完成作业。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as exemplary, you think they are extremely good and suitable to be copied by other people.

words.tr: adj. 似乎合理的；看似真实的；似乎可信的；看似真实的；
words.ex: His excuse sounded plausible.
words.ex_cn: 他的借口听起来似乎合理。
words.en: An explanation or statement that is plausible seems likely to be true or valid.

words.ex: The teacher will allot five minutes for questions.
words.ex_cn: 老师会分配五分钟提问。
words.en: If something is allotted to someone, it is given to them as their share.

words.tr: v. 侵蚀；腐蚀；逐渐丧失；削弱
words.ex: The wind erodes the sand slowly.
words.ex_cn: 风慢慢侵蚀着沙子。
words.en: If rock or soil erodes or is eroded by the weather, sea, or wind, it cracks and breaks so that it is gradually destroyed.

words.tr: n. 摧毁；拆毁；拆除；大败；
words.ex: The demolition of the old building started last week.
words.ex_cn: 那座旧楼的拆除上周开始了。
words.en: The act of demolishing something, especially a building.

words.ex: The team's loss was a total debacle.
words.ex_cn: 球队的失败是一场彻底的惨败。
words.en: A debacle is a sudden and complete failure or collapse, often in a way that is very embarrassing or causes a lot of damage.

words.ex: His stature in the scientific community is very high.
words.ex_cn: 他在科学界声望很高。
words.en: The height of a person or an animal in a standing position; the level of respect that people have for a person or organization because of their importance or success.

words.ex: The synonym of 'happy' is 'glad'.
words.ex_cn: ‘happy’的同义词是‘glad’。
words.en: A synonym is a word or phrase that means exactly or nearly the same as another word or phrase in the same language.

words.ex: They will negotiate the price with the seller.
words.ex_cn: 他们会与卖家协商价格。
words.en: If people negotiate with each other or negotiate an agreement, they talk about a problem or a situation such as a business arrangement in order to solve the problem or complete the arrangement.

words.ex: The projection of the movie started at 8 p.m.
words.ex_cn: 电影的放映晚上8点开始。
words.en: A projection is an estimate or forecast of a future situation or trend based on a study of present ones.

words.ex: His testimony proved the suspect was innocent.
words.ex_cn: 他的证词证明了嫌疑人是无辜的。
words.en: A formal written or spoken statement, especially one given in a court of law.

words.ex: He has an aversion to spicy food.
words.ex_cn: 他厌恶辛辣食物。
words.en: A strong dislike or disinclination towards someone or something.

words.ex: His avarice knew no bounds, always seeking more wealth.
words.ex_cn: 他的贪婪无止境，总是追求更多的财富。
words.en: Avarice is extremely strong desire for money and possessions.

words.tr: n. 自动装置；机器人；机器人似的人
words.ex: The factory was filled with automatons that performed repetitive tasks.
words.ex_cn: 工厂里满是执行重复任务的自动机。
words.en: An automaton is a machine that operates on its own without the need for human control, especially a robot in the form of a human.

words.ex: He is a legendary basketball player.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位传奇的篮球运动员。
words.en: Something or someone that is legendary is very famous and is often talked about in a way that suggests they are almost mythical.

words.tr: v. 豪饮；痛饮；开怀畅饮
words.ex: He quaffed the cold drink quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他快速地喝下了那杯冷饮。
words.en: To drink (a beverage) heartily and with gusto.

words.tr: v. 使显得琐碎（或不重要、不难等）
words.ex: He trivializes serious problems by laughing at them.
words.ex_cn: 他通过嘲笑严重的问题来轻视它们。
words.en: If you say that someone trivializes something important, you disapprove of them because they make it seem less important, serious, or complex than it is.

words.ex: The storm caused unprecedented damage.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴造成了前所未有的破坏。
words.en: If something is unprecedented, it has never happened before.

words.tr:
v. 艰难地行走；吃力地行进
n. 劳苦；沉重的脚步（声）
words.ex: He plodded through the snow with heavy boots.
words.ex_cn: 他穿着沉重的靴子艰难地在雪地中行走。
words.en: To plod means to walk slowly with heavy steps, especially because you are tired or working hard. It can also mean to work slowly and steadily at something, especially something that is boring or difficult.

words.ex: They conspire to cheat on the test.
words.ex_cn: 他们密谋在考试中作弊。
words.en: If two or more people or groups conspire to do something illegal or harmful, they make a secret agreement to do it.

words.tr:
v. （因发言冗长）妨碍（会议的进程）
n. （议会中为拖延表决的）冗长演说
words.ex: The senator used a filibuster to delay the vote on the bill.
words.ex_cn: 参议员使用阻挠议事行动来拖延对该法案的投票。
words.en: A filibuster is a tactic used in a legislative assembly to prevent a measure from being brought to a vote. It is most commonly associated with the U.S. Senate, where a senator or a group of senators may extend debate on a proposal indefinitely to delay or entirely prevent a decision on it.

words.tr: v. 使惊呆；使惊愕；使神志不清
words.ex: The sudden noise stupefied everyone.
words.ex_cn: 突然的噪音让所有人都惊呆了。
words.en: To stupefy someone means to make them unable to think clearly or to be surprised or shocked.

words.tr:
n. 怨恨；积怨；嫌隙
v. 勉强做；不情愿地给；吝惜
words.ex: He holds a grudge against his brother.
words.ex_cn: 他对他哥哥心怀怨恨。
words.en: A grudge is a persistent feeling of ill will or resentment resulting from a past insult or injury.

words.ex: She confides in her best friend.
words.ex_cn: 她向最好的朋友倾诉。
words.en: If you confide in someone, you tell them a secret.

words.tr:
n. 法令；判决
v. 判决；颁布；裁定
words.ex: The king issued a decree to stop the war.
words.ex_cn: 国王发布了一项法令来停止战争。
words.en: An official order issued by a legal authority.

words.ex: He staggered home after drinking too much.
words.ex_cn: 他喝多了后摇摇晃晃地走回家。
words.en: If you stagger, you walk very unsteadily, as if you are about to fall.

words.ex: The data points correlate with each other.
words.ex_cn: 这些数据点相互关联。
words.en: If one thing correlates with another, there is a close similarity or connection between them, often because one thing causes the other.

words.ex: He bought a new mirror because of his vanity.
words.ex_cn: 他因为虚荣心买了一面新镜子。
words.en: The quality of being vain; excessive pride in or admiration of one's own appearance or achievements.

words.ex: The benevolent man gave food to the poor.
words.ex_cn: 这位慈善的人给穷人提供了食物。
words.en: If you describe a person in authority as benevolent, you mean that they are kind and fair.

words.ex: He has a dual role as teacher and coach.
words.ex_cn: 他同时担任老师和教练的双重角色。
words.en: Having two parts or aspects.

words.ex: This information is relevant to our project.
words.ex_cn: 这些信息与我们的项目相关。
words.en: Something that is relevant to a situation or person is important or significant in that situation or to that person.

words.tr: v. 使安静；安慰；使缓和
words.ex: She sang a song to soothe the baby.
words.ex_cn: 她唱了一首歌来安抚婴儿。
words.en: To soothe someone means to make them feel calmer and less anxious, upset, or angry.

words.ex: It was an utter mistake.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个完全的错误。
words.en: To say something or to make a sound with your voice; complete or absolute.

words.tr: v. 充塞；充血；使拥挤；充满
words.ex: The traffic congests the city center during rush hour.
words.ex_cn: 高峰时段，交通堵塞了市中心。
words.en: If a place is congested, it is extremely crowded and blocked with traffic or people.

words.tr: v. 缠住；“dog”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The reporter dogged the politician everywhere.
words.ex_cn: 记者紧紧跟随这位政治家到处。
words.en: If you describe someone's actions as dogged, you mean that they are determined to continue with something even if it becomes difficult or dangerous.

words.tr: adj. 粗鲁的；莽撞的；唐突的
words.ex: He gave a brusque answer and walked away.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁地回答了一句，然后走开了。
words.en: If you describe a person or their behaviour as brusque, you mean that they deal with or say things quickly and shortly, so that they seem to be rude.

words.tr: adj. 娴静的；端庄的；假装矜持的
words.ex: She is a demure girl who never speaks loudly.
words.ex_cn: 她是一个文静的女孩，从不大声说话。
words.en: If you describe someone, especially a young woman, as demure, you mean they are quiet, shy, and behave so that they do not attract attention to themselves.

words.ex: She works out to augment her strength.
words.ex_cn: 她锻炼以增强力量。
words.en: If you augment something, you make it larger, stronger, or more effective by adding something to it.

words.tr: v. 象征；代表；用符号表示
words.ex: The dove symbolizes peace.
words.ex_cn: 鸽子象征和平。
words.en: If one thing symbolizes another, it is used or regarded as a symbol of it.

words.tr: adj. 说不出口的；无法形容的；不可说的
words.ex: The atrocities committed were unspeakable.
words.ex_cn: 所犯下的暴行是无法形容的。
words.en: If you describe something as unspeakable, you are emphasizing that it is extremely unpleasant or bad.

words.ex: He felt animosity toward his neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他对邻居感到敌意。
words.en: Animosity is a strong feeling of dislike and anger towards someone.

words.tr:
n. 倒塌；崩溃；暴跌；
v. 倒塌；崩溃；
words.ex: The collapse of the old bridge caused many problems.
words.ex_cn: 这座旧桥的倒塌引起了诸多问题。
words.en: If a building or other structure collapses, it falls down very suddenly.

words.tr: adj. 可理解的；明白易懂的；清楚的
words.ex: His explanation was intelligible to everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他的解释人人都能听懂。
words.en: Capable of being understood; comprehensible.

words.tr: v. 获得；取得；得到；“acquire”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 后天习得的；已获得的；
words.ex: He acquired a new skill last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年获得了一项新技能。
words.en: If you acquire something, you buy or obtain it for yourself, or someone gives it to you.

words.ex: His pride begets conflict.
words.ex_cn: 他的骄傲招致了冲突。
words.en: To beget means to cause something to happen or exist.

words.tr: adj. 无定形的；无组织的；
words.ex: The glass is amorphous because it lacks a regular shape.
words.ex_cn: 玻璃是无定形的，因为它没有规则的形状。
words.en: Lacking a clear shape or form; not clearly defined or structured.

words.ex: Hiking up the mountain was a strenuous task.
words.ex_cn: 爬山是一项艰苦的任务。
words.en: Requiring or using great effort or exertion.

words.tr: adj. 昏昏欲睡的；困倦的；催眠的
words.ex: He felt drowsy after lunch.
words.ex_cn: 他午饭后感到昏昏欲睡。
words.en: If you feel drowsy, you feel sleepy and cannot think clearly.

words.tr:
adj. 不拘一格的；兼收并蓄的；折中的
n. 折中主义者
words.ex: He has an eclectic taste in music.
words.ex_cn: 他对音乐的品味很广泛多样。
words.en: An eclectic collection or group is a wide range of different things or people.

words.tr: adj. 荒唐的；荒唐可笑的；
words.ex: It's absurd to wear a coat in summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天穿外套是荒唐的。
words.en: If you say that something is absurd, you are criticizing it because you think that it is ridiculous or that it does not make sense.

words.ex: The doctor used drops to dilate her pupils.
words.ex_cn: 医生用了滴眼液来扩大她的瞳孔。
words.en: If you dilate something such as a part of your body, or if it dilates, it becomes larger or wider.

words.ex: He follows a systematic approach to solve math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他用一种系统的方法来解决数学问题。
words.en: A systematic approach or method is one that is done according to a fixed plan, in a thorough and efficient way.

words.ex: The boy was punished for his misdeed.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩因他的恶劣行为而受到惩罚。
words.en: A misdeed is a wrong or illegal deed; a crime or sin.

words.ex: The bright light stimulated her eyes.
words.ex_cn: 强烈的光线刺激了她的眼睛。
words.en: To stimulate something means to encourage it to begin or develop further.

words.tr:
v. 盖印；印刻；使铭记
n. 盖印；痕迹
words.ex: He used a stamp to imprint his name on the box.
words.ex_cn: 他用印章在盒子上盖印了他的名字。
words.en: To imprint something means to mark or stamp it with a design or a symbol. It can also mean to fix something firmly in someone's mind.

words.ex: He will not forsake his family.
words.ex_cn: 他不会抛弃他的家人。
words.en: If you forsake someone, you leave them when you should have stayed, or you stop helping them or looking after them.

words.tr: adj. 铁石心肠的；无情的；起老茧的
words.ex: He was callous to his friend's pain.
words.ex_cn: 他对朋友的痛苦无动于衷。
words.en: A callous person or action is very cruel and shows no concern for other people or their feelings.

words.ex: His misstep on the icy path led to a fall.
words.ex_cn: 他在结冰的小路上失足摔倒了。
words.en: A misstep is an unintentional mistake or error in judgment or action.

words.ex: He faced undue pressure from his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他受到了来自老板的过度压力。
words.en: If you describe something bad as undue, you mean that it is greater or more extreme than you think is reasonable or appropriate.

words.ex: The stock market shows daily fluctuation.
words.ex_cn: 股票市场每天都有波动。
words.en: A fluctuation is a change in something, especially in a continuous process such as temperature, prices, or levels of activity.

words.ex: The teacher asked us to dissect the poem line by line.
words.ex_cn: 老师让我们逐行仔细分析这首诗。
words.en: To dissect something means to cut it into pieces in order to examine its structure, or to study something in great detail.

words.ex: He used a simile to compare her eyes to stars.
words.ex_cn: 他用了明喻把她的眼睛比作星星。
words.en: A simile is a figure of speech that directly compares two different things, usually by employing the words 'like' or 'as'.

words.ex: The old factory is now a derelict building.
words.ex_cn: 那座旧工厂现在是一座破败的建筑。
words.en: If a building or a piece of land is derelict, it is not cared for and is in bad condition. A derelict person or thing is one that has been abandoned or neglected.

words.ex: His opinion is subordinate to the manager's.
words.ex_cn: 他的意见比经理的次要。
words.en: If someone is your subordinate, they have a less important position than you in the organization that you both work for.

words.ex: The team comprises five players and one coach.
words.ex_cn: 这个团队包括五名球员和一名教练。
words.en: If you say that something comprises or is comprised of a number of things or people, you mean it has them as its parts or members.

words.ex: He went back to retrieve his keys.
words.ex_cn: 他回去取回他的钥匙。
words.en: To retrieve something means to get it back from somewhere, especially after it has been lost or taken away.

words.ex: The dragon is an imaginary creature.
words.ex_cn: 龙是一种想象中的生物。
words.en: An imaginary person, place, or thing is one that does not exist or is not real, but that people think about or talk about.

words.ex: He works on a naval ship.
words.ex_cn: 他在一艘军舰上工作。
words.en: Naval means relating to the navy, especially to ships that are used in war.

words.tr: adj. 傲慢的；盲目自大的
words.ex: His bumptious attitude annoyed everyone at the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他傲慢的态度让会议上的每个人都感到不快。
words.en: If you say that someone is bumptious, you are criticizing them because they are very pleased with themselves and their opinions.

words.ex: They decided to prolong the meeting by one hour.
words.ex_cn: 他们决定将会议延长一小时。
words.en: To prolong something means to make it last longer.

words.ex: His ulterior motive was to get money.
words.ex_cn: 他别有用心，目的是弄到钱。
words.en: If you say that someone has an ulterior motive for doing something, you believe that they have a hidden reason for doing it.

words.tr: adj. 无关紧要的；不相关的；
words.ex: His opinion is irrelevant to the decision.
words.ex_cn: 他的意见与这个决定无关紧要。
words.en: If you describe something as irrelevant, you mean that it is not important to or not connected with the present situation or discussion.

words.tr: n. 一致同意；全体赞同
words.ex: The team showed unanimity in voting for the new plan.
words.ex_cn: 团队在投票支持新计划时意见一致。
words.en: Unanimity is complete agreement among all members of a group.

words.ex: He failed the test, but subsequent efforts helped him pass.
words.ex_cn: 他考试没及格，但随后的努力让他通过了。
words.en: Following in time or order; succeeding.

words.ex: The joy was transient, like a brief smile.
words.ex_cn: 这种快乐是短暂的，像一个短暂的微笑。
words.en: If you describe something as transient, you mean that it lasts only for a short time.

words.ex: He learned a new technique to paint better.
words.ex_cn: 他学了一种新的绘画技术。
words.en: A technique is a particular method of doing an activity, usually a method that involves practical skills.

words.ex: He loves studying geology in high school.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢在高中学习地质学。
words.en: The science which deals with the physical structure and substance of the earth, their history, and the processes which act on them.

words.tr: n. 冒充内行者；庸医；骗子
words.ex: He is a charlatan who pretends to be a doctor.
words.ex_cn: 他是个冒充医生的骗子。
words.en: A charlatan is someone who pretends to have skills or knowledge that they do not really possess.

words.ex: The gravity of Earth pulls objects down.
words.ex_cn: 地球的重力把物体往下拉。
words.en: Gravity is the force that causes things to fall towards the Earth or towards any other physical body having mass.

words.tr: v. 详细说明；详细解释
words.ex: He will explicate the meaning of the poem.
words.ex_cn: 他将解释这首诗的含义。
words.en: To explicate something means to explain it in detail, making it clear and understandable.

words.tr:
n. 诱饵；（诱捕鸟兽的）动物
v. 引诱
words.ex: The hunter used a decoy to attract ducks.
words.ex_cn: 猎人用假鸭子来吸引鸭子。
words.en: A decoy is a person, thing, or action that is used to trick someone into doing something or going somewhere, especially by making them think they are going to get something they want.

words.tr: adj. 预言的；预示的；先知的
words.ex: His words were prophetic when the storm came.
words.ex_cn: 当风暴来临时，他的话应验了。
words.en: If something was prophetic, it described or suggested something that did actually happen later.

words.tr: adj. 比喻的；象征的；写实的
words.ex: He used figurative language to describe his feelings.
words.ex_cn: 他用了比喻性的语言来描述他的感受。
words.en: If you use a word or expression in a figurative sense, you use it with a more abstract or imaginative meaning than its ordinary literal one.

words.ex: The demise of the old king shocked the nation.
words.ex_cn: 老国王的去世震惊了全国。
words.en: The demise of something or someone is their end or death.

words.ex: I can't swim.
words.ex_cn: 我不会游泳。
words.en: Cannot; used to indicate that something is not possible or allowed.

words.tr:
n. 叙述；叙事；
adj. 叙述性的；
words.ex: He told a simple narrative about his childhood.
words.ex_cn: 他讲了一个关于他童年的简单故事。
words.en: A narrative is a story or an account of a series of events.

words.ex: His answer was erroneous because he added wrong.
words.ex_cn: 他的答案是错误的，因为他加错了。
words.en: If you describe someone's beliefs or opinions as erroneous, you mean that they are incorrect and based on false information.

words.ex: The acme of his career was winning the Nobel Prize.
words.ex_cn: 他职业生涯的顶点是获得诺贝尔奖。
words.en: The highest point of achievement or excellence.

words.tr:
n. 潜力；
adj. 潜在的；
words.ex: The young athlete shows great potential.
words.ex_cn: 这位年轻运动员展现出巨大的潜力。
words.en: If you say that someone or something has potential, you mean that they have the necessary abilities or qualities to become successful or useful in the future.

words.ex: The conflagration destroyed the whole forest.
words.ex_cn: 这场大火烧毁了整个森林。
words.en: A conflagration is a large and destructive fire that causes considerable damage.

words.ex: There are only two extant copies of the ancient book.
words.ex_cn: 这本古书现存只有两份。
words.en: If something is extant, it is still in existence, in spite of being very old.

words.ex: He is adroit at fixing broken machines.
words.ex_cn: 他擅长修理坏掉的机器。
words.en: Someone who is adroit is quick and skillful in their thoughts, behavior, or actions.

words.ex: His salary is commensurate with his experience.
words.ex_cn: 他的薪水与他的经验相称。
words.en: If the level of one thing is commensurate with another, the first level is in proportion to the second.

words.ex: They collaborate to finish the project.
words.ex_cn: 他们合作完成这个项目。
words.en: to work jointly with others or together especially in an intellectual endeavor

words.ex: I anticipate rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我预料明天会下雨。
words.en: If you anticipate an event, you realize in advance that it may happen and you are prepared for it.

words.tr: v. 躺；靠在；向后倾斜（坐椅）
words.ex: He reclines on the sofa after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他晚饭后躺在沙发上。
words.en: To recline means to lean or lie back in a relaxed position with the body supported.

words.tr:
n. 素食者；食草动物；
adj. 素食者的；素菜的；
words.ex: He is a vegetarian and doesn't eat meat.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名素食者，不吃肉。
words.en: A vegetarian is someone who does not eat meat or fish, and sometimes other animal products, especially for moral, religious, or health reasons.

words.ex: The book encompasses all basic math skills.
words.ex_cn: 这本书包含了所有基础数学技能。
words.en: If something encompasses particular things, it includes them.

words.tr:
adj. 下意识的；潜意识的；
n. 潜意识；下意识；
words.ex: He made a subconscious decision to help her.
words.ex_cn: 他下意识地决定帮助她。
words.en: The subconscious is the part of your mind that contains feelings and thoughts that you are not directly aware of but that can influence your behavior and emotions.

words.ex: The frog is an amphibious animal.
words.ex_cn: 青蛙是一种两栖动物。
words.en: An amphibious vehicle or craft is one that can operate on both land and water.

words.tr: adj. 善于接受的；能接纳的；
words.ex: He is receptive to new ideas.
words.ex_cn: 他善于接受新想法。
words.en: Willing to consider or accept new suggestions and ideas.

words.ex: The chef made a deft cut with the knife.
words.ex_cn: 厨师用刀熟练地切了一下。
words.en: A deft action is skilful and often quick.

words.tr:
v. 挑毛病；吹毛求疵
n. 挑剔；挑毛病
words.ex: He cavils at every small mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他挑剔每一个小错误。
words.en: If you say that someone cavils at something, you mean that they make criticisms of it that you think are unimportant or unnecessary.

words.ex: She abominates cruelty to animals.
words.ex_cn: 她痛恨对动物的残忍行为。
words.en: If you abominate something, you hate it very much.

words.ex: The moon reached its apogee last night.
words.ex_cn: 昨晚月亮到达了远地点。
words.en: The highest point in the development of something; a climax or culmination.

words.tr: n. 迷宫；错综复杂的曲径；
words.ex: The children got lost in the maze.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在迷宫里迷路了。
words.en: A maze is a complex system of paths or passages in which it is easy to get lost.

words.tr: n. 集合；合流；群众；中央大厅；车站广场
words.ex: The concourse of people filled the square.
words.ex_cn: 人群集合在广场上。
words.en: A concourse is a large open area inside or in front of a public building, such as a station or an airport, where people can meet or wait.

words.tr: v. 从事于；（使）参与；“engage”的现在分词； adj. 有趣的；
words.ex: He is engaging in community service.
words.ex_cn: 他正在从事社区服务。
words.en: An engaging person or thing is pleasant, interesting, and entertaining.

words.ex: The ship dropped its anchor in the harbor.
words.ex_cn: 船在港口放下了锚。
words.en: An anchor is a heavy object that is dropped from a boat or a ship into the water to prevent the vessel from moving.

words.tr:
v. 挡开；避开；回避
n. 挡开；闪避
words.ex: He parries the punch with his arm.
words.ex_cn: 他用胳膊格挡了这一拳。
words.en: If you parry a question or argument, you cleverly avoid answering it or dealing with it. In fencing, if you parry a blow, you defend yourself against it by pushing it away with your weapon.

words.ex: The two notes sound harmonic together.
words.ex_cn: 这两个音听起来很和谐。
words.en: Relating to or characterized by harmony; pleasing to the ear; melodious.

words.tr:
v. 打滚；翻滚
n. 混乱的一堆
words.ex: The box was full of a welter of old toys.
words.ex_cn: 盒子里堆满了各种旧玩具。
words.en: A welter is a state of general confusion or disorder. It can also refer to a heavy or confused mass of something, such as a welter of papers.

words.tr: v. 先占；使全神贯注；占据…的思想
words.ex: The old man preoccupies the best seat in the park.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人先占了公园里最好的座位。
words.en: If something is preoccupying you, you are thinking about it a lot or it is occupying your attention.

words.tr:
v. 触发；引起；发动；
n. 诱因；触发；
words.ex: The loud noise triggered the alarm.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音触发了警报。
words.en: A trigger is a device that activates a mechanism when it is pulled or pressed. It can also refer to something that causes a particular reaction or development.

words.ex: Water causes erosion of the soil.
words.ex_cn: 水会导致土壤腐蚀。
words.en: The process by which the surface of the earth is worn away by the action of water, glaciers, winds, waves, etc.

words.tr: v. 暂停；中止；延期； suspending
words.ex: The school will suspend the class due to snow.
words.ex_cn: 由于下雪，学校将暂停课程。
words.en: If you suspend something, you delay it or stop it from happening for a while or until a decision is made about it.

words.ex: The verification of the password took only a few seconds.
words.ex_cn: 密码的验证只花了几秒钟。
words.en: Verification is the process of establishing the truth, accuracy, or validity of something.

words.ex: The remnant of the old wall still stands.
words.ex_cn: 这堵旧墙的残余部分仍然矗立着。
words.en: A remnant is a small remaining quantity of something.

words.tr: adj. 迷信的；有迷信观念的
words.ex: He is superstitious about walking under ladders.
words.ex_cn: 他迷信地认为走过梯子下面会带来厄运。
words.en: Having or showing a belief in superstitions.

words.tr: v. 以朋友态度对待；帮助
words.ex: He decided to befriend the new student.
words.ex_cn: 他决定结交那个新生。
words.en: To befriend someone means to act as a friend to them by offering help, support, or companionship.

words.tr:
adj. 青少年的；幼稚的；
n. 少年；
words.ex: The book is written for juvenile readers.
words.ex_cn: 这本书是为青少年读者撰写的。
words.en: A juvenile is a child or young person who is not yet old enough to be considered an adult.

words.tr: n. 恩人；捐助者；赠送者
words.ex: The benefactor gave money to the school.
words.ex_cn: 资助人捐钱给学校。
words.en: A benefactor is a person who gives money or other help to a person or cause.

words.tr: adj. 有害的；造成伤害的
words.ex: Smoking has deleterious effects on your health.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟对你的健康有害。
words.en: Something that is deleterious has a harmful effect on something, especially on a person's health.

words.ex: He felt contentment after a simple dinner with his family.
words.ex_cn: 他在与家人共进一顿简单的晚餐后感到满足。
words.en: Contentment is a feeling of happiness and satisfaction.

words.ex: He gave a contemptuous smile when she spoke.
words.ex_cn: 当她说话时，他露出轻蔑的微笑。
words.en: If you are contemptuous of someone or something, you do not like or respect them at all.

words.ex: His contemptible lie made everyone angry.
words.ex_cn: 他可鄙的谎言让所有人都生气了。
words.en: If you feel that someone or something is contemptible, you feel strong dislike and lack of respect for them.

words.ex: The two situations are analogous.
words.ex_cn: 这两种情况是相似的。
words.en: If one thing is analogous to another, the two things are similar in some way.

words.tr: adj. 痛苦的；严重的；剧烈的
words.ex: The injury caused him grievous pain.
words.ex_cn: 这次受伤给他带来了巨大的痛苦。
words.en: If you describe something such as a loss or injury as grievous, you mean that it is extremely serious or worrying in its effects.

words.tr: n. 长诗的篇章（相当于书的一章）
words.ex: The poem is divided into several cantos.
words.ex_cn: 这首诗被分为几个篇章。
words.en: A canto is a principal division of a long poem or a section of a song.

words.tr:
prep. 除…以外；除非
v. 闩（门等）；阻碍；“bar”的现在分词
words.ex: Barring any unforeseen circumstances, the project will be completed on time.
words.ex_cn: 除非发生意外情况，否则项目将按时完成。
words.en: Unless there is something that prevents it from happening, barring is used to indicate that something will happen.

words.tr: adj. 像伯伯（或叔叔）似的；长辈风范的；慈爱的
words.ex: His avuncular demeanor put everyone at ease.
words.ex_cn: 他慈祥的态度让每个人都感到轻松。
words.en: If someone is avuncular, they are kind and helpful towards younger or less experienced people, in a way that is typical of an uncle.

words.ex: The storm bereaved the village of its power.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴使村庄失去了电力。
words.en: To deprive someone of a loved one through death.

words.tr: v. 使有生气；使生动活泼
words.ex: The painter uses bright colors to vivify the old mural.
words.ex_cn: 画家用鲜艳的色彩使这幅旧壁画焕发生机。
words.en: To give life or animation to; to enliven.

words.ex: He will append his name to the list.
words.ex_cn: 他将在名单上加上他的名字。
words.en: To add something to the end of a piece of writing.

words.ex: The teacher will appraise my essay next week.
words.ex_cn: 老师下周会评价我的作文。
words.en: If you appraise something or someone, you consider them carefully and form an opinion about them.

words.ex: I appreciate the beauty of nature.
words.ex_cn: 我欣赏大自然的美。
words.en: If you appreciate something, you recognize its value and feel grateful for it.

words.ex: He has prejudice against people from other countries.
words.ex_cn: 他对来自其他国家的人有偏见。
words.en: Prejudice is an unreasonable dislike of a particular group of people or things, or a preference for one group of people or things over another.

words.tr: adj. 适当的；合适的；恰当的；
words.ex: This dress is appropriate for a wedding.
words.ex_cn: 这条裙子适合参加婚礼。
words.en: Something that is appropriate is suitable or acceptable for a particular situation.

words.ex: There were candies galore at the party.
words.ex_cn: 聚会上有大量的糖果。
words.en: If you say that there is something galore, you mean that there is a lot of it.

words.tr: n. （年纪大的）坏脾气的人；脾气暴躁的人
words.ex: He was known as a curmudgeon who rarely smiled.
words.ex_cn: 他以脾气坏著称，很少笑。
words.en: A curmudgeon is a bad-tempered or difficult person, especially an old one.

words.ex: The knight held up his shield to block the arrow.
words.ex_cn: 骑士举起盾牌来挡箭。
words.en: A shield is a piece of armor held in the hand or worn on the arm to protect the body from missiles or blows. It can also refer to something that protects or defends someone or something from harm or danger.

words.ex: She coddles her little brother too much.
words.ex_cn: 她太宠着她的弟弟了。
words.en: To treat someone in an indulgent or overprotective way.

words.tr:
adj. 收敛性的；止血的；辛辣的；严厉的；涩的
n. 收敛剂； 止血药
words.ex: The astringent lotion helps reduce swelling.
words.ex_cn: 这种收敛性的爽肤水有助于减轻肿胀。
words.en: An astringent substance causes the contraction of body tissues, typically used to reduce bleeding from minor abrasions or as a skin toner.

words.ex: His sadness manifested in his quiet eyes.
words.ex_cn: 他的悲伤表现在他安静的眼神中。
words.en: To manifest something means to show it clearly and visibly.

words.tr: v. 深思熟虑；慎重考虑
words.ex: He cogitates before he answers the question.
words.ex_cn: 他在回答问题之前会深思。
words.en: To think deeply about something; to ponder or meditate.

words.ex: The ticket is invalid because it expired.
words.ex_cn: 这张票无效，因为它已经过期了。
words.en: If something is invalid, it is not legally or officially acceptable, or it is not based on truth or reason.

words.tr: adj. 可核实的；能证实的
words.ex: The result must be verifiable by anyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个结果必须能被任何人验证。
words.en: Capable of being verified or confirmed by evidence or testimony.

words.ex: The team was unanimous in choosing the new leader.
words.ex_cn: 团队在选择新领导时意见完全一致。
words.en: When a group of people are unanimous, they all agree about something or all vote for the same thing.

words.ex: He dominates the conversation.
words.ex_cn: 他主宰了谈话。
words.en: To dominate means to control or govern someone or something, or to be the most important or noticeable feature of something.

words.ex: The cheese is a derivative of milk.
words.ex_cn: 这种奶酪是牛奶的派生物。
words.en: A derivative is something which has been developed or obtained from something else.

words.ex: They deride him for wearing old clothes.
words.ex_cn: 他们嘲笑他穿旧衣服。
words.en: If you deride someone or something, you say that they are stupid or have no value.

words.ex: He chose teaching as his vocation.
words.ex_cn: 他选择了教学作为自己的职业。
words.en: A vocation is a type of work that you feel you are especially suited to do and to which you give much of your time and energy.

words.ex: The centurion led the Roman soldiers.
words.ex_cn: 百夫长带领着罗马士兵。
words.en: In ancient Rome, a centurion was an officer in charge of a century, a unit of the Roman army.

words.ex: He used artifice to win the game.
words.ex_cn: 他用诡计赢得了比赛。
words.en: Clever or cunning devices or expedients, especially as used to trick or deceive others.

words.tr: adj. 日间活动的；昼行性的
words.ex: The bird sings during diurnal hours.
words.ex_cn: 这只鸟在白天活动时鸣叫。
words.en: Relating to or occurring in a 24-hour period; daily.

words.tr:
n. 抢救；
v. 打捞；挽救；抢救；
words.ex: The salvage of the ship took three days.
words.ex_cn: 对这艘船的抢救花了三天时间。
words.en: To salvage something means to retrieve or preserve it from loss or destruction, especially from a shipwreck or fire. It can also refer to the act of saving or rescuing something from a difficult situation.

words.ex: The country tried to devalue its currency.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家试图使本国货币贬值。
words.en: If you devalue something, you cause it to be thought less impressive or less deserving of respect.

words.ex: He is ambidextrous and can write with both hands.
words.ex_cn: 他是左右手都灵巧的，可以用两只手写字。
words.en: Someone who is ambidextrous can use both their right and left hands equally well.

words.ex: The cacophony of car horns made it hard to think.
words.ex_cn: 汽车喇叭的刺耳噪音让人难以思考。
words.en: A cacophony is a mixture of loud and usually unpleasant sounds.

words.tr: adj. 即将发生的；临近的；
words.ex: An imminent storm is coming soon.
words.ex_cn: 一场即将发生的风暴很快就要来了。
words.en: If you say that something is imminent, especially something unpleasant, you mean it is almost certain to happen very soon.

words.ex: This is a comparative study of two languages.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个关于两种语言的比较研究。
words.en: You use comparative to show that you are judging something against a previous or different situation. For example, if you say that something is comparative luxury, you mean that it is luxurious compared to something else.

words.ex: I can't tolerate loud noises.
words.ex_cn: 我无法容忍巨大的噪音。
words.en: If you tolerate a situation or person, you accept them although you do not particularly like them.

words.ex: The castle endured a long siege during the war.
words.ex_cn: 这座城堡在战争中经历了长期的围攻。
words.en: A siege is a military operation in which enemy forces surround a town or building, cutting off essential supplies, with the aim of compelling those inside to surrender.

words.tr: adj. 善良的；慈祥的；有益的；良性的（肿瘤）
words.ex: The benignant old man always helped his neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 那位善良的老人总是帮助他的邻居。
words.en: A benignant person or action is kind and helpful, often in a way that shows they are concerned about the welfare of others.

words.tr: n. 营养品；养料；营养的来源；食物
words.ex: Food provides nutriment for the body.
words.ex_cn: 食物为身体提供营养。
words.en: Nutriment refers to substances that provide nourishment essential for the maintenance of life and for growth.

words.ex: Water can penetrate the soil slowly.
words.ex_cn: 水可以慢慢渗透进土壤。
words.en: To penetrate means to enter or pass through something, especially when this is difficult or when it is not obvious how to do it.

words.tr: n. 突降；苍白无力的结尾；令人扫兴的结尾
words.ex: The movie ended with an anticlimax.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影以一个平淡的结局收尾。
words.en: An anticlimax is a disappointing end to an exciting or impressive series of events.

words.ex: Children are vulnerable to colds in winter.
words.ex_cn: 儿童在冬天容易感冒。
words.en: If someone or something is vulnerable, they are weak and without protection, with the result that they are easily hurt physically or emotionally.

words.ex: He turned his head to avert the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他转过头去避免了事故。
words.en: If you avert something unpleasant, you prevent it from happening.

words.ex: The occupant of the room is sleeping.
words.ex_cn: 房间里的住户正在睡觉。
words.en: An occupant is someone who lives in or uses a particular room, building, or area of land.

words.ex: The government must redress the unfair law.
words.ex_cn: 政府必须纠正这部不公平的法律。
words.en: If you redress something such as a wrong or a complaint, you do something to correct it or to improve things for the person who has been wronged.

words.ex: His cupidity led him to make risky investments.
words.ex_cn: 他的贪婪导致他进行了高风险的投资。
words.en: Intense desire for wealth or possessions; greed.

words.ex: He shuns loud parties because he is shy.
words.ex_cn: 他因为害羞而避开热闹的派对。
words.en: If you shun someone or something, you deliberately avoid them or keep away from them.

words.ex: Her talent is unparalleled.
words.ex_cn: 她的才华是无比的。
words.en: Having no parallel or equal; unmatched.

words.tr: v. 制定（法律）；通过（法律）；扮演（角色）
words.ex: The government will enact a new law next month.
words.ex_cn: 政府下个月将颁布一项新法律。
words.en: To enact a law or rule means to make it official by passing it through a legislative body.

words.ex: He ignored the frivolous complaint and focused on the real issue.
words.ex_cn: 他忽略了这个无关紧要的投诉，专注于真正的问题。
words.en: If you describe someone as frivolous, you mean they behave in a silly or light-hearted way, rather than being serious and sensible.

words.ex: The birds live in a quiet marsh.
words.ex_cn: 这些鸟生活在一片宁静的沼泽中。
words.en: A marsh is an area of low-lying land which is flooded in wet seasons or at high tide, and typically remains waterlogged at all times.

words.ex: His supposition is that it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他的假设是明天会下雨。
words.en: A supposition is a guess or a theory that you have about something, which may not be true.

words.ex: The government does a census every ten years.
words.ex_cn: 政府每十年进行一次人口普查。
words.en: A census is an official count or survey of a population, typically recording various details of individuals.

words.tr: adj. 难以捉摸的；不易被抓获（觉察、理解或记忆）的；
words.ex: The truth remained elusive.
words.ex_cn: 真相难以捉摸。
words.en: Difficult to find, catch, or achieve; difficult to remember or understand.

words.ex: The ceremony was solemn and quiet.
words.ex_cn: 仪式庄严而安静。
words.en: Solemn means very serious and not cheerful, often because something important or sad is happening or being remembered.

words.tr: adj. 恶魔似的；残忍的；穷凶极恶的
words.ex: The plot of the movie was diabolical, filled with twists and turns.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影的情节充满了曲折和转折，非常恶魔化。
words.en: If you describe something as diabolical, you are emphasizing that it is very bad, extreme, or unpleasant.

words.tr: adj. 无法解释的；不能理解的；无责任的
words.ex: The manager made unaccountable decisions.
words.ex_cn: 这位经理做出了无法解释的决定。
words.en: If someone or something is unaccountable, there is no way of explaining why they behave in a particular way, and it is often strange or surprising.

words.ex: He showed deference to his teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他对老师表示尊敬。
words.en: Deference is a polite and respectful attitude towards someone, often because they are older or more experienced than you.

words.tr:
adj. （《圣经》中所说的大洪水前的）古老的；过时的
n.  年迈的人；不合时宜的人
words.ex: He uses an antediluvian typewriter to write letters.
words.ex_cn: 他用一台远古的打字机写信。
words.en: Belonging to the time before the biblical Flood; very old or old-fashioned.

words.ex: The watch works with great precision.
words.ex_cn: 这块手表运行得非常精确。
words.en: Precision is the quality of being exact and accurate.

words.tr:
n. 佯攻；虚击；假象
v. 佯攻；佯击；假装
words.ex: He made a feint to the left, then kicked right.
words.ex_cn: 他假装向左，然后右脚踢球。
words.en: A feint is a movement or an action that is intended to deceive someone, for example by making them think that you are going to do one thing when you are really going to do something else.

words.ex: He made a digression to tell a funny story.
words.ex_cn: 他岔开话题讲了个有趣的故事。
words.en: A digression is a temporary departure from the main subject in speech or writing.

words.tr: adj. 回顾的；回想的；溯及既往的
words.ex: He made a retrospective look at his childhood.
words.ex_cn: 他回顾了自己的童年。
words.en: A retrospective is an exhibition or compilation showing the development of an artist's work over a period of time. It can also refer to a look back at past events or situations.

words.ex: He wants to pursue his dream of becoming a writer.
words.ex_cn: 他想追求成为作家的梦想。
words.en: If you pursue an activity, interest, or plan, you carry it out or follow it.

words.tr: adj. 密切注意的；深切留心的
words.ex: He remained heedful of the teacher's instructions throughout the experiment.
words.ex_cn: 在整个实验过程中，他始终注意老师的指示。
words.en: If you are heedful of something, you pay careful attention to it.

words.tr: v. 晒太阳（取暖）；沉浸于
words.ex: He basks in the warm sunlight.
words.ex_cn: 他沐浴在温暖的阳光下。
words.en: If you bask in the sunshine, you lie somewhere sunny and enjoy the heat.

words.ex: The repetition of the same words made the lesson boring.
words.ex_cn: 相同词语的重复让这堂课变得无聊。
words.en: The act of repeating something that has already been said or written.

words.ex: The plan went awry when the rain started.
words.ex_cn: 当雨下起来时，计划就出差错了。
words.en: If something goes awry, it does not happen in the way that was planned.

words.tr: v. 接着发生；因而产生
words.ex: The storm ended, and peace ensued.
words.ex_cn: 风暴结束后，和平随之而来。
words.en: If something ensues, it happens immediately after another event, usually as a result of it.

words.ex: The lustrous pearl shone under the light.
words.ex_cn: 这颗有光泽的珍珠在光下闪耀。
words.en: Something that is lustrous shines brightly and gently, often because it is very smooth or clean.

words.ex: The answer is deducible from the given numbers.
words.ex_cn: 这个答案可以从给定的数字中推导出来。
words.en: If something is deducible, it can be logically inferred or concluded from something else.

words.ex: He felt a warm reminiscence of his childhood.
words.ex_cn: 他感受到了对童年的温馨回忆。
words.en: The act or process of recalling past experiences, events, etc.

words.tr: v. 使成杂色；使多样化
words.ex: The artist variegate the wall with colorful paints.
words.ex_cn: 艺术家用彩色油漆使墙壁变得五彩斑斓。
words.en: To make something more diverse or varied in appearance by adding different colors or elements.

words.ex: He is a dutiful son who helps his parents every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个孝顺的儿子，每天帮助父母。
words.en: Someone who is dutiful is careful to do the things that they are expected to do.

words.ex: He tried to inveigle her into lending him money.
words.ex_cn: 他试图哄骗她借钱给他。
words.en: If you inveigle someone into doing something, you cleverly persuade them to do it when they do not really want to.

words.tr: v. 倾倒；摇摇欲坠；将…推翻；使…跌倒
words.ex: The strong wind toppled the old tree.
words.ex_cn: 大风把那棵老树吹倒了。
words.en: If someone or something topples, or if someone or something topples them, they become unsteady or unstable and fall over.

words.tr:
n. 试听；试唱；试演；听力
v. 试听；试音；试镜；让…试演
words.ex: He went to an audition for the school play.
words.ex_cn: 他去参加学校话剧的试听。
words.en: An audition is a short performance given by an actor, dancer, or musician so that someone can decide if they are good enough to be in a play, film, or orchestra.

words.ex: The drought depletes the water supply.
words.ex_cn: 干旱耗尽了水源。
words.en: If you deplete something, you reduce the amount of it that is available or that exists.

words.tr:
n. 有志者；立志…的人
adj. 有野心的；有抱负的
words.ex: He is an aspirant for the job.
words.ex_cn: 他是这份工作的求职者。
words.en: An aspirant is someone who is ambitious and eager to achieve a particular goal or position.

words.ex: The evolution of birds from dinosaurs took millions of years.
words.ex_cn: 鸟类从恐龙进化而来花了数百万年。
words.en: The gradual development of something, especially from a simple to a more complex form.

words.ex: He quit his job because of coercion from his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他因为老板的强迫而辞了工作。
words.en: The act of persuading someone to do something by using force or threats.

words.tr: v. 给予 ... 生命力； 激发
words.ex: The new paint will vitalize the old house.
words.ex_cn: 新油漆会让这栋老房子焕然一新。
words.en: To give life or energy to something, making it more active or successful.

words.ex: He read a historical book about ancient Rome.
words.ex_cn: 他读了一本关于古罗马的历史书。
words.en: Historical means relating to the study of history or connected with the past.

words.tr:
adj. 辅助的；附属的
n. 辅助物；附属物；助动词
words.ex: He used an auxiliary verb to form the past tense.
words.ex_cn: 他使用了一个助动词来构成过去时。
words.en: An auxiliary is a person or thing that provides additional help or support.

words.ex: The sun makes the puddle evaporate quickly.
words.ex_cn: 太阳使水坑很快蒸发。
words.en: If a liquid evaporates, or if something evaporates it, it changes from a liquid state to a gas, because its temperature has increased.

words.tr: adj. 不同的；多种多样的；
words.ex: The class has diverse students from many countries.
words.ex_cn: 这个班级有来自许多国家的不同学生。
words.en: If a group or range of things is diverse, it is made up of a wide variety of things.

words.ex: He worked hard to accomplish his goal.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作以实现自己的目标。
words.en: To accomplish something means to succeed in doing it, especially after a lot of effort.

words.ex: He remained passive during the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他在争论中保持被动。
words.en: Accepting or allowing what happens or what others do, without active response or resistance.

words.tr: adj. 逻辑上的；合乎逻辑的；
words.ex: His argument is logical and easy to understand.
words.ex_cn: 他的论点合乎逻辑，容易理解。
words.en: In accordance with the principles of logic; reasonable.

words.tr:
n. 流量；流动；变动
v. 熔化；熔解；流出
words.ex: The flux of water through the pipe is very high.
words.ex_cn: 管道中水的流量非常高。
words.en: Flux is a state of constant change or a flow of liquid.

words.ex: They want to immigrate to Canada for a better life.
words.ex_cn: 他们想移民到加拿大过更好的生活。
words.en: To come to live permanently in a foreign country.

words.tr:
n. 影响力；冲击（力）；
v. 对…产生影响；
words.ex: The new law had a big impact on education.
words.ex_cn: 这项新法律对教育产生了重大影响。
words.en: The effect or influence of one person, thing, or action, on another.

words.ex: The epidemic spread quickly across the country.
words.ex_cn: 这种流行病迅速蔓延到全国。
words.en: An epidemic is a large number of cases of an infectious disease occurring at the same time.

words.ex: His fidelity to his friend never changed.
words.ex_cn: 他对朋友的忠诚从未改变。
words.en: Fidelity is loyalty to a person, organization, or set of beliefs.

words.tr:
adj. 不愿分享的；占有欲强的；所有格的
n. 所有格
words.ex: The cat is possessive of its toy.
words.ex_cn: 这只猫对它的玩具很占有。
words.en: If you are possessive about something that you own, you do not like lending it to other people or sharing it with other people.

words.ex: This forest has many different species of birds.
words.ex_cn: 这片森林有多种不同的鸟类物种。
words.en: A species is a class of plants or animals whose members have the same main characteristics and are able to breed with each other.

words.tr: adj. 符合礼仪的；得体的；高雅的
words.ex: She behaved in a decorous way at the dinner party.
words.ex_cn: 她在晚宴上举止得体。
words.en: If you say that something is decorous, you mean that it is dignified, proper, and socially acceptable.

words.ex: He gave a precise answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了准确的答案。
words.en: If you give precise information or precise instructions, you give exact details so that there is no confusion about what should be done.

words.ex: He likes to seclude himself in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢把自己 secluded 在森林里。
words.en: To seclude means to keep someone away from other people, or to keep something away from other things.

words.tr: adj. 先天的；天生的；生性的
words.ex: He was born with a congenital heart problem.
words.ex_cn: 他出生时就有先天性心脏病。
words.en: A congenital disease or condition exists at or from birth.

words.ex: The cold water gave her a sudden sensation.
words.ex_cn: 冷水给了她一种突然的感觉。
words.en: A sensation is a physical feeling or a reaction of interest or excitement that something causes in a person or in a group of people.

words.ex: We must eliminate the waste to protect the environment.
words.ex_cn: 我们必须消除浪费以保护环境。
words.en: To eliminate something, especially something you do not want or need, means to remove it completely.

words.tr:
adj. 沮丧的；低落的；垂头丧气的
v. 使…情绪低落；使沮丧；“deject”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He felt dejected after failing the test.
words.ex_cn: 他考试没及格后感到沮丧。
words.en: If you are dejected, you feel miserable or unhappy, especially because you have just been disappointed by something.

words.ex: The ornate ceiling had gold patterns and flowers.
words.ex_cn: 华丽的天花板上有金色的图案和花朵。
words.en: Something that is ornate is highly decorated with complex patterns.

words.tr: adj. 可疑的；怀疑的；拿不准的；
words.ex: The deal seemed dubious to me.
words.ex_cn: 这个交易在我看来很可疑。
words.en: If you describe something as dubious, you mean that you do not consider it to be completely honest, safe, or reliable.

words.ex: I perceive a change in his mood.
words.ex_cn: 我察觉到他的情绪有变化。
words.en: If you perceive something, you see, notice, or realize it, especially when it is not obvious.

words.ex: The teacher gave a cue to start the game.
words.ex_cn: 老师给出了开始游戏的提示。
words.en: A cue is a signal for someone to do something, or a piece of information that helps someone to understand something.

words.ex: There is a resemblance between the two brothers.
words.ex_cn: 这两兄弟之间有相似之处。
words.en: If there is a resemblance between two people or things, they are similar to each other.

words.ex: He made a permanent change to his lifestyle.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的生活方式做出了永久的改变。
words.en: Something that is permanent exists or happens all the time, or exists for a long time without changing.

words.ex: His rude behavior alienated his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁的行为使朋友们疏远了他。
