words.en: To cause someone to feel isolated or estranged; to transfer the ownership of property to another.

words.ex: He has business acumen and makes smart decisions.
words.ex_cn: 他有商业洞察力，能做出明智的决定。
words.en: The ability to make good judgments and quick decisions, typically in a particular domain.

words.tr: n. 爱国主义；爱国精神；
words.ex: He showed patriotism by serving his country in the army.
words.ex_cn: 他通过在军队中为国家服务表现出爱国主义。
words.en: Patriotism is the love and devotion to one's country.

words.ex: The teacher will enlighten the students about the truth.
words.ex_cn: 老师将向学生们阐明真相。
words.en: To enlighten someone means to give them more knowledge and greater understanding about something.

words.ex: The omission of his name was an accident.
words.ex_cn: 他的名字被漏掉是无意的。
words.en: An omission is something that has not been included or has not been done, either deliberately or accidentally.

words.ex: The predominant color in the room is blue.
words.ex_cn: 房间里的主导颜色是蓝色。
words.en: If something is predominant, it is more important, noticeable, or powerful than the other things in a situation.

words.tr:
adj. 反动的；保守的
n. 反动派；保守人士
words.ex: The reactionary government banned free speech.
words.ex_cn: 这个反动政府禁止了言论自由。
words.en: A reactionary person or group tries to prevent changes in the political or social system of their country.

words.tr: adj. 外来的；外国来的；奇异的；
words.ex: The market sells exotic fruits from other countries.
words.ex_cn: 这个市场出售来自其他国家的外来水果。
words.en: Something that is exotic is unusual and interesting because it comes from or is related to a distant country.

words.ex: The museum focuses on the preservation of old books.
words.ex_cn: 博物馆专注于旧书的保存。
words.en: The act of keeping something in its original state or in good condition.

words.tr: v. 使负义务；使有责任；强制
words.ex: The law obligate him to pay taxes.
words.ex_cn: 法律迫使他缴税。
words.en: To obligate someone means to make it necessary for them to do something, especially because of a law, rule, or agreement.

words.tr:
n. 询问；疑问；问号
v. 询问；怀疑
words.ex: He made a query about the bus schedule.
words.ex_cn: 他询问了公交车的时刻表。
words.en: A query is a question, especially one that you ask in order to check that something is true or correct.

words.ex: The radiance of the sun illuminated the entire landscape.
words.ex_cn: 太阳的光辉照亮了整个风景。
words.en: Radiance is a bright light that shines from something.

words.ex: The school will equip the lab with new computers.
words.ex_cn: 学校将为实验室配备新电脑。
words.en: To provide someone or something with the necessary items for a particular purpose.

words.ex: He is a reliable friend who always helps.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个可靠的朋友，总是帮忙。
words.en: Able to be trusted to do or provide what is needed or right.

words.tr: v. 描述…的特性；以…为特征；
words.ex: This book characterizes the hero as brave and kind.
words.ex_cn: 这本书将主人公描述为勇敢而善良的。
words.en: To describe the character or qualities of someone or something.

words.tr: n. 敏捷；活泼；欣然；乐意
words.ex: He answered the question with alacrity.
words.ex_cn: 他愉快地回答了问题。
words.en: If you do something with alacrity, you do it quickly and eagerly.

words.tr:
n. 漫画；讽刺画；滑稽模仿
v. 画成漫画讽刺
words.ex: He drew a caricature of the teacher with big eyes.
words.ex_cn: 他画了一幅老师大眼睛的漫画。
words.en: A caricature is a drawing or description of someone that exaggerates their appearance or behavior in a humorous or critical way.

words.ex: He is indebted to the bank for a large loan.
words.ex_cn: 他欠银行一大笔贷款。
words.en: If you say that you are indebted to someone for something, you mean that you are very grateful to them for something.

words.tr:
n. 提倡者；
v. 提倡；
words.ex: He is an advocate for clean water.
words.ex_cn: 他是清洁用水的提倡者。
words.en: If you advocate a particular action or plan, you recommend it publicly.

words.ex: The government wants to eradicate poverty.
words.ex_cn: 政府希望消灭贫困。
words.en: To eradicate something means to get rid of it completely.

words.ex: The witch stirred a magic potion.
words.ex_cn: 女巫搅拌了一瓶魔药。
words.en: A potion is a liquid that is believed to have magical or medicinal properties.

words.ex: The house has a commodious living room.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子有一个宽敞的客厅。
words.en: A commodious room or building is large and has a lot of space.

words.ex: The police will interrogate the suspect tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 警察明天会审问嫌疑人。
words.en: To interrogate someone means to ask them a lot of questions for a long time in order to get information, sometimes using threats.

words.ex: The accident caused paralysis in his legs.
words.ex_cn: 这次事故导致他双腿瘫痪。
words.en: Paralysis is the loss of the ability to move and sometimes to feel anything in part or most of the body, typically as a result of illness, poison, or injury.

words.ex: There is a dearth of clean water in the village.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄缺乏干净的水。
words.en: A dearth of something is a lack or scarcity of it.

words.tr: adj. 抬高的；地位高的； v. “elevate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The walkway is elevated above the road.
words.ex_cn: 这条人行道被抬高在道路之上。
words.en: An elevated place or thing is higher than the area around it.

words.tr: n. 脱离常规；误差；偏差；失常
words.ex: The sudden rain was an aberration in the dry season.
words.ex_cn: 这场突如其来的雨是旱季中的异常现象。
words.en: An aberration is an instance of straying from the normal or usual way, or something that is unusual or unexpected.

words.ex: His rude words provoked her anger.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁的话激怒了她。
words.en: If you provoke someone, you deliberately annoy them and try to make them behave aggressively.

words.ex: He is a conservative man who likes old traditions.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个喜欢古老传统的保守男子。
words.en: A conservative person or group is one that does not like changes or new ideas, especially in politics or religion.

words.tr: n. 替代选择；替代选择（alternative 的复数）；
words.ex: We need to find better alternatives to plastic.
words.ex_cn: 我们需要找到比塑料更好的替代选择。
words.en: An alternative is something that you can choose to do or use instead of something else.

words.ex: The butterfly has perfect symmetry.
words.ex_cn: 这只蝴蝶有完美的对称性。
words.en: Symmetry is the quality of being made up of exactly similar parts facing each other or around an axis.

words.ex: He had a meager meal after work.
words.ex_cn: 他下班后吃了一顿很少的饭。
words.en: If you describe an amount or quantity of something as meager, you are critical of it because it is very small or not enough.

words.tr:
v. 争论；争执；吵架
n. 争吵；口角
words.ex: They wrangle over the price every day.
words.ex_cn: 他们每天为价格争执。
words.en: If you wrangle with someone, you argue with them in a noisy or angry way.

words.ex: He is a conscientious student who always finishes his homework on time.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个尽责的学生，总是按时完成作业。
words.en: Someone who is conscientious is very careful to do their work properly.

words.tr: n. 韵律；节奏；抑扬顿挫
words.ex: The dancer moved with a steady cadence.
words.ex_cn: 舞者以稳定的节奏舞动。
words.en: The rhythm or sequence of sounds or movements in speech, music, dance, etc.

words.ex: He is the nominee for best actor.
words.ex_cn: 他是最佳男演员的提名人。
words.en: A nominee is someone who is proposed for an official position or for an honour or award.

words.ex: She wore a silver brooch on her coat.
words.ex_cn: 她把一枚银色胸针别在外套上。
words.en: A brooch is a piece of jewelry that has a pin at the back so it can be fastened to a dress, blouse, or coat.

words.tr: adj. 无感觉的；无知觉能力的
words.ex: His imperceptive nature made him oblivious to the subtle changes in her mood.
words.ex_cn: 他缺乏感知力的天性使他对她情绪的微妙变化毫无察觉。
words.en: Not having or showing the ability to perceive or understand things clearly.

words.ex: His handwriting is illegible.
words.ex_cn: 他的字迹无法辨认。
words.en: If something is illegible, it is impossible to read because the letters or characters are not clear, are not formed properly, or are obscured in some way.

words.ex: The invention of the wheel was a landmark in human history.
words.ex_cn: 轮子的发明是人类历史上的一个里程碑。
words.en: A landmark is a building or feature of a landscape that is easily seen and recognized from a distance, especially one that enables someone to establish their location.

words.ex: The gustatory sense helps us taste food.
words.ex_cn: 味觉帮助我们品尝食物。
words.en: Relating to the sense of taste.

words.ex: He gave an expository speech about how plants grow.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一次关于植物如何生长的说明性演讲。
words.en: Intended to explain or describe something.

words.tr: adj. 分离的； v. 脱离；拆卸；分离；“detach”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The house is detached from the neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子与邻居的房子是分开的。
words.en: If someone is detached, they do not have any emotional interest in a situation and therefore can make fair decisions.

words.ex: The invasive plant spreads quickly and kills other plants.
words.ex_cn: 这种侵入性植物生长迅速，会杀死其他植物。
words.en: If you describe something as invasive, you mean that it spreads very quickly and is difficult to stop.

words.tr: adj. 不能通行的；无路可通的
words.ex: The road became impassable after the heavy snowfall.
words.ex_cn: 大雪过后，这条路变得无法通行。
words.en: If a road or path is impassable, it is impossible to travel along it because it is blocked or in bad condition.

words.ex: She smiled inwardly, feeling a sense of satisfaction.
words.ex_cn: 她内心微笑，感到一种满足感。
words.en: In a way that is not expressed or shown outwardly; privately or secretly.

words.tr:
v. 嘎吱嘎吱地动；发嘎吱嘎吱声
n. 嘎吱声；艰难局面；危急情况
words.ex: The dog crunches the bone loudly.
words.ex_cn: 狗嘎吱嘎吱地咬着骨头。
words.en: To crunch means to chew noisily with your mouth open, or to make a loud noise like the sound of something being crushed. It can also refer to a critical point or situation, especially in financial contexts.

words.ex: The city needs better infrastructure for roads and water.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市需要更好的道路和供水设施。
words.en: The basic physical and organizational structures and facilities (e.g., buildings, roads, power supplies) needed for the operation of a society or enterprise.

words.ex: He has an addiction to video games.
words.ex_cn: 他对电子游戏上瘾了。
words.en: Addiction is the condition of being unable to stop using or doing something as a habit, especially something harmful.

words.ex: He is learning theoretical physics at university.
words.ex_cn: 他正在大学学习理论物理。
words.en: A theoretical study or explanation is based on or uses the ideas and abstract principles of a subject, rather than the practical aspects or uses of it.

words.tr:
v. 提出异议；表示反对
n. 异议；反对
words.ex: He demurred when asked to sign the contract.
words.ex_cn: 当被要求签署合同时，他提出了异议。
words.en: If you demur, you express reluctance or objection to something.

words.ex: The dove is an emblem of peace.
words.ex_cn: 鸽子是和平的象征。
words.en: An emblem is a design that represents a country, organization, or family.

words.tr: adj. 精密复杂的；老练的；
words.ex: The phone has a sophisticated camera.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机有一个精密复杂的摄像头。
words.en: A sophisticated person is intelligent and knows a lot, so that they are able to understand complicated situations. A sophisticated machine, device, or method is more advanced or complex than others.

words.ex: The court will prosecute him for theft.
words.ex_cn: 法院将因盗窃罪起诉他。
words.en: To prosecute means to institute legal proceedings against someone or to carry on a legal action against a defendant in a court of law. It also means to continue with or carry on an activity or enterprise.

words.tr: n. 区别；区分；优等评分；
words.ex: There is a clear distinction between right and wrong.
words.ex_cn: 对与错之间有明显的区别。
words.en: A distinction is a difference or contrast between similar things or people.

words.tr:
n. 胸；怀；（女性的）乳房
adj. 亲密的；知心的
words.ex: She held the baby close to her bosom.
words.ex_cn: 她把婴儿紧紧抱在胸前。
words.en: Your bosom is the front part of your chest, especially the part that is covered by your clothes and where your breasts are.

words.ex: He tried to evade the police by driving fast.
words.ex_cn: 他试图通过高速驾驶来逃避警察。
words.en: If you evade something, you find a way of not doing something that you really ought to do.

words.ex: The project cost overrun the budget.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目的成本超过了预算。
words.en: If an army or a group of people overruns a place, they take control of it by force. If something such as a place or a piece of land is overrun by things or people, it is filled with them and they spread everywhere.

words.ex: He used a euphemism to say he lost his job.
words.ex_cn: 他用了一个委婉语来表示他失业了。
words.en: A euphemism is a polite word or expression that is used to refer to things which people may find upsetting or embarrassing to talk about.

words.ex: The song evokes happy memories of childhood.
words.ex_cn: 这首歌唤起了对童年的美好回忆。
words.en: To evoke a particular memory, idea, emotion, or response means to cause it to occur.

words.tr: adj. 筋疲力尽的；耗尽的； v. 耗尽；用完；“exhaust”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He was exhausted after running five kilometers.
words.ex_cn: 他跑完五公里后筋疲力尽。
words.en: If you are exhausted, you are very tired and have no energy left.

words.ex: The manager will delegate the task to her assistant.
words.ex_cn: 经理将把这个任务委派给她的助手。
words.en: A delegate is a person who is chosen or elected to vote or make decisions on behalf of a group of people, especially at a conference or a meeting. As a verb, to delegate means to give a task or responsibility to another person, especially someone who is less senior than you.

words.ex: The news will disseminate quickly through social media.
words.ex_cn: 这条新闻会通过社交媒体迅速传播。
words.en: To disseminate means to spread or distribute something, especially information, widely.

words.ex: The effusion of joy made everyone smile.
words.ex_cn: 喜悦的流露让每个人都笑了。
words.en: An effusion is a liquid that escapes from a container or a place where it is confined, or the act of escaping in this way.

words.tr: adj. 合法的；正当的；正义的
words.ex: She claimed her rightful inheritance.
words.ex_cn: 她要求得到她合法的继承权。
words.en: If you say that someone or something has a rightful place or position, you mean that they deserve that place or position.

words.tr: adj. 漫不经心的；无忧无虑的
words.ex: He gave a blithe smile and walked away.
words.ex_cn: 他漫不经心地笑了笑，然后走开了。
words.en: If you describe someone as blithe, you mean that they are carefree and cheerful.

words.tr: adj. 赚大钱的；获利多的；
words.ex: He took a lucrative job at a tech company.
words.ex_cn: 他去了一家科技公司做一份赚大钱的工作。
words.en: A lucrative activity or job is one that you can earn a lot of money from.

words.ex: His dismissal made him very sad.
words.ex_cn: 他的被解雇让他非常难过。
words.en: The act of officially removing someone from their job, or the act of sending someone away or allowing them to leave.

words.ex: The comparison of the two phones helped me decide.
words.ex_cn: 对这两部手机的比较帮助我做出了决定。
words.en: When you make a comparison, you consider two or more things and discover the differences or similarities between them.

words.tr: adj. 明目张胆的；公然的；喧闹的
words.ex: He made a blatant lie to avoid punishment.
words.ex_cn: 他为了逃避惩罚，公然撒了谎。
words.en: If you describe an action as blatant, you mean that it is done in an open and obvious way, often with a lack of shame or embarrassment.

words.ex: The children were boisterous at the party.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在聚会上喧闹不已。
words.en: Someone who is boisterous is noisy, lively, and full of energy.

words.ex: The mixture is homogeneous and looks the same throughout.
words.ex_cn: 这种混合物是均一的，看起来处处都一样。
words.en: Something that is homogeneous is uniform in nature or character throughout.

words.ex: His smile belieed his true feelings.
words.ex_cn: 他的微笑掩饰了他真实的情感。
words.en: If one thing belies another, it hides the true situation and so creates a false idea or image of someone or something.

words.tr: adj. 基本的；基础的；根本的；
words.ex: Water is a fundamental need for life.
words.ex_cn: 水是生命的基本需求。
words.en: You use fundamental to describe things, activities, and principles that are very important or essential. They affect the basic nature of other things or are the most important element upon which other things depend.

words.ex: He told me a proverb: 'Slow and steady wins the race.'
words.ex_cn: 他告诉我一句谚语：‘慢而稳，胜千里。’
words.en: A proverb is a short, commonly known saying that expresses a truth or piece of advice.

words.ex: She felt great felicity when she won the prize.
words.ex_cn: 当她赢得奖品时，她感到极大的幸福。
words.en: Felicity is great happiness and pleasure.

words.ex: The refugees lived in abject poverty.
words.ex_cn: 这些难民过着凄惨的贫困生活。
words.en: Abject means extremely bad, unpleasant, and degrading.

words.ex: The doctor made a diagnosis after checking the symptoms.
words.ex_cn: 医生在检查了症状后做出了诊断。
words.en: The identification of the nature of an illness or other problem by examination of the symptoms.

words.ex: The team showed cohesive behavior during the project.
words.ex_cn: 这个团队在项目期间表现出有凝聚力的行为。
words.en: If something is cohesive, it consists of parts that fit together well and form a united whole.

words.ex: He gratifies his parents by getting good grades.
words.ex_cn: 他通过取得好成绩来让父母感到欣慰。
words.en: If you are gratified by something, it gives you pleasure or satisfaction.

words.tr:
n. 胆汁；胆量；怨恨；磨伤
v. 使愤怒（尤指因不公平引起）
words.ex: The bitter gall made him feel sick.
words.ex_cn: 苦涩的胆汁让他感到恶心。
words.en: Gall can refer to a bitter liquid produced by the liver, or it can describe someone's boldness or impudence. It can also mean to irritate or annoy someone.

words.tr: adj. 吹毛求疵的；挑剔的
words.ex: He made a captious comment about the small mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他对一个小错误发表了挑剔的评论。
words.en: Tending to find fault or raise petty objections.

words.tr: n. 贵族政治；贵族统治；贵族
words.ex: The aristocracy lived in big castles long ago.
words.ex_cn: 很久以前，贵族住在巨大的城堡里。
words.en: The highest class in certain societies, especially those holding hereditary titles or offices.

words.tr: v. 重新调整；重新适应
words.ex: He had to readjust his schedule after the meeting was moved.
words.ex_cn: 会议改期后，他不得不重新调整自己的日程。
words.en: To adjust or adapt again, especially to a new situation or environment.

words.tr: adj. 精明的；老谋深算的
words.ex: He is a canny trader who always makes smart choices.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个精明的交易员，总是做出明智的选择。
words.en: A canny person is clever and able to think quickly, especially in business or politics.

words.ex: He spread calumny about his neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他散布了关于他邻居的诽谤。
words.en: A false statement made to damage someone's reputation.

words.ex: He kept the dishes in the cabinet.
words.ex_cn: 他把盘子放在储藏柜里。
words.en: A cabinet is a piece of furniture with doors and shelves or drawers, used for storing or showing things. In politics, a cabinet is a group of people who are chosen by a head of state to give advice and to help set government policy.

words.tr: adj. 感伤的；感情的；多愁善感的
words.ex: He kept the old toy because he was sentimental about it.
words.ex_cn: 他保留了那个旧玩具，因为他对它有感情。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as sentimental, you mean that they are influenced by emotional feelings, especially about happy memories of past events or relationships with other people, rather than by careful thought and judgment based on facts.

words.ex: The team reached a consensus on the project plan.
words.ex_cn: 团队就项目计划达成了共识。
words.en: A consensus is general agreement among a group of people.

words.ex: The emancipation of slaves ended centuries of oppression.
words.ex_cn: 奴隶的解放结束了几个世纪的压迫。
words.en: The act of freeing someone from legal, social, or political restrictions.

words.tr: v. 隔离；使隔热；使隔音；使绝缘
words.ex: The walls insulate the house from cold air.
words.ex_cn: 墙壁将房子与冷空气隔离开。
words.en: To insulate something means to protect it from heat, cold, noise, or electricity by covering it in a material that prevents it from passing through.

words.ex: He goes to a music academy every weekend.
words.ex_cn: 他每周末去音乐学院。
words.en: An academy is a type of school for special training or a society for the advancement of art, science, or literature.

words.tr: adj. 固有的；内在的；本身的；
words.ex: Honesty is an intrinsic part of her character.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是她性格中固有的部分。
words.en: belonging to a thing by its very nature

words.ex: They had an altercation over the parking space.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为停车空间发生了争吵。
words.en: An altercation is a noisy argument or disagreement, especially in public.

words.ex: Water is a common solvent for salt.
words.ex_cn: 水是盐的常见溶剂。
words.en: A solvent is a substance that can dissolve other substances, or a person or company that has enough money to pay their debts.

words.ex: The city improved its drainage system after the flood.
words.ex_cn: 洪水之后，这座城市改进了它的排水系统。
words.en: Drainage is the system or process by which water or other liquids are drained from a place.

words.ex: The teacher will assess your homework tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 老师明天会评估你的作业。
words.en: to judge or decide the amount, value, quality, or importance of something

words.ex: The benefits outweigh the risks.
words.ex_cn: 好处超过了风险。
words.en: If one thing outweighs another, the first thing is of greater importance, benefit, or significance than the second thing.

words.tr: adj. 快乐安详的；幸福的
words.ex: She had a beatific smile after the prayer.
words.ex_cn: 祈祷后，她脸上带着宁静幸福的微笑。
words.en: A beatific expression, smile, or vision shows great happiness and calmness.

words.tr: v. 促进；使便利；使容易；
words.ex: The teacher facilitates learning by asking questions.
words.ex_cn: 老师通过提问来促进学习。
words.en: To make an action or process easier or more likely to happen.

words.ex: The malevolent wizard cast a dark spell.
words.ex_cn: 那个有恶意的巫师施了一个黑暗咒语。
words.en: Having or showing a wish to harm others; malicious.

words.tr: n. 年金；养老金；年金保险
words.ex: He receives an annuity every month.
words.ex_cn: 他每个月领取一笔年金。
words.en: An annuity is a fixed sum of money paid to someone each year, typically for the rest of their life.

words.tr: adj. 可触摸的；实际的；有形的；确凿的；
words.ex: The statue is tangible and can be touched.
words.ex_cn: 这座雕像可以触摸，是实实在在的。
words.en: Something that is tangible is clear enough or definite enough to be easily seen, felt, or noticed.

words.ex: Our team won the soccer match.
words.ex_cn: 我们的团队赢得了足球比赛。
words.en: A team is a group of people who play a particular sport or game together against other similar groups of people.

words.ex: The weather will deteriorate tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 明天天气会恶化。
words.en: If something deteriorates, it becomes worse in some way.

words.ex: He absconded with the money last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚携款逃跑了。
words.en: If someone absconds from somewhere, they leave there quickly and secretly because they have something to hide or are afraid of being caught.

words.ex: The blood will coagulate if it is left outside the body.
words.ex_cn: 血液如果留在体外，就会凝结。
words.en: If a liquid coagulates, it becomes thick and almost solid.

words.ex: Many people decry the use of plastic bags.
words.ex_cn: 许多人公开反对使用塑料袋。
words.en: If you decry something, you criticize it as being wrong or harmful.

words.ex: The juridical system is complex and often confusing.
words.ex_cn: 司法系统复杂且常常令人困惑。
words.en: Relating to the administration of justice or the function of a judge or legal scholar.

words.tr:
adj. 疏远的；冷淡的
adv. 远离地
words.ex: He stayed aloof during the party.
words.ex_cn: 他在派对上保持冷淡。
words.en: Someone who is aloof is not very friendly and does not like to spend time with other people.

words.tr:
adj. 裸体的
n. 裸体；裸体画；裸体像
words.ex: He painted a nude woman by the window.
words.ex_cn: 他画了一位在窗边的裸体女性。
words.en: A nude person is not wearing any clothes. A nude painting or sculpture shows a person who is not wearing any clothes.

words.ex: The team's morale improved after they won the game.
words.ex_cn: 球队赢了比赛后，士气提升了。
words.en: Morale is the amount of confidence and cheerfulness that a group of people have.

words.tr: adj. 慷慨的；丰富的；充足的
words.ex: She gave a bountiful donation to the orphanage.
words.ex_cn: 她向孤儿院慷慨地捐了一笔钱。
words.en: Something that is bountiful is large in quantity or number and is freely given.

words.ex: The government will implement new rules next month.
words.ex_cn: 政府下个月将实施新规定。
words.en: To implement something means to ensure that what has been planned is done.

words.tr: n. 沉思；反射；反映；反省；
words.ex: He sat quietly in the garden for reflection.
words.ex_cn: 他静静地坐在花园里沉思。
words.en: A reflection is an image that you can see in a mirror, glass, or water.

words.ex: The team worked in a harmonious way.
words.ex_cn: 这个团队以和谐的方式合作。
words.en: A harmonious situation, relationship, or agreement is one in which people are friendly and helpful to one another, and in which there is no serious disagreement or argument.

words.tr: n. 紧缩；艰苦朴素；节俭
words.ex: The government implemented austerity measures to reduce the budget deficit.
words.ex_cn: 政府实施了紧缩措施以减少预算赤字。
words.en: Austerity is a situation in which people's living standards are reduced because of economic difficulties.

words.tr: adj. 肉体的；肉欲的；性欲的
words.ex: He denied any carnal desires.
words.ex_cn: 他否认有任何肉体的欲望。
words.en: Carnal is used to describe things relating to the body or to sexual desires, often in contrast to spiritual or intellectual matters.

words.tr:
adj. 悲痛的；令人伤心的
v. 耙地；折磨；使愁苦；“harrow”的现在分词
words.ex: The harrowing story of the survivors left a deep impression on everyone.
words.ex_cn: 幸存者的悲惨故事给每个人留下了深刻的印象。
words.en: Causing feelings of deep distress or anguish.

words.tr: adj. 不善交际的；不圆滑的；笨拙的
words.ex: He made a gauche comment at the dinner party.
words.ex_cn: 他在晚宴上说了个笨拙的评论。
words.en: If you describe someone as gauche, you mean that they are awkward and uncomfortable in the company of other people, especially because they lack social skills.

words.tr:
v. 派遣；调遣；发送
n. 快信；发送；派遣
words.ex: He will dispatch the package tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会寄出这个包裹。
words.en: To send someone or something to a particular place for a particular purpose.

words.tr:
n. 拨浪鼓；嘎嘎声；咔嗒声
v. 发出格格声；使紧张不安；喋喋不休
words.ex: The baby laughed while shaking the rattle.
words.ex_cn: 宝宝摇着拨浪鼓笑了。
words.en: If something rattles or if you rattle it, it makes short sharp knocking sounds as it moves or shakes.

words.tr: adj. 好管闲事的；爱干预的
words.ex: She was always meddlesome, poking her nose into everyone's business.
words.ex_cn: 她总是爱管闲事，把鼻子伸进每个人的事务中。
words.en: If you describe a person as meddlesome, you are criticizing them because they try to influence or change things that do not concern them.

words.tr: adj. 穷困的；赤穷的；贫瘠的； v. “impoverish”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The impoverished family lived in a small house with no heating.
words.ex_cn: 这个贫困的家庭住在一个没有暖气的小房子里。
words.en: An impoverished person or area is very poor.

words.tr:
adj. 咸的；辛辣的；好吃的；好闻的
n. 咸味小吃
words.ex: The savory snack made her thirsty.
words.ex_cn: 这道咸味小吃让她口渴了。
words.en: Savory food is pleasantly salty or spicy and not sweet in taste.

words.ex: He gave an antagonistic reply to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了敌对的答复。
words.en: If someone is antagonistic to someone or something, they show hatred or opposition towards them.

words.ex: He gropped in the dark for the light switch.
words.ex_cn: 他在黑暗中摸索着找电灯开关。
words.en: If you grope for something that you cannot see, you try to find it by moving your hands around in order to feel it.

words.ex: He felt apprehension before the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他在考试前感到焦虑。
words.en: Anxiety or fear that something bad or unpleasant will happen; understanding; the action of arresting someone.

words.tr:
n. 蜂拥；狂奔；大西部赛马会（美国西部或加拿大）
v. 惊跑；蜂拥
words.ex: The cows ran in a stampede when they heard the loud noise.
words.ex_cn: 当牛群听到巨大的噪音时，它们惊慌狂奔。
words.en: A stampede is a situation in which a group of people or animals suddenly start running in a wild and uncontrolled way, often because they are frightened.

words.tr:
v. 潦草地写；涂写
n. 潦草的笔迹
words.ex: He scrawled his name on the paper.
words.ex_cn: 他在纸上潦草地写了自己的名字。
words.en: If you scrawl something, you write it in a careless and untidy way.

words.tr:
v. 改造；修整
n. 改组；改建
words.ex: They will revamp the old website next month.
words.ex_cn: 他们下个月将改造旧网站。
words.en: To revamp something means to change it in order to improve it or make it more modern.

words.ex: He submitted his application for the job last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周提交了那份工作申请。
words.en: An application is a formal request, often written, for something such as a job, a place at a university, or permission to do something. It can also refer to the act of putting something to a special use or purpose, or a program or piece of software designed to perform a specific function.

words.ex: He wrote his dissertation on climate change.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一篇关于气候变化的学位论文。
words.en: A dissertation is a long piece of writing on a particular subject, especially one written for a university degree.

words.ex: The child imitates her mother's voice.
words.ex_cn: 孩子模仿她妈妈的声音。
words.en: If you imitate someone, you copy what they do or produce.

words.tr: adj. 急剧的；引人注目的；戏剧（性）的；
words.ex: There was a dramatic increase in temperature yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 昨天温度急剧上升。
words.en: If something is dramatic, it happens or changes suddenly and noticeably.

words.ex: The garden has ornamental flowers.
words.ex_cn: 这个花园里有装饰性的花卉。
words.en: Something that is ornamental is intended to be attractive and is not necessary or useful.

words.ex: The superintendent of the school is very strict.
words.ex_cn: 学校的主管非常严格。
words.en: A superintendent is a person who is in charge of a particular department or activity, especially within a school, housing project, or police force.

words.ex: He doesn't know his parentage.
words.ex_cn: 他不知道自己的身世。
words.en: The identity or origins of one's parents.

words.ex: He ate a moderate amount of food.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了适量的食物。
words.en: If you moderate something or if it moderates, it becomes less extreme or violent, or if you moderate a discussion, you help the people in it to reach an agreement.

words.ex: I can't recollect where I put my keys.
words.ex_cn: 我想不起来把钥匙放在哪儿了。
words.en: If you recollect something, you remember it.

words.ex: The weather was unfavorable for the picnic.
words.ex_cn: 天气对野餐不利。
words.en: If conditions or circumstances are unfavorable, they make it difficult for something to happen or exist.

words.ex: He abetted his friend to steal the car.
words.ex_cn: 他教唆朋友偷车。
words.en: To abet someone to do something wrong means to help or encourage them to do it.

words.tr: n. 堡垒；防御工事；保障
words.ex: The new law serves as a bulwark against corruption.
words.ex_cn: 这项新法律起到了防止腐败的作用。
words.en: A bulwark is a wall built for defence, especially one that is part of a larger fortification system.

words.ex: The smell of bread pervades the kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 面包的香味弥漫在整个厨房里。
words.en: If something pervades a place or thing, it is present throughout it.

words.ex: His ken does not include quantum physics.
words.ex_cn: 他的知识范围不包括量子物理。
words.en: Ken is the range of one's knowledge or understanding.

words.ex: The lion lives in the jungle.
words.ex_cn: 狮子生活在丛林中。
words.en: A jungle is a dense, tropical forest that is home to a wide variety of plants and animals.

words.ex: He wrote copious notes during the lecture.
words.ex_cn: 他在讲座期间写了大量的笔记。
words.en: Something that is copious exists in large amounts.

words.tr: adj. 梦幻的；荒诞不经的
words.ex: His chimerical dream of flying without wings never came true.
words.ex_cn: 他那不切实际的、不用翅膀就能飞翔的梦想从未实现。
words.en: If you describe something as chimerical, you mean that it is imagined or hoped for but unlikely to be real or practical.

words.ex: The desert looks desolate and empty.
words.ex_cn: 这片沙漠看起来荒凉而空旷。
words.en: If you describe a place as desolate, you mean that it is empty and looks sad because there are no people there or because it has been damaged.

words.tr: adj. 有同情心的；表示怜悯的；
words.ex: She is a compassionate teacher who helps struggling students.
words.ex_cn: 她是一位有同情心的老师，帮助学习困难的学生。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as compassionate, you mean that they feel or show pity, sympathy, and understanding for people who are suffering.

words.ex: He antedated the contract by one week.
words.ex_cn: 他把合同的日期提前了一周。
words.en: To be of an earlier date than something else; to precede in time.

words.ex: The old law was antiquated by the new government.
words.ex_cn: 旧法律被新政府废除了。
words.en: To make something old-fashioned or obsolete.

words.ex: The diaphanous curtain let in the morning light.
words.ex_cn: 那层薄纱窗帘让晨光透了进来。
words.en: A diaphanous substance or fabric is very thin and almost transparent.

words.ex: This apple is a variant of the red delicious.
words.ex_cn: 这种苹果是红富士的一个变体。
words.en: A variant is something that is slightly different from other similar things.

words.ex: The word 'thou' is archaic in modern English.
words.ex_cn: ‘thou’这个词在现代英语中是过时的。
words.en: Very old or old-fashioned.

words.ex: He faced persecution for his beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 他因自己的信仰而遭受迫害。
words.en: Persecution is the act of treating someone cruelly or unfairly, especially because of their race, religion, or political beliefs.

words.ex: The synthesis of ideas helped solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 这些想法的综合帮助解决了问题。
words.en: The act of combining different ideas, influences, or objects into a new and coherent whole.

words.ex: He tried to retract his words after the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他在争吵后试图收回他的话。
words.en: If you retract something that you have said or written, you say that you did not mean it.

words.tr: n. 祝福者；表达良好祝愿的人
words.ex: She received many letters from well-wishers during her recovery.
words.ex_cn: 她在康复期间收到了许多祝福者的来信。
words.en: A well-wisher is someone who expresses good wishes or support for someone else.

words.ex: He could discern a small bird in the trees.
words.ex_cn: 他能辨明树上有一只小鸟。
words.en: If you can discern something, you are aware of it and know what it is.

words.tr:
adj. 集体的；
n. 集体；
words.ex: The collective decision was made by all members.
words.ex_cn: 这个集体决定是由所有成员做出的。
words.en: done or shared by all members of a group of people

words.ex: His words were contradictory.
words.ex_cn: 他的话是矛盾的。
words.en: If two or more facts, ideas, or statements are contradictory, they state or imply that opposite things are true.

words.tr: n. 裂口；深坑；显著差别
words.ex: The earthquake created a deep chasm in the ground.
words.ex_cn: 地震在地面上造成了一道深深的裂口。
words.en: A chasm is a very deep, narrow opening in rock, ice, or the ground.

words.ex: He uses colloquial words when talking with friends.
words.ex_cn: 他和朋友聊天时使用口语化的词语。
words.en: Colloquial language is informal language that is used in ordinary conversation rather than in writing or formal speech.

words.ex: Smoking is injurious to your health.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟对你的健康有害。
words.en: Something that is injurious causes harm or damage.

words.ex: He lives in a big mansion near the lake.
words.ex_cn: 他住在湖边的一座大宅子里。
words.en: A mansion is a very large, impressive house, especially one that is the home of a wealthy or important person.

words.ex: The baleful glare of the enemy sent shivers down their spines.
words.ex_cn: 敌人恶意的目光让他们不寒而栗。
words.en: Baleful means threatening harm or evil.

words.tr: adj. 清醒的；严肃的；素淡的；
words.ex: He stayed sober after drinking only water.
words.ex_cn: 他只喝了水，保持清醒。
words.en: If you are sober, you are not drunk. If you are sober, you are serious and thoughtful.

words.ex: He has great proficiency in English.
words.ex_cn: 他的英语水平很高。
words.en: If you show proficiency in something, you show ability or skill at it.

words.tr: n. 年鉴；编年史；历史记载；年报
words.ex: The annals of history record many great kings.
words.ex_cn: 历史年鉴记录了许多伟大的国王。
words.en: A chronological record of events, especially those of a particular organization, institution, or community.

words.tr:
n. 倒塌；崩溃；暴跌；
v. 倒塌；崩溃；
words.ex: The collapse of the old bridge caused many problems.
words.ex_cn: 这座旧桥的倒塌引起了诸多问题。
words.en: If a building or other structure collapses, it falls down very suddenly.

words.ex: He took an intensive English course last summer.
words.ex_cn: 去年夏天，他参加了一个密集的英语课程。
words.en: Intensive is used to describe something that involves a lot of effort, energy, or attention in a short period of time.

words.ex: He spoke with fervor about his dreams.
words.ex_cn: 他充满热情地谈论自己的梦想。
words.en: Fervor is intense and passionate feeling.

words.ex: The movie is controversial because it shows violence.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影因为展示暴力而有争议。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as controversial, you mean that they are the subject of intense public argument, disagreement, or disapproval.

words.tr: n. 政党会议；核心小组会议；特别利益集团
words.ex: The caucus decided on a new strategy for the upcoming election.
words.ex_cn: 党团会议决定了一项新的选举策略。
words.en: A caucus is a meeting of the members of a political party to select candidates or decide policy.

words.tr:
adj. 抽象的；非具体的；
n. 摘要；概要；抽象派艺术作品；
words.ex: The painting shows an abstract shape.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画展示了一个抽象的形状。
words.en: An abstract idea or way of thinking is based on general ideas rather than on real things and events.

words.tr: n. 兴致；热情；趣味；（用于调味的）柠檬皮；橙皮
words.ex: He cooks with zest and loves spicy food.
words.ex_cn: 他做菜很有激情，喜欢辣的食物。
words.en: Great enthusiasm and energy.

words.ex: His eloquence moved everyone in the room.
words.ex_cn: 他的雄辩打动了房间里每一个人。
words.en: The ability to speak or write in a way that is fluent, persuasive, and expressive.

words.tr: n. 仲裁人；公断人；权威
words.ex: He is the arbiter of the dispute.
words.ex_cn: 他是这场纠纷的仲裁者。
words.en: An arbiter is a person or agency officially appointed to settle a dispute.

words.ex: The turtle outlives the rabbit.
words.ex_cn: 乌龟比兔子活得长。
words.en: To live longer than someone else; to survive something.

words.tr: adj. 腼腆的；怕羞的；忸怩的
words.ex: She gave a coy smile when asked about her new boyfriend.
words.ex_cn: 当被问及她的新男友时，她露出了腼腆的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as coy, you mean they are pretending to be shy about something in order to attract attention or to deceive people.

words.ex: The government subsidize small businesses to help them grow.
words.ex_cn: 政府资助小企业以帮助它们发展。
words.en: To subsidize something means to pay part of the cost of it, usually as a way of helping people or organizations that cannot afford to pay the full cost themselves.

words.tr:
n. 接触（的机会或权利）；进入；通道；
v. 获取；使用；接近；
words.ex: Students need access to the library.
words.ex_cn: 学生需要有接触图书馆的机会。
words.en: If you have access to a building or other place, you are able to enter it or use it.

words.ex: His speech was full of vacuity.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲充满空洞。
words.en: If you refer to the vacuity of something or someone, you are critical of them because they lack intelligent thought or ideas.

words.ex: He gave a vicious smile before leaving.
words.ex_cn: 他离开前露出一个恶毒的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as vicious, you mean that they are violent and cruel, or that they are intended to cause someone great harm or suffering.

words.ex: The rain precludes a picnic.
words.ex_cn: 下雨阻止了野餐。
words.en: If something precludes an event or action, it prevents it from happening.

words.ex: He works in the sales department.
words.ex_cn: 他在销售部工作。
words.en: A department is one of the sections in an organization such as a government, business, or university.

words.tr:
adj.  张口发呆的；目瞪口呆的
adv. 张口发呆地；目瞪口呆地
words.ex: The child stood agape at the magic show.
words.ex_cn: 孩子目瞪口呆地看着魔术表演。
words.en: If you describe someone as being agape, you mean that their mouth is open wide, often because they are very surprised by something.

words.ex: He faced ridicule for wearing old clothes.
words.ex_cn: 他因为穿旧衣服而遭到嘲笑。
words.en: To ridicule someone or something means to make fun of them in an unkind way.

words.ex: He wrote his autobiography when he was 70.
words.ex_cn: 他70岁时写了自传。
words.en: An autobiography is a book about the life of a person, written by that person.

words.tr: n. 不幸的人；潦倒的人；恶棍；坏蛋
words.ex: The poor wretch had no food or shelter.
words.ex_cn: 那个可怜的人没有食物和住所。
words.en: A wretch is someone who is extremely unhappy or unfortunate, or someone who behaves in a way that is morally bad.

words.ex: The lab has a new apparatus for measuring temperature.
words.ex_cn: 实验室有一台新的温度测量装置。
words.en: The complex structure of a particular system or organization, or the equipment used for a specific purpose.

words.ex: He is irritable when he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 他累了的时候容易烦躁。
words.en: If someone is irritable, they are easily annoyed.

words.ex: This plan is practicable.
words.ex_cn: 这个计划是可行的。
words.en: If a task, plan, or idea is practicable, it can be successfully done or achieved.

words.ex: The aboriginal people live in the forests of Australia.
words.ex_cn: 土著居民生活在澳大利亚的森林里。
words.en: An aboriginal person or thing is one that has been in a country or region from the earliest known times or from before the arrival of colonists.

words.ex: The computer will execute the program quickly.
words.ex_cn: 计算机将快速执行该程序。
words.en: To execute means to carry out or put into effect a plan, order, or course of action. It can also refer to the act of legally killing someone as a punishment.

words.ex: The storm anteceded the flood.
words.ex_cn: 风暴发生在洪水之前。
words.en: To go before in time or order; precede.

words.tr: adj. 讲究礼仪的；隆重的
words.ex: He gave a ceremonious speech at the wedding.
words.ex_cn: 他在婚礼上发表了一篇庄重的演讲。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as ceremonious, you mean that they are very formal or polite.

words.tr: adj. 可计算的；可推断出的
words.ex: The risk is calculable and manageable.
words.ex_cn: 这种风险是可以计算和管理的。
words.en: If something is calculable, it can be calculated or estimated.

words.tr:
n. 合同；契约；
v. 收缩；
words.ex: They signed a contract to buy the house.
words.ex_cn: 他们签署了一份购买房子的合同。
words.en: A contract is a legal agreement between two or more parties. It can also mean to become smaller or tighter, or to catch a disease.

words.tr:
n. 埋伏；伏击
v. 埋伏；伏击
words.ex: The soldiers set an ambush at night.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们在夜间设下埋伏。
words.en: An ambush is a surprise attack by people lying in wait in a concealed position.

words.tr:
n. 批准；允许；认可；制裁；处罚
v. 批准；认可；制裁；处罚
words.ex: The company got official sanction to open a new branch.
words.ex_cn: 该公司获得了开设新分公司的正式批准。
words.en: A sanction is a penalty for disobeying a law or rule, or an official permission or approval for an action.

words.ex: Pop music is part of the mainstream.
words.ex_cn: 流行音乐是主流的一部分。
words.en: The ideas, attitudes, or activities that are shared by most people and regarded as normal or conventional.

words.tr:
n. 顾虑；顾忌；踌躇
v. 顾虑；有顾忌
words.ex: He had a scruple about lying to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他对于对朋友撒谎感到不安。
words.en: A scruple is a feeling of doubt or hesitation with regard to the morality or propriety of a course of action.

words.ex: The teacher asked a simple question to elicit answers from students.
words.ex_cn: 老师问了一个简单的问题来引出学生的回答。
words.en: To elicit a response or a reaction means to cause it to happen by something that you say or do.

words.ex: The wind propels the sailboat forward.
words.ex_cn: 风推动帆船前进。
words.en: To propel something in a particular direction means to cause it to move in that direction.

words.tr: adj. 短暂的；朝生暮死的
words.ex: The flowers are ephemeral and last only one day.
words.ex_cn: 这些花是短暂的，只持续一天。
words.en: Something that is ephemeral lasts for only a very short time.

words.tr: adj. 值得注意的；显著的；著名的；
words.ex: This is a notable achievement.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个值得注意的成就。
words.en: Worthy of attention or notice; remarkable.

words.tr: adj. 粗鲁的；无礼的；脾气坏的
words.ex: His churlish behavior at the meeting was uncalled for.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议上的粗鲁行为是完全没有必要的。
words.en: If someone is churlish, they are rude, bad-tempered, and impolite.

words.tr: v. 使变形；使改观；美化
words.ex: The makeup artist transfigured the actress for the role.
words.ex_cn: 化妆师为演员的角色进行了改观。
words.en: To transform into something more beautiful or elevated.

words.tr: adj. 不直接的；不正直的；迂回的；
words.ex: He gave a devious answer to avoid telling the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他给出了一个不直接的回答，以避免说出真相。
words.en: If you describe someone as devious, you mean that they are dishonest and unfair in the way that they behave, often by using indirect methods to achieve their aims.

words.ex: Her strident voice broke the silence.
words.ex_cn: 她尖锐的声音打破了寂静。
words.en: If you use strident to describe someone or the way they express themselves, you mean that they make their feelings or opinions known in a very strong way that perhaps makes people uncomfortable.

words.tr:
n. 睡眠；
v. 睡觉；
words.ex: He needs more sleep to feel better.
words.ex_cn: 他需要更多的睡眠来感觉好些。
words.en: Sleep is the natural state of rest in which your eyes are closed, your body is inactive, and your mind is unconscious.

words.tr: adj. 弯曲的； v. 弯曲；使弯曲；“bend”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The bent pipe leaked water.
words.ex_cn: 弯曲的管道漏水了。
words.en: Bent is used to describe something that is not straight but has a curve or angle in it. It can also refer to someone's natural talent or inclination towards a particular activity or subject.

words.tr: adj. 分成方格的； v. “checker”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The table has a checkered cloth.
words.ex_cn: 这张桌子上有块方格布。
words.en: Something that is checkered has a pattern of squares, usually of two different colors, or has had a lot of different experiences or events, often both good and bad.

words.tr: adj. 记性好的；有保持力的
words.ex: She has a very retentive memory.
words.ex_cn: 她有非常好的记忆力。
words.en: If you have a retentive memory, you are able to remember things easily.

words.tr: v. 使不抱幻想；使不再着迷；使醒悟
words.ex: The truth disenchant him about his hero.
words.ex_cn: 真相让他对他的偶像不再抱有幻想。
words.en: If you are disenchanted with something, you are disappointed with it and no longer believe that it is good or worthwhile.

words.tr: v. 使大吃一惊；使目瞪口呆
words.ex: The news flabbergasted her.
words.ex_cn: 这个消息让她惊呆了。
words.en: If you are flabbergasted by something, you are extremely surprised by it.

words.ex: Farmers grow corn as a crop.
words.ex_cn: 农民种植玉米作为农作物。
words.en: A crop is a plant such as wheat, potatoes, or cotton that is grown in large quantities by farmers.

words.tr: v. 激怒；使急躁；使疼痛
words.ex: Loud noises irritate my baby.
words.ex_cn: 噪音会激怒我的宝宝。
words.en: If something irritates you, it keeps annoying you.

words.tr: adj. 富有魅力的；迷人的；
words.ex: She wore a glamorous dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条富有魅力的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as glamorous, you mean that they are more attractive, exciting, or interesting than ordinary people or things.

words.ex: The desert is inhospitable and has no water.
words.ex_cn: 这个沙漠不适合居住，也没有水。
words.en: If you describe a place as inhospitable, you mean that it is difficult to live or stay there because there is no shelter or the weather is bad. If you describe a person or their behaviour as inhospitable, you mean that they do not make people welcome.

words.ex: He read a biography of Nelson Mandela.
words.ex_cn: 他读了一本关于纳尔逊·曼德拉的传记。
words.en: A biography is a detailed description of a person's life. It involves more than just the basic facts like education, work, relationships, and death; it portrays a person's experience of these life events.

words.ex: His answers were inconsistent.
words.ex_cn: 他的答案不一致。
words.en: If you describe someone as inconsistent, you are criticizing them for not behaving in the same way every time a similar situation occurs.

words.tr: adj. 红润的；红的；淡红色
words.ex: Her complexion was ruddy from the cold weather.
words.ex_cn: 她的脸色因寒冷的天气而变得红润。
words.en: Having a healthy red color, especially in the face.

words.ex: He will outlast his rivals in the race.
words.ex_cn: 他将在比赛中胜过他的对手。
words.en: To continue to exist or be effective for a longer time than someone or something else.

words.ex: The whisper was barely audible.
words.ex_cn: 那耳语几乎听不见。
words.en: If a sound is audible, it is loud enough for you to hear it.

words.ex: He showed disdain for the lazy students.
words.ex_cn: 他对那些懒惰的学生表现出蔑视。
words.en: If you feel disdain for someone or something, you dislike them because you think that they are inferior or unimportant.

words.ex: He is a famous playwright who writes plays.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位著名的剧作家，写剧本。
words.en: A playwright is a person who writes plays.

words.ex: The fretful child cried all night.
words.ex_cn: 这个烦躁的孩子整晚都在哭。
words.en: If someone is fretful, they behave in a way that shows that they are worried or unhappy about something.

words.ex: The duration of the movie is two hours.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影的持续时间是两小时。
words.en: The duration of an event or state is the time during which it happens or exists.

words.tr:
v. 把…归因于；由…引起；
n. 品质；属性；特征；属性；
words.ex: He attributes his success to hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的成功归因于努力工作。
words.en: If you attribute something to an event or situation, you think that it was caused by that event or situation.

words.tr: adj. 可疑的；有问题的；不可靠的；
words.ex: The deal seemed questionable.
words.ex_cn: 这笔交易看起来可疑。
words.en: If you say that something is questionable, you mean that it is not obviously true or real, and therefore possibly not valid or reliable.

words.tr: adj. 颤抖的；战栗的；畏缩的
words.ex: Her voice was tremulous when she spoke.
words.ex_cn: 她说话时声音颤抖。
words.en: If someone's voice, smile, or actions are tremulous, they are unsteady because the person is uncertain, afraid, or upset.

words.ex: The proximity of the school to the park makes it nice for kids.
words.ex_cn: 学校靠近公园，对孩子们来说很好。
words.en: Proximity refers to the state of being near in space or time.

words.tr: v. 使遭危险或伤害；危害；危及
words.ex: Pollution can endanger animals.
words.ex_cn: 污染会危及动物。
words.en: To put someone or something at risk or in danger.

words.tr: adj. 手工精巧的；技艺熟练的
words.ex: The carpenter's work was workmanlike and precise.
words.ex_cn: 木匠的工作技术熟练且精确。
words.en: If you describe something as workmanlike, you mean that it is done efficiently and competently, but without any special flair or originality.

words.tr: adj. 公正的；不偏不倚的；
words.ex: The judge was impartial in the trial.
words.ex_cn: 法官在审判中是公正的。
words.en: Someone who is impartial is not directly involved in a particular situation, and is therefore able to give a fair opinion or decision about it.

words.ex: His indolence at work was becoming a serious issue.
words.ex_cn: 他在工作中的懒散正成为一个严重的问题。
words.en: Indolence is the state of being lazy or not wanting to do any work.

words.ex: They stayed in a small lodge near the forest.
words.ex_cn: 他们住在森林附近的一座小屋里。
words.en: A lodge is a small house in the country, especially one that is used by people on holiday or by people taking part in a sport such as skiing or hunting. As a verb, to lodge means to stay somewhere, especially temporarily, or to formally submit something, such as a complaint or an application.

words.ex: She used a lot of blandishment to get what she wanted.
words.ex_cn: 她使用了许多奉承话来达到她的目的。
words.en: Blandishment refers to the act of flattering or coaxing someone in order to persuade them to do something.

words.ex: He tries to negate the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他试图否认事实。
words.en: If someone negates something, they say that it does not exist or is not true.

words.tr: adj. 威胁的； v. “menace”的现在分词；
words.ex: The dark clouds look menacing.
words.ex_cn: 乌云看起来很有威胁。
words.en: If someone or something is menacing, they seem to be threatening or dangerous.

words.ex: The affluent family bought a big house by the lake.
words.ex_cn: 这个富裕的家庭在湖边买了一栋大房子。
words.en: Having a great deal of money; wealthy.

words.ex: Going first is a privilege, not a right.
words.ex_cn: 优先权是一种特权，而不是权利。
words.en: A privilege is a special right or advantage that only one person or group has.

words.ex: He gave an intentional wrong answer to confuse the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他故意答错答案来迷惑老师。
words.en: Something that is intentional is done on purpose, not by chance.

words.tr:
adj. 智力的；
n. 知识分子；
words.ex: He is an intellectual person who loves solving math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个热爱解决数学问题的智力型人。
words.en: An intellectual is someone who spends a lot of time studying and thinking about complicated ideas.

words.ex: The police intercepted the stolen car.
words.ex_cn: 警察拦截了那辆被盗的汽车。
words.en: If you intercept someone or something that is going from one place to another, you stop them before they get there.

words.tr:
n. 性格外向者；爱交际的人
adj. 外向的
words.ex: He is an extrovert who loves talking to people.
words.ex_cn: 他是个外向的人，喜欢和人交谈。
words.en: An extrovert is someone who is very outgoing, sociable, and enjoys being around other people.

words.ex: The doctor did an autopsy to find the cause of death.
words.ex_cn: 医生做了尸检以查明死因。
words.en: An autopsy is a medical examination of a dead body to discover the cause of death.

words.ex: He didn't refer to the book during the talk.
words.ex_cn: 他在演讲中没有提到那本书。
words.en: If you refer to a particular subject or person, you talk about them or mention them. If you refer to someone or something as a particular thing, you use a particular word, expression, or name to mention or describe them.

words.ex: I eat carrot and broccoli every day as vegetable.
words.ex_cn: 我每天吃胡萝卜和西兰花作为蔬菜。
words.en: A vegetable is a plant or part of a plant that is used as food, typically as accompaniment to meat or fish, such as a cabbage, potato, carrot, or bean.

words.ex: The legislator voted for a new law.
words.ex_cn: 这位立法者投票支持了一项新法律。
words.en: A legislator is a person who is a member of a legislature, especially in a democratic country.

words.ex: Each family was given an allotment of land to farm.
words.ex_cn: 每个家庭都被分配了一块土地来耕种。
words.en: An allotment is a share or portion of something that has been divided or distributed.

words.tr: adj. 根本的；彻底的；激进的；
words.ex: The government made radical changes to the education system.
words.ex_cn: 政府对教育系统进行了根本性的改革。
words.en: A radical change or difference is very big and important.

words.ex: At this juncture, we need to make a decision.
words.ex_cn: 在这一关键时刻，我们需要做出决定。
words.en: A particular point in events or time, especially one that is critical or decisive.

words.ex: He used too much jargon in his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他在演讲中用了太多行话。
words.en: Special words or expressions that are used by a particular profession or group and are difficult for others to understand.

words.tr: adj. 精明的；敏锐的；机灵的；
words.ex: He made a shrewd decision to buy the house low.
words.ex_cn: 他精明地决定低价买下这栋房子。
words.en: A shrewd person is able to understand and judge a situation quickly and to use this understanding to their own advantage.

words.tr:
adj. 苦行的；禁欲主义的
n. 苦行者；禁欲者
words.ex: He lives an ascetic life with no luxury.
words.ex_cn: 他过着简朴的生活，没有任何奢侈。
words.en: An ascetic person has a way of life that is simple and strict, usually because of their religious beliefs.

words.ex: Blue jeans are in vogue this year.
words.ex_cn: 今年牛仔裤很时髦。
words.en: If something is in vogue, it is very popular and fashionable.

words.ex: She is a vivacious girl who laughs loudly.
words.ex_cn: 她是一个活泼的女孩，笑得很响亮。
words.en: If you describe someone as vivacious, you mean that they are lively, exciting, and attractive.

words.tr: adj. 怀疑的；令人怀疑的；
words.ex: The police felt suspicious about the man's behavior.
words.ex_cn: 警察对这个人的行为感到怀疑。
words.en: If you are suspicious of someone or something, you do not trust them, and are careful when dealing with them.

words.ex: The country enjoys prosperity after years of peace.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家在多年的和平后迎来了繁荣。
words.en: Prosperity is a condition in which a person, community, or country is thriving and successful, especially in financial terms.

words.tr: adj. 和蔼可亲的；亲切友好的
words.ex: He is an amiable man who always smiles.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个和蔼可亲的人，总是面带微笑。
words.en: Someone who is amiable is friendly and pleasant to be with.

words.ex: The actor received acclaim for his performance.
words.ex_cn: 这位演员因他的表演而受到赞扬。
words.en: If someone or something is acclaimed, they are praised enthusiastically and publicly.

words.ex: The teacher will not condone cheating in exams.
words.ex_cn: 老师不会容忍考试作弊。
words.en: To condone something means to accept or allow behavior that is considered wrong.

words.ex: The king abrogated the old law.
words.ex_cn: 国王废除了旧法律。
words.en: If someone in a position of authority abrogates something such as a law, agreement, or practice, they put an end to it.

words.ex: The climate is hospitable for growing oranges.
words.ex_cn: 这种气候适合种植橙子。
words.en: If someone is hospitable, they are friendly, welcoming, and generous to guests or strangers.

words.tr: adj. 单纯的；自然的；不做作的
words.ex: Her artless smile made everyone feel at ease.
words.ex_cn: 她那天真的微笑让每个人都感到轻松。
words.en: If you describe someone as artless, you mean that they are simple and honest, and do not try to deceive other people.

words.ex: He gave an ultimatum: leave now or stay forever.
words.ex_cn: 他发出最后通牒：现在走，或者永远留下。
words.en: An ultimatum is a final demand or statement of terms, the rejection of which will result in retaliation or a breakdown in relations.

words.ex: Children need literacy to read books and write letters.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们需要有读写能力才能读书和写信。
words.en: Literacy is the ability to read and write.

words.tr:
n. 漠视；忽视；
v. 漠视；不理会；不顾；
words.ex: His advice was met with disregard.
words.ex_cn: 他的建议遭到了漠视。
words.en: If you disregard something, you ignore it or do not take account of it.

words.tr: v. 影响；“affect”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 染病的；受感动的；
words.ex: The rain affected the game.
words.ex_cn: 雨影响了比赛。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as affected, you disapprove of the fact that they behave in an unnatural way that is intended to impress other people.

words.ex: The pain was endurable, so she kept going.
words.ex_cn: 疼痛是可以忍受的，所以她继续前行。
words.en: If something is endurable, it is possible to be tolerated or endured.

words.ex: He is an interpreter for the United Nations.
words.ex_cn: 他是联合国的口译员。
words.en: An interpreter is a person whose job is to translate what someone is saying into another language, especially in a situation where people are speaking different languages.

words.ex: The earthquake was a catastrophe.
words.ex_cn: 这场地震是一场灾难。
words.en: An event causing great and often sudden damage or suffering; a disaster.

words.ex: She drank water to assuage her thirst.
words.ex_cn: 她喝水来缓解口渴。
words.en: If you assuage an unpleasant feeling that someone has, you make them feel it less strongly. To assuage a problem or situation means to make it less intense or severe.

words.tr:
v. 拖曳；搅乱；洗牌；移来移去
n. 拖着脚走；洗牌；混在一起
words.ex: He shuffle his feet across the floor.
words.ex_cn: 他拖着脚在地板上走。
words.en: To shuffle is to walk by dragging one's feet along or without lifting them fully from the ground. It also means to mix up the order of things, especially cards in a deck.

words.tr: adj. 有独创性的；巧妙的；
words.ex: The child came up with an ingenious way to solve the puzzle.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子想出了一个有独创性的方式来解决这个谜题。
words.en: Something that is ingenious is very clever and involves new ideas, methods, or equipment.

words.ex: The brevity of his speech surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他讲话的短暂让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: Brevity is the use of only a few words to say something, or the quality of being short in time.

words.tr: n. 热心者；热衷于…的人
words.ex: He is an enthusiast of basketball.
words.ex_cn: 他是篮球的爱好者。
words.en: An enthusiast is a person who is very interested in a particular activity or subject and who spends a lot of time on it.

words.ex: The witness gave credence to the story by crying.
words.ex_cn: 证人通过哭泣使这个故事显得可信。
words.en: Credence is a belief in or acceptance of something as true.

words.ex: Their betrothal was announced at the family gathering.
words.ex_cn: 他们的订婚在家庭聚会上宣布了。
words.en: A betrothal is a formal agreement to get married.

words.ex: The injury led to a complication in his recovery.
words.ex_cn: 这次受伤使他的康复过程复杂化了。
words.en: A complication is a problem or difficulty that makes a situation harder to deal with.

words.ex: The old man has a cataract in his right eye.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人右眼有白内障。
words.en: A cataract is a medical condition in which the lens of the eye becomes progressively opaque, resulting in blurred vision. It can also refer to a large waterfall.

words.tr: n. 朗诵；朗读；背诵；逐个叙述
words.ex: The boy did a recitation of the poem in class.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩在课堂上背诵了这首诗。
words.en: A recitation is the act of saying a piece of poetry or literature that you have learned to an audience.

words.ex: He was wary of strangers who offered free gifts.
words.ex_cn: 他对那些提供免费礼物的陌生人保持谨慎。
words.en: If you are wary of something or someone, you are cautious because you do not know much about them and you believe they may be dangerous or cause problems.

words.tr: v. 公开放弃；发誓断绝
words.ex: He had to abjure his old beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不放弃他的旧信仰。
words.en: If you abjure something such as a belief or way of life, you state publicly that you will give it up or that you reject it.

words.tr: v. 强烈吸引住；使着迷；
words.ex: The magic show fascinated the children.
words.ex_cn: 魔术表演深深吸引了孩子们。
words.en: If something fascinates you, it interests and delights you so much that your thoughts tend to concentrate on it.

words.ex: The teacher asked students to annotate the text with notes.
words.ex_cn: 老师让学生们在文本上做注释。
words.en: To add notes or comments to a text or diagram, providing explanation or criticism.

words.tr: n. 滑稽；丑态；插科打诨
words.ex: The play was filled with buffoonery to entertain the audience.
words.ex_cn: 这部戏充满了滑稽表演，以娱乐观众。
words.en: Buffoonery refers to behavior that is ridiculous but amusing, often involving silly jokes or actions.

words.ex: The plant's roots help in the absorption of water.
words.ex_cn: 植物的根有助于水分的吸收。
words.en: The process by which one thing absorbs or is absorbed by another.

words.tr: v. 详细检查；仔细察看
words.ex: The teacher scrutinizes every student's homework.
words.ex_cn: 老师仔细检查每位学生的作业。
words.en: If you scrutinize something, you examine it very carefully, often to find out some information from it or about it.

words.ex: The long meeting was tedious.
words.ex_cn: 这场漫长的会议很沉闷。
words.en: If you describe something such as a job, task, or situation as tedious, you mean it is boring and rather frustrating.

words.ex: He tries to belittle his brother's success.
words.ex_cn: 他试图贬低他哥哥的成功。
words.en: To belittle someone or something means to make them seem less important or less good than they really are.

words.ex: The peccant official was removed from his post.
words.ex_cn: 这名有过失的官员被免职了。
words.en: Guilty of a moral offense; sinning.

words.ex: The mechanical toy moves with batteries.
words.ex_cn: 这个机械玩具用电池驱动。
words.en: Relating to machines or machinery; operated by or involving a machine or machines.

words.ex: The morning was foggy, so I could not see the road.
words.ex_cn: 早晨有雾，所以我看不到路。
words.en: If it is foggy, there is fog.

words.ex: He was circumspect before signing the contract.
words.ex_cn: 他在签署合同之前非常谨慎。
words.en: If you are circumspect, you think carefully about something before doing it, because there may be risks involved.

words.ex: The circumference of the circle is 31.4 cm.
words.ex_cn: 这个圆的周长是31.4厘米。
words.en: The circumference of a circle is the distance around it.

words.tr:
n. 纤毛虫
adj. 有纤毛的；具缘毛的
words.ex: The ciliate protozoa are characterized by the presence of cilia.
words.ex_cn: 纤毛原生动物的特点是具有纤毛。
words.en: Having cilia; relating to or characteristic of ciliates.

words.ex: The law circumscribes what companies can do.
words.ex_cn: 法律限制了公司能做的事情。
words.en: To circumscribe something means to limit its size, activity, or scope, often by setting boundaries or restrictions.

words.ex: He was a despicable liar who hurt everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个可鄙的骗子，伤害了所有人。
words.en: If you say that a person or action is despicable, you are emphasizing that they are extremely nasty, cruel, or evil.

words.tr:
adv. 彻底地；立刻地；
adj. 完全的；彻底的；
words.ex: He refused the offer outright.
words.ex_cn: 他彻底拒绝了这个提议。
words.en: If something is done outright, it is done completely and without any hesitation or attempt to hide it.

words.ex: The child let out a loud shriek when she saw the spider.
words.ex_cn: 当孩子看到蜘蛛时，发出了一声大叫。
words.en: If someone shrieks, they make a short, very loud cry, for example because they are suddenly surprised, are in pain, or are laughing.

words.ex: The clothier provided high-quality fabrics for tailoring.
words.ex_cn: 这家衣庄提供了高质量的布料用于裁缝。
words.en: A clothier is a person or company that makes or sells clothes or cloth.

words.tr: adj. 有怪想的；想入非非的；任性顽固的；脾气坏的
words.ex: He became increasingly crotchety in his old age.
words.ex_cn: 他在老年时变得越来越反复无常。
words.en: If you describe someone as crotchety, you mean they are bad-tempered and easily irritated.

words.tr:
n. 索具装备；钻探设备；装备
v. 配备索具；操纵；舞弊
words.ex: He uses a rig to hold the camera steady.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个支架来固定相机。
words.en: To rig something means to arrange or set it up in a particular way, often in a temporary or makeshift manner. It can also refer to the equipment used in drilling for oil or gas, or the sails and ropes on a ship.

words.tr:
adj. 柔软的；可塑的；易弯曲的；有弹性的
v. 使柔软；把（火炮）系在前车上；做热身运动
n. （拖炮车的）前车
words.ex: The gymnast's body is remarkably limber.
words.ex_cn: 这位体操运动员的身体非常柔软。
words.en: Capable of moving or bending easily; flexible.

words.tr: v. 大批杀死；大量毁灭
words.ex: The storm decimated the village.
words.ex_cn: 风暴摧毁了这个村庄。
words.en: To decimate something such as a group of people or animals means to destroy a very large number of them.

words.ex: The old house looked dilapidated after years of neglect.
words.ex_cn: 这所老房子因多年疏于维护而显得残破。
words.en: A building that is dilapidated is old and in a generally bad condition.

words.tr: adj. 退化的；倒退的；回归的
words.ex: The patient's condition showed a regressive trend after the surgery.
words.ex_cn: 手术后，病人的情况显示出退化的趋势。
words.en: A regressive action, process, or idea is one that involves returning to an earlier and less advanced stage of development.

words.ex: The depth of the ocean is unfathomable.
words.ex_cn: 海洋的深度是深不可测的。
words.en: If something is unfathomable, it is so mysterious or complicated that it is impossible to understand or explain.

words.ex: He digresses when he talks about his vacation.
words.ex_cn: 他谈论假期时会跑题。
words.en: If you digress, you move away from the subject you are talking or writing about and talk or write about something different for a while.

words.ex: He made a plea for help.
words.ex_cn: 他恳求帮助。
words.en: A plea is a request or an appeal made in an urgent or emotional manner, or a statement made by someone in a court of law in which they say whether they are guilty of a crime or not.

words.tr:
n. 瘟疫；疫病；
v. 困扰；折磨；
words.ex: The plague killed many people in medieval Europe.
words.ex_cn: 瘟疫在中世纪的欧洲杀死了许多人。
words.en: A plague is a very infectious disease that spreads quickly and kills a lot of people. It can also refer to a large number of insects or animals that cause damage or are a nuisance.

words.ex: He lives in seclusion in the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 他住在山里，过着与世隔绝的生活。
words.en: The state of being private and away from other people.

words.ex: He was arrested for bilking investors out of millions of dollars.
words.ex_cn: 他因诈骗投资者数百万美元而被捕。
words.en: To bilk someone means to cheat them, especially out of money.

words.ex: He resents being ignored by his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他怨恨被老板忽视。
words.en: If you resent someone or something, you feel bitter and angry about them.

words.ex: Children have reliance on their parents for food and shelter.
words.ex_cn: 孩子依赖父母提供食物和住所。
words.en: Reliance is the state of depending on or trusting in someone or something.

words.tr: v. 声称；“allege”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 所谓的；
words.ex: He alleged that the witness lied.
words.ex_cn: 他声称证人说了谎。
words.en: An alleged fact has been stated but has not been proved.

words.ex: The castle was beleaguered by enemy soldiers.
words.ex_cn: 城堡被敌军围攻。
words.en: To beleaguer means to lay siege to or to cause trouble or difficulty for someone over a period of time.

words.ex: The dark clouds forebode a storm.
words.ex_cn: 乌云预示着一场风暴。
words.en: If something forebodes a future event, it suggests that it is going to happen.

words.tr: n. 恢复；重新开始；继续进行
words.ex: The resumption of classes was delayed by one week.
words.ex_cn: 课程的恢复被推迟了一周。
words.en: The act of starting something again after a pause or interruption.

words.tr: v. 兜售；沿街叫卖； 散播
words.ex: He tries to peddle fake watches on the street.
words.ex_cn: 他试图在街上兜售假手表。
words.en: To peddle goods or ideas means to try to sell them or make them accepted by going from place to place.

words.tr: adj. 辛辣的；苦涩的；刺激的；尖刻的
words.ex: The smoke from the fire had an acrid smell.
words.ex_cn: 火灾的烟雾有一种刺鼻的气味。
words.en: An acrid smell or taste is strong and sharp, and usually unpleasant. It can also describe a manner or expression that is bitter or harsh.

words.tr:
n. 否决；否决权
v. 否决
words.ex: The president used his veto to stop the law.
words.ex_cn: 总统行使否决权阻止了这项法律。
words.en: If someone in authority vetoes something, they forbid it, or they stop it from being put into action.

words.tr: v. 承认；公开宣称声明
words.ex: He avows his love for her.
words.ex_cn: 他坦承自己对她的爱。
words.en: If you avow something, you declare it or admit it openly.

words.ex: He deluded himself into thinking he would win.
words.ex_cn: 他欺骗自己，以为自己会赢。
words.en: If you delude yourself, you let yourself believe that something is true, even though it is not true.

words.ex: The word means different things in different context.
words.ex_cn: 这个词在不同的上下文中意思不同。
words.en: The context of an idea or event is the general situation that relates to it, and which helps it to be understood.

words.ex: The invasion of privacy is a serious problem.
words.ex_cn: 侵犯隐私是一个严重的问题。
words.en: An invasion is an instance of invading a country or region with an armed force.

words.ex: The judge will arbitrate the dispute between the two neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 法官将调解这两个邻居之间的纠纷。
words.en: To arbitrate means to officially settle a dispute by making a decision that both sides accept.

words.ex: He predetermines the outcome before the game starts.
words.ex_cn: 他在比赛开始前就决定了结果。
words.en: To decide or settle (something) in advance.

words.tr: adj. 较合意的；更可取的；
words.ex: Tea is preferable to coffee in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 早上喝茶比喝咖啡更合意。
words.en: If you say that one thing is preferable to another, you mean that it is more desirable or suitable.

words.ex: He looked incredulous when he heard the news.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到这个消息时，他一脸难以置信。
words.en: If someone is incredulous, they are unable to believe something because it is very surprising or shocking.

words.ex: It was futile to try to fix the broken clock.
words.ex_cn: 试图修理坏掉的钟表是徒劳的。
words.en: If you say that something is futile, you mean there is no point in doing it, usually because it has no chance of succeeding.

words.tr: adj. 野兽的；野兽般的；极残忍的
words.ex: The bestial treatment of the prisoners shocked everyone.
words.ex_cn: 对囚犯的兽性对待震惊了所有人。
words.en: If you describe behavior or a situation as bestial, you mean that it is very unpleasant or disgusting.

words.tr: adj. 全世界的；四海一家的；
words.ex: This city has a cosmopolitan population.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市有着来自世界各地的人口。
words.en: A cosmopolitan place or society is full of people from many different countries and cultures.

words.tr: adj. 暗示的；影射的；性暗示的
words.ex: His look was suggestive of sadness.
words.ex_cn: 他的眼神暗示着悲伤。
words.en: Something that is suggestive of something else is likely to make you think about or remember it.

words.tr: adj. 资源丰富的；机敏的；足智多谋的
words.ex: He is a resourceful man who can fix anything with little material.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个资源丰富的男人，能用很少的材料修好任何东西。
words.en: If someone is resourceful, they are good at finding ways of dealing with problems.

words.tr: adj. 适合居住的；可居住的；
words.ex: The planet is habitable because it has water and air.
words.ex_cn: 这颗行星有水和空气，适合居住。
words.en: A place that is habitable is suitable or good enough for people to live in.

words.tr: adj. 不透明的；难懂的；晦涩的
words.ex: The glass is opaque, so I cannot see through it.
words.ex_cn: 这扇玻璃是不透明的，所以我看不到它后面的东西。
words.en: If an object or substance is opaque, you cannot see through it.

words.tr: n. 不适当；不正确；不得体
words.ex: His impropriety at the meeting shocked everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议上的不恰当行为让所有人都感到震惊。
words.en: Impropriety is the quality or state of being improper, especially in behavior or speech.

words.tr:
n. 库存；股票；家畜；
v. 备有；贮存；
words.ex: The store has low stock of winter coats.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店的冬衣库存很少。
words.en: The supply of goods available for sale in a store; the capital raised by a company through the issue of shares.

words.ex: She led a reclusive life in the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 她在山中过着隐居的生活。
words.en: If you describe someone as reclusive, you mean that they live alone and do not like seeing or talking to other people.

words.tr: v. 使迷惑；使...不知所措
words.ex: The strange signs bewilder the children.
words.ex_cn: 这些奇怪的符号让孩子们感到迷惑。
words.en: If something bewilders you, it is so confusing or difficult that you cannot understand it.

words.tr: v. 叙述；给（电视或电影）作旁白
words.ex: He will narrate the story to his little sister.
words.ex_cn: 他将为他的小妹妹讲述这个故事。
words.en: If you narrate a story, you tell it from your own point of view.

words.ex: The immigrants quickly learned the language and culture, showing rapid assimilation.
words.ex_cn: 这些移民很快学会了语言和文化，显示出快速的同化。
words.en: The process of taking in and fully understanding information or ideas.

words.ex: His familiarity with the city helped him find the way.
words.ex_cn: 他对这座城市的熟悉帮助他找到了路。
words.en: A thorough knowledge or mastery of a subject, place, or situation, often gained through experience.

words.tr:
adj. 狂热入迷的；盲信的
n. 狂热者；盲信者
words.ex: He is a fanatic fan of soccer.
words.ex_cn: 他对足球狂热入迷。
words.en: A fanatic is a person who is very enthusiastic about and devoted to a particular activity, cause, or belief, often to an extreme degree.

words.tr:
v. 少要价钱；少算价钱；填充不足
n. 低的索价；填不够量的火药；充电不足
words.ex: The mechanic undercharged me for the repair work.
words.ex_cn: 修理工给我的修理工作索价低于常价。
words.en: To charge someone less than the correct or usual amount for something.

words.tr:
n. 编年史；年代记
v. 按时间顺序记录
words.ex: He writes a chronicle of his daily life.
words.ex_cn: 他记录自己每天的生活。
words.en: A chronicle is a historical account of events arranged in chronological order, typically without analysis or interpretation.

words.ex: The expanse of the desert stretched far beyond the horizon.
words.ex_cn: 沙漠的辽阔延伸到了地平线之外。
words.en: An expanse is a wide and open area or surface.

words.ex: The chemicals are hazardous to health.
words.ex_cn: 这些化学物质对健康有危险。
words.en: Something that is hazardous is dangerous, especially to people's health or safety.

words.ex: He has amnesia and cannot remember his name.
words.ex_cn: 他患有失忆症，想不起自己的名字。
words.en: Amnesia is a medical condition that affects someone's memory and they are unable to remember events or information.

words.ex: They had an amicable talk after the argument.
words.ex_cn: 争吵之后，他们进行了一次友好的交谈。
words.en: When people have an amicable relationship, they are pleasant towards each other and solve their problems without arguing.

words.ex: Heretofore, he did not understand the problem.
words.ex_cn: 到目前为止，他不明白这个问题。
words.en: Up to this time; until now.

words.tr: v. 使羞惭；使不安；使窘迫
words.ex: He was abashed when he forgot his lines.
words.ex_cn: 当他忘记台词时，他感到尴尬。
words.en: If someone is abashed, they feel embarrassed and ashamed.

words.ex: He conveyed his thanks with a smile.
words.ex_cn: 他微笑着表达了谢意。
words.en: If you convey information or a message, you communicate it to someone, often in a way that is not direct.

words.ex: He refused to disclose the secret.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝透露这个秘密。
words.en: To disclose information means to make it known to the public.

words.tr: adj. 暂定的；不确定的；试验性的；
words.ex: We made a tentative plan to meet next week.
words.ex_cn: 我们制定了一个下周见面的暂定计划。
words.en: If you make a tentative suggestion or plan, you make it without being sure that it is right or acceptable.

words.ex: The doctor wrote a prescription for medicine.
words.ex_cn: 医生开了一张药方。
words.en: A prescription is a written order from a physician for the preparation and administration of a drug or device for a patient.

words.tr: adj. 爱挑剔的；吹毛求疵的
words.ex: He is censorious about everyone's mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他对每个人的错误都吹毛求疵。
words.en: If you describe someone as censorious, you mean that they strongly disapprove of and criticize someone else's behavior.

words.ex: He looked at her with suspicion.
words.ex_cn: 他带着怀疑的眼神看着她。
words.en: A feeling or thought that something is possible, likely, or true, especially something bad or wrong, without having proof.

words.ex: Too many rules can complicate the game.
words.ex_cn: 太多的规则会使游戏变得复杂。
words.en: To make something more difficult to understand or deal with by adding more parts or details.

words.tr:
adj. 腐蚀性的；苛性的；尖酸刻薄的
n. 腐蚀剂
words.ex: The caustic liquid burned through the metal.
words.ex_cn: 这种腐蚀性的液体腐蚀了金属。
words.en: A caustic substance is able to burn or destroy organic tissue by chemical action. Caustic remarks are extremely critical, sarcastic, or bitter.

words.ex: This coupon is valid until next month.
words.ex_cn: 这张优惠券到下个月都有效。
words.en: If something such as a document or agreement is valid, it is legally acceptable or officially recognized.

words.ex: He was conscious after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故后他醒了过来。
words.en: If you are conscious of something, you notice it or are aware of it.

words.ex: The sun will desiccate the leaves in summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天阳光会把叶子晒干。
words.en: To remove the moisture from something, typically in order to preserve it.

words.ex: He contends that education is the key to success.
words.ex_cn: 他主张教育是成功的关键。
words.en: If you contend with someone or contend with something, you have to deal with a difficult situation or problem. If you contend that something is true, you state or argue that it is true.

words.ex: He pretends to sleep when his mom asks him to clean his room.
words.ex_cn: 当妈妈让他打扫房间时，他假装睡觉。
words.en: If you pretend that something is the case, you act in a way that is intended to make people believe that it is the case, although in fact it is not.

words.ex: This car is economical because it uses little fuel.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车很经济，因为它耗油少。
words.en: Using money, resources, or time in a careful and effective way.

words.ex: The pastoral man tends his sheep on the hill.
words.ex_cn: 这位牧人在山上照看他的羊。
words.en: Relating to the countryside or to the work of a shepherd; idyllically rural.

words.ex: The room was devoid of any furniture.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间里全无家具。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is devoid of a quality or thing, you are emphasizing that they have none of it.

words.ex: He used a pretext to leave the meeting early.
words.ex_cn: 他找了个借口提前离开了会议。
words.en: A pretext is a false reason that you give for doing something, usually something bad, in order to hide the real reason.

words.ex: The onset of winter brought heavy snow.
words.ex_cn: 冬天的开始带来了大雪。
words.en: The onset of something is the beginning of it, especially something unpleasant.

words.tr: v. 要求归还；收回；开垦；感化
words.ex: He wants to reclaim his lost wallet.
words.ex_cn: 他想要要求归还他丢失的钱包。
words.en: If you reclaim something that you have lost or that has been taken away from you, you succeed in getting it back. If you reclaim land, you make it suitable for use, for example by draining it or by getting rid of unwanted buildings or plants.

words.tr:
n. 日食；月食；黯然失色
v. 使失色
words.ex: We watched the solar eclipse last night.
words.ex_cn: 我们昨晚观看了日食。
words.en: An eclipse occurs when one celestial body moves into the shadow of another, temporarily obscuring it or cutting off its light.

words.ex: The glass is brittle and breaks easily.
words.ex_cn: 这种玻璃很硬但容易碎。
words.en: If something is brittle, it is hard and easily broken.

words.tr: v. 哄；用好话劝诱；哄骗
words.ex: He tried to coax the cat out from under the bed.
words.ex_cn: 他试图哄猫从床底下出来。
words.en: To coax someone means to persuade them to do something by gentle persuasion or flattery.

words.ex: The premise of his argument is that everyone is equal.
words.ex_cn: 他论点的前提是人人平等。
words.en: A premise is a statement or idea that forms the basis for a reasonable line of argument.

words.tr: adj. 有竞争力的；竞争的；
words.ex: She is a competitive runner who wins many races.
words.ex_cn: 她是一个有竞争力的跑步者，赢得了许多比赛。
words.en: Competitive is used to describe situations or activities in which people or firms compete with each other.

words.ex: He is amenable to new ideas.
words.ex_cn: 他愿意接受新想法。
words.en: If you are amenable to something, you are willing to do it or accept it.

words.ex: It is rational to save money for the future.
words.ex_cn: 为未来存钱是合理的。
words.en: Based on or in accordance with reason or logic.

words.ex: The price of the phone is prohibitive for most students.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机的价格对大多数学生来说太贵了。
words.en: If the cost of something is prohibitive, it is so high that it prevents people from buying it or doing it.

words.ex: The emergence of new technology changed our lives.
words.ex_cn: 新技术的出现改变了我们的生活。
words.en: The process of coming into view or becoming exposed after being concealed.

words.ex: They will demolish the old building next week.
words.ex_cn: 他们下周会拆掉那座旧建筑。
