words.ex_cn: 有隔热保护的墙壁使房子在冬天保持温暖。
words.en: Protected from heat, cold, noise, etc., by being surrounded with material that reduces or prevents the transmission of heat or sound.

words.ex: He tried to agitate the workers to strike.
words.ex_cn: 他试图鼓动工人罢工。
words.en: If you agitate something, you stir it up or shake it. If something agitates you, it makes you feel anxious or upset.

words.ex: The teacher punished the boy for his misbehavior.
words.ex_cn: 老师因为他的不良行为惩罚了那个男孩。
words.en: Misbehavior refers to actions or conduct that are considered inappropriate or unacceptable in a given context, especially by children or students in an educational setting.

words.tr: n. 视角；观点；（对事物的）合理判断；
words.ex: His perspective on life is very positive.
words.ex_cn: 他对生活的看法非常积极。
words.en: A particular attitude towards or way of regarding something; a point of view.

words.ex: His speech was coherent and easy to understand.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲连贯且易于理解。
words.en: If something is coherent, it is well planned, so that it is clear and sensible and all its parts go well with each other.

words.tr: adj. 大量的；重大的；实质性的；
words.ex: He made a substantial profit from the sale.
words.ex_cn: 他从这次销售中获得了大量的利润。
words.en: Something that is substantial is large in size, amount, or importance.

words.tr: adj. 无可匹敌的；盖世无双的
words.ex: Her singing is peerless.
words.ex_cn: 她的歌唱无人能及。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as peerless, you mean that they are better than any other person or thing of the same type.

words.tr: n. 政治阴谋小集团；秘密团体
words.ex: The cabal plotted to overthrow the government.
words.ex_cn: 这个阴谋集团策划推翻政府。
words.en: A cabal is a small group of people who are involved in secret plans to achieve political or social change, often by illegal or dishonest methods.

words.ex: He reads books in his leisure.
words.ex_cn: 他在空闲时间读书。
words.en: Leisure is the time when you are not working and you can relax and do things that you enjoy.

words.ex: The team showed great camaraderie during the match.
words.ex_cn: 团队在比赛中展现了深厚的友爱。
words.en: A feeling of good friendship among the people in a group.

words.ex: It's an irony that the fire station burned down.
words.ex_cn: 消防站着火了，这真是讽刺。
words.en: Irony is a subtle form of humor which involves saying things that you do not mean.

words.tr: v. 使夷为平地；彻底摧毁
words.ex: They will raze the old building next week.
words.ex_cn: 他们下周将把那座旧建筑夷为平地。
words.en: To raze a building, town, or forest means to completely destroy it, especially by knocking it down or burning it.

words.ex: He engraves his name on the ring.
words.ex_cn: 他把名字刻在戒指上。
words.en: To engrave means to cut or carve a design or letters into a hard surface, or to be strongly impressed in someone's memory.

words.ex: The bright light was a stimulus for the baby to open his eyes.
words.ex_cn: 明亮的光线是让婴儿睁开眼睛的刺激物。
words.en: Something that causes growth or activity.

words.ex: The earthquake was a sudden cataclysm.
words.ex_cn: 这场地震是一场突如其来的灾难。
words.en: A cataclysm is an event that causes great damage or makes a big change to something.

words.tr:
v. 把…归因于；由…引起；
n. 品质；属性；特征；属性；
words.ex: He attributes his success to hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的成功归因于努力工作。
words.en: If you attribute something to an event or situation, you think that it was caused by that event or situation.

words.tr:
n. 分钟；一会儿；
adj. 微小的；极小的；
words.ex: I waited for five minutes.
words.ex_cn: 我等了五分钟。
words.en: A minute is a unit of time equal to sixty seconds or a sixtieth of an hour.

words.tr: adj. 苍白的；像尸体的；枯槁的
words.ex: His cadaverous appearance frightened the children.
words.ex_cn: 他那尸体般的惨白面容吓坏了孩子们。
words.en: If you describe someone as cadaverous, you mean they are extremely thin and pale.

words.tr: n. 拼贴画；拼贴艺术；杂烩
words.ex: He made a collage from old magazine pictures.
words.ex_cn: 他用旧杂志的图片做了一幅拼贴画。
words.en: A collage is a picture that has been made by sticking pieces of colored paper, cloth, or photographs onto a surface.

words.ex: He felt indignant when they blamed him for the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 当他们把错误归咎于他时，他感到愤愤不平。
words.en: If you are indignant, you are shocked and angry, because you think that something is unjust or unfair.

words.tr: v. 重新考虑；重新审议
words.ex: He must reconsider his decision.
words.ex_cn: 他必须重新考虑他的决定。
words.en: If you reconsider a decision or opinion, you think about it and try to decide whether it should be changed.

words.ex: He will delineate the plan clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他将清晰地描述这个计划。
words.en: To delineate something means to describe or portray it precisely.

words.tr: v. 使屈辱；使丢脸；使蒙羞
words.ex: He tried to humiliate her in front of the class.
words.ex_cn: 他试图在全班面前羞辱她。
words.en: To humiliate someone means to make them feel ashamed or stupid, especially in front of other people.

words.ex: He lives independently and makes his own decisions.
words.ex_cn: 他独立生活，并自己做决定。
words.en: If one thing or person is independent of another, they are separate and not connected, so that the first one is not affected or influenced by the second.

words.ex: The rebellious boy refused to follow the rules.
words.ex_cn: 这个叛逆的男孩拒绝遵守规则。
words.en: If you think someone is rebellious, you mean that they are deliberately not obeying people in authority or rules of behaviour.

words.tr:
v. 指责；斥责
n. 指责；谴责
words.ex: The teacher gave him a rebuke for talking in class.
words.ex_cn: 老师因为他上课讲话而责备了他。
words.en: If you rebuke someone, you speak severely to them because they have said or done something that you do not approve of.

words.ex: This book is about the realm of artificial intelligence.
words.ex_cn: 这本书是关于人工智能领域的。
words.en: A realm is a country ruled by a king or queen, or an area of activity, interest, or knowledge.

words.tr:
v. 使困惑；难倒；阻碍
n. 挡板；遮护物；阻碍体
words.ex: The magic trick baffled the children.
words.ex_cn: 这个魔术让孩子们感到困惑。
words.en: If something baffles you, you cannot understand it or explain it.

words.ex: The people showed resistance against the unfair law.
words.ex_cn: 人们对这项不公平的法律表示抵抗。
words.en: Resistance is the refusal to accept or comply with something; the attempt to prevent something by action or argument.

words.tr: adj. 焦虑的；渴望的；担忧的；
words.ex: He feels anxious before every test.
words.ex_cn: 他每次考试前都感到焦虑。
words.en: If you are anxious to do something or anxious that something should happen, you very much want to do it or very much want it to happen.

words.ex: He reject the job offer.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝了这份工作邀请。
words.en: If you reject something such as a proposal, a request, or an offer, you do not accept it or you do not agree to it.

words.tr:
n. 过度工作；过度劳累；滥用
v. 工作过度；劳累过度；对…使用过度
words.ex: He got sick from overwork.
words.ex_cn: 他因过度工作而生病了。
words.en: If you overwork or if someone overworks you, you work too hard, often to the point of exhaustion.

words.tr: n. 违反；妨碍；侵犯；违背；
words.ex: The driver got a ticket for traffic violation.
words.ex_cn: 司机因违反交通规则被开罚单。
words.en: A violation is an action that breaks a law, agreement, principle, etc.

words.ex: We need to reduce waste in our daily life.
words.ex_cn: 我们需要减少日常生活中的浪费。
words.en: If you reduce something, you make it smaller in size or amount, or less in degree.

words.ex: His benevolence helped the poor family.
words.ex_cn: 他的仁慈帮助了这个贫困家庭。
words.en: The quality of being well meaning; kindness.

words.ex: The renaissance brought new art and ideas to Europe.
words.ex_cn: 文艺复兴为欧洲带来了新的艺术和思想。
words.en: The Renaissance was a period in European history marking the transition from the Middle Ages to modernity and covering the 15th and 16th centuries, characterized by an effort to revive and surpass ideas and achievements of classical antiquity.

words.ex: The judge showed clemency and reduced the sentence.
words.ex_cn: 法官表现出宽大，减轻了刑罚。
words.en: Clemency is kindness and forgiveness, especially towards someone who could be punished severely.

words.ex: His answer was apposite to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答与问题很贴切。
words.en: Something that is apposite is suitable for or appropriate to what is happening or being discussed.

words.ex: He bought a new accessory for his phone.
words.ex_cn: 他为他的手机买了一个新配件。
words.en: An accessory is something such as a bag or piece of jewelry that you wear or carry because it is attractive.

words.tr: v. 促进；推动；宣传；推销；
words.ex: Exercise can promote good health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以促进健康。
words.en: To promote means to help something to happen, develop, or increase, or to raise someone to a higher position or rank.

words.tr:
v. 补充；与…相辅相成；
n. 补足物；补语；余角；
words.ex: The red scarf complements her blue coat.
words.ex_cn: 这条红围巾补充了她的蓝外套。
words.en: To complement something means to make it complete or perfect by adding something to it.

words.ex: He sang a old ballad about love and war.
words.ex_cn: 他唱了一首关于爱情与战争的老民谣。
words.en: A ballad is a type of song that tells a story, often a folk song or a slow romantic song.

words.tr: adj. 傲慢的；高傲自大的
words.ex: He gave a haughty smile when he won the prize.
words.ex_cn: 他赢得奖品时露出了傲慢的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as haughty, you mean that they behave in a proud, unfriendly way, because they think that they are better than other people.

words.ex: The celebrity smiled at the fans outside the theater.
words.ex_cn: 这位名人向剧院外的粉丝微笑。
words.en: A celebrity is a famous person, especially in entertainment or sports.

words.tr: v. 使可见；使形象化；设想；
words.ex: He uses maps to visualize the data.
words.ex_cn: 他使用地图来使数据可见。
words.en: If you visualize something, you imagine what it is like by forming a mental picture of it.

words.ex: His reputation was besmirched by the false accusations.
words.ex_cn: 他的名声被这些虚假的指控玷污了。
words.en: To besmirch someone or something means to spoil their good reputation.

words.ex: The cat overleaps the fence easily.
words.ex_cn: 这只猫轻松地跳过了篱笆。
words.en: To jump over or across something; to omit or ignore something.

words.tr: n. 微积分学；（人体内的）结石
words.ex: He is learning calculus at school.
words.ex_cn: 他正在学校学习微积分。
words.en: Calculus is a branch of mathematics that deals with the finding and properties of derivatives and integrals of functions, by methods originally based on the summation of infinitesimal differences.

words.ex: The bridge can withstand strong winds.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥能经受住强风。
words.en: If something or someone withstands a force or action, they survive it or do not give in to it.

words.tr: adj. 迷人的；娇媚的； v. “charm”的现在分词；
words.ex: The little village is charming with its flowers and quiet streets.
words.ex_cn: 这个小村庄以其花朵和宁静的街道而迷人。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as charming, you mean they are very pleasant and attractive.

words.ex: He committed apostasy by leaving his religion.
words.ex_cn: 他因放弃自己的宗教而犯了背教罪。
words.en: Apostasy is the act of abandoning or renouncing a religious or political belief or principle.

words.ex: Two events happen concurrently.
words.ex_cn: 两个事件同时发生。
words.en: Happening or existing at the same time.

words.ex: The medical students studied the anatomy of the cadaver.
words.ex_cn: 医学生们研究了尸体的解剖结构。
words.en: A dead body, especially one that is intended for dissection.

words.tr:
n. 藏物处；隐藏物；
v. 匿藏；
words.ex: The hunters found a cache of food under the rocks.
words.ex_cn: 猎人们在石头下发现了一个食物藏匿处。
words.en: A cache is a hidden store of things such as weapons or a supply of food.

words.tr: v. 以甜言蜜语哄骗；勾引
words.ex: He tried to cajole his sister into lending him money.
words.ex_cn: 他试图哄骗妹妹把钱借给他。
words.en: If you cajole someone into doing something, you persuade them to do it by flattery or by making promises.

words.tr:
adj. 迅速的；敏捷的；快的；
n. 雨燕；
words.ex: The swift runner won the race.
words.ex_cn: 这位迅速的跑步者赢得了比赛。
words.en: moving or capable of moving at great speed, or happening within a very short time; fast.

words.ex: He earned the esteem of his colleagues through hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他通过努力工作赢得了同事们的尊重。
words.en: If you esteem someone or something, you respect or admire them.

words.ex: He tried to suppress his anger.
words.ex_cn: 他试图抑制自己的愤怒。
words.en: To suppress something means to prevent it from being expressed, known, or continuing.

words.ex: He surpassed his brother in math scores.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学成绩上超过了他弟弟。
words.en: If one person or thing surpasses another, the first is better than, or has more of a particular quality than, the second.

words.tr: adj. 易怒的；暴躁的；脾气不好的
words.ex: He is a choleric man who shouts when he is angry.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个易怒的人，一生气就大喊大叫。
words.en: A choleric person is someone who gets angry very easily.

words.ex: He cannot comprehend the simple math problem.
words.ex_cn: 他无法理解这个简单的数学问题。
words.en: To comprehend something means to understand it fully.

words.tr: adj. 单调乏味的；毫无变化的；
words.ex: The work is monotonous and boring.
words.ex_cn: 这份工作单调乏味。
words.en: Something that is monotonous is very boring because it has a regular, repeated pattern which never changes.

words.ex: He has a natural aptitude for math.
words.ex_cn: 他天生有数学天赋。
words.en: An aptitude is a natural ability to do something.

words.tr: v. 损毁…的外形；使变丑
words.ex: The accident disfigured his face.
words.ex_cn: 那次事故使他的脸变形了。
words.en: To disfigure someone or something means to spoil their appearance.

words.tr: adj. 坚决的；毅然的；有决心的；
words.ex: He was resolute in his decision to quit smoking.
words.ex_cn: 他决心戒烟。
words.en: If you describe someone as resolute, you approve of them because they are very determined not to change their mind or not to give up a course of action.

words.tr: n. 获得；得到的东西；收购；
words.ex: The acquisition of new skills takes time.
words.ex_cn: 获得新技能需要时间。
words.en: An acquisition is something that someone buys, often to add to a collection of things.

words.ex: The quantity of water in the bottle is small.
words.ex_cn: 瓶子里的水量很少。
words.en: A quantity is an amount that you can measure or count.

words.ex: The priest gave his benison to the newlyweds.
words.ex_cn: 牧师为新婚夫妇送上祝福。
words.en: A benison is a blessing or a prayer asking for divine favor and protection.

words.ex: He sat by the window to ponder his future.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在窗边深思自己的未来。
words.en: If you ponder something, you think about it carefully.

words.ex: The project involves simple math and writing.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目包括简单的数学和写作。
words.en: If a situation or activity involves something, that thing is a necessary part or consequence of it.

words.tr:
v. 嘲笑；嘲弄；
adj. 仿制的；
words.ex: They mock him for his accent.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为他口音而嘲笑他。
words.en: To mock someone means to laugh at them, tease them, or make them look foolish, often by imitating their behavior or speech.

words.ex: His reaction was quick when the ball came at him.
words.ex_cn: 当球朝他飞来时，他的反应很快。
words.en: Your reaction to something that has happened or something that you have experienced is what you feel, say, or do because of it.

words.ex: Parents habituate children to eat vegetables early.
words.ex_cn: 父母从小就让孩子习惯吃蔬菜。
words.en: To make or become used to something as a result of repeated exposure.

words.ex: He commiserated with his friend after the loss.
words.ex_cn: 他在朋友失利后安慰了他。
words.en: If you commiserate with someone, you show them pity or sympathy because something unpleasant has happened to them.

words.ex: He works in a laboratory on Fridays.
words.ex_cn: 他在星期五去实验室工作。
words.en: A laboratory is a place equipped for scientific research, experiments, or teaching.

words.tr: n. 时代错误；不合时代的事；过时的事或人
words.ex: The knight in the movie uses a smartphone, which is an anachronism.
words.ex_cn: 电影中的骑士使用智能手机，这是不合时宜的。
words.en: An anachronism is something that is out of place in terms of time or chronology, such as an object, a custom, or an idea that belongs to a different time period than the one in which it is placed.

words.ex: The baby's neural connections are developing fast.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿的神经连接正在迅速发展。
words.en: Neural relates to a nerve or the nervous system.

words.tr: adj. 易变的；无常的；感情不专的
words.ex: He is fickle and changes his mind every day.
words.ex_cn: 他善变，每天都会改变主意。
words.en: If you describe someone as fickle, you disapprove of them because they keep changing their mind about what they like or want.

words.tr: adj. 无意识的；无知觉的；
words.ex: He was unconscious after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，他失去了意识。
words.en: If someone is unconscious, they are not awake, usually because they have had a severe injury or illness.

words.ex: He believes in atheism and does not follow any religion.
words.ex_cn: 他信仰无神论，不信仰任何宗教。
words.en: The belief that there is no God or gods.

words.ex: The wind generates electricity.
words.ex_cn: 风产生电力。
words.en: To generate something means to cause it to begin and develop.

words.ex: The software bloat makes the phone slow.
words.ex_cn: 软件臃肿让手机变慢。
words.en: To bloat means to cause something to swell up or become excessively large, often in an unhealthy or undesirable way.

words.tr:
adj. 不满的；不忠的；有叛意的
v. 使不满；使疏远；“disaffect”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The disaffected youth joined the protest.
words.ex_cn: 不满的青年加入了抗议活动。
words.en: If you are disaffected, you no longer support or are satisfied with something or someone, especially a group or organization that you used to support.

words.ex: The two companies will amalgamate next month.
words.ex_cn: 这两家公司下个月将合并。
words.en: If two or more organizations amalgamate, they join together and become one organization.

words.tr: v. 跌倒；下降；砍伐；“fall”的过去式；
words.ex: He fell off the bike.
words.ex_cn: 他从自行车上摔了下来。
words.en: To cut down (a tree); to knock down (a person or animal); the skin of an animal with the hair or wool still on it; fierce or cruel.

words.ex: The rain was a concomitant of the storm.
words.ex_cn: 雨水是这场风暴的同时发生的事。
words.en: Something that is concomitant with something else, especially something undesirable, happens at the same time as it or is connected with it.

words.tr: adj. 任性的；故意的；蓄意的
words.ex: The willful child refused to eat his vegetables.
words.ex_cn: 这个任性的孩子拒绝吃蔬菜。
words.en: If you describe actions or attitudes as willful, you are critical of them because they are done or expressed deliberately, especially with the intention of causing harm, or they are stubborn and unreasonable.

words.ex: The reversal of the decision made everyone happy.
words.ex_cn: 这个决定的逆转让每个人都高兴。
words.en: A reversal is a change to an opposite direction, position, or course of action.

words.ex: The dress gave her a lot of glamour.
words.ex_cn: 这条裙子给她增添了许多魅力。
words.en: If someone or something has glamour, they are attractive and exciting in a way that is not ordinary.

words.tr: v. 使沮丧气馁；使灰心
words.ex: The bad news disheartened the team.
words.ex_cn: 这个坏消息使团队灰心了。
words.en: To dishearten someone means to cause them to lose hope or enthusiasm.

words.ex: There was a contention between the two students about the answer.
words.ex_cn: 两个学生对答案发生了争论。
words.en: A contention is a strong disagreement or argument about something. It can also refer to a point or statement that someone argues is true.

words.ex: A flurry of snow covered the streets last night.
words.ex_cn: 昨晚一阵风雪覆盖了街道。
words.en: A flurry is a sudden, short period of activity, emotion, or excitement, often accompanied by confusion or haste.

words.ex: The school decided to adopt a new teaching method.
words.ex_cn: 学校决定采纳一种新的教学方法。
words.en: To adopt means to take up or start to use or follow (an idea, method, or course of action). It can also mean to legally take another's child and bring it up as one's own.

words.tr: n. 生态学家；生态学者；
words.ex: The ecologist studied birds in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 这位生态学家研究了森林里的鸟类。
words.en: An ecologist is a scientist who studies the relationships between living things and their environment.

words.ex: He gave an explicit answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了明确的答案。
words.en: Something that is explicit is expressed or shown clearly and openly, without any attempt to hide anything.

words.ex: He estranged his brother with harsh words.
words.ex_cn: 他用刻薄的话与兄弟疏远了。
words.en: If you estrange someone, especially a member of your family, you cause them to stop being friendly or close to you.

words.tr: adj. 根据事实的；真实的；
words.ex: His report is factual and accurate.
words.ex_cn: 他的报告是基于事实且准确的。
words.en: If something is factual, it is based on facts or concerns facts.

words.ex: He will defer his trip until next month.
words.ex_cn: 他将把旅行推迟到下个月。
words.en: If you defer an event or action, you arrange for it to happen at a later date, rather than immediately or at the previously planned time.

words.tr:
v. 擦亮；磨光
n. 光泽
words.ex: He burnishes the old metal every weekend.
words.ex_cn: 他每个周末都抛光那块旧金属。
words.en: To burnish something means to polish it and make it shine by rubbing it.

words.tr:
n. 亡命之徒；逃犯；被剥夺法律权益者
v. 宣布…为非法；使…成为非法
words.ex: The police caught the outlaw last night.
words.ex_cn: 警察昨晚抓住了那个不法之徒。
words.en: An outlaw is a person who has broken the law and who is hiding or running away to avoid punishment. To outlaw something means to make it illegal.

words.ex: He looked at the catalog to find the book.
words.ex_cn: 他翻看目录来找那本书。
words.en: A catalog is a list of things, such as the goods you can buy from a particular company, the objects in a museum, or the books in a library.

words.tr: phrase. 卡片目录（用于图书馆中按卡片索引图书的系统）
words.ex: He found the book using the card catalogue.
words.ex_cn: 他通过卡片目录找到了这本书。
words.en: A card catalogue is a system for organizing information about the books and other materials in a library, consisting of cards with information on them that are arranged in a particular order.

words.ex: The new policy will ameliorate living conditions.
words.ex_cn: 新政策将改善生活条件。
words.en: To make something better or improve a situation.

words.tr: v. 使社会化；进行社交活动；与人交往
words.ex: The school helps children socialize with others.
words.ex_cn: 学校帮助孩子们与他人社会化。
words.en: If you socialize, you meet other people socially, for example at parties.

words.tr:
n. 腐肉；死肉
adj. 腐肉的；吃腐肉的
words.ex: The vulture eats carrion on the ground.
words.ex_cn: 秃鹫在地面上吃腐肉。
words.en: The dead and rotting flesh of an animal.

words.ex: The Magna Carta is an old charter of rights.
words.ex_cn: 《大宪章》是一份古老的权力宪章。
words.en: A charter is a formal document describing the rights, aims, or principles of an organization or group of people.

words.tr: n. 神话；神话学；神话集；
words.ex: He loves reading Greek mythology.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢读希腊神话。
words.en: Mythology is a collection of myths, especially one belonging to a particular religious or cultural tradition.

words.tr:
n. 理想主义者；唯心论者
adj. 唯心主义的
words.ex: He is an idealist who believes in world peace.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个相信世界和平的理想主义者。
words.en: An idealist is someone who believes that very good things can be achieved, often when this does not seem likely to others.

words.ex: The mistake was trivial and didn't affect the result.
words.ex_cn: 这个错误不重要，没有影响结果。
words.en: If you describe something as trivial, you mean that it is not important or significant, or is not worth serious consideration.

words.tr:
adv. 歪地；斜着
adj. 歪斜的
words.ex: The picture was hanging askew on the wall.
words.ex_cn: 那幅画在墙上挂歪了。
words.en: Not in a straight or level position.

words.ex: His words showed great acerbity.
words.ex_cn: 他的话表现出极大的尖刻。
words.en: Acerbity refers to a sharp bitterness or severity of temper or expression.

words.ex: His asinine remark made everyone laugh nervously.
words.ex_cn: 他那愚蠢的言论让所有人都尴尬地笑了。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as asinine, you mean that they are very foolish.

words.ex: His intellect helps him solve difficult problems.
words.ex_cn: 他的智力帮助他解决难题。
words.en: The ability to understand and think in a logical way about things.

words.ex: His conviction that honesty is important never changed.
words.ex_cn: 他坚信诚实很重要，从未改变。
words.en: A conviction is a strong belief or opinion, or the state of being found guilty of a crime in a court of law.

words.tr:
n. 折扣；
v. 不全信；不重视；
words.ex: The store gave a 20% discount on all shoes.
words.ex_cn: 商店对所有鞋子提供了20%的折扣。
words.en: A reduction in the usual price of something, or the act of reducing the price.

words.ex: He amass wealth by working hard.
words.ex_cn: 他通过努力工作积累财富。
words.en: If you amass something such as money or information, you gradually collect a large amount of it.

words.ex: He became the champion of the tennis tournament.
words.ex_cn: 他赢得了网球锦标赛的冠军。
words.en: A champion is someone who has won first prize in a competition, contest, or fight.

words.ex: His sudden win in the race was a real coup.
words.ex_cn: 他在比赛中突然获胜，真是了不起的成就。
words.en: A coup is a sudden, violent, and illegal seizure of power from a government.

words.tr:
n. 收费；负责；指控；
v. 收费；充电；
words.ex: The hotel charge is $50 per night.
words.ex_cn: 酒店的收费是每晚50美元。
words.en: If you charge someone, you ask them to pay an amount of money for something that you have sold to them or done for them.

words.ex: Smartphones are ubiquitous in modern life.
words.ex_cn: 智能手机在现代生活中无处不在。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as ubiquitous, you mean that they seem to be everywhere.

words.tr: v. 驱散；消散；浪费；挥霍
words.ex: The fog will dissipate by noon.
words.ex_cn: 雾将在中午前消散。
words.en: If something dissipates or is dissipated, it becomes less or becomes less strong until it disappears or goes away completely.

words.ex: He is averse to changing his routine.
words.ex_cn: 他反对改变自己的日常安排。
words.en: If you say that someone is averse to something, you mean they dislike it or have a strong opposition to it.

words.ex: He performed the ablution before entering the temple.
words.ex_cn: 他在进入寺庙前进行了沐浴。
words.en: The act of washing oneself, especially as a religious ritual.

words.tr: adj. 恶毒的；恶性的；恶意的
words.ex: His malignant words hurt everyone around him.
words.ex_cn: 他恶毒的话语伤害了周围的所有人。
words.en: If you say that someone is malignant, you mean they are very dangerous and cause harm to people.

words.tr:
adj. 极重要的；
n. 紧急的事；
words.ex: It is imperative to drink water every day.
words.ex_cn: 每天喝水非常重要。
words.en: If it is imperative that something is done, that thing is extremely important and must be done.

words.ex: The adverse weather delayed the flight.
words.ex_cn: 不利的天气延误了航班。
words.en: If something is adverse, it is harmful or unfavorable.

words.tr: v. 捐赠；订阅；订购；签署；认购（股份）
words.ex: He decided to subscribe $50 to the charity each month.
words.ex_cn: 他决定每月向慈善机构捐赠50美元。
words.en: If you subscribe to a magazine or a service, you pay to receive it regularly.

words.ex: Children develop cognitive skills as they grow.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在成长过程中发展认知能力。
words.en: Cognitive means relating to the mental process involved in knowing, learning, and understanding things.

words.ex: The storm disrupted the train service.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴中断了火车服务。
words.en: To disrupt a system, process, or event means to prevent it from continuing or operating in a normal way.

words.ex: I saw an advert on TV for new shoes.
words.ex_cn: 我在电视上看到一双新鞋的广告。
words.en: An advert is a notice or announcement in a public medium promoting a product, service, or event.

words.ex: The limitation of the phone is its short battery life.
words.ex_cn: 这款手机的限制是电池续航时间短。
words.en: A limitation is a rule or situation that restricts what you can do or what can happen.

words.ex: The movie ended with suspense, and no one knew what happened next.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影以悬念结束，没人知道接下来发生了什么。
words.en: Suspense is a state of excitement or anxiety about something that is going to happen very soon, especially something that could be either good or bad.

words.tr: adj. 断断续续的；间歇的
words.ex: The rain is intermittent today.
words.ex_cn: 今天雨断断续续地下。
words.en: Something that is intermittent happens occasionally rather than continuously.

words.ex: He made a gesture of welcome with his hands.
words.ex_cn: 他用手做了一个欢迎的姿态。
words.en: A gesture is a movement that you make with a part of your body, especially your hands, to express emotion or information.

words.ex: His avocation is painting on weekends.
words.ex_cn: 他的业余爱好是周末画画。
words.en: An avocation is an activity that you do because you are interested in it, rather than as your main job.

words.tr:
adj. 退步的；堕落的；腐化的
v. 退化；堕落
n. 堕落的人
words.ex: The old machine became degenerate and stopped working.
words.ex_cn: 这台旧机器退步了，停止工作了。
words.en: If you say that someone or something degenerates, you mean that they become worse in some way, for example, poorer, weaker, or less respectable.

words.ex: The theorist wrote a simple book about stars.
words.ex_cn: 这位理论家写了一本关于恒星的简单书籍。
words.en: A theorist is someone who develops or studies theories, especially in science or philosophy.

words.ex: He is culpable for the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他对这起事故负有责任。
words.en: If someone is culpable, they are responsible for something wrong or bad that has happened.

words.ex: He handed me a pamphlet about the new park.
words.ex_cn: 他递给我一份关于新公园的小册子。
words.en: A pamphlet is a small book containing information on a particular subject or expressing political or religious views.

words.tr: adj. 现代的；当代的；同时代的；
words.ex: This museum displays contemporary art.
words.ex_cn: 这个博物馆展示现代艺术。
words.en: Belonging to or occurring in the present; or a person or thing living or existing at the same time as another.

words.tr: adj. 未成熟的；无处世经验的；乳臭未干的
words.ex: The new recruits were callow and inexperienced.
words.ex_cn: 新兵们年轻而无经验。
words.en: If you describe someone as callow, you mean that they are inexperienced and immature.

words.ex: Don't jeopardize your health by skipping meals.
words.ex_cn: 不要因为不吃饭而危及你的健康。
words.en: To jeopardize something means to do something that may destroy it or cause it to be lost.

words.tr: adj. 大胆的；鲁莽的；大胆创新的
words.ex: He made an audacious plan to climb the mountain alone.
words.ex_cn: 他制定了一个大胆的计划，独自攀登那座山。
words.en: If you describe someone as audacious, you mean that they take risks in order to achieve something and show a willingness to challenge conventional ideas.

words.ex: The treaty established amity between the two nations.
words.ex_cn: 该条约确立了两国之间的友好关系。
words.en: A friendly relationship between people or countries.

words.ex: He wore a coat made of badger.
words.ex_cn: 他穿了一件用獾皮毛制成的外套。
words.en: To badger someone means to repeatedly ask them to do something or to repeatedly question them about something, often in an annoying way.

words.tr: adj. 热烈的；强烈的；热情的
words.ex: He is a fervent supporter of environmental protection.
words.ex_cn: 他是环境保护的热心支持者。
words.en: having or showing very strong and sincere feelings about something

words.ex: He accumulates coins from different countries.
words.ex_cn: 他收集来自不同国家的硬币。
words.en: To accumulate means to gradually gather or acquire an increasing number or quantity of something.

words.ex: He is learning alchemy from an old book.
words.ex_cn: 他正从一本旧书中学习炼金术。
words.en: Alchemy is an ancient practice that aimed to transform base metals into gold and to discover a universal cure for disease and a way of extending life.

words.tr: n. 仔细研究；详细检查；
words.ex: The teacher examined the student's work under close scrutiny.
words.ex_cn: 老师对学生的作业进行了仔细研究。
words.en: If someone or something is under scrutiny, they are being studied or observed very carefully.

words.ex: The two parties formed a coalition to win the election.
words.ex_cn: 这两个政党联合起来以赢得选举。
words.en: A coalition is a temporary alliance for combined action, especially of political parties forming a government.

words.ex: The transition from school to work was hard for him.
words.ex_cn: 从学校到工作的转变对他来说很难。
words.en: The process or a period of changing from one state or condition to another.

words.ex: Legends say that some heroes are immortal.
words.ex_cn: 传说有些英雄是不死的。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as immortal, you mean that they are so famous or popular that they will be remembered for a very long time.

words.tr:
n. 杂乱；混乱
v. 弄乱
words.ex: The table is full of clutter.
words.ex_cn: 桌子上堆满了杂物。
words.en: If things or people clutter a place, they fill it in an untidy way.

words.ex: The loud music was a diversion from his worries.
words.ex_cn: 那嘈杂的音乐分散了他对烦恼的注意力。
words.en: A diversion is an action or event that attracts your attention away from what you are doing or should be doing.

words.ex: He bought a luxury car as an extravagance.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一辆豪华汽车作为奢侈品。
words.en: Extravagance refers to the spending of more money than is reasonable or than you can afford, or the use of more of something than is necessary.

words.tr: adj. 吵闹的；喧哗的；吵吵嚷嚷的
words.ex: The clamorous crowd cheered loudly for the winner.
words.ex_cn: 喧闹的人群为获胜者大声欢呼。
words.en: If you describe people or their voices as clamorous, you mean they are talking loudly or shouting.

words.tr: adj. 自满的；自鸣得意的
words.ex: He is complacent about his good grades.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的好成绩感到自满。
words.en: A complacent person is very pleased with themselves or feels that they do not need to do anything about a situation, even though the situation may be uncertain or dangerous.

words.ex: The suspect was arraigned in court yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 嫌疑人昨天在法庭上被传讯。
words.en: If someone is arraigned, they are brought to court and formally charged with a crime.

words.tr: adj. 像人类的（动物）；像猿猴的（人）
words.ex: The monkey is an anthropoid.
words.ex_cn: 这只猴子是一种类人猿。
words.en: Resembling a human being in form.

words.ex: He faced a dilemma: stay home or go to work.
words.ex_cn: 他面临一个困境：是待在家里还是去上班。
words.en: A situation in which a difficult choice has to be made between two or more alternatives, especially equally undesirable ones.

words.tr: adj. 天生的；先天的；天赋的
words.ex: He has an inborn talent for music.
words.ex_cn: 他天生就有音乐才能。
words.en: An inborn quality or ability is one that you have had naturally since birth.

words.ex: The beneficent man gave food to the poor.
words.ex_cn: 这位仁慈的人给穷人提供了食物。
words.en: A beneficent person or organization helps people or results in something good.

words.ex: The advent of smartphones changed how we communicate.
words.ex_cn: 智能手机的到来改变了我们的交流方式。
words.en: The arrival of a notable person, thing, or event.

words.tr: v. 区分；“distinguish”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 卓越的；著名的；
words.ex: He distinguished the fake coin from the real one.
words.ex_cn: 他把假硬币和真硬币区分开来。
words.en: If you describe a person or their work as distinguished, you mean that they have been very successful in their career and have a good reputation.

words.tr: n. 被排斥者；被抛弃者；
words.ex: He became an outcast after speaking the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他因为说出真相而被排斥。
words.en: An outcast is someone who is not accepted by a group of people or by society.

words.tr:
adj. 热诚的；友好的
n. 甜露酒
words.ex: He gave a cordial smile to his neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他对着邻居露出了热情的微笑。
words.en: warm and friendly

words.tr:
n. 大洪水；暴雨；泛滥
v. 泛滥；大量涌入
words.ex: The rain caused a deluge in the town.
words.ex_cn: 这场雨在镇上引发了洪水。
words.en: A deluge is a severe flood or a very heavy fall of rain that causes a lot of damage.

words.ex: The child mimics her mother's voice.
words.ex_cn: 孩子模仿她妈妈的声音。
words.en: If someone or something mimics another person or thing, they try to be like them or copy their behavior or characteristics.

words.ex: He bought a generic brand of painkiller.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一种普通的止痛药品牌。
words.en: Generic refers to something that is not specific or unique, often used to describe products that are not branded or are general in nature.

words.tr:
adj. 有杂色的；斑驳的
v. 使成杂色，使有斑点；“mottle”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The mottled skin of the frog helps it hide in the leaves.
words.ex_cn: 青蛙斑驳的皮肤帮助它藏在树叶中。
words.en: Something that is mottled has spots or patches of different colors.

words.ex: He wakes up at six every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上六点醒来。
words.en: To wake means to stop sleeping or to cause someone to stop sleeping. It can also refer to the trail left by a moving ship.

words.ex: He showed his passport at the airport.
words.ex_cn: 他在机场出示了他的护照。
words.en: A passport is an official document that identifies you as a citizen of a particular country and gives you the right to travel to and from that country.

words.tr:
v. 调情；轻率地对待
n. 与多人调情的人
words.ex: He flirts with her at the coffee shop.
words.ex_cn: 他在咖啡店向她调情。
words.en: If you flirt with someone, you behave as if you are sexually attracted to them, in a playful or not very serious way.

words.tr: adj. 矫揉造作的；不自然的；守规矩的；彬彬有礼的
words.ex: Her mannered speech was hard to understand.
words.ex_cn: 她矫揉造作的言辞让人难以理解。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior or a work of art as mannered, you dislike it because it is elaborate or formal, and therefore seems false or artificial.

words.ex: The ape climbed slowly up the tree.
words.ex_cn: 这只猿慢慢爬上了树。
words.en: An ape is a large primate that does not have a tail, for example a chimpanzee or gorilla.

words.ex: The children stood in awe at the sight of the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们看到山时感到敬畏。
words.en: A feeling of reverential respect mixed with fear or wonder.

words.ex: He is conversant with basic math.
words.ex_cn: 他熟悉基础数学。
words.en: If you are conversant with something, you are familiar with it and able to deal with it.

words.ex: He has a disinclination to speak in public.
words.ex_cn: 他不愿意在公众场合讲话。
words.en: A disinclination to do something is a feeling of not wanting to do it.

words.tr:
n. 疑虑；怀疑
v. 使疑虑；使担忧；“misgive”的现在分词
words.ex: He had a misgiving about the plan.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个计划感到不安。
words.en: A misgiving is a feeling of doubt or anxiety about something that might happen or might have happened.

words.ex: He persevered despite many failures.
words.ex_cn: 尽管多次失败，他仍然坚持不懈。
words.en: If you persevere with something, you keep trying to do it and do not give up, even though it is difficult.

words.tr: n. 不赞成；持反对意见；非难
words.ex: He felt disapprobation when he saw the messy room.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到凌乱的房间时，他感到不满。
words.en: Disapprobation is a strong feeling of disapproval or condemnation.

words.ex: The lake offers tranquillity after a long day.
words.ex_cn: 湖水在漫长的一天后带来宁静。
words.en: Tranquillity refers to a state of peace and quiet.

words.ex: His defection shocked the whole team.
words.ex_cn: 他的叛逃让整个团队震惊。
words.en: The act of abandoning a cause, party, or nation, especially in favor of an opposing one.

words.tr:
adj. 偏僻的；离群的；孤独的；内向的
v. 撤回；撤退；“withdraw”的过去分词
words.ex: The cabin is in a withdrawn area, far from the town.
words.ex_cn: 小木屋位于一个偏僻的地方，远离城镇。
words.en: If someone is withdrawn, they are very quiet, and do not want to talk to other people. If something is withdrawn, it is taken back or removed.

words.ex: The birds flew through the aerial sky.
words.ex_cn: 鸟儿在空中飞翔。
words.en: An aerial is a wire or rod that sends or receives radio or television signals. As an adjective, aerial describes things that are in the air or related to the air.

words.ex: The teacher underscored the importance of homework.
words.ex_cn: 老师强调了作业的重要性。
words.en: To emphasize the importance of something or to draw a line underneath a word or phrase.

words.tr: adj. 不容置疑的；无可否认的
words.ex: The evidence is incontrovertible.
words.ex_cn: 证据是无可辩驳的。
words.en: If something is incontrovertible, it is definitely true and cannot be disputed.

words.tr:
v. 牺牲；
n. 牺牲（品）；
words.ex: He sacrificed his time to help his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他牺牲了自己的时间来帮助朋友。
words.en: If you sacrifice something that is valuable or important, you give it up, usually to obtain something else for yourself or for other people.

words.tr:
adj. 交战的；寻衅的；好战的
n. 交战国；交战团体
words.ex: The two belligerent nations signed a peace treaty.
words.ex_cn: 这两个交战国家签署了和平条约。
words.en: A belligerent person or country is aggressive and eager to fight.

words.ex: He will initiate a new project next week.
words.ex_cn: 他将在下周发起一个新项目。
words.en: To initiate something means to start it or cause it to happen.

words.ex: The report gives an exhaustive list of all the rules.
words.ex_cn: 这份报告给出了所有规则的详尽列表。
words.en: If you describe a study, search, or list as exhaustive, you mean that it is very thorough and complete.

words.ex: He spoke with candor about his mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他坦率地谈到了自己的错误。
words.en: the quality of being open and honest in expression; frankness.

words.ex: Wear a helmet to counteract the risk of head injury.
words.ex_cn: 戴头盔以对抗头部受伤的风险。
words.en: If you counteract something, you reduce its effect by doing something that produces an opposite effect.

words.ex: He can foretell the weather by looking at the sky.
words.ex_cn: 他可以通过观察天空来预知天气。
words.en: To tell or indicate beforehand; predict.

words.ex: He fractured his arm during the soccer game.
words.ex_cn: 他在足球比赛中摔断了手臂。
words.en: If something such as a bone fractures or is fractured, it breaks or cracks.

words.ex: The camel walks across the desert.
words.ex_cn: 骆驼穿越沙漠。
words.en: A desert is a large area of land that has very little water and very few plants growing on it. Many deserts are covered by sand. If you desert someone or something, you leave them and no longer help or support them.

words.ex: He made an abrupt stop at the red light.
words.ex_cn: 他在红灯前突然停了下来。
words.en: If something happens abruptly, it happens suddenly and unexpectedly.

words.tr:
n. 试验；化验；定量分析
v. 试验；化验；定量分析
words.ex: The lab will assay the blood sample tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 实验室明天将检测这个血液样本。
words.en: An assay is a test to determine the presence, absence, or quantity of one or more components.

words.tr: v. 导航；应付（复杂情况）；
words.ex: He uses a map to navigate the city.
words.ex_cn: 他用地图来导航这座城市。
words.en: To navigate is to plan and direct the route or course of a ship, aircraft, or other form of transport, especially by using instruments or maps.

words.ex: He is steadfast in his beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己信念坚定不移。
words.en: If someone is steadfast, they are very loyal and constant in their attitudes or actions.

words.ex: He said it with sarcasm, even though he seemed happy.
words.ex_cn: 他说这话时带着讽刺，尽管他看起来很高兴。
words.en: Sarcasm is a sharp, bitter, or cutting expression or remark; a bitter gibe or taunt.

words.ex: The cat shows great agility when jumping over the fence.
words.ex_cn: 这只猫跳过围栏时表现出极大的灵活性。
words.en: Agility is the ability to move quickly and easily.

words.tr: v. 使气馁；使胆怯；吓倒
words.ex: The loud noise did not daunt her.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音并没有吓倒她。
words.en: If something daunts you, it makes you feel slightly afraid or worried about dealing with it.

words.ex: The club has an affiliation with the university.
words.ex_cn: 这个俱乐部与大学有从属关系。
words.en: An affiliation is a close connection or association with a particular group, organization, or institution.

words.ex: The king decided to abdicate in favor of his son.
words.ex_cn: 国王决定退位，让位给他的儿子。
words.en: If a king or queen abdicates, he or she gives up being king or queen.

words.ex: The weather was congenial for a picnic.
words.ex_cn: 天气非常适合野餐。
words.en: A congenial person, place, or environment is pleasant because it suits your character or nature.

words.tr: n. 叛教者；脱党者；变节者
words.ex: He became an apostate after leaving the church.
words.ex_cn: 他离开教会后成了叛教者。
words.en: An apostate is someone who has abandoned their religious faith, political loyalties, or principles.

words.ex: The apex of the mountain is covered with snow.
words.ex_cn: 山的最高点被雪覆盖。
words.en: The highest point or top of something; the climax or culmination of something.

words.tr:
adj. 周期的；定期的
n. 期刊
words.ex: The plant has a periodical blooming cycle.
words.ex_cn: 这种植物有周期性的开花周期。
words.en: A periodical is a magazine, especially one that is published regularly, or something that happens at regular intervals.

words.ex: It's ironic that the fire station burned down.
words.ex_cn: 消防站着火了，这真是讽刺。
words.en: If you say that it is ironic that something happens, you mean that it is odd or amusing because it involves a contrast or is the opposite of what you would expect.

words.ex: The mediator helped the two sides reach an agreement.
words.ex_cn: 调解人帮助双方达成了协议。
words.en: A mediator is a person who tries to end a disagreement by helping the two sides to talk about and agree on a solution.

words.ex: He always follows social propriety.
words.ex_cn: 他总是遵守社交礼仪。
words.en: Propriety is the quality of being proper, suitable, or appropriate in behavior or conduct.

words.tr: v. 消灭；歼灭；彻底击败
words.ex: The bomb will annihilate the building.
words.ex_cn: 炸弹会摧毁那栋大楼。
words.en: To annihilate something means to destroy it completely.

words.ex: Doctors must follow medical ethics.
words.ex_cn: 医生必须遵守医学道德规范。
words.en: Ethics are moral beliefs and rules about right and wrong.

words.ex: I loathe waking up early.
words.ex_cn: 我讨厌早起。
words.en: If you loathe something or someone, you dislike them very much.

words.tr: n. 强迫；强制；难以抗拒的冲动
words.ex: He felt a compulsion to check the door again.
words.ex_cn: 他感到一种必须再次检查门的强迫感。
words.en: A compulsion is a very strong desire to do something, which you find difficult to control.

words.ex: The problem recurs every week.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题每周都会再次出现。
words.en: If something recurs, it happens again, either once or several times.

words.tr: adj. 品行端正的；品德高的；
words.ex: He is a virtuous man who always tells the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个品行端正的人，总是说真话。
words.en: Having or showing high moral standards.

words.ex: The cession of land was agreed upon by both countries.
words.ex_cn: 两国同意转让土地。
words.en: The act of ceding or giving up something, especially land or rights, to another party.

words.ex: He speculates that it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他推测明天会下雨。
words.en: If you speculate about something, you make guesses about its nature or identity, or about what might happen.

words.ex: The young manager is the successor to the CEO.
words.ex_cn: 这位年轻经理是首席执行官的接班人。
words.en: A successor is a person who takes a job or position previously held by someone else.

words.tr: adj. 多方面的；有多种技能的；
words.ex: He is a versatile player who can play many positions.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名多方面的运动员，能打多个位置。
words.en: Able to adapt or be adapted to many different functions or activities.

words.tr: adj.  忧郁的；阴沉的；阴暗的
words.ex: The room had a somber mood.
words.ex_cn: 房间里有一种阴郁的气氛。
words.en: If someone is somber, they are serious or sad.

words.ex: My generation grew up with smartphones.
words.ex_cn: 我们这一代人是伴随着智能手机长大的。
words.en: A generation is all the people in a group or country who are of a similar age, especially when they are considered as having the same experiences or attitudes.

words.ex: The jury gave a guilty verdict.
words.ex_cn: 陪审团作出了有罪裁决。
words.en: A verdict is a decision made after a lot of consideration, especially one made by a jury in a court of law.

words.tr: v. 痛击；痛斥；冗长地解释
words.ex: He belabored the point until everyone was bored.
words.ex_cn: 他反复讨论那个观点，直到大家都感到厌烦。
words.en: To argue or discuss (a subject) in excessive detail; to attack or criticize (someone) persistently.

words.ex: He acquired a new skill last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年获得了一项新技能。
words.en: If you acquire something, you buy or obtain it for yourself, or someone gives it to you.

words.ex: The train runs on the rail.
words.ex_cn: 火车在铁轨上行驶。
words.en: A rail is a horizontal bar, typically made of metal or wood, used as a support or barrier; or a track made of steel rails along which trains run.

words.ex: He abased himself before the king.
words.ex_cn: 他在国王面前贬低自己。
words.en: To abase someone or something means to lower them in rank, status, or esteem.

words.ex: The king proclaimed a new law.
words.ex_cn: 国王宣告了一项新法律。
words.en: If you proclaim something, you formally announce it or declare it publicly.

words.ex: This experiment is a paradigm of scientific method.
words.ex_cn: 这个实验是科学方法的范例。
words.en: A paradigm is a model or pattern that is considered to be a typical example of something.

words.ex: He kept his equanimity during the storm.
words.ex_cn: 他在风暴中保持了冷静。
words.en: If you face a difficult situation with equanimity, you remain calm and do not get upset or angry.

words.ex: Exercise can elevate your mood.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以提升你的情绪。
words.en: To elevate something means to raise it to a higher position or level, either physically or in terms of its status or importance.

words.ex: The smell repels insects.
words.ex_cn: 这种气味能击退昆虫。
words.en: If something repels you, it is so unpleasant or offensive that you want to avoid it or push it away.

words.ex: The plaintiff sued the company for damages.
words.ex_cn: 原告起诉该公司要求赔偿。
words.en: A plaintiff is a person who brings a case against another in a court of law.

words.ex: The autocrat rules the country with no elections.
words.ex_cn: 独裁者在没有选举的情况下统治国家。
words.en: An autocrat is a ruler who has absolute power.

words.tr: n. 设施；特色功能；特定场所；资质；
words.ex: The school has a new sports facility.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校有一个新的体育设施。
words.en: A facility is a place, building, or service that is designed for a particular purpose.

words.tr: v. 断言；宣称；坚持；维护
words.ex: He asserts that the answer is correct.
words.ex_cn: 他坚持认为答案是正确的。
words.en: To state a fact or belief confidently and forcefully.

words.tr: n. 骑士（爵士）资格（地位、身份）；骑士精神
words.ex: He received knighthood for his service to medicine.
words.ex_cn: 他因对医学的贡献而被授予骑士头衔。
words.en: The rank or title of a knight; the qualities befitting a knight, such as bravery, courtesy, honor, and gallantry toward women.

words.ex: The country has an agrarian economy.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家有一个农业经济。
words.en: Relating to land, especially agricultural land, or to the ownership or division of such land.

words.ex: The appellation 'Doctor' is used to address a person with a medical degree.
words.ex_cn: 称呼 'Doctor' 用于称呼拥有医学学位的人。
words.en: An appellation is a name or title that someone or something is known by.

words.ex: He postdated the check to next month.
words.ex_cn: 他把支票的日期写成下个月。
words.en: To write a date on a document that is later than the actual date.

words.ex: He showed apathy toward the news.
words.ex_cn: 他对这则新闻漠不关心。
words.en: Apathy is a lack of feeling, emotion, interest, or concern about something. It is a state of indifference, or the suppression of emotions such as concern, excitement, motivation, or passion.

words.ex: She took a glance at the clock.
words.ex_cn: 她瞥了一眼钟。
words.en: If you glance at something or someone, you look at them very quickly and then look away again immediately.

words.tr: adj. 色情的； 多情的； 爱情的
words.ex: The movie showed amorous scenes that shocked the audience.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影展示了让观众震惊的色情场景。
words.en: If you describe someone's feelings or actions as amorous, you mean that they involve sexual desire.

words.ex: His credo is to always tell the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他的信条是永远说真话。
words.en: A credo is a set of beliefs, principles, or opinions that strongly influence the way a person lives or works.

words.ex: It is feasible to finish the project in one week.
words.ex_cn: 一周内完成这个项目是可行的。
words.en: If something is feasible, it can be done, made, or achieved.

words.tr: adj. 敏锐的；急性的；严重的；
words.ex: He has an acute mind and solves problems quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他思维敏锐，能快速解决问题。
words.en: An acute problem or negative feeling is very severe.

words.ex: He saw a mirage in the desert.
words.ex_cn: 他在沙漠中看到了海市蜃楼。
words.en: An optical illusion caused by atmospheric conditions, especially the appearance of a sheet of water in a desert or on a hot road caused by the refraction of light from the sky by heated air.

words.tr: adj. 封建的；封建制度的
words.ex: The land was owned by feudal lords.
words.ex_cn: 土地由封建领主拥有。
words.en: Relating to, resembling, or characteristic of feudalism.

words.tr: n. 开始；毕业典礼；学位授予典礼
words.ex: The commencement of the class was at 9 a.m.
words.ex_cn: 课程的开始时间是上午9点。
words.en: The commencement of something is its beginning.

words.ex: The room has good acoustic properties.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间有良好的声音效果。
words.en: Relating to sound or the sense of hearing.

words.tr: v. 抢劫；掠夺；蹂躏；破坏
words.ex: The invaders despoiled the village.
words.ex_cn: 入侵者抢劫了村庄。
words.en: To despoil something means to steal from it or damage it, especially in a violent or destructive way.

words.ex: The intruder broke into the house at night.
words.ex_cn: 入侵者在晚上闯入了房子。
words.en: An intruder is a person who enters a place or situation where they are not wanted.

words.ex: The eerie silence made us feel scared.
words.ex_cn: 那怪异的寂静让我们感到害怕。
words.en: If you describe something as eerie, you mean that it seems strange and frightening, and makes you feel nervous.

words.tr:
n. 蠕动；扭动；蜿蜒
v. 蠕动；扭动；蜿蜒前进
words.ex: The worm made a small wriggle in the soil.
words.ex_cn: 这条蠕虫在泥土中蠕动了一下。
words.en: To move or cause to move with short, quick twisting or turning motions.

words.ex: The convergent series gets closer to a final number.
words.ex_cn: 这个会聚级数逐渐接近一个最终数值。
words.en: Convergent refers to the process or state of coming together or moving toward union or uniformity, especially in the context of ideas, cultures, or scientific phenomena.

words.tr:
adj. 明白表示的；证实的；公然表示情绪的
n. 指示词
words.ex: He is demonstrative with his love for his family.
words.ex_cn: 他对家人表达爱意时很外露。
words.en: If you are demonstrative, you show your feelings or behave in a way that shows your love for someone.

words.ex: The boundless sky made her feel free.
words.ex_cn: 无边无际的天空让她感到自由。
words.en: If you describe something as boundless, you mean that it has no limits or seems to be without limits.

words.tr: adj. 国内的；公民的；民用的；
words.ex: The country is recovering from a civil war.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家正在从一场内战中恢复。
words.en: relating to ordinary citizens and their concerns, as distinct from military or ecclesiastical matters.

words.tr: adj. 强制性的；义务的；必须的；
words.ex: Wearing a helmet is obligatory for cyclists.
words.ex_cn: 骑自行车时戴头盔是强制性的。
words.en: If something is obligatory, you must do it because of a rule or law.

words.ex: He enciphers his messages with a simple code.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个简单的密码加密他的信息。
words.en: To convert (a message or information) into a cipher or code.

words.ex: The dictionary gives a clear definition of the word.
words.ex_cn: 词典给出了这个词的清晰定义。
words.en: A statement of the exact meaning of a word, phrase, or concept.

words.tr: v. 买得起；担负得起；有时间做；
words.ex: I can't afford a new car.
words.ex_cn: 我买不起一辆新车。
words.en: If you cannot afford something, you do not have enough money to pay for it.

words.tr:
n. 媒介；方法；
adj. 中等的；适中的；
words.ex: TV is a popular medium for advertising.
words.ex_cn: 电视是一种流行的广告媒介。
words.en: A medium is a method or way of expressing something.

words.tr:
n. 混凝土；
adj. 具体的；
words.ex: The workers poured concrete to build the foundation.
words.ex_cn: 工人们浇筑混凝土来建造地基。
words.en: Concrete is a hard, strong construction material made by mixing a cementing material (such as Portland cement) and a mineral aggregate (such as sand and gravel) with sufficient water to cause the cement to set and bind the entire mass. In a broader sense, concrete can also refer to something that is tangible, specific, or real.

words.tr: n. 分离；拆开；支队；超然；分遣队
words.ex: The detachment of the two teams caused confusion.
words.ex_cn: 两个团队的分离造成了混乱。
words.en: If you refer to someone's detachment, you mean that they do not become involved in other people's problems or emotions, or that they do not show their own feelings.

words.tr: n. 精心制作；详尽的细节；
words.ex: The chef gave an elaboration to the dish with fresh herbs.
words.ex_cn: 厨师用新鲜香草对这道菜进行了精心制作。
words.en: The process of developing or presenting a theory, policy, or system in detail.

words.ex: He made a generalization from the data.
words.ex_cn: 他从数据中做出了一个概括。
words.en: A generalization is a statement that seems to be true in most situations or for most people, but that may not be completely true in all cases.

words.tr: v. 反映；反射；反省；思考；仔细考虑；
words.ex: The mirror reflects the sunlight.
words.ex_cn: 镜子反射阳光。
words.en: If a surface reflects light, heat, sound, or an image, it sends the light, etc. back and does not absorb it. If something is reflected in a mirror or in water, you can see its image in the mirror or in the water.

words.tr:
v. 稀释
adj. 经稀释的
words.ex: He dilutes the juice with water.
words.ex_cn: 他用水稀释果汁。
words.en: To dilute a liquid means to make it thinner or weaker by adding water or another liquid to it.

words.tr: adj. 不可宽恕的；无法原谅的
words.ex: It is inexcusable to lie to your teacher.
words.ex_cn: 对老师撒谎是不可原谅的。
words.en: If you say that something is inexcusable, you are emphasizing that it cannot be justified or tolerated because it is extremely bad.

words.tr: adj. （言行）谨慎的；不显眼的；朴素的
words.ex: He was discreet about his personal life.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的私生活很低调。
words.en: If you are discreet, you are polite and careful in what you do or say, because you want to avoid embarrassing or offending someone.

words.tr: adj. 特定的；明确的；具体的；
words.ex: He gave a specific reason for being late.
words.ex_cn: 他给出了一个迟到的具体原因。
words.en: If someone is specific, they give a description that is precise and exact.

words.ex: The butterfly is symmetrical.
words.ex_cn: 这只蝴蝶是对称的。
words.en: Something that is symmetrical has parts that are equal in size, shape, and position, and that are arranged in a balanced way.

words.tr: adj. 居高临下的v. 屈尊；俯就；表现出优越感；“condescend”的现在分词
words.ex: He gave a condescending smile when she asked a simple question.
words.ex_cn: 当她问了一个简单的问题时，他露出了一副屈尊俯就的微笑。
words.en: If you say that someone is condescending, you are showing your disapproval of the fact that they talk or behave in a way which shows that they think they are superior to other people.

words.ex: The regularity of his daily routine helps him stay focused.
words.ex_cn: 他日常作息的规律性帮助他保持专注。
words.en: The quality or state of being regular; the condition of being governed by or according to rules, principles, or established customs.

words.ex: He tries to assimilate new words every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天努力吸收新单词。
words.en: To assimilate means to take in and understand fully ideas, information, or culture, or to make something become part of a group or system.

words.tr: adj. 无计谋的；得过且过的；无能的
words.ex: He was lazy and shiftless, never willing to put in the effort.
words.ex_cn: 他很懒惰且无能，从不愿付出努力。
words.en: If you describe someone as shiftless, you mean that they are lazy and have no intention of working hard or improving their life.

words.ex: The smoke began to stifle her breathing.
words.ex_cn: 烟雾开始让她窒息。
words.en: To stifle something means to prevent it from happening, continuing, or developing.

words.ex: He wrote a script for a short movie.
words.ex_cn: 他为一部短片写了剧本。
words.en: A script is the written form of a play, film, or broadcast. It includes the dialogue and stage directions.

words.ex: Please vacate the room by noon.
words.ex_cn: 请在中午前腾出房间。
words.en: To vacate a place or position means to leave it or give it up, making it available for other people.

words.ex: The public condemned the corrupt politician.
words.ex_cn: 公众谴责了这位腐败的政客。
words.en: If you condemn something, you say that it is very bad and unacceptable.

words.ex: The story is an allegory about kindness.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事是一个关于善良的寓言。
words.en: An allegory is a story, poem, or picture which can be interpreted to reveal a hidden meaning, typically a moral or political one.

words.ex: The court followed the precedent set in 1995.
words.ex_cn: 法院遵循了1995年确立的先例。
words.en: A precedent is an action or decision that is used as an example when someone wants to do a similar thing in the future.

words.tr: adj. 认识的；知晓的；察知的
words.ex: He is cognizant of the rules.
words.ex_cn: 他了解这些规则。
words.en: If someone is cognizant of something, they are aware of it or understand it.

words.ex: He spoke in a hoarse voice after shouting all day.
words.ex_cn: 他喊了一整天后，声音变得沙哑。
words.en: If your voice is hoarse or if you are hoarse, your voice sounds rough and unclear, for example because your throat is sore.

words.tr:
v. 逝去；过去
n. （光阴）逝去
words.ex: Two hours elapsed while he waited for the bus.
words.ex_cn: 他等公交车时，两个小时过去了。
words.en: If time elapses, it passes.

words.tr: adj. 狡猾的；诡计多端的
words.ex: The wily fox tricked the chicken.
words.ex_cn: 狡猾的狐狸骗了鸡。
words.en: If you describe someone or their behaviour as wily, you mean that they are clever at achieving what they want, especially by tricking people.

words.ex: The barren land cannot grow any crops.
words.ex_cn: 这片贫瘠的土地无法种植任何庄稼。
words.en: If you describe something as barren, you mean that it is not able to produce anything, especially plants or crops.

words.ex: They discriminate against people because of their race.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为种族而歧视他人。
words.en: To discriminate means to recognize a distinction; differentiate. It can also mean to make an unjust or prejudicial distinction in the treatment of different categories of people, especially on the grounds of race, sex, or age.

words.ex: He lost his job because of his integrity.
words.ex_cn: 他因为正直而失去了工作。
words.en: Integrity is the quality of being honest and having strong moral principles.

words.ex: This store is convenient for buying groceries.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店买杂货很方便。
words.en: If something is convenient, it is easy to use or do, or it is useful and suitable for a particular purpose.

words.ex: He was arrested as an accomplice to the robbery.
words.ex_cn: 他因作为抢劫的帮凶而被逮捕。
words.en: An accomplice is someone who helps another person to commit a crime.

words.ex: He handed in his resignation last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周递交了辞职信。
words.en: The act of giving up a job or position in a formal or official way; also refers to the acceptance of something undesirable but inevitable.

words.tr: adj. 使疲倦的；令人厌烦的；乏味的
words.ex: The wearisome task of filling out forms took hours.
words.ex_cn: 填写表格这项乏味的任务花了好几个小时。
words.en: If you describe something as wearisome, you mean that it is very tiring and boring or frustrating.

words.tr: v. 骚扰；烦扰；屡次侵扰
words.ex: He harasses his coworkers with loud jokes.
words.ex_cn: 他用大声的笑话骚扰他的同事。
words.en: If someone harasses you, they trouble or annoy you, for example by attacking you repeatedly or by causing you as many problems as they can.

words.tr: adj. 殷勤的；顺从的；讨好的
words.ex: He was overly complaisant to his boss, always agreeing with everything he said.
words.ex_cn: 他对老板过于顺从，总是同意他说的每一件事。
words.en: Willing to please others; obliging; agreeable.

words.ex: The injury impaired his ability to walk.
words.ex_cn: 这次受伤损害了他走路的能力。
words.en: If something impairs something such as an ability or the way something works, it damages it or makes it worse.

words.ex: He feels weak because he has anemia.
words.ex_cn: 他感到虚弱，因为他患有贫血。
words.en: A condition in which there is a deficiency of red cells or of haemoglobin in the blood, resulting in pallor and weariness.

words.tr: v. 蒸馏；用蒸馏法提取；蒸馏出；提炼
words.ex: They distill water to remove impurities.
words.ex_cn: 他们通过蒸馏去除水中的杂质。
words.en: To distill a liquid means to purify it by heating it until it becomes a gas and then cooling it so that it becomes a liquid again. This process can also be used to extract the essential elements or meanings from something.

words.tr: adj. 漂亮的；迷人的；讨人喜欢的
words.ex: The winsome girl smiled at everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个可爱的女孩对每个人微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as winsome, you mean that they are attractive and charming.

words.tr: n. 露天历史剧；盛装游行（或庆典）；选美比赛
words.ex: The town held a pageant to show the history of the old kingdom.
words.ex_cn: 这个小镇举办了一场露天历史剧，以展示古老王国的历史。
words.en: A pageant is a public entertainment consisting of a procession of people in elaborate, colorful costumes, or an outdoor performance of a historical scene.

words.ex: Her motto is 'Never give up.'
words.ex_cn: 她的座右铭是‘永不放弃’。
words.en: A motto is a short sentence or phrase that expresses a rule for sensible behavior, especially a way of behaving in a particular situation.

words.ex: The earthquake devastated the small town.
words.ex_cn: 地震摧毁了这个小镇。
words.en: To devastate means to destroy or ruin something completely, or to cause someone to feel extreme sadness or shock.

words.ex: The argument started small but soon escalate.
words.ex_cn: 争论起初很小，但很快逐步升高。
words.en: If a bad situation escalates or if someone or something escalates it, it becomes greater in size, seriousness, or intensity.

words.ex: He abbreviates the word 'example' as 'ex.'.
words.ex_cn: 他把单词 'example' 缩写为 'ex.'。
words.en: To abbreviate something means to make it shorter, especially by using a particular word or phrase to represent it.

words.tr: adj. 可渗透的；可渗入的；
words.ex: The soil is permeable, so water passes through easily.
words.ex_cn: 这种土壤是可渗透的，所以水很容易通过。
words.en: If a substance is permeable, it allows liquids or gases to pass through it.

words.ex: The diamond has many smooth facets.
words.ex_cn: 这颗钻石有许多光滑的小平面。
words.en: A particular aspect or feature of something.

words.ex: The cerebral cortex controls thinking and memory.
words.ex_cn: 大脑皮层控制思考和记忆。
words.en: Relating to the brain or the intellect.

words.ex: I bought a souvenir from the beach.
words.ex_cn: 我从海边买了一个纪念品。
words.en: A souvenir is something which you buy or keep to remind you of a holiday, place, or event.

words.ex: The company wants to innovate its production process.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司想改革它的生产流程。
words.en: To innovate means to introduce changes and new ideas in the way something is done or made.

words.ex: The new policy is for the promotion of clean energy.
words.ex_cn: 这项新政策是为了促进清洁能源。
words.en: A promotion is a move to a more important job or rank in a company or organization.

words.ex: He is a zealot for environmental protection.
words.ex_cn: 他是环境保护的热心者。
words.en: A zealot is someone who is extremely enthusiastic about something, especially religion or politics.

words.ex: The price of oil fluctuates every day.
words.ex_cn: 油价每天都在波动。
words.en: To fluctuate means to change or vary frequently and unpredictably.

words.ex: The smell was disagreeable.
words.ex_cn: 这气味令人不愉快。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as disagreeable, you mean that they are rather unpleasant.

words.tr:
v. 策划
n. 决策者；出谋划策者
words.ex: He is the mastermind behind the plan.
words.ex_cn: 他是这个计划的幕后主谋。
words.en: A mastermind is someone who plans and directs a complex and often devious scheme or enterprise.

words.ex: The teacher admonished the student to finish his homework.
words.ex_cn: 老师劝告学生完成作业。
words.en: To admonish someone means to tell them in a serious way that they have done something wrong.

words.tr: v. 奉为神圣；贡献；奉献
words.ex: They consecrate the church with prayer and song.
words.ex_cn: 他们用祈祷和歌声将教堂奉为神圣。
words.en: To consecrate something means to officially declare it to be holy and to be used for religious purposes.

words.ex: He received an accolade for his excellent work.
words.ex_cn: 他因出色的工作而获得了一项荣誉。
words.en: An accolade is something done or given to someone as a special honor or as a sign of approval.

words.ex: The school values diversity in its students.
words.ex_cn: 学校重视学生的多样性。
words.en: The state of being diverse; variety.

words.tr:
adj. 要求严格的；要求小心仔细的；苛求的
v. 强求；急需；要求；“exact”的现在分词
words.ex: He is an exacting teacher who wants perfect work.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个要求严格的老师，要求完美无缺的作业。
words.en: requiring a lot of effort, care, or attention

words.ex: She had a premonition that something bad was going to happen.
words.ex_cn: 她有一种不祥的预感，觉得会有坏事发生。
words.en: A premonition is a feeling that something, especially something unpleasant, is going to happen.

words.ex: The anthropologist studies ancient tribes.
words.ex_cn: 这位人类学家研究古代部落。
words.en: An anthropologist is a person who studies anthropology, which is the study of human societies and cultures and their development.

words.tr: n. 假定；推定；冒昧；放肆
words.ex: His presumption that he would win surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他以为自己会赢的这种假设让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: A presumption is something that is thought to be true because it is likely, although there is no proof.

words.ex: He adheres to his principles even when it's hard.
words.ex_cn: 即使很难，他仍然坚持自己的原则。
words.en: If you adhere to a rule or agreement, you act in the way that it says you should.

words.ex: The painter portrays a happy family in the photo.
words.ex_cn: 这位画家在画中描绘了一个幸福的家庭。
words.en: To portray someone or something means to show or represent them in a painting, film, book, or other artistic work.

words.tr: adj. 立法的；制定法律的；
words.ex: The legislative branch makes laws.
words.ex_cn: 立法部门制定法律。
words.en: Relating to the making of laws.

words.ex: He adduce evidence to prove his point.
words.ex_cn: 他提出证据来证明自己的观点。
words.en: To cite as evidence or proof; to bring forward in argument or as proof.

words.ex: They believed there was a conspiracy to hide the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他们相信有人密谋隐瞒真相。
words.en: A conspiracy is a secret plan by a group of people to do something harmful or illegal.

words.tr:
v. 闪烁；隐约闪现
n. 亮光；闪光
words.ex: The sun gleams on the water.
words.ex_cn: 阳光照在水面上，闪闪发亮。
words.en: A gleam is a small, bright light, especially one that shines for a short time.

words.ex: Align your goals with your actions.
words.ex_cn: 让你的目标与行动保持一致。
words.en: To arrange something in a straight line or in the correct position in relation to something else, usually so that it is parallel to it.

words.ex: He is a novice at playing the guitar.
words.ex_cn: 他是个吉他新手。
words.en: A novice is someone who has just started learning or doing something and does not have much experience.

words.ex: He felt ecstasy after winning the prize.
words.ex_cn: 他赢得奖品后感到无比喜悦。
words.en: Ecstasy is a feeling of very great happiness.

words.tr:
v. 吹拂；（随风）飘荡；使飘荡
n. 一股（在空气中飘荡的味或烟）；风信旗；飘荡
words.ex: The smell of bread wafted from the kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 面包的香味从厨房里飘来。
words.en: If sounds or smells waft through the air, or if something such as a light wind wafts them, they move gently through the air.

words.ex: He turned his head to avert the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他转过头去避免了事故。
words.en: If you avert something unpleasant, you prevent it from happening.

words.ex: He went berserk when he saw the mess in his room.
words.ex_cn: 他看到房间里的混乱时，气得发疯。
words.en: If someone goes berserk, they lose control of themselves and become very angry or violent.

words.ex: The old house has a colonial style.
words.ex_cn: 这所老房子具有殖民地风格。
words.en: Colonial means relating to a system or period of colonization, or to the people who live in a colony.

words.ex: The dark clouds bode a storm.
words.ex_cn: 乌云预示着一场风暴。
words.en: If something bodes ill, it makes you think that something bad will happen in the future. If something bodes well, it makes you think that something good will happen.

words.tr: adj. 仆人的；枯燥的；琐碎的
words.ex: He did menial work to earn money.
words.ex_cn: 他做琐碎的工作来赚钱。
words.en: A menial task is one that is considered to be lowly or degrading, often involving physical work and requiring little skill or education.

words.ex: He has a knack for fixing bikes.
words.ex_cn: 他有修自行车的技巧。
words.en: A knack is a special skill or ability that someone has, especially one that is hard to explain or teach.

words.ex: The weather was dire, with heavy rain and strong winds.
words.ex_cn: 天气非常可怕，下着大雨，刮着大风。
words.en: If you describe a situation as dire, you are emphasizing that it is very bad or serious.

words.tr: n. 挽歌；哀歌；忧伤的歌
words.ex: They sang a slow dirge at the funeral.
words.ex_cn: 他们在葬礼上唱了一首缓慢的哀歌。
words.en: A dirge is a slow, sad song or piece of music, sometimes played at a funeral.

words.tr: adj. 保险统计师的；保险精算的
words.ex: He is learning actuarial science to work in insurance.
words.ex_cn: 他正在学习精算科学，以便从事保险工作。
words.en: Actuarial work involves the use of statistical methods to assess risk in insurance and finance industries.

words.ex: The sun can dehydrate your skin quickly.
words.ex_cn: 太阳会很快使你的皮肤脱水。
words.en: To dehydrate something means to remove all the water from it, often in order to preserve it. If you dehydrate, you lose too much water from your body, usually because of illness or extreme heat.

words.ex: He was mortified when he forgot his lines on stage.
words.ex_cn: 当他忘记舞台上的台词时，他感到非常羞愧。
words.en: To mortify someone means to cause them to feel very embarrassed or ashamed. To mortify a part of your body means to discipline it by denying it things that it wants or needs.

words.ex: He was jailed for embezzlement from his company.
words.ex_cn: 他因盗用公司公款而入狱。
words.en: Embezzlement is the act of dishonestly taking or using money that belongs to someone else, especially when it is in your care or belongs to the organization you work for.

words.ex: The secession of the southern states led to the Civil War.
words.ex_cn: 南方各州的脱离导致了内战。
words.en: The action of withdrawing formally from membership of a federation or body, especially a political state.

words.ex: He used a match to ignite the fire.
words.ex_cn: 他用火柴点燃了火。
words.en: If you ignite something or if it ignites, it starts burning or explodes.

words.ex: He showed restraint when he stayed calm during the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他在争论中保持冷静，表现出了克制。
words.en: Restraint is a measure or condition that keeps someone or something under control or within limits.

words.tr: adj. 拉紧的；绷紧的；紧张的
words.ex: The sail was taut in the strong wind.
words.ex_cn: 帆在强风中绷得紧紧的。
words.en: If something such as a rope or wire is taut, it is stretched very tight. If muscles or parts of the body are taut, they are stretched tight, often because of physical effort or anxiety.

words.tr:
n. 灾难；祸患；鞭子
v. 鞭打；折磨；使受苦难
words.ex: Pollution is a scourge on the environment.
words.ex_cn: 污染是对环境的祸害。
words.en: A scourge is something that causes a lot of trouble or suffering, or a whip used as an instrument of punishment.

words.ex: The river water looked murky after the rain.
words.ex_cn: 雨后，河水看起来污浊。
words.en: If you describe something as murky, you mean that the details of it are not clear or that it is difficult to understand.

words.ex: The mechanic tightened the bolt with a wrench.
words.ex_cn: 机械师用扳手拧紧了螺栓。
words.en: A bolt is a type of fastener consisting of a threaded pin or rod with a head at one end, designed to be inserted through holes in assembled parts and tightened by a nut from the other end. It can also refer to a sudden dash or run, or to eat food quickly and without chewing.

words.tr:
n. 彻底检修；大修；彻底革新；全面修订
v. 彻底检修；超过（赛跑对手）
words.ex: The plane needs an overhaul before the next flight.
words.ex_cn: 这架飞机在下次飞行前需要彻底检修。
words.en: If you overhaul a system or method, you examine it carefully and make many changes in it in order to improve it.

words.tr: adj. 享有声望的；声望很高的；
words.ex: He got into a prestigious university.
words.ex_cn: 他进入了一所享有声望的大学。
words.en: A prestigious institution, job, or activity is respected and admired because it is considered to be of very high quality.

words.ex: The relentless rain flooded the streets.
words.ex_cn: 无情的雨水淹没了街道。
words.en: Someone who is relentless is determined to do something and refuses to give up, even if what they are doing is unpleasant or cruel.

words.ex: He will delete the old file.
words.ex_cn: 他会删除那个旧文件。
words.en: To delete something means to remove it or erase it.

words.tr:
adj. 沮丧的；气馁的
v. 使沮丧；使气馁；“dispirit”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He felt dispirited after losing the game.
words.ex_cn: 输掉比赛后，他感到灰心丧气。
words.en: If you are dispirited, you have lost your enthusiasm and excitement.

words.tr: adj. 马虎的；敷衍了事的
words.ex: He gave a slipshod answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个敷衍的回答。
words.en: If something is slipshod, it is done in a careless or lazy way, without attention to detail.

words.tr: adj. 潇洒的；风度翩翩的；温文尔雅的
words.ex: He had a debonair manner that put everyone at ease.
words.ex_cn: 他温文尔雅的举止让每个人都感到轻松自在。
words.en: A debonair man is charming, confident, and stylish, especially in his behavior and appearance.

words.ex: The ship docked at the harbor.
words.ex_cn: 船停靠在海港。
words.en: A harbor is a place on the coast where ships may moor in shelter, especially one protected from rough water by piers, jetties, and other artificial structures.

words.ex: His derogatory remarks hurt her feelings.
words.ex_cn: 他毁谤的言辞伤害了她的感情。
words.en: If you make a derogatory remark or comment about someone or something, you say something that shows you have a low opinion of them.

words.ex: They exalt their hero with cheers.
words.ex_cn: 他们用欢呼赞美他们的英雄。
words.en: To exalt someone or something means to praise them very highly.

words.tr: adj. 无法克服的；难以解决的；不可逾越的
words.ex: The problem seemed insurmountable.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题似乎无法克服。
words.en: If you describe something as insurmountable, you mean that it is so great or severe that it cannot be dealt with.

words.ex: He controverts the claim with clear evidence.
words.ex_cn: 他用清晰的证据反驳了这一说法。
words.en: To argue about (a subject) in a formal manner; to dispute or contradict.

words.tr: adj. 脱离正道的；脱离常轨的
words.ex: His aberrant behavior surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他反常的行为让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: An aberrant person or thing is one that is unusual or unexpected, especially in an unwelcome way.

words.tr: adj. 青黑色的；苍白的；暴怒的
words.ex: His face turned livid after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，他的脸变得青黑色。
words.en: If you say that someone is livid, you mean that they are extremely angry.

words.tr:
n. 蔑视
v. 蔑视
words.ex: He looked at the lie with scorn.
words.ex_cn: 他轻蔑地看着这个谎言。
words.en: If you scorn someone or something, you feel or show contempt for them.

words.tr: adj. 不调和的；不一致的；不和谐的
words.ex: The two voices sounded discordant.
words.ex_cn: 这两声音听起来不和谐。
words.en: Something that is discordant is strange or unpleasant because it does not fit in with other things.

words.ex: A horde of children ran to the ice cream truck.
words.ex_cn: 一群孩子跑向冰淇淋车。
words.en: A horde is a large group of people or animals, especially one that is moving or acting together.

words.ex: The workers load stones from the quarry.
words.ex_cn: 工人们从采石场装载石头。
words.en: A quarry is a place where stone, sand, etc., is dug out of the ground. It can also refer to an animal or person that is being hunted or chased.

words.ex: The government's goal is the extirpation of poverty in the region.
words.ex_cn: 政府的目的是在该地区消灭贫困。
words.en: The act of completely destroying or getting rid of something.

words.ex: He used caulk to seal the gaps around the window.
words.ex_cn: 他用填料密封了窗户周围的缝隙。
words.en: To fill or seal (a gap or seam) to make it watertight.

words.ex: The two groups are discrete and do not overlap.
words.ex_cn: 这两个群体是分离的，没有重叠。
words.en: Something that is discrete is separate and distinct in form or concept.

words.tr:
adj. 怪诞的；丑陋奇异的；奇形怪状的
n. 奇形怪状的东西；奇异风格
words.ex: The painting showed a grotesque face with twisted eyes.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画上有一个扭曲眼睛的怪诞面孔。
words.en: If you say that something is grotesque, you mean that it is extremely unattractive, exaggerated, and often shocking or disturbing.

words.ex: We had dinner at a buffet with many dishes to choose from.
words.ex_cn: 我们在自助餐吃了晚饭，有很多菜可以选。
words.en: A buffet is a meal consisting of several dishes from which guests serve themselves. As a verb, to buffet means to strike repeatedly and violently.

words.tr:
n. 脚注；次要者
v. 为…作脚注
words.ex: He added a footnote to explain the word.
words.ex_cn: 他加了一个脚注来解释这个词。
words.en: A footnote is a note at the bottom of a page in a book which provides more detailed information about something mentioned in the text above it.

words.ex: The indigent man asked for food at the shelter.
words.ex_cn: 这位贫困的人在收容所里请求食物。
words.en: Someone who is indigent is very poor.

words.ex: The government will expropriate the land for the new road.
words.ex_cn: 政府将征用这块土地用于新建道路。
words.en: If a government or other authority expropriates someone's property, they take it away from them for public use or benefit.

words.ex: The imputation of blame was unjust.
words.ex_cn: 归咎于责备是不公平的。
words.en: The act of imputing something, especially a fault or crime, to someone.

words.ex: He shows piety by praying every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天祈祷，表现出虔诚。
words.en: Piety is strong religious belief, or behaviour that is religious or morally correct.

words.tr: adj. 不乐意的；不情愿的；
words.ex: He is loath to apologize for his mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他不乐意为自己的错误道歉。
words.en: If you are loath to do something, you do not want to do it.

words.ex: The mouse is gnawing on the wood.
words.ex_cn: 老鼠正在啃木头。
words.en: To gnaw means to bite or chew something persistently, especially something hard, or to cause persistent worry or discomfort.

words.tr:
v. 弄脏；亵渎；玷污
n. 小道；狭谷
words.ex: They defile the river with trash.
words.ex_cn: 他们用垃圾污染了这条河。
words.en: To defile something means to make it dirty or impure. As a noun, it refers to a narrow pass or gorge between mountains.

words.tr:
n. 艰苦跋涉；
v. 长途跋涉；
words.ex: The trek across the mountains took five days.
words.ex_cn: 穿越群山的艰苦跋涉花了五天时间。
words.en: A trek is a long and often difficult journey, especially one made on foot.

words.ex: His article was a polemic against government corruption.
words.ex_cn: 他的文章是对政府腐败的抨击。
words.en: A polemic is a very strong written or spoken attack on, or defence of, a particular belief or opinion.

words.tr: adj. 角的；有角的；尖角的；
words.ex: The angular shape of the triangle is clear.
words.ex_cn: 三角形的角形很清晰。
words.en: having angles or sharp corners; lean and bony

words.tr:
n. （统治者的）配偶；一组
v. 厮混；结交
words.ex: The king walked with his consort at the parade.
words.ex_cn: 国王在游行中与他的配偶一起行走。
