words.en: A consort is a husband or wife, especially of a reigning monarch. As a verb, it means to habitually associate with someone, typically with the implication of a close or intimate relationship.

words.tr:
n. 假象；假冒者；冒牌货
adj. 虚假的
v. 假装
words.ex: The gift was a sham, not real.
words.ex_cn: 这份礼物是假的，不是真的。
words.en: A sham is something that is not what it appears to be and is intended to deceive people.

words.tr:
n. 茎；词干；
v. 起源于(~ from)；
words.ex: The flower grows on a long green stem.
words.ex_cn: 花长在一根长长的绿色茎上。
words.en: The main body or stalk of a plant or shrub, typically rising above ground but occasionally subterranean; to stop or restrict (the flow of something).

words.tr:
v. 捻接；粘接；结合
n. 粘接处；绞接处
words.ex: He spliced the two ropes together.
words.ex_cn: 他把两根绳子捻接在一起。
words.en: To join or unite (ropes or rope ends) by interweaving the strands.

words.ex: The painting depicts a quiet village at sunset.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画描绘了一个宁静的村庄在日落时分的景象。
words.en: To depict someone or something means to show or represent them in a work of art such as a drawing or painting.

words.tr:
n. 骗局；恶作剧；戏弄
v. 愚弄
words.ex: The news was a hoax to scare people.
words.ex_cn: 这则新闻是个骗局，为了吓唬人。
words.en: A hoax is a plan to deceive someone, such as telling the police there is a bomb somewhere when there is not, or a trick in which someone tells people a lie.

words.tr: n. 专门知识；专门技能；
words.ex: His expertise in computers helps the team solve problems.
words.ex_cn: 他在计算机方面的专门知识帮助团队解决问题。
words.en: Expertise is special skill or knowledge that is acquired by training, study, or practice.

words.tr:
v. 烤焦；烧灼
adj. 烧焦的；枯萎的
n. 烙印；焦痕
words.ex: He sears the steak on the grill.
words.ex_cn: 他在烤架上把牛排煎至表面焦黄。
words.en: To burn or scorch the surface of something with a sudden, intense heat.

words.tr: adj. 节日的；喜庆的；欢乐的
words.ex: The streets are festive during Christmas.
words.ex_cn: 圣诞节期间，街道上充满了节日气氛。
words.en: Something that is festive is special, colorful, or exciting, especially because it is connected with a festival or celebration.

words.tr: v. 诽谤；中伤；损毁名誉
words.ex: He tried to defame his rival with false stories.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用虚假的故事诋毁他的竞争对手。
words.en: To defame someone means to damage their reputation by saying or writing bad things about them that are not true.

words.tr:
n. 被愚弄的人；容易受骗的人
v. 欺骗；诈骗；愚弄
words.ex: He was duped into buying a fake watch.
words.ex_cn: 他被骗去买了一块假手表。
words.en: A dupe is someone who is easily deceived or cheated, often because they are too trusting. As a verb, to dupe means to deceive or trick someone into believing something that is not true.

words.tr:
n. 谷壳；糠；揶揄
v. 开玩笑；戏弄
words.ex: The wind blew away the chaff from the wheat.
words.ex_cn: 风吹走了小麦中的糠秕。
words.en: Chaff is the outer covering of the seeds of grain such as wheat, which is separated from the grain before it is used as food.

words.tr:
adj. 用柏油覆盖的
v. 耽搁；逗留
words.ex: The workers tarry at the road, waiting for the asphalt to dry.
words.ex_cn: 工人们在道路上耽搁，等着沥青变干。
words.en: To tarry means to stay longer than intended or to delay leaving a place.

words.tr:
v. 上釉；上玻璃；浇浆汁于；变呆滞
n. 釉料；光滑面；覆罩的一层
words.ex: The potter glazes the clay bowl before firing it.
words.ex_cn: 陶匠在烧制前给陶碗上釉。
words.en: To glaze means to fit panes of glass into a window frame or similar structure. It can also refer to the process of applying a glossy, often transparent, coating to pottery or other materials.

words.ex: The mountains look distant from here.
words.ex_cn: 从这里看，山显得很远。
words.en: If you describe something as distant, you mean that it is far away in space or time.

words.tr:
adj. 崇高的；壮丽的；极端的；过分的
v. 变高尚；升华
n. 庄严；崇高；顶点
words.ex: The view from the mountain is sublime.
words.ex_cn: 从山上看到的景色是壮丽的。
words.en: If you describe something as sublime, you mean that it has a wonderful quality that affects you deeply.

words.ex: This plan is viable and can be done with little money.
words.ex_cn: 这个计划是可行的，而且用很少的钱就能完成。
words.en: If something is viable, it is capable of doing what it is intended to do.

words.tr:
adj. 酒醉的；陶醉的
v. 使醉；使陶醉；“inebriate”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He was inebriated after a night of heavy drinking.
words.ex_cn: 经过一夜的酗酒，他醉了。
words.en: If someone is inebriated, they have drunk too much alcohol and are drunk.

words.tr: n. （身体或精神的）极度痛苦
words.ex: He felt deep anguish after losing his dog.
words.ex_cn: 失去狗后，他感到极度痛苦。
words.en: Anguish is extreme mental suffering or physical pain.

words.ex: The man was punished for fraud.
words.ex_cn: 这个人因欺骗而受到惩罚。
words.en: Fraud is the crime of gaining money or financial benefits by a trick or by lying.

words.ex: The view from the hill is panoramic.
words.ex_cn: 从山上望去，景色一览无余。
words.en: A panoramic view or picture is one that shows a wide area of land or sea.

words.ex: The flowers wither in the hot sun.
words.ex_cn: 花朵在烈日下枯萎。
words.en: If a plant withers, it dries up and dies. If something withers, it becomes weaker or less important until it disappears completely.

words.ex: His calm temperament helps him stay peaceful in stress.
words.ex_cn: 他平静的性情让他在压力下保持平和。
words.en: Your temperament is your basic nature, especially as it is shown in the way that you react to situations or to other people.

words.tr: adj. 没有钱的；身无分文的；贫穷的
words.ex: The impecunious student had to rely on scholarships to continue his education.
words.ex_cn: 这个贫穷的学生不得不依靠奖学金来继续他的学业。
words.en: If you describe someone as impecunious, you mean that they have very little money.

words.ex: He exclaim when he saw the surprise.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到惊喜时，他大喊起来。
words.en: If you exclaim, you say something suddenly and loudly, often because you are surprised, excited, or angry.

words.ex: The lost hikers began to famish after three days without food.
words.ex_cn: 这些迷路的徒步者在三天没有食物后开始挨饿。
words.en: To cause someone to suffer severely from hunger.

words.tr:
n. 文件；公文；文献；
v. 记录；为…提供证明；
words.ex: He submitted the document to the office.
words.ex_cn: 他把文件提交给了办公室。
words.en: A document is a piece of text or graphics, for example a letter, that is stored as a file on a computer and that you can access in order to read it or change it.

words.ex: The old book had a musty smell.
words.ex_cn: 那本旧书有一股霉味。
words.en: A musty smell is unpleasant and stale, often because something is old and has not been used or aired for a long time.

words.tr: adj. 复仇心重的；报复的
words.ex: He was vengeful after his friend lied to him.
words.ex_cn: 他的朋友骗了他之后，他变得报复心很强。
words.en: If you describe someone as vengeful, you are critical of them because they feel a great desire for revenge.

words.tr: adj. 浑浊的；污浊不清的；
words.ex: The river water looks turbid after the rain.
words.ex_cn: 雨后河水看起来浑浊。
words.en: If you describe something as turbid, you mean that it is cloudy, dirty, or muddy.

words.tr:
n. 折扣；退款
v. 减少
words.ex: He got a rebate on his new TV.
words.ex_cn: 他买新电视时得到了一笔回扣。
words.en: A rebate is a partial refund to someone who has paid too much for tax, rent, or a utility.

words.ex: The government gives a subsidy to farmers.
words.ex_cn: 政府向农民提供补贴。
words.en: A subsidy is money that is paid by a government or other authority in order to help an industry or business, or to pay for a public service.

words.ex: The hikers walked through a deep gorge.
words.ex_cn: 徒步者走过一个深峡谷。
words.en: A gorge is a deep, narrow valley with steep sides, often carved by a river. It can also refer to the act of eating greedily.

words.ex: His smile evinces joy.
words.ex_cn: 他的微笑流露出快乐。
words.en: To show clearly that you have a particular quality, feeling, or ability.

words.tr: adj. 经验主义的；以经验为根据的；
words.ex: The scientist used empirical data to support her theory.
words.ex_cn: 这位科学家使用经验数据来支持她的理论。
words.en: Empirical evidence or study relies on practical experience rather than theories.

words.ex: The burly man carried two heavy boxes easily.
words.ex_cn: 那个健壮的男人轻松地搬了两个重箱子。
words.en: A burly person is big and strong.

words.tr: adj. 不合时宜的；不是时候的
words.ex: He called at an inopportune time.
words.ex_cn: 他在不恰当的时候打了电话。
words.en: If you describe something as inopportune, you mean that it happens at an unfortunate or unsuitable time, and causes trouble or embarrassment because of this.

words.ex: He tried to hoodwink her with a fake story.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用一个虚假的故事欺骗她。
words.en: To deceive or trick someone.

words.tr: adj. 狂乱无秩序的；喧闹的；难控制的
words.ex: The rambunctious children were causing chaos in the classroom.
words.ex_cn: 喧闹的孩子们在教室里制造混乱。
words.en: If you describe someone, especially a child, as rambunctious, you mean that they are full of energy and difficult to control.

words.ex: They have good rapport with their students.
words.ex_cn: 他们与学生关系友好。
words.en: A friendly relationship in which people understand each other very well.

words.ex: We will review the meeting agenda tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我们明天将审查会议议程。
words.en: An agenda is a list or plan of things to be done or considered, especially in a meeting.

words.ex: The university sent me the prospectus for the course.
words.ex_cn: 大学给我寄了这门课程的简章。
words.en: A prospectus is a formal document that describes a new project, business, or product, especially one that is offered for sale or investment.

words.ex: He imparts knowledge to his students every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天向学生传授知识。
words.en: If you impart information to people, you tell it to them. To impart a particular quality to something means to give it that quality.

words.ex: The divisive comment caused a fight among friends.
words.ex_cn: 这个制造分裂的言论引发了朋友们之间的争吵。
words.en: Causing or likely to cause disagreement or division between people.

words.ex: He dawdled away the afternoon at the park.
words.ex_cn: 他在公园里混掉了整个下午。
words.en: If you dawdle, you spend more time than is necessary going somewhere or doing something.

words.ex: The allure of money made him take the risky job.
words.ex_cn: 金钱的诱惑让他接受了这份高风险的工作。
words.en: The quality of being powerfully and mysteriously attractive or fascinating.

words.tr:
n. 猛冲；冲刺；扑
v. 猛冲；冲刺；扑
words.ex: He made a sudden lunge at the ball.
words.ex_cn: 他突然向前扑向球。
words.en: If you lunge in a particular direction, you move in that direction suddenly and forcefully.

words.tr:
v. 喷涌；滔滔不绝地说
n. 涌出；喷出
words.ex: Water gushed from the broken pipe.
words.ex_cn: 水从破裂的管道中喷涌而出。
words.en: If someone gushes, they express their admiration or pleasure in an exaggerated way.

words.tr:
adj. 激进的；好战的
n. 激进；好战
words.ex: He is a militant who protests every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个每天抗议的激进分子。
words.en: A militant person is someone who is engaged in warfare or combat, or who is aggressively active in a cause.

words.tr: adj. 不能挽回的；不能复原的
words.ex: The damage to the painting was deemed irretrievable.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画的损坏被认为是无法修复的。
words.en: If something is irretrievable, it cannot be recovered or corrected.

words.tr: adj. 皇家的；尊贵的；富丽堂皇的
words.ex: The queen wore a regal crown.
words.ex_cn: 女王戴着一顶威严的王冠。
words.en: If you describe something as regal, you mean that it is suitable for a king or queen, because it is very impressive or beautiful.

words.tr:
v. 目瞪口呆地看；裂开
n. 目瞪口呆地看；裂口
words.ex: The children gape at the magic show.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们张大嘴看着魔术表演。
words.en: To open the mouth wide; to stare with open mouth, as in wonder.

words.tr: adj. 无可置疑的；决定性的；
words.ex: The evidence was conclusive.
words.ex_cn: 证据是无可置疑的。
words.en: If something is conclusive, it means that it proves something in a way that is certain and leaves no doubt.

words.ex: The magazine has a glossy cover.
words.ex_cn: 这本杂志有一个光滑的封面。
words.en: Something that is glossy is smooth and shiny.

words.tr:
v. 使惊慌失措；使慌张
n. 慌张；慌乱
words.ex: He got flustered when the teacher asked him a question.
words.ex_cn: 当老师问他问题时，他变得慌乱了。
words.en: If you fluster someone, you make them feel nervous and confused by rushing them or by making it difficult for them to concentrate on what they are doing.

words.ex: The shop tries to entice customers with cheap prices.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店试图以低价吸引顾客。
words.en: If you entice someone, you attract them to a particular place or activity by making it seem attractive or interesting.

words.ex: The default setting is on.
words.ex_cn: 默认设置是开启的。
words.en: If a person, company, or country defaults on something that they have legally agreed to do, such as paying a debt or keeping to an agreement, they fail to do it.

words.tr: v. 考虑；深思；凝视；思考…的可能性
words.ex: He contemplates quitting his job.
words.ex_cn: 他正在考虑辞去工作。
words.en: If you contemplate an action, you think about whether to do it or not.

words.tr:
n. 天主教徒；
adj. 天主教的；
words.ex: He is a catholic who goes to church every Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名每周日都去教堂的天主教徒。
words.en: If you describe a collection of things or people as catholic, you are emphasizing that it is varied and includes many different types of things or people.

words.tr: v. 主持；指挥；担任会议主席
words.ex: He presides over the meeting every Monday.
words.ex_cn: 他每周一主持会议。
words.en: To preside means to be in charge of a formal meeting, ceremony, or other event.

words.tr:
n. 喧嚷；大声的要求
v. 喧嚷；大声地要求
words.ex: The crowd made a loud clamor for justice.
words.ex_cn: 人群为正义发出大声喧哗。
words.en: If people are clamoring for something, they are demanding it in a noisy or angry way.

words.tr: n. 厚颜无耻；无礼；放肆
words.ex: His impudence surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他的无礼让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as impudence, you mean it is rude and disrespectful.

words.ex: The two countries signed an accord to stop the war.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家签署了一项协议以停止战争。
words.en: An accord is an official agreement or treaty. It can also refer to a state of agreement or harmony.

words.ex: He craves chocolate when he is stressed.
words.ex_cn: 当他感到压力时，他渴望吃巧克力。
words.en: If you crave something, or crave for it, you want to have it very much.

words.ex: This temperature is the optimum for growing plants.
words.ex_cn: 这个温度是最适宜植物生长的。
words.en: The optimum is the best or most favorable condition, degree, amount, etc., for achieving a particular result.

words.ex: The mirror deflects the light to the wall.
words.ex_cn: 镜子把光线反射到墙上。
words.en: If you deflect something such as criticism or attention, you act in a way that prevents it from being directed towards you or affecting you.

words.tr: adj. 深不可测的；极坏的；糟透的
words.ex: The abysmal depth of the ocean scared the divers.
words.ex_cn: 海洋的深不可测吓到了潜水员。
words.en: If you describe a situation or the condition of something as abysmal, you think that it is very bad or poor in quality.

words.ex: Many people lost jobs during the recession.
words.ex_cn: 在经济不景气期间，许多人失去了工作。
words.en: A recession is a period when the economy of a country is not doing well, industrial production and business activity are at a low level, and many people are unemployed.

words.ex: The roof has a sharp slant.
words.ex_cn: 屋顶有一个陡峭的倾斜。
words.en: If something slants or if you slant it, it is at an angle rather than being straight up and down or straight from side to side.

words.ex: His excuse was insubstantial and unconvincing.
words.ex_cn: 他的借口是无实质的，毫无说服力。
words.en: If something is insubstantial, it is not solid, large, or strong, and therefore often seems unsatisfactory or unimportant.

words.ex: His coat is threadbare from many years of use.
words.ex_cn: 他的外套因为用了多年而变得破旧。
words.en: Worn out by overuse; shabby and old.

words.ex: They lionize the famous singer everywhere she goes.
words.ex_cn: 无论她去哪里，人们都把她当作名人追捧。
words.en: To treat someone as a celebrity or hero.

words.tr:
n. 刻板印象；陈规老套
v. 对…存有成见；把…模式化
words.ex: He broke the stereotype that boys cannot cry.
words.ex_cn: 他打破了男孩不能哭的刻板印象。
words.en: A stereotype is a fixed general image or set of characteristics that a lot of people believe represent a particular type of person or thing.

words.tr: adj. 有进取心的；有魄力的；
words.ex: He is an enterprising boy who starts small businesses.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个有进取心的男孩，会经营小生意。
words.en: If you describe someone as enterprising, you mean that they are willing to try out new, unusual ways of doing or achieving something.

words.tr: v. 亲如兄弟；友善交往；和敌兵亲善
words.ex: They quickly began to fraternize with the locals.
words.ex_cn: 他们很快就开始与当地人友好交往。
words.en: If one group of people fraternize with another, they meet or spend time together in a friendly way, especially when they are not supposed to.

words.tr: adj. 发狂的；狂热的；疯狂的
words.ex: He had a maniacal glint in his eyes as he spoke about his new project.
words.ex_cn: 他谈起自己的新项目时，眼中闪烁着狂热的光芒。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as maniacal, you mean that it is extremely wild and often violent because they are mentally ill or very angry.

words.tr: v. 证明…是真实的；鉴别
words.ex: He must authenticate his identity with a password.
words.ex_cn: 他必须用密码验证自己的身份。
words.en: To authenticate something means to prove or confirm that it is genuine or true.

words.tr: v. 参与；从事；吸引；与…建立密切关系；
words.ex: He engages in community volunteer work.
words.ex_cn: 他参与社区志愿工作。
words.en: To engage means to occupy, attract, or involve someone or oneself in a particular activity or situation.

words.tr: adj. 无法仿效的；不可比拟的
words.ex: Her inimitable style of writing has captured the hearts of many readers.
words.ex_cn: 她那独特的写作风格赢得了许多读者的心。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as inimitable, you mean that they are so good or unusual that it is unlikely that anyone or anything else could be like them.

words.ex: He drew a simple schematic of the circuit.
words.ex_cn: 他画了一个电路的简单示意图。
words.en: A schematic diagram or representation is a simple drawing that uses symbols to show the parts of something and how they are connected.

words.tr: n. 弹幕射击；掩护炮火；拦河坝
words.ex: The soldiers faced a barrage of bullets.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们面对着一阵弹雨。
words.en: A barrage is a heavy and continuous bombardment of gunfire or a dam built across a river to control the flow of water.

words.ex: The factory buys lumber to make furniture.
words.ex_cn: 这家工厂购买木材来制造家具。
words.en: Lumber refers to wood that has been processed into beams and planks, a stage in the process of wood production. It is also used to describe the action of moving in a slow, heavy, awkward way.

words.tr:
adj. 无法精确估量的
n. 无法估量的事物
words.ex: The reason for his silence is imponderable.
words.ex_cn: 他沉默的原因无法衡量。
words.en: An imponderable factor or element is one that cannot be precisely measured or assessed.

words.ex: The team canvass voters for their opinions.
words.ex_cn: 团队征询选民的意见。
words.en: To canvass means to ask people for their votes or opinions, especially in a political context, or to examine something carefully.

words.ex: The cool water helped to slake his thirst.
words.ex_cn: 清凉的水帮助他解渴。
words.en: If you slake a thirst, desire, or need, you satisfy it.

words.tr:
adj. 腐蚀性的；起破坏作用的
n. 腐蚀性物品
words.ex: The acid is corrosive and can damage metal.
words.ex_cn: 这种酸具有腐蚀性，会损坏金属。
words.en: A corrosive substance is able to destroy solid materials by a chemical reaction.

words.tr: n. 准确；精确；细节；细微的差别
words.ex: The nicety of the measurement surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个测量的准确性让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: A nicety is a fine detail or distinction, especially one that is considered to be important or elegant.

words.tr: adj. 清澈的；透明的；清晰的
words.ex: The lake water is limpid and clear.
words.ex_cn: 湖水清澈透明。
words.en: Clear and transparent, especially in a way that makes it easy to understand.

words.tr: adj. 风度好的；个性或外表宜人的；英俊的；貌美的；有魅力的
words.ex: He was a personable young man, always ready to help others.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个品貌兼优的年轻人，总是乐于助人。
words.en: If you describe someone as personable, you mean that they are pleasant and attractive in appearance and character.

words.tr: adj. 古怪的；离奇的；诡诈的
words.ex: He wears quirky hats every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天都戴些古怪的帽子。
words.en: Something or someone that is quirky is unusual or unpredictable in an interesting or appealing way.

words.tr:
adj. 甜熟的；醇香的；柔和的；成熟的；沉醉的
v. （使）成熟；（使颜色）柔和；（使酒）更加醇香
words.ex: The apple became mellow after a few days.
words.ex_cn: 几天后，苹果变软了。
words.en: If someone mellows or if something mellows them, they become kinder or less extreme in their behavior, often as a result of becoming older or more experienced.

words.ex: The circles are concentric and share the same center.
words.ex_cn: 这些圆是同心的，拥有同一个中心。
words.en: Having a common center, as circles or spheres.

words.tr:
n. 殉道者；殉教者；烈士
v. 处死；折磨
words.ex: He became a martyr for freedom.
words.ex_cn: 他为自由而成为烈士。
words.en: A martyr is someone who is killed or made to suffer greatly because of their religious or political beliefs, and is admired and respected by people who share those beliefs.

words.ex: They exchanged light-hearted badinage during the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他们在会议期间轻松地互相打趣。
words.en: Badinage is light, playful, or humorous conversation or writing.

words.tr: adj. 持久的；不朽的； v. 忍受；“endure”的现在分词；
words.ex: This is an enduring friendship.
words.ex_cn: 这是一段持久的友谊。
words.en: Lasting for a long time; continuing or enduring over a period of time.

words.ex: He will emend the report tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会修改这份报告。
words.en: To emend something means to correct or improve it by changing it slightly.

words.tr: n. 意识形态；思想体系；
words.ex: His ideology is based on equality and justice.
words.ex_cn: 他的意识形态基于平等与正义。
words.en: An ideology is a set of beliefs, especially one held by a particular group, that influences the way people think and behave.

words.ex: The decision was consequential for the future of the company.
words.ex_cn: 这个决定对公司未来意义重大。
words.en: Something that is consequential is important or significant, often because it has effects on other things.

words.tr: v. 损伤…的外观；在…上乱涂乱画
words.ex: They deface the wall with graffiti.
words.ex_cn: 他们用涂鸦破坏了墙壁。
words.en: To deface something means to spoil its appearance by writing or drawing on it, or by damaging it in some other way.

words.tr: v. 割让（领土）；放弃（权力）
words.ex: He will cede his land to the government.
words.ex_cn: 他将把土地让给政府。
words.en: To give up control or possession of something, especially land or territory, often as a result of war or negotiation.

words.ex: He runs with great vigour every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都充满精力地跑步。
words.en: Physical or mental strength and energy.

words.ex: The flowers exude a sweet smell.
words.ex_cn: 花朵散发出甜美的香味。
words.en: If someone exudes a quality or feeling, or if it exudes, they show that they have it to a great extent.

words.tr: adj. 又黑又脏的；昏暗的；肮脏的
words.ex: The room was dingy and small.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间又脏又小。
words.en: If you describe a place or thing as dingy, you mean that it is rather dull and depressing to look at, and perhaps also dirty.

words.ex: He won the game with great finesse.
words.ex_cn: 他以高超的技巧赢得了比赛。
words.en: If you finesse something, you handle it in a skillful and often slightly deceptive way.

words.tr: v. （清楚地）发音；清楚地表明；阐明
words.ex: He tries to enunciate each word clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他努力清晰地发出每个单词的音。
words.en: To enunciate means to pronounce words clearly and distinctly, or to state something clearly and in detail.

words.tr: adj. 散漫的；不着边际的
words.ex: He gave a discursive speech about many topics.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一篇关于许多主题的散漫演讲。
words.en: If a style of writing or speech is discursive, it includes a lot of information that is not relevant to the main subject.

words.ex: His domicile is in New York.
words.ex_cn: 他的住所位于纽约。
words.en: A domicile is the place where a person lives or has their home.

words.tr: v. 解开(~ sth. out)；使更复杂(~ sth. up)
words.ex: She raveled the tangled yarn out slowly.
words.ex_cn: 她慢慢地把缠绕的毛线解开。
words.en: To ravel means to tangle or untangle threads or fibers, or to become tangled or untangled. It can also refer to the process of separating the threads of a woven or knitted fabric, or to confuse or complicate a situation.

words.ex: He faced his adversary in the final match.
words.ex_cn: 他在决赛中对阵对手。
words.en: An adversary is someone who you are competing with, or who is opposing you or what you are trying to do.

words.tr:
v. 使滞留；使搁浅；
n. 方面；
words.ex: The storm stranded the travelers on the island.
words.ex_cn: 风暴使旅行者滞留在岛上。
words.en: If someone is stranded, they are left in a place that is difficult for them to get away from. A strand of something such as hair, wire, or thread is a single thin piece of it.

words.tr:
n. 供过于求；过量
v. 使充满；过量供应
words.ex: The market has a glut of cheap phones.
words.ex_cn: 市场上廉价手机泛滥。
words.en: An excessive supply of something, more than is needed, wanted, or can be used; to supply or fill to excess.

words.ex: He was branded a turncoat after switching political parties.
words.ex_cn: 他在更换政党后被贴上了变节者的标签。
words.en: A turncoat is someone who changes their allegiance or loyalty, especially in a way that is considered treacherous or disloyal.

words.tr:
v. 鼓起；集合；召集
n. 集合；集合的人群
words.ex: He must muster courage to speak in public.
words.ex_cn: 他必须鼓起勇气在公众面前发言。
words.en: To muster means to gather or assemble (troops, etc.), especially for inspection or in preparation for battle. It can also mean to summon up (a feeling, attitude, or response).

words.ex: His exceptionable behavior upset the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他令人反感的行为让老师很生气。
words.en: If you describe something as exceptionable, you mean that it is open to objection or criticism.

words.ex: The contract stipulates that payments must be made monthly.
words.ex_cn: 合同规定付款必须按月进行。
words.en: If you stipulate a condition or stipulate that something must be done, you say clearly that it must be done.

words.ex: The court decided to expunge his record.
words.ex_cn: 法院决定删除他的记录。
words.en: If you expunge something, you get rid of it completely, because it causes problems or bad feelings.

words.ex: He tried to manipulate the results to win the game.
words.ex_cn: 他试图操纵结果来赢得比赛。
words.en: To manipulate something means to handle or control it skillfully, often in a way that is considered unfair or dishonest.

words.tr: adj. 无可指责的；无过失的
words.ex: Her behavior has always been irreproachable.
words.ex_cn: 她的行为一直无可指责。
words.en: If you say that someone's character or behaviour is irreproachable, you mean that they behave so well that they cannot be criticized.

words.tr: v. 压制；平息；消除；减轻
words.ex: The police tried to quell the riot.
words.ex_cn: 警察试图平息暴乱。
words.en: To quell something, especially a feeling, means to stop it or reduce its intensity.

words.ex: I concur with your opinion.
words.ex_cn: 我同意你的观点。
words.en: If one person concurs with another person, the first person agrees with the second person.

words.tr: adj. 油腔滑调的；口齿伶俐的；圆滑的
words.ex: He gave a glib answer to the difficult question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个难题给出了一个轻率的回答。
words.en: If you describe what someone says as glib, you disapprove of it because it implies that something is simple or easy, or that there are no problems involved, when this is not the case.

words.ex: The monster was just a figment of his imagination.
words.ex_cn: 那个怪物只是他想象出来的。
words.en: A figment is something that someone imagines or invents, often something that is not real.

words.ex: His melodramatic crying made everyone laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他感情夸张的哭泣让大家都笑了。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as melodramatic, you are criticizing them for acting in a way that is too emotional or exaggerated.

words.ex: The abrasive surface wore down the metal.
words.ex_cn: 磨损的表面磨耗了金属。
words.en: An abrasive substance is rough and can be used to clean surfaces or to make them smooth by rubbing. An abrasive person is someone who is harsh and rude.

words.ex: His antic behavior made everyone laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他滑稽的行为让大家都笑了。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as antic, you mean that it is strange and foolish in a way that is amusing.

words.tr: adj. 不能和解的；不能平息的
words.ex: He is an implacable enemy who never forgives.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个永不原谅的不可调和的敌人。
words.en: If you say that someone is implacable, you mean that they have very strong feelings of hostility or disapproval which nobody can change.

words.tr: v. 使冲昏头脑；弄糊涂；使着迷
words.ex: He is infatuated with his new classmate.
words.ex_cn: 他迷上了他的新同学。
words.en: To inspire with a foolish or extravagant love or admiration.

words.ex: We took a different route to avoid traffic.
words.ex_cn: 我们换了条路线以避开交通拥堵。
words.en: A route is a way from one place to another, or the path that something follows to reach a destination.

words.tr: v. 声明放弃；与...断绝关系
words.ex: He renounced his citizenship last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年放弃了国籍。
words.en: If you renounce a belief or a way of behaving, you say and show that you no longer hold that belief or will behave in that way.

words.ex: The language barrier was insuperable for him.
words.ex_cn: 语言障碍对他来说是难以克服的。
words.en: If you describe a problem or obstacle as insuperable, you mean that it is impossible to overcome.

words.tr: adj. 猜疑的；机警的；有戒心的
words.ex: He was leery of strangers and preferred to keep to himself.
words.ex_cn: 他对陌生人很猜疑，宁愿独来独往。
words.en: If you are leery of something or someone, you are cautious or suspicious about them.

words.tr:
adj. 认命的；顺从的；勉强接受的
v. 辞职；“resign”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He was resigned to losing the game.
words.ex_cn: 他认命地接受了输掉比赛的结果。
words.en: If you are resigned to an unpleasant situation or fact, you accept it without complaining because you realize that you cannot change it.

words.ex: It is a hypothetical situation.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个假设的情况。
words.en: A hypothetical situation, idea, or explanation is based on possible ideas or situations rather than actual ones.

words.tr:
adj. 免费的；无偿的
adv. 免费地；无偿地
words.ex: You can download the software gratis from the company's website.
words.ex_cn: 你可以从公司网站免费下载该软件。
words.en: If something is done or given gratis, it is done or given without payment.

words.tr: adj. 温和宜人的（气候）；芳香的
words.ex: The balmy wind felt nice on her skin.
words.ex_cn: 温暖的微风轻拂她的皮肤。
words.en: Balmy weather is pleasantly warm and mild.

words.tr: adj. 天空的；天体的；天国的；
words.ex: The celestial lights shone brightly in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 天空中的光芒在夜空中明亮地闪耀。
words.en: Relating to the sky or the heavens; belonging or relating to heaven as the abode of the gods.

words.ex: The committee will convene tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 委员会明天将召开会议。
words.en: If someone convenes a meeting or conference, they arrange for it to take place. They can also be said to convene when they meet.

words.ex: The toddler is walking slowly by the sofa.
words.ex_cn: 这个幼儿正慢慢地在沙发旁走路。
words.en: A toddler is a young child who has just learned to walk or who is learning to walk.

words.ex: He practices martial arts every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天练习武术。
words.en: Martial is used to describe things relating to soldiers or war.

words.tr:
n. 恶棍；无赖；流氓
v. 草率地做
words.ex: He was always getting into trouble, but he was a lovable scamp.
words.ex_cn: 他总是惹麻烦，但他是个讨人喜欢的小流氓。
words.en: A scamp is a person, especially a child, who is mischievous in a likable or amusing way.

words.tr: adj. 装饰性的；作装饰用的；
words.ex: The room has decorative flowers on the table.
words.ex_cn: 房间里桌上有一些装饰性的花。
words.en: Something that is decorative is intended to look pretty or attractive.

words.ex: He is chary of spending money on useless things.
words.ex_cn: 他不愿意把钱花在无用的东西上。
words.en: If you are chary of doing something, you are cautious or hesitant about doing it because you are worried that it might have bad consequences.

words.tr: adj. 顺从的；服从的；恭顺的；
words.ex: The submissive dog waited quietly for its owner's command.
words.ex_cn: 这只顺从的狗安静地等待主人的命令。
words.en: If you are submissive, you obey someone without arguing.

words.ex: The injury incapacitated him for weeks.
words.ex_cn: 这次受伤使他几周无法行动。
words.en: To make someone unable to do something, especially because of injury or illness.

words.tr: n. 纪念品；用以回忆的东西
words.ex: She keeps a photo as a memento of her trip.
words.ex_cn: 她保留了一张照片作为旅行的纪念品。
words.en: A memento is an object which you keep because it reminds you of a person or a special event.

words.ex: The hen incubate eggs until they hatch.
words.ex_cn: 母鸡孵化鸡蛋直到小鸡孵出。
words.en: to keep eggs warm so that they develop and hatch, or to keep cells, bacteria, etc. at a suitable temperature so that they develop

words.tr:
n. 栖枝；鲈鱼；
v. 栖息；处于（高处）；
words.ex: The bird sat on a perch near the tree.
words.ex_cn: 鸟停在树旁的一根栖枝上。
words.en: A perch is a branch or rod where a bird rests or a high position where someone or something is located. As a verb, it means to rest or be located in a high position.

words.tr: n. 大量；丰富；慷慨；浪费
words.ex: There is a profusion of flowers in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 花园里有大量花朵。
words.en: If there is a profusion of something or it occurs in profusion, there is a very large quantity or variety of it.

words.tr: adj. 不确定的；不明确的
words.ex: The result is indeterminate.
words.ex_cn: 结果是不确定的。
words.en: If something is indeterminate, you cannot say exactly what it is.

words.ex: He used the sun to orient himself.
words.ex_cn: 他用太阳来确定方向。
words.en: To orient means to align or position something in relation to the points of a compass or other specified positions, or to familiarize someone with a new situation or environment.

words.ex: The buxom woman smiled warmly at the children.
words.ex_cn: 这位丰满的女士对孩子们温暖地笑了。
words.en: If you describe a woman as buxom, you mean that she has a full, rounded figure and is usually large-breasted.

words.tr: n. 严酷的考验；痛苦的经历；煎熬
words.ex: He went through a long ordeal before he found peace.
words.ex_cn: 他在找到平静之前经历了一段漫长的磨难。
words.en: An ordeal is a very unpleasant and prolonged experience.

words.tr: adj. 明目张胆的；丑恶可耻的；公然的
words.ex: He made a flagrant mistake during the game.
words.ex_cn: 他在比赛中犯了一个明显的错误。
words.en: If you describe an action as flagrant, you mean that it is done in an open and obvious way and is intended to shock or offend people.

words.tr:
n. 闪光；一刹那；
v. 闪光；闪现；
words.ex: The camera captured a sudden flash of light.
words.ex_cn: 相机捕捉到了一道突然的闪光。
words.en: A flash is a sudden bright light that quickly disappears. As a verb, it means to shine brightly for a short time or to appear or pass suddenly.

words.tr: v. （将刀剑）入鞘；放进套里；包；覆盖
words.ex: He sheathes his knife after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他晚饭后把刀收进刀鞘。
words.en: To put something, especially a weapon, into a sheath; to cover or protect something with a sheath.

words.ex: He wrote a manifesto to explain his ideas.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一份宣言来解释他的观点。
words.en: A manifesto is a written statement of the beliefs, aims, and policies of an organization, especially a political party.

words.ex: The company agreed to defray the travel expenses.
words.ex_cn: 公司同意支付差旅费。
words.en: If you defray someone's costs or expenses, you give them money which represents the amount that they have spent, for example while they have been doing something for you or acting on your behalf.

words.ex: He used a stick to dislodge the rock from the path.
words.ex_cn: 他用一根棍子把石头从路上移出。
words.en: To dislodge something means to remove it from a place where it is fixed or held.

words.ex: The restaurant caters to vegetarians.
words.ex_cn: 这家餐厅满足素食者的需求。
words.en: To cater means to provide food and drink at an event, often as a business service, or to provide what is needed or wanted by a particular person or group.

words.tr: adj. 倾向性的；有偏见的；有争议的
words.ex: The media's tendentious reporting often misrepresents the truth.
words.ex_cn: 媒体的带有倾向性的报道常常歪曲事实。
words.en: If something is tendentious, it expresses a particular opinion or point of view very strongly, especially one that many people disagree with.

words.ex: The problem is intractable and no one can solve it.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题很难处理，没人能解决。
words.en: If you describe a problem or a person as intractable, you mean that it is very difficult to deal with or to change.

words.tr: v. 背叛；出卖；泄露；暴露
words.ex: He betrays his friend by telling the secret.
words.ex_cn: 他通过泄露秘密背叛了朋友。
words.en: If you betray someone who loves or trusts you, your actions hurt and disappoint them.

words.ex: His creed is to always tell the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他的信条是永远说真话。
words.en: A creed is a set of beliefs, principles, or opinions that strongly influence the way people live or work.

words.tr:
v. 抑制；降低；减弱
n. （制革用的）软化剂
words.ex: The hawk bated its wings in anticipation.
words.ex_cn: 鹰在期待中鼓翅躁动。
words.en: To lessen the force or intensity of something; to restrain or hold back.

words.ex: The judge was disinterested in the case.
words.ex_cn: 法官对这个案件持客观态度。
words.en: If someone is disinterested in something, they have no personal involvement or investment in it and are therefore able to judge it fairly.

words.tr:
n. 地址；演讲；
v. 解决；向…讲话；
words.ex: Please write your address on the form.
words.ex_cn: 请把你的地址写在表格上。
words.en: The particulars of the place where someone lives or an organization is situated; a formal speech delivered to an audience.

words.tr: adj. 明显的； v. “glare”的现在分词；
words.ex: The mistake was glaring to everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个错误对每个人来说都很明显。
words.en: If you describe something bad as glaring, you are emphasizing that it is very obvious and easily seen.

words.tr: adj. 有辨别力的；能洞悉的；眼光敏锐的； v. “discern”的现在分词；
words.ex: She is a discerning shopper who always finds the best quality.
words.ex_cn: 她是一个有辨别力的购物者，总是能找到最好的质量。
words.en: If you describe someone as discerning, you mean that they are able to judge which things of a particular kind are good and which are bad.

words.tr: v. 研究；学习；“study”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He studied the behavior of birds in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 他研究了森林中鸟类的行为。
words.en: If you describe something as studied, you mean that it is deliberate and planned, rather than natural or spontaneous.

words.tr:
n. 元帅；高级军官；典礼官；消防局长
v. 整理；集结
words.ex: The marshal led the army into battle.
words.ex_cn: 元帅率领军队上战场。
words.en: A marshal is a high-ranking officer in the armed forces, especially in the army or air force, or a person who arranges or directs a public event.

words.tr:
v. 挤作一团
n. 挤作一团
words.ex: The team huddled together to plan their next move.
words.ex_cn: 团队聚在一起规划下一步行动。
words.en: If people huddle together, they stand, sit, or lie close to each other because they are cold or frightened.

words.ex: There was a spike in sales after the advertisement.
words.ex_cn: 广告发布后，销量出现了激增。
words.en: A spike is a thin, pointed piece of metal, wood, or another hard material, or a sudden increase in something.

words.tr: adj. 欢乐的；轻松快活的；好交际的
words.ex: The party was convivial and everyone laughed a lot.
words.ex_cn: 派对气氛友好愉快，大家都笑得很开心。
words.en: A convivial atmosphere or event is friendly and pleasant, and people enjoy being together.

words.tr:
v. 缓行；溜蹄
n. 溜蹄；缓行漫步
words.ex: He amble through the park after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他晚饭后在公园里缓行。
words.en: To walk at a slow, relaxed pace, especially for pleasure.

words.ex: He has an obsessive need to clean everything.
words.ex_cn: 他有一种强迫性的需求，要把一切都打扫干净。
words.en: If someone's behaviour is obsessive, they cannot stop doing a particular thing or behaving in a particular way.

words.ex: He can translate words into pictures.
words.ex_cn: 他能把词语转化为图画。
words.en: To translate means to change written or spoken words from one language into another, or to explain something in a way that is easier to understand.

words.tr:
n. 撑杆；支柱
v. 趾高气扬地走；昂首阔步
words.ex: The bridge has metal struts to support the weight.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥有金属撑杆来支撑重量。
words.en: If someone struts, they walk in a proud way, with their chest out and trying to look important.

words.ex: The assembly of the car took three days.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车的装配花了三天时间。
words.en: An assembly is a group of people gathered together for a particular purpose, such as a meeting or a legislative session. It can also refer to the process of fitting together the component parts of a machine or other object.

words.ex: The old building has a beautiful facade with stone pillars.
words.ex_cn: 这栋老建筑有一个带有石柱的漂亮正面。
words.en: The front of a building, especially an imposing or decorative one. Also, a superficial appearance or illusion of something.

words.tr: adj. 不能调和的；无法化解的；不兼容的
words.ex: Their views are irreconcilable.
words.ex_cn: 他们的观点无法调和。
words.en: If two things such as opinions or proposals are irreconcilable, they are so different from each other that it is not possible to believe or have both of them.

words.ex: She tried to prevail on him to change his mind.
words.ex_cn: 她试图劝服他改变主意。
words.en: If a proposal, principle, or opinion prevails, it gains influence or is accepted, often after a struggle or argument.

words.ex: The room was decorated with gaudy colors that hurt the eyes.
words.ex_cn: 房间用俗丽的颜色装饰，刺眼。
words.en: If you describe something as gaudy, you mean that it is very brightly coloured and showy, but not in an attractive way.

words.ex: The horse canter around the field.
words.ex_cn: 马在田野里慢跑。
words.en: If a horse canters, it moves at a speed that is slower than a gallop but faster than a trot.

words.ex: He writes his name in cursive.
words.ex_cn: 他用草书写自己的名字。
words.en: Cursive is a style of handwriting in which the letters are joined together in a flowing manner.

words.tr: n. 骗子；江湖骗子；诈骗犯
words.ex: The swindler tricked old people with fake promises.
words.ex_cn: 这个骗子用虚假的承诺欺骗了老人。
words.en: A swindler is someone who swindles, that is, someone who cheats or tricks someone else out of money or property.

words.tr:
v. 安慰；慰问
n. 控制台；操纵台
words.ex: She whispered kind words to console her crying friend.
words.ex_cn: 她轻声说些安慰的话来安抚哭泣的朋友。
words.en: If you console someone who is unhappy about something, you try to make them feel more cheerful.

words.ex: The resolution of the conflict took many meetings.
words.ex_cn: 这个冲突的解决花了多次会议。
words.en: A resolution is a formal decision made at a meeting by the vote of the people who are there. It can also refer to a firm decision to do or not to do something.

words.ex: The volcano began to disgorge lava.
words.ex_cn: 火山开始喷出岩浆。
words.en: If something disgorges its contents or if it is disgorged, its contents come out, often in a sudden and violent way.

words.ex: The two countries reached a concord on trade.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家在贸易上达成了一致。
words.en: Concord is a state of agreement or harmony between people or groups.

words.tr:
v. 闲逛；漫步
n. 闲逛；漫步
words.ex: We decided to saunter along the beach.
words.ex_cn: 我们决定沿着海滩漫步。
words.en: If you saunter somewhere, you walk there in a slow, relaxed way.

words.tr: adj. 衣冠楚楚的；干净利落的；短小精悍的
words.ex: He was a dapper man, always impeccably dressed.
words.ex_cn: 他是个衣冠楚楚的人，总是穿着无可挑剔。
words.en: If you describe a man as dapper, you mean that he is small and neat in appearance and moves quickly and energetically.

words.ex: The sponge is porous and absorbs water easily.
words.ex_cn: 海绵是多孔的，容易吸水。
words.en: If something is porous, it has a lot of tiny holes in it that allow water or air to pass through slowly.

words.ex: The detective tried to ascertain the truth.
words.ex_cn: 侦探试图查明真相。
words.en: If you ascertain the truth about something, you find out what it is, especially by making a deliberate effort to do so.

words.tr:
v. 染上点颜色
n. 一丝痕迹；色调
words.ex: The sky has a tinge of pink at sunset.
words.ex_cn: 日落时，天空有一丝粉红色。
words.en: A tinge of a colour, feeling, or quality is a small amount of it.

words.tr: adj. 兼容的；可和谐共存的；
words.ex: This printer is compatible with my computer.
words.ex_cn: 这个打印机与我的电脑兼容。
words.en: If things, for example, systems, ideas, and beliefs, are compatible, they work well together or can exist together successfully.

words.ex: He likes to dabble in various hobbies.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢涉猎各种爱好。
words.en: If you dabble in something, you take part in it but not very seriously.

words.ex: I caught a whiff of fresh bread.
words.ex_cn: 我闻到了一点新鲜面包的气味。
words.en: A whiff is a brief, gentle gust of air, or a slight smell of something.

words.tr: adj. 过分劳累的；过度兴奋的；过分紧张的
words.ex: He felt overwrought after working 16 hours straight.
words.ex_cn: 他连续工作了16个小时，感到精疲力尽。
words.en: If someone is overwrought, they are very upset and are not thinking or behaving calmly or sensibly.

words.tr: v. 舍不得给；节省；克扣
words.ex: She skimped on the ingredients to save money.
words.ex_cn: 她为了省钱，在食材上克扣。
words.en: To skimp means to spend less time, money, or effort on something than is really needed, often resulting in a lower quality outcome.

words.ex: He reneged on his promise to help me.
words.ex_cn: 他背弃了帮助我的承诺。
words.en: If someone reneges on a promise or an agreement, they do not do what they have promised or agreed to do.

words.tr: v. 兴旺；繁荣；茁壮成长；
words.ex: Plants thrive in sunny places.
words.ex_cn: 植物在阳光充足的地方茁壮成长。
words.en: To thrive means to grow or develop well or vigorously.

words.tr:
v. （使）成波浪状；（使）起涟漪；作潺潺声 
n. 微波；涟漪；潺潺声
words.ex: The wind ripples the surface of the lake.
words.ex_cn: 风使湖面泛起波浪。
words.en: If something ripples, it moves in small waves or if you ripple it, you make it move in small waves.

words.ex: They traverse the forest to reach the village.
words.ex_cn: 他们横穿森林去到达村庄。
words.en: To traverse something means to move or travel across it, often with some difficulty.

words.tr: adj. 偶然的；外来的；不定的
words.ex: The plant grew adventitious roots from its stem.
words.ex_cn: 这种植物从茎上长出了不定根。
words.en: Adventitious means happening or carried on according to chance rather than design or inherent nature.

words.tr:
v. 使湿透；浸透
n. 弄湿；浸液
words.ex: The rain drenched his clothes.
words.ex_cn: 雨把他的衣服淋湿了。
words.en: To drench something or someone means to make them completely wet.

words.ex: They are discussing marital problems.
words.ex_cn: 他们正在讨论婚姻问题。
words.en: Marital is used to describe things relating to marriage.

words.ex: She is thrifty and saves money every week.
words.ex_cn: 她很节约，每周都存钱。
words.en: If you say that someone is thrifty, you are praising them for saving money and not spending it on unnecessary things.

words.tr:
n. 卷轴；
v. 卷动；
words.ex: He unrolled the ancient scroll.
words.ex_cn: 他展开了一卷古老的卷轴。
words.en: A scroll is a roll of paper or parchment with writing or pictures on it. As a verb, to scroll means to move displayed text or graphics on a screen in a particular direction in order to view different parts of them.

words.ex: The car deviated from the road.
words.ex_cn: 汽车偏离了道路。
words.en: To deviate means to do something that is different from the usual or common way of behaving.

words.ex: He has the capacity to solve hard math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他有能力解决复杂的数学问题。
words.en: The capacity of a place or container is the amount of things or people that it can hold.

words.tr:
v. （艰难地）爬上；攀登
n. （艰难地）爬；攀登
words.ex: The boy clambered up the rocky hill.
words.ex_cn: 男孩爬上了多石的山丘。
words.en: If you clamber somewhere, you climb there with difficulty, usually using your hands as well as your feet.

words.ex: The astral plane is believed to be a level of existence beyond the physical world.
words.ex_cn: 人们相信星界是超越物质世界的一个存在层面。
words.en: Relating to or resembling the stars.

words.ex: Honesty is an integral part of a good relationship.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是良好关系中不可或缺的一部分。
words.en: Something that is integral is very important or necessary. If something is an integral part of a whole, it is an essential part of that whole.

words.tr: v. 点燃；生火；激起；发亮
words.ex: He used a match to kindle the fire.
words.ex_cn: 他用火柴点燃了火。
words.en: To kindle something means to cause it to begin burning or to arouse or inspire it.

words.ex: The rain offset the heat yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 昨天的雨抵消了炎热。
words.en: If one thing is offset by another, the effect of the first thing is reduced by the second, so that any advantage or disadvantage is cancelled out.

words.tr: n. 指标；索引；指数；“index”的复数
words.ex: The company tracks key indices to measure performance.
words.ex_cn: 该公司追踪关键指标以衡量表现。
words.en: Indices are used to measure or indicate something, such as economic health or the performance of a stock market.

words.tr: adj. 不会受伤害的；攻不破的；固若金汤的
words.ex: The fortress was said to be invulnerable.
words.ex_cn: 这座要塞据说无懈可击。
words.en: If someone or something is invulnerable, they cannot be harmed or damaged.

words.tr: adj. 天使般可爱的；天使般纯真的
words.ex: The cherubic boy smiled at everyone.
words.ex_cn: 那个天使般的孩子对每个人微笑。
words.en: Having the innocence or plump prettiness of a cherub.

words.ex: The meeting felt interminable.
words.ex_cn: 这场会议感觉没完没了。
words.en: If you describe something as interminable, you are emphasizing that it continues for a very long time and indicating that you find it boring or annoying.

words.tr:
v. 交换；
n. 交换；
words.ex: They swap books every week.
words.ex_cn: 他们每周交换书籍。
words.en: If you swap something with someone, you give it to them and receive a different thing in exchange.

words.ex: The software allows you to truncate long filenames.
words.ex_cn: 该软件允许你截断过长的文件名。
words.en: To shorten something by cutting off the top or the end.

words.tr:
n. 坟墓；
adj. 严重的；
words.ex: They visited the grave of their grandfather.
words.ex_cn: 他们参观了祖父的坟墓。
words.en: A grave is a place where a dead person is buried. When used as an adjective, grave means serious or solemn.

words.tr:
v. 扭打；混战
n. 扭打；混战
words.ex: The two boys had a scuffle over the ball.
words.ex_cn: 两个男孩为了球打了一架。
words.en: A scuffle is a short, confused fight or struggle at close quarters.

words.ex: The difference is discernible to the naked eye.
words.ex_cn: 这个差异肉眼可见。
words.en: able to be discerned; perceptible

words.tr: n. 对应物；相当之物；副本；
words.ex: The CEO's counterpart in China signed the agreement.
words.ex_cn: 中国方面的对应人物签署了协议。
words.en: Someone's or something's counterpart is another person or thing that has a similar function or position in a different place.

words.ex: He inferred that she was tired from her yawns.
words.ex_cn: 他从她的哈欠推断出她很累。
words.en: If you infer that something is the case, you decide that it is true on the basis of information that you already have.

words.tr: adj. 逃避的；推托的；闪烁其辞的
words.ex: He gave an evasive answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个回避的答案。
words.en: If you describe someone as evasive, you mean that they deliberately avoid giving clear direct answers to questions.

words.tr: adj. 实用的；实际的；实践的；
words.ex: This tool is practical for everyday use.
words.ex_cn: 这个工具日常使用很实用。
words.en: relating to what is real rather than to what is possible or imagined; likely to succeed or be effective in real circumstances; involving or concerned with experience or actual use; not theoretical

words.ex: He is a charismatic leader who inspires everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位有魅力的领导者，能激励每个人。
words.en: A charismatic person attracts, influences, and inspires people by their personal qualities.

words.tr: adj. 极不公正的；邪恶的
words.ex: The judge's iniquitous decision sparked widespread outrage.
words.ex_cn: 法官的不公正判决引发了广泛的愤怒。
words.en: If you describe something as iniquitous, you mean that it is very unfair or morally bad.

words.tr:
v. 轻弹；轻击；轻拂；忽然摇动
n. 轻弹；轻拂；快速的轻打
words.ex: He flicked the light switch on.
words.ex_cn: 他 flick 了一下电灯开关。
words.en: To move or hit something with a quick, sharp movement.

words.ex: The car stopped at the verge of the road.
words.ex_cn: 汽车停在了道路的边缘。
words.en: The edge or border of something; to be close to a certain state or condition.

words.ex: The smell of bread permeate the kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 面包的香味弥漫了整个厨房。
words.en: If something permeates a place, it spreads throughout it.

words.tr: adj. 外界的；外在的；非固有的；
words.ex: The reward was extrinsic, not from within.
words.ex_cn: 这个奖励是外界的，不是来自内心的。
words.en: Extrinsic means not forming part of or belonging to a thing; external.

words.tr: adj. 虔诚的；衷心的；诚挚的；
words.ex: He is a devout Christian who goes to church every Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名虔诚的基督徒，每周日都去教堂。
words.en: If you describe someone as devout, you mean that they have a deep religious faith.

words.ex: The spy practiced espionage to get secret information.
words.ex_cn: 间谍从事间谍活动以获取秘密信息。
words.en: The practice of spying or of using spies, typically by governments to obtain political and military information.

words.tr: adj. 爱玩的；嬉戏玩笑的；喜爱运动的
words.ex: He is sportive and loves playing basketball.
words.ex_cn: 他很有运动精神，喜欢打篮球。
words.en: If you describe someone as sportive, you mean that they are lively and enjoy playing games or sports.

words.ex: The boy showed defiance by refusing to follow the rules.
words.ex_cn: 男孩通过拒绝遵守规则来表现违抗。
words.en: Defiance is behaviour or an attitude which shows that you are not willing to obey someone or something.

words.tr: n. 火把；燃烧的木柴；煽动者
words.ex: He is a firebrand who speaks loudly against injustice.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个大声反对不公的激进分子。
words.en: A firebrand is a person who is passionate about a particular cause, often inciting others to action or rebellion.

words.tr: adj. 不能渗透的；不透水的
words.ex: The raincoat is impermeable and keeps you dry.
words.ex_cn: 这件雨衣不透水，能让你保持干燥。
words.en: An impermeable material does not allow liquids or gases to pass through it.

words.ex: The severity of the storm caused many power outages.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴的严重性导致了许多停电。
words.en: The severity of something is the degree to which it is serious or severe.

words.ex: The farmer milks the cow every morning.
words.ex_cn: 农夫每天早上给母牛挤奶。
words.en: A cow is a large female animal that is kept on farms for its milk.

words.ex: The axe will cleave the wood in two.
words.ex_cn: 斧头会把木头劈成两半。
words.en: To split or sever something, especially along a natural line or grain; to adhere firmly and closely or loyally and unwaveringly to something.

words.tr:
n. 羊毛；一只羊一次剪下的毛
vt. 剪下羊毛；敲诈；诈取
words.ex: The sheep is losing its fleece in spring.
words.ex_cn: 这只羊在春天掉毛。
words.en: Fleece can refer to the wool coat of a sheep or similar animal, or to a soft fabric made from this wool. As a verb, it means to shear the wool from a sheep or to swindle someone.

words.tr: adj. 真实性可疑的；杜撰的
words.ex: The story about the ghost is apocryphal.
words.ex_cn: 关于鬼魂的故事是不可信的。
words.en: An apocryphal story is one that is probably not true or did not happen, although it is often told and believed by some people to be true.

words.ex: This rule is universal for all students.
words.ex_cn: 这条规则对所有学生都是普遍适用的。
words.en: Something that is universal affects or relates to every part of the world or the universe.

words.tr: v. 开创；为（某人）举行就职典礼；为…举行开幕仪式
words.ex: The president will inaugurate the new hospital next week.
words.ex_cn: 总统将于下周为新医院举行揭幕仪式。
words.en: If you inaugurate a new system, service, or project, you start it or introduce it officially.

words.tr: adj. 冒犯的；令人不快的；进攻性的；
words.ex: His offensive words made her cry.
words.ex_cn: 他冒犯的话让她哭了。
words.en: If you describe someone's language or behavior as offensive, you mean that it is rude or insulting.

words.ex: The mobile table can be moved easily.
words.ex_cn: 这个可移动的桌子很容易搬动。
words.en: A mobile is something that can move or be moved easily.

words.ex: The police arrested the thief last night.
words.ex_cn: 警察昨晚逮捕了那个小偷。
words.en: If the police arrest you, they take charge of you and take you to a police station, because they believe you may have committed a crime.

words.ex: The focal point of the room is the big painting.
words.ex_cn: 房间的中心是那幅大画。
words.en: relating to the center or main point of interest

words.tr: v. 解释；把…逐字译出；作句法分析
words.ex: He construes her silence as a yes.
words.ex_cn: 他把她的沉默理解为同意。
words.en: If you construe something in a particular way, you interpret it in that way.

words.ex: He frets about his exam results.
words.ex_cn: 他为考试成绩感到烦躁不安。
words.en: If you fret about something, you worry about it.

words.ex: The army stopped the incursion at the border.
words.ex_cn: 军队在边境阻止了入侵。
words.en: An incursion is a sudden attack on or invasion of a place.

words.ex: He didn't flinch when the needle touched his skin.
words.ex_cn: 当针碰到他的皮肤时，他没有退缩。
words.en: If you flinch, you make a small sudden movement, especially when something surprises you or hurts you.

words.tr: adj. 一年两度的；每年两次的
words.ex: The meeting is biannual, so it happens twice a year.
words.ex_cn: 这个会议是半年一次的，所以每年发生两次。
words.en: A biannual event happens twice a year.

words.ex: The luminous moon lights up the night.
words.ex_cn: 明亮的月亮照亮了夜晚。
words.en: Something that is luminous shines or glows in the dark.

words.tr: adj. 地狱的；恶魔似的；可憎的
words.ex: The heat in the room was infernal.
words.ex_cn: 房间里的热量像地狱一样。
words.en: If you describe something as infernal, you are emphasizing that it is extremely annoying or unpleasant.

words.tr:
n. 裂缝；裂口
adj. 劈开的
v. 劈开；砍开；坚守；信守；忠于；“cleave”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The rock has a small cleft where water collects.
words.ex_cn: 这块岩石上有一个小裂缝，水会积在那里。
words.en: A cleft is a narrow opening or fissure, especially in a rock or the ground.

words.ex: The storm caused the train to halt.
words.ex_cn: 风暴使火车中断了。
words.en: Halting is used to describe something that is done in a hesitant or faltering manner, often because of uncertainty or lack of confidence.

words.tr:
v. 吊起；悬挂；投掷
n. 投掷；悬带
words.ex: The nurse slung the arm in a bandage.
words.ex_cn: 护士用绷带吊起手臂。
words.en: To throw or hurl something with force; to suspend or hang something loosely.

words.ex: His physiological response to stress is very strong.
words.ex_cn: 他对压力的生理反应非常强烈。
words.en: Physiological refers to the normal functions of living organisms and their parts, or to the branch of biology that deals with these functions.

words.tr: adj. （适用于）步行的；非固定的；可移动的；流动的
words.ex: The hospital has an ambulatory care unit for patients needing less intensive treatment.
words.ex_cn: 这家医院设有一个流动护理单元，供需要较少密集治疗的患者使用。
words.en: Relating to or adapted for walking; able to walk about and not bedridden.

words.ex: He is an extroverted boy who loves talking to new people.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个外向的男孩，喜欢和新人交谈。
words.en: Someone who is extroverted is very active, lively, and sociable.

words.tr: adj. 发烧的；紧张忙乱的；极度紧张（或兴奋）的
words.ex: He is feverish after running in the sun.
words.ex_cn: 他在太阳下跑步后发高烧。
words.en: If you are feverish, you are suffering from a fever, or you are extremely excited or worried about something.

words.ex: The man was incarcerated for stealing.
words.ex_cn: 这个人因偷窃而被监禁。
words.en: If people are incarcerated, they are kept in a prison or other place.

words.ex: The wheelchair goes up the ramp easily.
words.ex_cn: 轮椅可以轻松地走上坡道。
words.en: A ramp is a sloping surface connecting two levels, such as a road or a path.

words.ex: He delves into the history of ancient civilizations.
words.ex_cn: 他探究古代文明的历史。
words.en: If you delve into something, you try to discover new information about it by searching or investigating carefully.

words.tr:
v. 斗嘴；闪烁
n. 口角
words.ex: They bicker over small things every day.
words.ex_cn: 他们每天为小事争吵。
words.en: If people bicker, they argue or quarrel about unimportant things.

words.tr:
n. 织布机；
v. 迫近；
words.ex: The old loom made a loud clicking sound.
words.ex_cn: 那台旧织布机发出很大的咔嗒声。
words.en: If something looms over you, it appears as a large or unclear shape, often in a way that is frightening or causes worry.

words.ex: He is grappled with the math problem for hours.
words.ex_cn: 他花了好几个小时努力解决这道数学题。
words.en: To grapple with something means to try hard to understand or deal with a difficult problem or subject.

words.tr: adj. 灵巧的（手）；熟练的；敏捷的
words.ex: He is dexterous with his hands.
words.ex_cn: 他双手很灵巧。
words.en: Someone who is dexterous is skillful with their hands.

words.ex: The old man walked with a slow gait.
words.ex_cn: 老人走路步伐缓慢。
words.en: A person's manner of walking.

words.tr: v. 撕碎；劈开；揪扯；割裂
words.ex: The storm rends the tree from its roots.
words.ex_cn: 暴风雨将树从根部撕裂。
words.en: To tear or split something apart with great force.

words.tr: adj. 断断续续的；一阵阵的
words.ex: He had fitful sleep last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚睡得断断续续。
words.en: Something that is fitful happens for irregular periods of time or occurs at irregular times, rather than being continuous.

words.ex: The walls were painted a drab color.
words.ex_cn: 墙壁被刷成了土褐色。
words.en: If you describe something as drab, you think that it is dull and boring to look at or experience.

words.tr: adj. 无道德观念的；不辨是非的
words.ex: He made an amoral decision to lie for money.
words.ex_cn: 他为了钱做出了一个不道德的决定。
words.en: If you describe someone as amoral, you mean that they do not consider whether their behavior is morally right or wrong.

words.tr:
v. 散发臭气；发出难闻的气味；洋溢；充满
n. 恶臭；难闻的气味
words.ex: The garbage reeks in the hot sun.
words.ex_cn: 垃圾在烈日下散发恶臭。
words.en: To reek of something means to smell very strongly of it, especially in an unpleasant way.

words.ex: He unraveled the knotted string.
words.ex_cn: 他把打结的绳子拆散了。
words.en: To unravel means to separate or disentangle the threads of a fabric or a rope, or to solve or explain something that is complicated or mysterious.

words.tr: v. 连续猛击；反复拳打；捶打
words.ex: The boxer pummels his opponent with fast punches.
words.ex_cn: 拳击手用快速的拳击击打他的对手。
words.en: To pummel someone or something means to hit them many times using your fists.

words.tr: adj. 合适的；得体的；合乎礼仪的
words.ex: He dressed in a seemly way for the interview.
words.ex_cn: 他为了面试穿得得体。
words.en: Seemly behavior or actions are those that are appropriate and suitable for a particular situation.

words.ex: He envisions a world without war.
words.ex_cn: 他想象一个没有战争的世界。
words.en: To envision something is to imagine it as a future possibility; it is often used to describe the act of foreseeing or planning for the future.

words.tr: n. 飞地；被包围的领土
words.ex: The village is an enclave surrounded by forest.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄是一个被森林包围的飞地。
words.en: An enclave is a part of a country or a group of people that is surrounded by another country or group of people.

words.tr:
v. 弥漫；
adj. 分散的；
words.ex: Smoke began to diffuse through the room.
words.ex_cn: 烟开始弥漫在整个房间里。
words.en: If something such as knowledge or information is diffused, or if it diffuses, it is made known over a wide area or to a lot of people.

words.ex: The chair is inanimate.
words.ex_cn: 这把椅子是没有生命的。
words.en: Something that is inanimate is not alive, such as a rock or a chair. It can also describe something that lacks energy or spirit.

words.ex: The government decided to abolish the old law.
words.ex_cn: 政府决定废除这项旧法律。
words.en: If someone in authority abolishes a system or practice, they formally put an end to it.

words.ex: The pope is considered infallible in matters of faith by some Catholics.
words.ex_cn: 一些天主教徒认为教皇在信仰问题上是一贯正确的。
words.en: If a person or thing is infallible, they are never wrong or never fail.

words.tr:
n. 熏香；熏香的烟
v. 使愤怒；激怒
words.ex: The smell of incense fills the room.
words.ex_cn: 香火的气味充满了房间。
words.en: Incense is a substance that is burned for its pleasant smell, often used in religious ceremonies. As a verb, to incense means to make someone very angry.

words.ex: The cost of lunch was incidental to the main expense.
words.ex_cn: 午餐的费用是主要开销的附带部分。
words.en: If one thing is incidental to another, it is less important than the other thing or is not a major part of it.

words.ex: The music is evocative of childhood memories.
words.ex_cn: 这音乐唤起了童年的回忆。
words.en: If you describe something as evocative, you mean that it is good or interesting because it produces pleasant memories, ideas, emotions, and responses in people.

words.ex: The iron fence will corrode in the rain.
words.ex_cn: 铁栅栏在雨中会生锈。
words.en: If metal or stone corrodes, or if something corrodes it, it is gradually destroyed by a chemical reaction.

words.tr:
v. 争论；讲价
n. 讨价还价；争论
words.ex: They haggle over the price of the car.
words.ex_cn: 他们为汽车的价格争论。
words.en: If you haggle, you argue about something, especially about the price of something you want to buy.

words.tr: adj. 文雅的；有教养的；上流社会的；装绅士派头的
words.ex: She spoke in a genteel way at the dinner party.
words.ex_cn: 她在晚宴上说话很文雅。
words.en: Someone who is genteel behaves in a polite and refined way, often in a manner that is considered typical of someone from a high social class.

words.tr: v. 黏合；连结；附着；连贯；形成整体
words.ex: The pieces cohere to form a complete picture.
words.ex_cn: 这些碎片组合在一起形成一幅完整的图画。
words.en: If the different elements of a piece of writing, a theory, or a policy cohere, they fit together well so that they form a united whole.

words.ex: The teacher exhorts students to study hard.
words.ex_cn: 老师敦促学生努力学习。
words.en: To strongly encourage or try to persuade someone to do something.

words.ex: She was betrothed to a wealthy businessman.
words.ex_cn: 她与一位富商订婚了。
words.en: To promise to marry someone or to be married to someone.

words.ex: The spy tried to infiltrate the enemy base.
words.ex_cn: 间谍试图渗透敌方基地。
words.en: To enter or gain access to (an organization, place, etc.) surreptitiously and gradually, especially in order to acquire secret information.

words.tr:
adv. 有毛病地；出差错地；不合适地
adj. 有毛病的；出差错的；不合适的
words.ex: Something is amiss with the machine.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器有些不对劲。
words.en: If something is amiss, there is something wrong.

words.tr: adj. 物质的；有形的；实体的；身体的
words.ex: He believes that the soul is not corporeal.
words.ex_cn: 他相信灵魂不是物质的。
words.en: Relating to a person's body, especially as opposed to their spirit.

words.ex: He tries to invert the numbers to find the answer.
words.ex_cn: 他试图将数字倒过来以找到答案。
words.en: To invert something means to turn it upside down or to reverse its position, order, or relationship.

words.ex: The meek boy quietly listened to the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 那个温顺的男孩静静地听老师讲课。
words.en: If you describe a person as meek, you think that they are gentle and quiet, and likely to do what other people say.

words.tr: adj. 美味的；使人愉快的
words.ex: The cake was delectable.
words.ex_cn: 这个蛋糕非常美味。
words.en: If you describe something, especially food or drink, as delectable, you mean that it is very pleasant.

words.ex: The old computer is antiquated and slow.
words.ex_cn: 这台旧电脑过时且缓慢。
words.en: Something that is antiquated is old-fashioned or outdated and no longer suitable for modern conditions or purposes.

words.tr:
v. （风）狂吹；咆哮；恫吓；咄咄逼人
n. 狂风声；咆哮；吓唬；夸口
words.ex: The wind blustered through the trees all night.
words.ex_cn: 风整晚狂吹着穿过树木。
words.en: If you say that someone is blustering, you mean that they are speaking aggressively but without authority, often because they are angry or offended.

words.ex: The ancient text contained arcane symbols that no one could understand.
words.ex_cn: 这本古籍中包含着无人能理解的晦涩难解的符号。
words.en: Arcane refers to something that is mysterious or difficult to understand, often because it is known or understood by only a few people.

words.tr:
adv. 头向前地；倒栽葱地；急速地；鲁莽地
adj. 头向前的；倒栽葱的；急速的；急骤的
words.ex: He jumped headlong into the pool.
words.ex_cn: 他头向前地跳进了泳池。
words.en: If you move headlong in a particular direction, you move there very quickly and without thinking carefully about what you are doing.

words.tr: adj. 爱管闲事的；爱打听的
words.ex: The nosy neighbor always asks too many questions.
words.ex_cn: 那个爱管闲事的邻居总是问太多问题。
words.en: If you describe someone as nosy, you mean that they are too interested in things that do not concern them, especially other people's affairs.

words.ex: He felt tired after the exertion of running up the hill.
words.ex_cn: 在努力跑上山后，他感到很累。
words.en: The use of physical or mental energy; hard work.

words.tr:
n. 垂饰；悬挂物
adj. 吊着的；悬垂的；悬而未决的
words.ex: She wears a silver pendant around her neck.
words.ex_cn: 她戴着一条银色吊坠在脖子上。
words.en: A pendant is a piece of jewelry that hangs from a chain worn around the neck.

words.ex: He enjoys solitude in the woods.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢在森林中独处。
words.en: The state or situation of being alone.

words.ex: He made an uncouth remark at dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他在晚餐时说了句粗俗的话。
words.en: If you describe a person as uncouth, you mean that their behavior is vulgar, rude, or socially unacceptable.

words.ex: The army besiege the small town.
words.ex_cn: 军队围攻这座小镇。
words.en: To surround a place with armed forces in order to capture it or force its surrender; to overwhelm someone with requests or complaints.

words.ex: The two houses are adjacent to each other.
words.ex_cn: 这两栋房子彼此相邻。
words.en: If one thing is adjacent to another, it is next to it or adjoining it.

words.tr:
n. 雪橇
v. 乘雪橇
words.ex: The children enjoyed riding on the sleigh.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们喜欢乘雪橇。
words.en: A sleigh is a vehicle which slides over snow, usually pulled by a horse.

words.ex: The farmer works hard to sustain his crops.
words.ex_cn: 这位农民努力维持他的庄稼。
words.en: To sustain something means to continue it or maintain it for a period of time.

words.ex: His converse was the opposite of what he said earlier.
words.ex_cn: 他的相反言论与他之前说的话相反。
words.en: To engage in conversation; to talk informally with someone.

words.ex: The two roads converge at the town center.
words.ex_cn: 这两条路在镇中心交汇。
words.en: If roads or lines converge, they meet or join at a particular place.

words.ex: He adapted to the new school quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他很快就适应了新学校。
words.en: To make suitable to or fit for a specific use or situation.

words.ex: Her irrepressible laugh filled the room.
words.ex_cn: 她抑制不住的笑声充满了房间。
words.en: If someone is irrepressible, they are full of energy and enthusiasm and cannot be controlled or stopped.

words.ex: That park was in its heyday in the 1990s.
words.ex_cn: 那个公园在20世纪90年代是它的鼎盛时期。
words.en: The period of a person's or thing's greatest success, popularity, or vigor.

words.ex: The temperature increases by one increment every hour.
words.ex_cn: 温度每小时增加一个单位。
words.en: An increment is an amount by which something increases or is increased.

words.ex: The course covers a wide breadth of topics.
words.ex_cn: 这门课程涵盖了广泛的主题。
words.en: The distance or measurement from side to side of something; width.

words.ex: It is muggy outside today.
words.ex_cn: 今天外面闷热。
words.en: If you describe the weather as muggy, you mean that it is unpleasantly warm and damp.

words.ex: The gentry owned most of the land in the old village.
words.ex_cn: 绅士阶层拥有这个古老村庄的大部分土地。
words.en: The gentry are people of high social class, especially in the past.

words.ex: The incidence of flu increased last winter.
words.ex_cn: 去年冬天流感的发生率上升了。
words.en: The incidence of something is the frequency with which it occurs or the rate at which it happens.

words.ex: The old man looked gaunt after his illness.
words.ex_cn: 这场病后，老人显得消瘦。
words.en: If someone looks gaunt, they look very thin, usually because they have been ill or worried.

words.ex: He can articulate his ideas clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他能清楚地表达自己的想法。
words.en: If you describe someone as articulate, you mean that they are able to express their thoughts and ideas easily and clearly.

words.tr: v. 提出；提议；提出…供考虑
words.ex: He propound a new theory in class.
words.ex_cn: 他在课堂上提出了一种新理论。
words.en: To propound means to suggest or put forward an idea, theory, or point of view for consideration.

words.tr:
v. 神气十足地走；大摇大摆地走
n. 大摇大摆；神气十足
words.ex: He walks with swagger down the street.
words.ex_cn: 他大摇大摆地走在街上。
words.en: If someone swaggers, they walk in a very proud and confident way, often in a way that annoys other people.

words.ex: Exercise can reinforce your muscles.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以增强你的肌肉。
words.en: To reinforce something means to make it stronger or more effective.

words.ex: She daubed the wall with paint.
words.ex_cn: 她在墙上随意涂抹颜料。
words.en: To daub means to spread a substance such as paint, mud, or oil over a surface in a rough or careless way.

words.ex: The heavy fine is a deterrent to cheating.
words.ex_cn: 高额罚款是一种威慑作弊的力量。
words.en: Something that discourages or is intended to discourage someone from doing something.

words.tr: adj. 绝对的；确定无疑的；分类的
words.ex: He gave a categorical no to the offer.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个提议给出了明确的拒绝。
words.en: If you are categorical about something, you state your views very definitely and firmly.

words.tr:
v. 沉思
n. （作家、画家等的）灵感；缪斯
words.ex: He often muses about the meaning of life.
words.ex_cn: 他常常沉思生命的意义。
words.en: In Greek mythology, the Muses are the goddesses of the inspiration of literature, science and the arts. As a verb, to muse means to think about something carefully and for a long time.

words.ex: This rule pertains to all students.
words.ex_cn: 这条规则适用于所有学生。
words.en: If one thing pertains to another, it relates, belongs, or applies to it.

words.ex: A quiet room is conducive to studying.
words.ex_cn: 安静的房间有助于学习。
words.en: If one thing is conducive to another thing, it makes the other thing likely to happen.

words.ex: He used an idiom to explain his idea.
words.ex_cn: 他用了一个成语来解释他的想法。
words.en: An idiom is a group of words in a fixed order that have a particular meaning that is different from the meanings of each word on its own.

words.tr: v. 感到极度焦虑；折磨；苦苦思索
words.ex: He agonizes over his decision every night.
words.ex_cn: 他每天晚上都为自己的决定而痛苦挣扎。
words.en: To agonize over something means to spend a lot of time worrying and being anxious about it.

words.ex: The wizard conjure a fireball with ancient words.
words.ex_cn: 巫师用古老的咒语召唤出一个火球。
words.en: If you conjure something out of nothing, you make it appear as if by magic.

words.ex: The danger impels him to act quickly.
words.ex_cn: 危险驱使他迅速行动。
words.en: If something impels you to do something, it makes you feel very strongly that you must do it.

words.ex: The sentence has ambiguity because it can mean two things.
words.ex_cn: 这句话有歧义，因为它可以有两种意思。
words.en: If you say that there is ambiguity in something, you mean that it is unclear or confusing, or it can be understood in more than one way.

words.ex: The rules show uniformity in all schools.
words.ex_cn: 这些规则在所有学校中都保持一致。
words.en: The state or quality of being uniform; consistency.

words.ex: He lives in a big metropolis with many tall buildings.
words.ex_cn: 他住在一个有很多高楼的大都市里。
words.en: A metropolis is a very large city, often the most important city in a country or area.

words.ex: He is a glutton who eats too much candy.
words.ex_cn: 他是个贪吃糖的暴食者。
words.en: A glutton is a person who eats and drinks excessively or voraciously.

words.tr: n. 入学介绍；岗前训练；方向；取向；
words.ex: The school held an orientation for new students on Monday.
words.ex_cn: 学校在周一为新生举行了入学介绍。
words.en: The act of orienting or the state of being oriented; the determination of the relative position of something or someone (especially oneself).

words.tr: n. 诘问者；激烈质问者
words.ex: The heckler shouted during the speech.
words.ex_cn: 那个挑衅者在演讲期间大喊大叫。
words.en: A heckler is someone who interrupts a performer or speaker, often with rude or aggressive comments.

words.ex: His conceit makes him ignore others' advice.
words.ex_cn: 他的自负让他忽视别人的建议。
words.en: An excessively favorable opinion of one's own abilities or worth; vanity.

words.tr: v. 解除武装；缴械；裁减军备
words.ex: The soldier will disarm the bomb.
words.ex_cn: 士兵将拆除炸弹。
words.en: To disarm someone means to make them less hostile or suspicious by removing their weapons or by being friendly.

words.tr:
v. 集合起来；振作；复苏
n. 集会
words.ex: The crowd rallied to support their team.
words.ex_cn: 人群聚集起来支持他们的球队。
words.en: A rally is a large public meeting that is held in order to show support for something such as a political party or a sports team. It can also mean to come together again in order to continue fighting or arguing after a defeat or a period of confusion.

words.ex: The expansive desert stretches for miles.
words.ex_cn: 广阔的沙漠延伸数英里。
words.en: If you describe something such as a period of time or a piece of writing as expansive, you mean that it is very long or detailed.

words.ex: The ball has a convex surface.
words.ex_cn: 这个球有一个凸出的表面。
words.en: A convex surface curves outward in the middle.

words.ex: He alleges that the manager stole money.
words.ex_cn: 他声称经理偷了钱。
words.en: If you allege that something bad is true, you say it but do not prove it.

words.tr: adj. 美味的；甘美的；满足感官的；性感的
words.ex: The fruit was luscious and sweet.
words.ex_cn: 这种水果甘甜可口。
words.en: If you describe something as luscious, you mean that it is very pleasant to taste, smell, look at, or listen to.

words.ex: The aftermath of the storm left many trees down.
words.ex_cn: 风暴过后，许多树被吹倒了。
words.en: The aftermath of an important event, especially a harmful one, is the situation that results from it.

words.tr:
v. 用布包裹；用绷带缠
n. 长而宽的一长条；割刈的带状地
words.ex: She swathed the baby in a soft blanket.
words.ex_cn: 她用一条柔软的毯子把婴儿裹起来。
words.en: To wrap or bind in or as if in a bandage or cloth.

words.tr: adj. 令人兴奋的； v. “exhilarate”的现在分词；
words.ex: The roller coaster ride was exhilarating.
words.ex_cn: 过山车之旅令人兴奋。
words.en: If you describe something as exhilarating, you mean that it makes you feel very happy and excited.

words.tr: adj. 根本的；潜在的； v. “underlie”的现在分词；
words.ex: The underlying cause of the problem is poverty.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题的根本原因是贫困。
words.en: An underlying thing is the thing that is the most important or basic, although it is not easily noticed or stated directly.

words.ex: He changed his stance on climate change.
words.ex_cn: 他改变了对气候变化的立场。
words.en: A stance is a particular way of standing, especially in sports such as golf or baseball, or a person's attitude or opinion about something, especially when it is stated publicly.

words.tr: v. 毕业；“graduate”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 标有刻度的；
words.ex: He graduated from high school last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年从高中毕业。
words.en: Having successfully completed a course of study and received a degree or diploma.

words.ex: He tried to counterfeit money.
words.ex_cn: 他试图伪造货币。
words.en: Made in exact imitation of something valuable with the intention to deceive or defraud.

words.tr: v. 剥夺…的权利（尤指选举权）
words.ex: The law disenfranchises many poor people.
words.ex_cn: 这项法律剥夺了许多穷人的投票权。
words.en: To disenfranchise someone means to take away their right to vote or to deprive them of a privilege or a right.

words.tr: v. 驱（魔）；除去（痛苦的想法等）
words.ex: The priest tried to exorcise the demon from the house.
words.ex_cn: 牧师试图将恶魔从房子里驱逐出去。
words.en: To exorcise means to drive out or attempt to drive out (a supposed evil spirit) from a person or place.

words.ex: He collates the papers before the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议前整理了这些文件。
words.en: To collate information or data means to collect it together and examine it carefully in order to compare it or find something out.

words.ex: Italian cuisine is famous for pasta and pizza.
words.ex_cn: 意大利烹调风格以意大利面和披萨闻名。
words.en: A style or method of cooking, especially as characteristic of a particular country, region, or establishment.

words.ex: He decided to embark on a new career.
words.ex_cn: 他决定从事一份新职业。
words.en: To embark on something means to start it, especially something new, difficult, or exciting.

words.ex: The empress ruled the empire with wisdom.
words.ex_cn: 皇后以智慧统治帝国。
words.en: A woman who is the sovereign ruler of an empire or the wife of an emperor.

words.tr: v. 使慌张；使窘迫；使不安
words.ex: The sudden noise disconcerted her.
words.ex_cn: 突然的噪音让她感到不安。
words.en: If something disconcerts you, it makes you feel anxious, confused, or embarrassed.

words.ex: His speech was full of incoherence.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲充满了不连贯。
words.en: Incoherence is the quality of being unclear, confused, or not logical, especially in thought or speech.

words.tr:
n. (从事某项活动的)规定期限
v. 吝惜；节省
words.ex: He did a short stint as a teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他短暂地当过一段时间老师。
words.en: A stint is a fixed period of time during which someone does a particular job or activity.

words.tr:
v. 生产；获利；
n. 产量；
words.ex: This farm yields a lot of wheat each year.
words.ex_cn: 这个农场每年生产大量小麦。
words.en: If you yield to someone or something, you stop resisting them. If a tree or plant yields fruit or flowers, it produces them.

words.tr: v. 浸入水中；泼上水；熄灭
words.ex: He doused the burning log in water.
words.ex_cn: 他把燃烧的木头浸入水中。
words.en: To douse something means to quickly throw water over it in order to put out a fire, or to pour a lot of liquid over it.

words.tr: adj. 绝望的；孤立无助的；被弃置的
words.ex: The forlorn dog sat by the door, waiting for its owner.
words.ex_cn: 那条孤单的狗坐在门边，等待它的主人。
words.en: If someone is forlorn, they feel alone and unhappy.

words.tr:
v. 假定；要求
n. 假定；假设
words.ex: He postulates that all humans are equal.
words.ex_cn: 他假定所有人都是平等的。
words.en: If you postulate something, you suggest it as the basis for a theory, argument, or calculation.

words.ex: A small fissure appeared in the wall.
words.ex_cn: 墙上出现了一道小裂缝。
words.en: A fissure is a long, narrow opening or line of breakage made by cracking or splitting, especially in rock or earth.

words.ex: The police confiscate illegal drugs.
words.ex_cn: 警察没收非法毒品。
words.en: If you confiscate something from someone, you take it away from them, usually as a punishment.

words.ex: He tried to disabuse her of the idea that money solves everything.
words.ex_cn: 他试图让她明白，钱并不能解决所有问题。
words.en: If you disabuse someone of something, you tell them or persuade them that what they believe is in fact not true.

words.ex: The children are vibrant and full of energy.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们充满活力。
words.en: If you describe something as vibrant, you mean that it is bright, lively, and full of energy.

words.ex: The new policy is problematic for small businesses.
words.ex_cn: 这项新政策对小企业来说成问题。
words.en: If something is problematic, it involves problems and is difficult to deal with or solve.

words.tr:
n. 傻笑；假笑
v. 傻笑；自鸣得意地笑
words.ex: He gave a smirk when he won the game.
