words.ex_cn: 他赢了比赛时露出了冷笑。
words.en: A smirk is a smile expressing smugness or scorn instead of pleasure.

words.tr: adj. 讨厌的；令人厌烦的
words.ex: The long meeting was tiresome.
words.ex_cn: 这场漫长的会议很讨厌。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as tiresome, you mean that you find them irritating or boring.

words.tr: n. 痴迷；困扰；着魔；强迫观念；
words.ex: His obsession with video games made him ignore his studies.
words.ex_cn: 他对电子游戏的痴迷让他忽略了学业。
words.en: An obsession is an idea or thought that continually preoccupies or intrudes on a person's mind.

words.tr:
v. 挤；推；撞；争夺
n. 挤拥；推撞
words.ex: People jostle in the crowded market.
words.ex_cn: 人们在拥挤的市场里推挤。
words.en: To jostle someone means to push or knock against them, usually in a crowd.

words.ex: The unexpected news discombobulated her.
words.ex_cn: 突如其来的消息使她感到困惑。
words.en: To discombobulate someone means to confuse them a lot.

words.tr:
adj. 颠覆性的；破坏性的
n. 颠覆分子；危险分子
words.ex: The subversive poster tried to break the government's rules.
words.ex_cn: 那张颠覆性的海报试图破坏政府的规则。
words.en: A subversive person or activity is one that is intended to weaken or destroy a political system or government.

words.ex: The plastic is pliable and easy to bend.
words.ex_cn: 这种塑料柔韧，容易弯曲。
words.en: A pliable object or material is easy to bend or shape without breaking.

words.ex: He is my confidant and I tell him everything.
words.ex_cn: 他是我的知己，我什么都告诉他。
words.en: A confidant is someone you can share your secrets with or discuss personal matters with, knowing that they will keep your information private.

words.ex: The river is contaminated by factory waste.
words.ex_cn: 这条河被工厂废料污染了。
words.en: To contaminate something means to make it impure or polluted by contact or mixture with something unclean or harmful.

words.tr:
adj. 即时的；未经准备的；唐突无礼的
adv. 即时地；未经思索地；随便地
words.ex: He gave an offhand answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个即时的回答。
words.en: If you say something offhand, you say it without checking the details or facts of it beforehand.

words.tr: n. 认识；知晓；察觉；注意
words.ex: He took cognizance of the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他注意到了这个错误。
words.en: Cognizance is the state or quality of being aware or having knowledge of something.

words.tr: v. 改编为戏剧；渲染；使戏剧化
words.ex: They dramatize the novel for the stage.
words.ex_cn: 他们将这部小说改编成舞台剧。
words.en: If a book or story is dramatized, it is written or presented as a play, film, or television drama.

words.tr:
adj. 富有经验的；加佐料的；风干的
v. 给 ... 调味；适应；风干；“season”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He is a seasoned cook with many years of experience.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位有多年经验的熟练厨师。
words.en: If someone is seasoned, they have a lot of experience of something and are therefore able to deal with it in a confident way.

words.tr:
n. 保护区；储备；保留；
v. 预订；
words.ex: The wildlife reserve is home to many endangered animals.
words.ex_cn: 这个自然保护区是许多濒危动物的家园。
words.en: If you reserve something such as a table, ticket, or magazine, you arrange for it to be kept for you and not given to anyone else.

words.ex: His infirmity made it hard to walk.
words.ex_cn: 他的虚弱使他走路困难。
words.en: An infirmity is a physical or mental weakness.

words.tr:
v. 密谋；激起…的兴趣
n. 阴谋诡计；密谋策划
words.ex: They intrigue to take over the company.
words.ex_cn: 他们密谋接管这家公司。
words.en: If something intrigues you, it interests you a lot because it seems strange or mysterious.

words.ex: He is the recipient of the prize.
words.ex_cn: 他是这个奖项的接受者。
words.en: A recipient is a person who receives something.

words.tr: adj. 赤贫的；贫困的；一无所有的；
words.ex: The destitute family had no food or shelter.
words.ex_cn: 这个赤贫的家庭没有食物和住所。
words.en: If you describe someone as destitute, you mean they have absolutely nothing, especially no money.

words.tr: v. 使浸透；使湿透；使满；使饱和
words.ex: The sponge will saturate if you pour too much water.
words.ex_cn: 如果你倒太多水，海绵会吸满。
words.en: To saturate something means to make it completely wet, or to fill it completely with something so that no more can be added.

words.ex: He outwit the opponent with a clever trick.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个聪明的计策胜过了对手。
words.en: To outwit someone means to use your intelligence or a clever trick to defeat them or gain an advantage over them.

words.tr: adj. 不定时发生的；时有时无的；零星的
words.ex: He makes sporadic visits to his grandparents.
words.ex_cn: 他时不时去看望他的祖父母。
words.en: occurring at irregular intervals or only in a few places; scattered or isolated

words.ex: The company will deploy new software next week.
words.ex_cn: 公司将在下周部署新软件。
words.en: To deploy troops or military resources means to organize or position them so that they are ready to be used.

words.ex: He made an expeditious decision to leave.
words.ex_cn: 他迅速做出了离开的决定。
words.en: If you describe something as expeditious, you mean that it is done quickly and efficiently.

words.tr:
adj. 向外弯曲的；罗圈的
n. 简化式曲棍球
v. 把（球）打来打去；来回摆弄；交换；议论
words.ex: He has a bandy leg from playing football for years.
words.ex_cn: 他因为多年踢足球而有一条罗圈腿。
words.en: If you bandy words with someone, you argue or quarrel with them in an aggressive or unpleasant way.

words.tr: adj. 值得注意的；显著的；
words.ex: This result is noteworthy because it changes our understanding.
words.ex_cn: 这个结果值得注意，因为它改变了我们的理解。
words.en: If you describe something as noteworthy, you mean that it is interesting, significant, or important enough to deserve attention or to be noticed.

words.ex: People often stigmatize those with mental illness.
words.ex_cn: 人们常常污名化患有精神疾病的人。
words.en: If someone or something is stigmatized, they are unfairly regarded by many people as being bad or having something to be ashamed of.

words.tr: adj. 洪亮的；共振的；引起共鸣的；
words.ex: The bell has a resonant sound.
words.ex_cn: 这口钟的声音洪亮。
words.en: A sound that is resonant is deep, strong, and clear, often because it is produced in a space that echoes or amplifies it.

words.ex: The book has a compact design.
words.ex_cn: 这本书的设计很紧凑。
words.en: A compact object or substance is small and dense, with all its parts closely packed together.

words.ex: The extent of his knowledge surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他的知识广度让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: The area or length to which something extends.

words.tr:
v. 猛击；打；击
n. 敲打；猛击；影响力
words.ex: He clouted the ball with his bat.
words.ex_cn: 他用球棒猛击了球。
words.en: Clout refers to the power or influence that someone has, especially in politics or business.

words.ex: The confluence of the two rivers created a fertile valley.
words.ex_cn: 两条河流的汇流形成了一个肥沃的山谷。
words.en: The confluence of two or more things is the junction or merging of them, often forming something greater or more complex.

words.ex: You need basic math as a prerequisite for this course.
words.ex_cn: 你学习这门课程的前提是掌握基础数学。
words.en: A prerequisite is something that must exist or happen before something else can exist or happen.

words.tr: adj. 爱发号施令的；多管闲事的
words.ex: The officious clerk refused to help unless I filled out another form.
words.ex_cn: 那位爱多管闲事的职员拒绝帮忙，除非我再填一份表格。
words.en: If you describe someone as officious, you are critical of them because they are eager to tell people what to do when you think they should not.

words.ex: The effects of the medication are impermanent.
words.ex_cn: 这种药物的效果是暂时的。
words.en: Something that is impermanent does not last forever or for a very long time.

words.ex: The family is in a difficult plight after losing their home.
words.ex_cn: 这家人在失去家园后陷入了困境。
words.en: A plight is a difficult or adverse situation, especially one that is hard to escape. It can also refer to a solemn promise or pledge.

words.ex: He is an equable man who never gets angry.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个性情恬静的人，从不生气。
words.en: If you describe someone as equable, you mean that they are calm, cheerful, and fair with other people, even in difficult circumstances.

words.ex: He accepted a nominal fee for the service.
words.ex_cn: 他为这项服务收取了微不足道的费用。
words.en: If you say that something is nominal, you mean that it is very small in comparison to the real value or importance of something.

words.ex: He was known for his venturesome spirit and willingness to take risks.
words.ex_cn: 他以冒险精神和愿意承担风险而闻名。
words.en: If you describe someone as venturesome, you mean that they are willing to take risks, especially in order to try out new things.

words.tr: adj. 使用多种语言的；说多种语言的；
words.ex: He is a multilingual teacher who speaks three languages.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位会说三种语言的多语言教师。
words.en: Using or able to use several languages.

words.tr: n. 前任；前辈；原有事物
words.ex: He became the new manager, replacing his predecessor.
words.ex_cn: 他成为了新经理，接替了他的前任。
words.en: A predecessor is someone who had a job or a position before someone else, or something that comes before another thing in time or in a series.

words.tr:
n. 路障；栅栏；阻碍
v. 设路障；阻挡
words.ex: The police put up a barricade to stop the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 警察设了一个路障来阻止人群。
words.en: A barricade is a temporary structure that is built across a road, entrance, or other route to prevent people from passing. It can also refer to the act of creating such a structure.

words.ex: He compiles data from many surveys.
words.ex_cn: 他汇编来自许多调查的数据。
words.en: To compile means to collect information from different places and arrange it in a book, report, or list.

words.ex: The game simulates real traffic conditions.
words.ex_cn: 这个游戏模拟了真实的交通状况。
words.en: To simulate is to create a model or representation of a situation, process, or system for the purpose of study, analysis, or training. It involves imitating the conditions of a real event or environment to understand its effects or to practice responses to it.

words.tr:
n. 污染；腐坏；玷污
v. 污染；使腐坏；玷污
words.ex: The water has a taint from the factory waste.
words.ex_cn: 这种水因工厂废料而受到污染。
words.en: If something is tainted, it is affected by something bad or undesirable.

words.ex: Honesty is a great virtue.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是一种伟大的美德。
words.en: A virtue is a good quality or way of behaving.

words.tr: v. 遗赠；遗留；把…传下去
words.ex: He bequeathed his house to his daughter.
words.ex_cn: 他把房子遗赠给了他的女儿。
words.en: If you bequeath your money or property to someone, you legally state that they should have it when you die.

words.tr:
n. 提示；
v. 促使；
adj. 迅速的；准时的；
words.ex: The teacher gave a prompt to help students start writing.
words.ex_cn: 老师给了一个提示，帮助学生开始写作。
words.en: If you prompt someone when they stop speaking, you encourage or help them to continue. If you are prompt to do something, you do it without delay or you are not late.

words.tr: n. 冲击；主力；首当其冲
words.ex: The farmers bore the brunt of the drought.
words.ex_cn: 农民们承受了干旱的主要打击。
words.en: The main force or impact of something, especially something unpleasant.

words.ex: The baby ate the tender broccoli.
words.ex_cn: 宝宝吃了嫩的西兰花。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as tender, you mean that they are kind, gentle, and sympathetic. If meat or other food is tender, it is easy to cut or chew. To tender something such as a service or a resignation means to formally offer or present it.

words.tr:
n. 叛徒；变节者；叛教者
adj. 背叛的；变节的
v. 背叛
words.ex: He is a renegade who left the team suddenly.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个突然离开团队的叛徒。
words.en: A renegade is a person who deserts and betrays an organization, country, or set of principles.

words.ex: The gland secrete sweat to cool the body.
words.ex_cn: 腺体分泌汗液来降温。
words.en: If part of a plant, animal, or human secretes a liquid or substance, it produces it.

words.tr: adj. 卑屈的；恭顺的；次要的；从属的
words.ex: He is subservient to his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他对他的老板唯命是从。
words.en: If you are subservient, you do whatever someone wants you to do.

words.ex: The fugitive hid in the woods for weeks.
words.ex_cn: 这名逃亡者在树林里躲了几个星期。
words.en: A fugitive is someone who is running away or hiding, usually in order to avoid being caught by the police.

words.tr:
v. 握紧；捏紧；咬牙切齿
n. 抓紧；咬紧；抓紧用具
words.ex: He clenched his fist when he heard the news.
words.ex_cn: 他听到这个消息时握紧了拳头。
words.en: To close or hold something very tightly, especially in a determined or angry way.

words.tr: v. 教唆；收买；贿赂某人作伪证
words.ex: He tried to suborn a witness with money.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用钱收买证人。
words.en: To induce someone to commit an unlawful or wrongful act, especially to give false testimony in court.

words.tr:
n. 丛；笨重的脚步声；土块
v. 使成一丛；凝结成块；拖着沉重的步子走
words.ex: The grass formed a clump near the fence.
words.ex_cn: 草在篱笆附近长成了一簇。
words.en: A clump of things such as trees or plants is a small group of them growing together. A clump of earth or mud is a small, solid mass of it.

words.tr:
v. 酿造；沏；酝酿
n. 酿造的饮料；啤酒
words.ex: He brews coffee every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上冲咖啡。
words.en: If you brew tea or coffee, you make it by pouring hot water over tea leaves or ground coffee. If you brew beer, you make it by soaking grain in water and then fermenting it.

words.ex: He tried to eavesdrop on their conversation.
words.ex_cn: 他试图偷听他们的对话。
words.en: To eavesdrop means to listen secretly to other people's conversations.

words.tr: adj. 无节制的；不能保持的；失禁的
words.ex: He is incontinent after the surgery.
words.ex_cn: 他手术后无法控制排尿。
words.en: Lacking voluntary control over urination or defecation; unable to restrain natural impulses or desires.

words.tr:
n. 球类运动（squash）；
v. 压碎；
words.ex: He plays squash every weekend with his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他每周末和朋友打壁球。
words.en: To squash something means to press or squeeze it so that it becomes flat, soft, or out of shape. It can also refer to the sport of squash or a type of vegetable.

words.tr: adj. 感觉不到的；极细微的
words.ex: The change was imperceptible to the naked eye.
words.ex_cn: 这个变化肉眼无法察觉。
words.en: Something that is imperceptible is so small or slight that it cannot be seen or noticed.

words.tr: v. 神化；把…奉若神明；崇拜
words.ex: They deify their ancient heroes.
words.ex_cn: 他们崇拜自己的古代英雄。
words.en: To treat someone or something as a god or goddess, or to consider them as if they were divine.

words.tr:
n. 轭；枷锁；束缚
v. 上轭；使强行结合
words.ex: The farmer put a yoke on the oxen.
words.ex_cn: 农夫给牛套上了轭。
words.en: A yoke is a wooden bar that is fastened over the necks of two animals, especially cattle, and connected to the vehicle or load that they are pulling. It can also refer to something that binds people together or something that people find oppressive.

words.ex: The inverse order of the numbers is 5, 4, 3, 2, 1.
words.ex_cn: 这些数字的倒序是5、4、3、2、1。
words.en: If there is an inverse relationship between two things, one of them becomes larger as the other becomes smaller.

words.tr: adj. 婚姻的；夫妻（关系）的
words.ex: They have a connubial relationship after 30 years of marriage.
words.ex_cn: 他们结婚30年后依然有着婚姻关系。
words.en: Relating to marriage or the relationship between a husband and wife.

words.ex: The band will disband next month.
words.ex_cn: 这个乐队下个月将解散。
words.en: If someone disbands a group of people, or if the group disbands, it stops operating as a single unit.

words.ex: The test results confirm he has the disease.
words.ex_cn: 检测结果证实他患有这种疾病。
words.en: To confirm something means to establish its truth or validity by providing evidence or proof.

words.tr: v. 繁荣兴旺；茁壮成长；
words.ex: The business flourishes in the new market.
words.ex_cn: 这家企业在新市场中繁荣兴旺。
words.en: If something flourishes, it is successful, active, or common, and developing quickly and strongly.

words.tr: n. 眼镜商；验光师；眼镜商店
words.ex: He visited the optician to get new glasses.
words.ex_cn: 他去眼镜店配了新眼镜。
words.en: A person who makes or sells eyeglasses and other optical instruments.

words.tr:
v. 虚张声势；唬人
n. 虚张声势；吓唬；峭壁
adj. 直率的
words.ex: He used a bluff to win the game.
words.ex_cn: 他用虚张声势赢得了比赛。
words.en: If you bluff, you try to make someone believe that you will do something when you do not really intend to do it, or that you know something when you do not really know it.

words.tr:
v. 大步走；大步跑
n. 大步慢跑；平稳、轻松的步伐
words.ex: The deer loped gracefully through the forest.
words.ex_cn: 鹿优雅地大步慢跑穿过森林。
words.en: To run or move with a long, easy stride.

words.tr: adj. 注意的；专心的；留心的；关心的
words.ex: The child is attentive in class.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子上课很专心。
words.en: If you are attentive, you are paying close attention to what is being said or done.

words.ex: The police helped to defuse the situation.
words.ex_cn: 警察帮助减少了危险。
words.en: To remove the fuse from (an explosive device) in order to prevent it from exploding; to reduce the danger or tension in (a situation).

words.tr: adj. 满怀敬意的；恭敬的；虔诚的
words.ex: He spoke in a reverential tone about his late father.
words.ex_cn: 他以一种尊敬的语气谈起他已故的父亲。
words.en: Showing or characterized by great respect or reverence; deeply respectful.

words.ex: Her husband cooks dinner every night.
words.ex_cn: 她的丈夫每天晚上做晚饭。
words.en: A married man considered in relation to his spouse.

words.tr: adj. 海岛的；孤立的；思想褊狭的
words.ex: The insular village has no bridge to the mainland.
words.ex_cn: 这个海岛村庄没有桥通向大陆。
words.en: If you describe someone as insular, you are being critical of them because they are unwilling to meet new people or to consider new ideas.

words.tr: adj. 边缘的；页边的；微不足道的；不重要的
words.ex: The village is on the marginal area of the city.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄位于城市的边缘地区。
words.en: If you describe something as marginal, you mean that it is small or not very important.

words.ex: He is disincline to join the trip.
words.ex_cn: 他不愿意参加这次旅行。
words.en: To make someone feel unwilling or reluctant to do something.

words.tr: v. 计算；“calculate”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 计算的；
words.ex: He calculated the total cost quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他快速计算了总费用。
words.en: If something is calculated to have a particular effect, it is deliberately done in order to have that effect.

words.tr:
adj. 人为的；预谋的；做作的
v. 图谋；发明；设计；设法做到；“contrive”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The story's ending felt contrived.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事的结局显得很牵强。
words.en: If you say that something someone says or does is contrived, you mean it seems false and artificial, and is not likely to fool or convince anyone.

words.ex: Birds are migratory in winter.
words.ex_cn: 鸟类在冬天是迁徙的。
words.en: Relating to or characterized by migration; tending to migrate.

words.tr:
v. 嘲笑；讥讽
n. 嘲笑；讥讽
words.ex: He sneered at her simple answer.
words.ex_cn: 他嗤之以鼻地对待她的简单答案。
words.en: If you sneer at someone or something, you express your contempt for them by the expression on your face or by what you say.

words.ex: He has good spatial skills for drawing maps.
words.ex_cn: 他画地图有很好的空间能力。
words.en: Relating to or occupying space.

words.tr: n. 一圈；（人坐着时）大腿部；
words.ex: He ran three laps around the track.
words.ex_cn: 他在跑道上跑了三圈。
words.en: The upper part of the legs of a seated person; a single turn or round in a race or other competition.

words.tr: v. 熄灭；平息；抑制（欲望）；用水冷却
words.ex: He quenched the fire with water.
words.ex_cn: 他用水熄灭了火。
words.en: To satisfy one's thirst or to extinguish a fire or to suppress a feeling or desire.

words.tr:
n. 带位员；接待员；门房
v. 引领；招待；做招待员
words.ex: The usher showed us to our seats in the theater.
words.ex_cn: 带位员带我们到了剧院的座位。
words.en: An usher is someone who shows people where to sit, especially at a formal event such as a wedding or a concert. As a verb, to usher means to show someone where to go or to lead them somewhere.

words.tr: adj. 松弛的；软弱的；无活力的
words.ex: The leaves looked flaccid after the long dry spell.
words.ex_cn: 长时间干旱后，树叶看起来软弱无力。
words.en: Lacking firmness, resilience, or muscle tone; soft and limp.

words.ex: The storm left debris on the road.
words.ex_cn: 风暴在道路上留下了碎片。
words.en: The remains of something that has been destroyed or broken up.

words.ex: He lingered by the door, not wanting to leave.
words.ex_cn: 他逗留在门口，不想离开。
words.en: If you linger somewhere, you stay there for a longer time than is necessary, for example because you are enjoying yourself.

words.ex: The movie's depiction of ancient life is very realistic.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影对古代生活的描写非常真实。
words.en: A depiction of something is a picture or a written description of it.

words.tr: adj. 不可言喻的；无法形容的；避讳的
words.ex: The beauty of the sunset was ineffable.
words.ex_cn: 日落的美是无法言喻的。
words.en: If you describe something as ineffable, you mean that it is so impressive or extreme that it cannot be described in words.

words.ex: Happy is synonymous with joyful.
words.ex_cn: 快乐与喜悦是同义的。
words.en: If you say that one thing is synonymous with another, you mean that the two things are very closely associated with each other so that one suggests the other or one cannot exist without the other.

words.tr: v. 惠顾；资助；屈尊俯就
words.ex: He often patronizes the local bakery.
words.ex_cn: 他经常光顾这家本地面包店。
words.en: If someone patronizes you, they speak or behave towards you in a way which seems friendly, but which shows that they think they are superior to you in some way.

words.ex: His eccentricity makes him unique.
words.ex_cn: 他的古怪使他与众不同。
words.en: The quality of being eccentric; behaviour that is unusual, peculiar, or odd.

words.ex: This decision is pivotal for the company's future.
words.ex_cn: 这个决定对公司未来至关重要。
words.en: Of crucial importance in relation to the development or success of something else.

words.ex: The rotten food has a bad odor.
words.ex_cn: 腐烂的食物有一种难闻的气味。
words.en: An odor is a particular and distinctive smell.

words.tr:
v. 责备；指责
n. 责备；指责
words.ex: She reproached him for being late.
words.ex_cn: 她责备他迟到了。
words.en: To express disapproval or disappointment towards someone because of their actions or behavior.

words.ex: His opening gambit was a simple question.
words.ex_cn: 他的开场白是一个简单的问题。
words.en: A gambit is a clever action in a game or other situation that is intended to achieve an advantage and usually involves taking a risk.

words.ex: He despises lying.
words.ex_cn: 他鄙视撒谎。
words.en: If you despise something or someone, you dislike them and have a very low opinion of them.

words.tr: v. 劝慰；使息怒；谋求好感
words.ex: He brought flowers to propitiate his angry wife.
words.ex_cn: 他带了花去劝慰他生气的妻子。
words.en: To propitiate someone means to make them less angry or hostile by doing something to please them.

words.ex: He traced his lineage back to ancient kings.
words.ex_cn: 他追溯了自己的家系到古代的国王。
words.en: Your lineage is the series of families from which you are directly descended.

words.ex: He is confined to his room because he is sick.
words.ex_cn: 他因为生病被限制在房间里。
words.en: If you confine something or someone, you limit them to a particular place or situation.

words.ex: The police dispersed the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 警察驱散了人群。
words.en: If a crowd of people disperses or is dispersed, it breaks up and the people go in different directions.

words.tr:
n. 狗吠声；短促、尖利的叫喊声
v. 吠；（因疼痛等）尖叫
words.ex: The dog let out a loud yelp when it saw the stranger.
words.ex_cn: 狗看到陌生人时发出了一声大声的吠叫。
words.en: To yelp means to make a short, sharp, high-pitched sound, often because of pain or surprise.

words.tr:
v. 呆头呆脑地盯着
n. 呆子
words.ex: He just stood there gawking at the accident scene.
words.ex_cn: 他只是站在那里，呆呆地看着事故现场。
words.en: To gawk means to stare openly and stupidly.

words.tr: adj. 群体的；社区的；公有的；
words.ex: They share a communal kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 他们共用一个群体厨房。
words.en: Communal means relating to or shared by all the members of a community.

words.tr: adj. 不关心政治的；不重视政治的；与政党无关的
words.ex: He is apolitical and never talks about elections.
words.ex_cn: 他不关心政治，从不谈论选举。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as apolitical, you mean that they are not interested in or involved with politics.

words.tr: adj. 不善言辞的；口齿不清的
words.ex: He was inarticulate when he tried to explain the problem.
words.ex_cn: 当他试图解释这个问题时，他表达不清。
words.en: If someone is inarticulate, they are unable to express themselves easily or well in speech.

words.ex: This painting is unique because no other like it exists.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画是独特的，因为没有其他类似的。
words.en: Something that is unique is the only one of its kind.

words.ex: In a patriarchy, men usually make the big decisions.
words.ex_cn: 在父权制社会中，男人通常做重大决定。
words.en: A social system in which the father is the head of the family and descent is traced through the male line.

words.ex: The smoke came out of the vent.
words.ex_cn: 烟从排气口飘了出来。
words.en: A vent is a hole or opening that allows air, gas, or liquid to pass out of or into a confined space.

words.ex: They tried to desecrate the holy church.
words.ex_cn: 他们试图亵渎那座神圣的教堂。
words.en: To desecrate something means to spoil or damage something that is considered to be holy or very important.

words.tr:
n. 傻笑；假笑；痴笑
v. 傻笑；假笑；痴笑
words.ex: She simpered at him, trying to catch his attention.
words.ex_cn: 她对他假笑，试图引起他的注意。
words.en: To smile in a silly or affected way, often to appear more attractive or to hide one's true feelings.

words.tr:
adj. 习惯的
v. 使习惯（于）；“inure”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He is inured to loud noises.
words.ex_cn: 他对嘈杂的声音已经习惯了。
words.en: If you are inured to something unpleasant, you have become used to it so that it no longer affects you.

words.tr: adj. 能吃苦耐劳的；耐寒的；
words.ex: He is a hardy farmer who works in the field all day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个能吃苦耐劳的农民，整天在田里干活。
words.en: Someone who is hardy is strong and able to cope with difficult conditions.

words.ex: He whittled a small bird from wood.
words.ex_cn: 他用木头削出了一只小鸟。
words.en: To whittle means to cut or shape a piece of wood by repeatedly cutting small slices from it, or to reduce something in size, amount, or extent by a gradual series of steps.

words.tr:
n. 泥潭；泥沼；困境
v. 使陷进泥坑里
words.ex: The car got stuck in the mire.
words.ex_cn: 汽车陷在泥沼里了。
words.en: Mire refers to an area of wet, soggy ground or a difficult situation from which it is hard to extricate oneself.

words.tr:
adj. 激励的；充满活力（或激情）的；令人振奋的
v. 唤醒；觉醒；“rouse”的现在分词
words.ex: The speech was a rousing call to action.
words.ex_cn: 这次演讲是一次激动人心的行动号召。
words.en: Causing great excitement or enthusiasm; stirring.

words.ex: The teacher gave an authoritative answer.
words.ex_cn: 老师给出了一个权威性的回答。
words.en: If something is authoritative, it is respected and accepted as true or correct because it comes from a reliable source.

words.tr:
v. 注意；留心
n. 注意；留心
words.ex: He did not heed the warning.
words.ex_cn: 他没有理会那个警告。
words.en: If you heed someone's advice or warning, you pay attention to it and do what they suggest.

words.ex: The dog gave a small nip to his leg.
words.ex_cn: 狗轻轻咬了他的腿一口。
words.en: To nip means to pinch, squeeze, or bite something quickly and sharply. It can also refer to taking a small amount of a drink.

words.ex: He spurned the offer because it was too low.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝了这个提议，因为报酬太低。
words.en: If you spurn someone or something, you reject them with contempt.

words.tr: adj. 密封的；不透气的；与外界隔绝的
words.ex: The container was hermetic to ensure the contents stayed fresh.
words.ex_cn: 这个容器是密封的，以确保内容物保持新鲜。
words.en: If something is hermetic, it is so tightly sealed that no air can get in or out.

words.tr: adj. 独自的；单独的；孤寂的；
words.ex: He lives in a solitary house far from the town.
words.ex_cn: 他住在离城镇很远的独自一人的房子里。
words.en: A solitary person or thing is the only one in a place.

words.tr: v. 切断；脱离；切成两段
words.ex: He severed the rope with a knife.
words.ex_cn: 他用刀把绳子割断了。
words.en: To sever something means to cut through it or to break it off completely.

words.tr: v. 攻击；困扰；抨击；袭击
words.ex: The storm assailed the small village.
words.ex_cn: 风暴袭击了这个小村庄。
words.en: If someone assails you, they attack you violently, either physically or with words.

words.tr: adj. 深感懊悔的；痛悔的；悔悟的
words.ex: He felt contrite after lying to his mother.
words.ex_cn: 他在对母亲撒谎后感到悔恨。
words.en: Feeling or expressing remorse or penitence; affected by guilt.

words.ex: They disinterred the body last week.
words.ex_cn: 他们上周把尸体挖了出来。
words.en: To dig up something that has been buried, especially a corpse.

words.ex: The rain rendered the road slippery.
words.ex_cn: 雨水使道路变得滑溜。
words.en: To render something means to cause it to become or to provide it. It can also mean to express or translate something.

words.ex: The rifle has a 5.56 mm caliber.
words.ex_cn: 这把步枪的口径是5.56毫米。
words.en: The caliber of something or someone is their quality, especially when this is high.

words.ex: The thick forest was impenetrable.
words.ex_cn: 这片茂密的森林无法穿越。
words.en: Impenetrable is used to describe something that cannot be passed through, entered, or understood.

words.ex: The king will bestow a medal on the hero.
words.ex_cn: 国王将把奖章授予这位英雄。
words.en: To bestow something on someone means to give or present it to them.

words.tr: v. 重铸；改写；更换（演员）
words.ex: The director decided to recast the play with a different set of actors.
words.ex_cn: 导演决定用另一组演员重新排演这出戏。
words.en: To recast something means to change it by organizing it in a different way or presenting it in a different form.

words.ex: He apprised her of the change.
words.ex_cn: 他通知了她这个变化。
words.en: If you are apprised of something, someone tells you about it.

words.tr: n. 标准；尺度；准则；“criterion”的复数；
words.ex: The main criteria for selection are skill and experience.
words.ex_cn: 选择的主要标准是技能和经验。
words.en: A criterion is a standard or principle by which something is judged or decided.

words.tr: adj. 无可辩驳的；不能否认的
words.ex: The evidence is irrefutable.
words.ex_cn: 证据是无可辩驳的。
words.en: If you describe something such as evidence or a fact as irrefutable, you mean that it cannot be denied or disproved.

words.ex: The strange phenomena in the forest puzzled scientists.
words.ex_cn: 森林中奇怪的现象让科学家们感到困惑。
words.en: A phenomenon is something that is observed to happen or exist, especially something interesting or unusual.

words.tr:
n. 人群；一大群；众多
v. 群集；挤满；涌进
words.ex: A throng of people waited outside the store.
words.ex_cn: 一大群人站在商店外面等候。
words.en: A large, densely packed crowd of people or animals.

words.ex: Dark clouds portend a storm.
words.ex_cn: 乌云预示着一场风暴。
words.en: If something portends something else, it indicates that it is likely to happen in the future.

words.tr: adj. 多种的；各式各样的
words.ex: She has multifarious hobbies, like painting, singing, and gardening.
words.ex_cn: 她有很多不同的爱好，比如绘画、唱歌和园艺。
words.en: If you describe things as multifarious, you mean that they are many and of various types.

words.ex: The drummer changed the tempo of the song.
words.ex_cn: 鼓手改变了这首歌的拍子。
words.en: The speed at which a piece of music is played or the rate or speed of motion or activity.

words.ex: The court will quash the false order.
words.ex_cn: 法院将撤销这个虚假的命令。
words.en: If a court or someone in authority quashes a decision or judgment, they officially reject it and say that it is not valid.

words.tr: adj. 可选择的；非强制的；
words.ex: The field trip is optional.
words.ex_cn: 这次郊游是可选的。
words.en: If something is optional, you can choose whether or not you do it or have it.

words.ex: The spoon has a concave surface.
words.ex_cn: 勺子有一个凹的表面。
words.en: A concave surface is curved inward, like the inside of a bowl.

words.tr: adj. 世俗的；非宗教的；长期的
words.ex: He lives a secular life without religion.
words.ex_cn: 他过着没有宗教的世俗生活。
words.en: Secular activities, attitudes, or things have no connection with religion.

words.ex: The witness lost credibility after lying.
words.ex_cn: 证人因撒谎而失去了可信性。
words.en: The quality of being trusted and believed in.

words.ex: He computes the total cost quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他很快算出总成本。
words.en: If you compute a total, amount, or result, you calculate it.

words.tr: adj. 暴虐的；压制的；残暴的
words.ex: The tyrannical king punished people for small mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 这个暴虐的国王因为小错误惩罚人民。
words.en: Using power in a cruel and unfair way over people in a country or group.

words.ex: His histrionic gestures made the play very exciting.
words.ex_cn: 他戏剧性的手势让这场戏非常精彩。
words.en: If you refer to someone's behaviour as histrionic, you are critical of it because it is very dramatic, exaggerated, and insincere.

words.tr: adj. 昏迷不醒的；不省人事的；困乏的
words.ex: The man became comatose after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，这个人陷入了昏迷。
words.en: If someone is comatose, they are in a coma and are not conscious.

words.ex: He tries to reinterpret the old rule.
words.ex_cn: 他试图重新解释这条旧规则。
words.en: To interpret something in a new or different way.

words.ex: The snake slithered through the grass.
words.ex_cn: 蛇在草丛中滑行。
words.en: To move smoothly and quietly with a twisting or oscillating motion, like a snake.

words.ex: The argument caused an estrangement between the brothers.
words.ex_cn: 这场争吵导致兄弟之间的疏远。
words.en: Estrangement is the state of being estranged; a feeling of being alienated or separated from someone or something.

words.tr:
n. 毛孔；小孔
v. 细看；钻研；凝视
words.ex: Sweat comes out through the pores of the skin.
words.ex_cn: 汗水通过皮肤上的毛孔排出。
words.en: A pore is a tiny opening in a surface that allows liquids or gases to pass through. As a verb, to pore means to read or study something very carefully.

words.tr: v. 使预先有倾向；使易接受；使易于患（病）
words.ex: Genes can predispose a person to diabetes.
words.ex_cn: 基因可能使人更容易患糖尿病。
words.en: If something predisposes you to think or behave in a particular way, it makes it likely that you will think or behave in that way.

words.tr:
n. 蜡；
v. 给…上蜡；
words.ex: Bees make wax to build their hives.
words.ex_cn: 蜜蜂用蜡建造蜂巢。
words.en: Wax is a solid, slightly shiny substance made of fat or oil that is used to make candles, polish, and other products. It can also refer to the process of applying wax to something or the natural substance found in the ear.

words.ex: The old man is frail and needs help to walk.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人瘦弱，需要帮助才能走路。
words.en: Someone who is frail is not very strong or healthy.

words.ex: He did not premeditate the crime; it happened in the moment.
words.ex_cn: 他没有预谋犯罪；那是当场发生的。
words.en: If you premeditate an action, especially a crime, you plan it or think about it before you do it.

words.tr: n. 单调；枯燥；千篇一律
words.ex: He felt bored because of the monotony of his daily work.
words.ex_cn: 他因为日常工作的单调而感到无聊。
words.en: If you refer to the monotony of something, you are criticizing it because it is boring and has no variety.

words.ex: His irreverence towards the sacred object was met with shock and disapproval.
words.ex_cn: 他对神圣物品的不敬行为遭到了震惊和反对。
words.en: Irreverence is a lack of respect for people or things that are generally taken seriously.

words.tr:
adj. 有斑点的；斑驳的
v. （使）有斑纹；“dapple”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The dappled sunlight fell on the grass.
words.ex_cn: 斑驳的阳光洒在草地上。
words.en: Something that is dappled is marked with spots of a different color or shade.

words.ex: The diminution of water in the lake is obvious.
words.ex_cn: 湖中水量的减少是显而易见的。
words.en: A diminution of something is its reduction in size, importance, or intensity.

words.ex: He incurred a fine for speeding.
words.ex_cn: 他因超速而招致了一笔罚款。
words.en: If you incur something unpleasant, it happens to you because of something you have done.

words.ex: He embeds the photo in the document.
words.ex_cn: 他把照片插入到文档中。
words.en: To fix something firmly and deeply in a surrounding mass.

words.tr:
v. 弄乱；使混乱
n. 无秩序；混乱；衣冠不整
words.ex: The storm disarrayed the books on the shelf.
words.ex_cn: 风暴把书架上的书弄乱了。
words.en: a state of disorganization or untidiness

words.tr: adj. 放纵的；无节制的；过度的
words.ex: His intemperate lifestyle led to numerous health problems.
words.ex_cn: 他放纵的生活方式导致了许多健康问题。
words.en: If you describe someone's words or behaviour as intemperate, you are critical of them because they are too extreme and uncontrolled.

words.tr:
v. 窃笑
n. 窃笑
words.ex: She couldn't help but snicker at the joke.
words.ex_cn: 她忍不住对那个笑话窃笑。
words.en: To laugh in a half-suppressed, typically scornful way.

words.ex: He gave a concise answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了简明的回答。
words.en: Something that is concise says everything that is necessary without using any unnecessary words.

words.ex: He is prone to colds in winter.
words.ex_cn: 他冬天容易感冒。
words.en: If you are prone to a particular problem or characteristic, you are likely to be affected by it or to have it.

words.tr:
n. 烤架；铁格子
v. 烧烤；拷问
words.ex: He cooked the burgers on the grill.
words.ex_cn: 他用烤架烤了汉堡。
words.en: To cook food on a metal frame over a fire, or a metal frame used for cooking food in this way.

words.ex: My mother chides me for coming home late.
words.ex_cn: 我妈妈因为我回家晚而责备我。
words.en: If you chide someone, you speak to them angrily because they have done something wrong.

words.tr:
n. （赶牲畜的）尖头棒；激励；刺激
v. 刺激；驱使
words.ex: The farmer used a goad to guide the oxen.
words.ex_cn: 农夫用一根尖头棒赶牛。
words.en: If you goad someone, you deliberately make them feel angry or irritated, often causing them to react by doing something.

words.tr: adj. 充满（不愉快事物）的；
words.ex: The journey was fraught with delays.
words.ex_cn: 这次旅程充满了延误。
words.en: If a situation or activity is fraught with problems or risks, it is full of them.

words.ex: The parable of the Good Samaritan teaches compassion and kindness.
words.ex_cn: 好撒玛利亚人的寓言教导了同情和善良。
words.en: A simple story used to illustrate a moral or spiritual lesson, as told by Jesus in the Gospels.

words.ex: The molten lava flowed down the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 熔化的岩浆从山上流下。
words.en: Molten is used to describe substances that have been heated to a very high temperature and have turned into a liquid.

words.ex: He took a provisional job until he found a better one.
words.ex_cn: 他在找到更好的工作之前做了一份临时工作。
words.en: Something that is provisional is temporary and likely to be changed or replaced in the future.

words.tr: adj. 疑惑的；嘲弄的；揶揄的
words.ex: He gave a quizzical look when he heard the news.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到这个消息时，他露出困惑的表情。
words.en: If you give someone a quizzical look or smile, you look at them or smile at them in a way that shows that you are surprised or amused by their behavior.

words.tr: adj. 自我本位的；任性的；自负的
words.ex: He is egotistical and always talks about himself.
words.ex_cn: 他很自我中心，总是谈论自己。
words.en: If you describe someone as egotistical, you disapprove of them because they behave as if they are more important or better than other people.

words.ex: The country's economy is growing fast.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家的经济正在快速增长。
words.en: The economy of a country or region is the system by which money, industry, and trade are organized.

words.tr:
v. 潜伏；隐藏
n. 潜伏；埋伏
words.ex: A cat lurks behind the bush.
words.ex_cn: 一只猫躲在灌木丛后。
words.en: To lurk means to wait or move in a secretive way so that you cannot be seen, especially because you are about to attack someone or do something wrong.

words.tr: adj. 倾向于…的； v. “incline”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He is inclined to help others.
words.ex_cn: 他倾向于帮助别人。
words.en: Having a tendency or preference towards something; likely to do or be something.

words.ex: He was regarded as a clumsy lout by his colleagues.
words.ex_cn: 他的同事们认为他是个笨拙的人。
words.en: A lout is a man who behaves in a rude and aggressive way.

words.tr: n. 代理人；特工；经纪人；（药）剂；动因；
words.ex: The real estate agent helped them buy a house.
words.ex_cn: 房地产代理人帮助他们买了一所房子。
words.en: An agent is a person who acts on behalf of another person or group.

words.tr: adj. 传染性的；有感染力的；
words.ex: The flu is contagious and spreads easily.
words.ex_cn: 流感具有传染性，容易传播。
words.en: A contagious disease can be caught by touching someone who has the disease or by touching an infected object or by breathing in infected air.

words.ex: The gale knocked down several trees.
words.ex_cn: 大风刮倒了几棵树。
words.en: A gale is a very strong wind.

words.tr:
v. 咕哝；（猪等）打呼噜
n. 咕哝；呼噜声
words.ex: He grunted when he lifted the heavy box.
words.ex_cn: 他搬起沉重的箱子时咕哝了一声。
words.en: To make a low, short guttural sound, typically to express dissatisfaction or effort.

words.tr: v. 簸扬（谷）；分出好坏；筛选
words.ex: He winnows the wheat to remove the chaff.
words.ex_cn: 他用扬谷法去除麦子中的糠壳。
words.en: To winnow means to separate the grain from the chaff or to separate the good from the bad.

words.tr: n. 围长；周长；肚带；腰围
words.ex: The tree has a large girth.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树的树干很粗。
words.en: The distance around something, especially the middle part of a person's body or a tree.

words.ex: He exults when his team wins the game.
words.ex_cn: 当他的球队赢得比赛时，他欢呼雀跃。
words.en: If you exult in a triumph or success that you have had, you feel and show great happiness and pride because of it.

words.tr: n. 恶名；坏名声；声名狼藉
words.ex: The criminal gained notoriety for his bold robberies.
words.ex_cn: 这名罪犯因大胆的抢劫而声名狼藉。
words.en: Notoriety is the state of being famous or well known for something bad.

words.tr: adj. 愚蠢的；空洞的；无意义的
words.ex: His inane comments made everyone bored.
words.ex_cn: 他无聊的评论让每个人都感到无聊。
words.en: If you describe someone's comments or ideas as inane, you mean they are very silly or stupid.

words.tr:
n. 茎；柄；梗
v. 跟踪；偷偷接近；昂首阔步地走
words.ex: The stalk of the sunflower is very tall.
words.ex_cn: 向日葵的茎很高。
words.en: The main stem of a plant, typically rising above ground but occasionally subterranean. Also, to pursue or approach stealthily.

words.tr: v. 到达…的顶点；达到高潮；告终
words.ex: The concert culminated with a loud fireworks show.
words.ex_cn: 音乐会以一场响亮的烟花表演结束。
words.en: If an event or series of events culminates in something, it ends with it, having developed until it reaches this point.

words.tr: adj. 不顾将来的；无远见的；不节俭的
words.ex: He is improvident and spends all his money.
words.ex_cn: 他挥霍无度，花光了所有钱。
words.en: If you describe someone as improvident, you mean that they do not think about the future and do not plan for it carefully, often spending money in a careless way.

words.tr: adj. 破坏性的；引起混乱的；
words.ex: The new technology caused disruptive changes in the market.
words.ex_cn: 这项新技术给市场带来了破坏性的变化。
words.en: Causing or tending to cause disruption.

words.tr: n. 必然的结果（或结论）；推论
words.ex: The theorem leads to a simple corollary.
words.ex_cn: 这个定理引出了一个简单的推论。
words.en: A corollary is a statement that follows on from another statement, and that is usually easily understood or proved.

words.ex: The fracas at the party scared everyone.
words.ex_cn: 派对上的骚乱吓到了所有人。
words.en: A fracas is a noisy quarrel or fight.

words.tr: adj. 有骑士风度的；彬彬有礼的；侠义的
words.ex: The knight was chivalrous and helped the lady.
words.ex_cn: 这位骑士有骑士精神，帮助了那位女士。
words.en: A chivalrous man is polite, kind, and unselfish, especially towards women.

words.tr:
v. 钻孔开口；开瓶；提出一个话题讨论
n. 胸针；钻头
words.ex: He broached a hole in the metal plate.
words.ex_cn: 他在金属板上钻了一个孔。
words.en: To broach a subject is to mention it in order to start a discussion on it. A broach is also a tool used for making holes.

words.tr: adj. 无辔头的；不受控制的；放纵的
words.ex: The unbridled horse ran across the field.
words.ex_cn: 那匹无辔头的马在田野上奔跑。
words.en: If you describe behaviour or feelings as unbridled, you mean that they are not controlled or limited in any way.

words.ex: He punched the wall in anger.
words.ex_cn: 他生气地打了墙一拳。
words.en: To punch means to hit someone or something hard with your fist, or to make a hole in something using a tool.

words.ex: The new song caused a furor among teenagers.
words.ex_cn: 这首歌在青少年中引起了狂热。
words.en: A furor is a very angry or excited reaction by people to something.

words.tr:
n. 嘲笑；嘲弄
v. 嘲笑；狼吞虎咽
words.ex: His joke received a scoff from the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 他的笑话引来了人群的嘲笑。
words.en: If you scoff at something, you speak about it in a way that shows you think it is ridiculous or inadequate.

words.ex: The sodden clothes stuck to her skin.
words.ex_cn: 湿透的衣服贴在她的皮肤上。
words.en: Something that is sodden is extremely wet.

words.ex: The teacher reproved the student for being late.
words.ex_cn: 老师因为学生迟到而责骂了他。
words.en: If you reprove someone, you speak angrily or seriously to them because they have behaved in a wrong or foolish way.

words.ex: His idiosyncratic style makes his art easy to recognize.
words.ex_cn: 他独特的风格使他的艺术容易被认出。
words.en: If you describe someone's actions or characteristics as idiosyncratic, you mean that they are rather unusual.

words.tr: v. 举例说明；例证；例示
words.ex: This example exemplifies the rule clearly.
words.ex_cn: 这个例子清楚地说明了这条规则。
words.en: To exemplify means to be a typical example of something or to give an example of something.

words.ex: The climbers reached the summit of the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 登山者到达了山顶。
words.en: The highest point of a hill or mountain; a meeting between heads of government.

words.tr:
v. 小步疾走；急赶
n. 快跑声；疾走
words.ex: The mouse scurried under the table.
words.ex_cn: 老鼠迅速跑到了桌子底下。
words.en: If people or small animals scurry somewhere, they move there quickly and hurriedly, especially because they are frightened.

words.tr:
n. 进口；重要性；
v. 进口；
words.ex: The country increased its import of oil last year.
words.ex_cn: 去年这个国家增加了石油的进口。
words.en: To bring in (goods or services) from a foreign country for sale or use.

words.ex: He is an avid reader of mystery novels.
words.ex_cn: 他热衷于阅读侦探小说。
words.en: If you say that someone is avid for something, you mean that they are very eager to get it.

words.ex: My forebear came from Ireland long ago.
words.ex_cn: 我的祖先很久以前来自爱尔兰。
words.en: Your forebears are your ancestors, especially your grandparents or earlier relatives.

words.ex: He was imprisoned for stealing.
words.ex_cn: 他因偷窃而被监禁。
words.en: To put someone in prison or keep them as a prisoner.

words.ex: The university has great prestige for its research.
words.ex_cn: 这所大学因其研究而享有很高的声望。
words.en: The widespread respect and admiration felt for someone or something on the basis of a perception of their achievements or quality.

words.ex: The city improved its power grid to handle more electricity.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市改进了其电力输送网，以承载更多的电力。
words.en: A grid is a pattern of straight lines that cross each other to form squares. It is used to help you draw or to help you find places on a map.

words.ex: His silence implies he disagrees.
words.ex_cn: 他的沉默暗示他不同意。
words.en: To suggest or indicate something indirectly rather than stating it explicitly.

words.ex: He shirks his homework every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天逃避作业。
words.en: If someone shirks their duties or responsibilities, they deliberately avoid doing them.

words.ex: The book has a gloss at the bottom of each page.
words.ex_cn: 这本书每页底部都有注释。
words.en: A gloss is a bright shine on the surface of something. It can also refer to a superficial appearance or interpretation that conceals the true nature of something.

words.tr: adj. 单个的；单数的；特异的；
words.ex: Each singular student must submit a form.
words.ex_cn: 每个学生都必须提交一份表格。
words.en: In grammar, singular means relating to or being a form of a word that refers to one person or thing.

words.tr: adj. 不知疲倦的；不屈不挠的
words.ex: He is an indefatigable worker who never stops.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个不知疲倦的工作者，从不停止。
words.en: Someone who is indefatigable can work or continue doing something for a very long time without getting tired.

words.tr: adj. 沾满血的； 沾满血污的；血迹斑斑的
words.ex: The movie was too gory for my taste.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影对我来说太血腥了。
words.en: Involving or showing violence and bloodshed.

words.tr: n. 大笑；笑死我了 (used to express amusement)
words.ex: He told a funny joke and got a big lol.
words.ex_cn: 他讲了个有趣的笑话，引得大家大笑。
words.en: To laugh out loud, especially in response to something humorous.

words.tr: adj. 不合理的；没有根据的；无端的
words.ex: The teacher gave an unwarranted warning.
words.ex_cn: 老师给了一个没有理由的警告。
words.en: If you describe something as unwarranted, you are critical of it because there is no need or reason for it.

words.tr: adj. 朦胧的；模糊的；不清楚的
words.ex: The sky looks hazy this morning.
words.ex_cn: 今天早上天空看起来雾蒙蒙的。
words.en: If it is hazy, it is not clear because there is a lot of mist, smoke, or dust in the air.

words.ex: The hawk made a sudden swoop to catch the mouse.
words.ex_cn: 老鹰突然俯冲下来抓老鼠。
words.en: To move very quickly and easily through the air, especially down from a height in order to attack.

words.ex: The dog grovelled on the ground to beg for food.
words.ex_cn: 狗趴在地上乞求食物。
words.en: If you grovel, you behave in a very submissive way in order to show that you are sorry for something wrong that you have done or to try to get someone to forgive you or do something for you.

words.ex: The two rooms adjoin each other.
words.ex_cn: 这两个房间彼此相邻。
words.en: If one room, place, or object adjoins another, they are next to each other.

words.ex: They have an intimate friendship.
words.ex_cn: 他们有着亲密的友谊。
words.en: having a close, friendly, or personal relationship with someone; private and personal

words.ex: The baby babbles when she is happy.
words.ex_cn: 当宝宝开心时，她会含糊不清地说话。
words.en: To babble means to talk rapidly and continuously in a foolish, excited, or incomprehensible way.

words.tr:
n. 权宜之计；应急办法
adj. 权宜的
words.ex: Closing the factory was an expedient to save money.
words.ex_cn: 关闭工厂是为了省钱的权宜之计。
words.en: An expedient action or solution to a problem is one that is convenient or practical, although it may not be morally right.

words.ex: He paddles a canoe on the lake.
words.ex_cn: 他划着独木舟在湖上航行。
words.en: A canoe is a small, narrow boat that you move through the water using a paddle.

words.ex: The loan requires collateral documents.
words.ex_cn: 这笔贷款需要附属文件。
words.en: Collateral is something pledged as security for repayment of a loan, to be forfeited in the event of a default.

words.tr: n. 优势；有利条件；好处；
words.ex: His height gives him an advantage in basketball.
words.ex_cn: 他的身高在篮球中给了他优势。
words.en: An advantage is a factor or circumstance that puts you in a favorable or superior position.

words.ex: I watched a clip of the movie on YouTube.
words.ex_cn: 我在YouTube上看了这部电影的一个片段。
words.en: A clip is a small device, usually made of metal or plastic, that is specially shaped for holding things together. As a verb, to clip means to cut something, especially to make it shorter or neater.

words.ex: The stain on the carpet is a mar.
words.ex_cn: 地毯上的污渍是一个污点。
words.en: To mar something means to spoil or damage it.

words.ex: The company received patronage from a local businessman.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司收到了一位本地商人的赞助。
words.en: The support, encouragement, privilege, or financial aid that an organization or individual bestows to another.

words.tr: adv. 激烈地；猛烈地；强烈地
words.ex: She vehemently denied the accusation.
words.ex_cn: 她强烈否认了这项指控。
words.en: If you say or do something vehemently, you do it with great energy or passion because you feel very strongly about it.

words.ex: The farmer shears sheep every spring.
words.ex_cn: 农夫每年春天给羊剪毛。
words.en: To shear means to cut the wool off a sheep or to cut or trim something with scissors or shears.

words.tr: adj. 偏离规则的；反常的
words.ex: The temperature was anomalous for this season.
words.ex_cn: 这个季节的温度异常。
words.en: Deviating from what is standard, normal, or expected.

words.tr:
n. 滑稽模仿；讽刺作品
adj. 滑稽模仿的；讽刺性作品的
v. 模仿嘲弄
words.ex: The burlesque show was a hit with the audience.
words.ex_cn: 滑稽讽刺表演受到了观众的热烈欢迎。
words.en: A burlesque is a performance or a piece of writing that makes fun of something or someone by copying them in an exaggerated way.

words.tr: adj. 母亲的；母性的；母系的；
words.ex: Her maternal love kept the family strong.
words.ex_cn: 她的母爱让家庭保持坚强。
words.en: Maternal feelings or actions are typical of a kind, loving mother.

words.tr:
v. 摩擦；擦痛；惹怒
n. 擦伤；激怒
words.ex: His socks chafe his ankles.
words.ex_cn: 他的袜子磨得脚踝疼。
words.en: If skin chafes, it becomes sore because something is rubbing against it; to feel impatient or irritated.

words.ex: The speech stoked anger among the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 这篇演讲激起了人群的愤怒。
words.en: To stoke a fire means to add fuel to it to make it burn more strongly. It can also mean to encourage or increase strong feelings or emotions.

words.tr:
v. 发出（响亮而刺耳的声音）
n. 响亮刺耳的声音
words.ex: The car alarm blares loudly at night.
words.ex_cn: 汽车警报在夜里大声响着。
words.en: If something such as a siren or radio blares or if you blare it, it makes a loud, unpleasant noise.

words.ex: I like to browse the internet for fun.
words.ex_cn: 我喜欢上网浏览消遣。
words.en: To look through or glance at reading matter casually or randomly.

words.ex: The imperial palace was built long ago.
words.ex_cn: 这座帝国宫殿是很久以前建造的。
words.en: relating to an empire or an emperor; majestic or superior in quality or size

words.tr: adj. 不安宁的； 焦躁不安的；难驾驭的；倔强的
words.ex: The audience grew restive as the speaker droned on.
words.ex_cn: 演讲者喋喋不休，听众开始焦躁不安。
words.en: If you are restive, you are impatient or bored with a situation and you want it to change.

words.ex: The only egress from the building was blocked by debris.
words.ex_cn: 建筑物的唯一出口被碎片堵住了。
words.en: Egress refers to the act of going out or exiting from a place.

words.ex: Can you tell me the gist of the story?
words.ex_cn: 你能告诉我这个故事的要点吗？
words.en: The main or essential part of a matter.

words.ex: Her heart palpitated with excitement.
words.ex_cn: 她的心脏因兴奋而悸动。
words.en: If your heart palpitates, it beats very fast and in an irregular way, usually because you are anxious or frightened.

words.tr:
v. 挖洞；钻进；翻寻
n. 地洞
words.ex: The rabbit burrows under the tree.
words.ex_cn: 兔子在树下打洞。
words.en: A burrow is a hole or tunnel dug by a small animal, such as a rabbit or a mole, as a dwelling. As a verb, to burrow means to dig a hole or tunnel for habitation or refuge.

words.ex: He does not want to intrude on their conversation.
words.ex_cn: 他不想插话他们的谈话。
words.en: To intrude means to enter somewhere or become involved in a situation where you are not wanted or are not supposed to be.

words.ex: They tried to indoctrinate the children with their beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 他们试图用他们的信仰灌输孩子们。
words.en: To indoctrinate someone means to teach them a particular belief or set of beliefs, especially with the aim of making them accept it without questioning it.

words.tr: adj. 婴儿的；幼稚的；孩子气的
words.ex: The infantile smile made everyone feel warm.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿般的微笑让每个人都感到温暖。
words.en: Infantile behavior or illnesses are typical of very young children.

words.tr: adj. 不兼容的；不相配的；
words.ex: The software is incompatible with old systems.
words.ex_cn: 这个软件与旧系统不兼容。
words.en: If one thing or person is incompatible with another, they are very different in important ways, and do not suit each other or agree with each other.

words.ex: The budget is a constraint on our project.
words.ex_cn: 预算是我们项目的限制。
words.en: A constraint is something that limits or controls what you can do.

words.tr: v. 蹒跚；踉跄；摇摇欲坠
words.ex: The old man totters when he walks.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人走路时摇摇晃晃。
words.en: To move in a feeble or unsteady way.

words.tr:
n. 媒介；方法；
adj. 中等的；适中的；
words.ex: TV is a popular medium for advertising.
words.ex_cn: 电视是一种流行的广告媒介。
words.en: A medium is a method or way of expressing something.

words.ex: Running a business entails hard work.
words.ex_cn: 经营企业必然需要努力工作。
words.en: If one thing entails another, it involves it or causes it.

words.ex: His silence was an implicit apology.
words.ex_cn: 他的沉默是一种含蓄的道歉。
words.en: Something that is implicit is expressed in an indirect way.

words.tr: adj. 轻率的；轻浮的；不严肃的
words.ex: His flippant remarks annoyed everyone at the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他轻率的言论让会议上的每个人都感到恼火。
words.en: If you describe a person or what they say as flippant, you are criticizing them because you think they are not taking something as seriously as they should.

words.tr: adj. 有帮助的；乐器的；仪器的；
words.ex: Her advice was instrumental in helping me pass the exam.
words.ex_cn: 她的建议对帮助我通过考试很有帮助。
words.en: If someone or something is instrumental in a process, plan, or system, they are one of the most important influences in causing it to happen.

words.ex: The map has an indicative arrow to show the way.
words.ex_cn: 这张地图上有一个指示方向的箭头。
words.en: If one thing is indicative of another, it suggests what the other thing is likely to be.

words.tr: adj. 鲁莽的；无礼的；不相干的
words.ex: He gave an impertinent answer to his teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他给了老师一个鲁莽的回答。
words.en: If someone talks or behaves in a rather impolite and disrespectful way, especially towards someone who is older or in a position of authority, you can describe that person or their behaviour as impertinent.

words.ex: The rain caused a torrent down the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 大雨在山间形成了一股急流。
words.en: A torrent is a fast-moving stream of water or other liquid.

words.ex: He gave an enumeration of all the books on the shelf.
words.ex_cn: 他列出了书架上所有的书。
words.en: The act of naming things one by one or a list of items.

words.ex: He showed filial love by taking care of his old parents.
words.ex_cn: 他通过照顾年迈的父母表现出子女的孝心。
words.en: Filial is used to describe the relationship between children and their parents, especially emphasizing the duty and respect that children should show towards their parents.

words.ex: He arranged the books in a haphazard way.
words.ex_cn: 他随意地摆放了书。
words.en: If you describe something as haphazard, you are critical of it because it is not at all organized or is not arranged according to a plan.

words.ex: He tries to mediate between the two friends.
words.ex_cn: 他试图在两个朋友之间调解。
words.en: To intervene between people or parties in order to bring about an agreement or reconciliation.

words.ex: The speaker will amplify the sound for everyone to hear.
words.ex_cn: 扬声器会放大声音，让每个人都能听到。
words.en: To amplify something means to make it louder, stronger, or more detailed.

words.ex: His speech impediment made it hard for him to talk clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他的口吃使他难以清晰地说话。
words.en: An impediment is something that makes it difficult to do or achieve something.

words.ex: The two roads diverge after the bridge.
words.ex_cn: 两条路在桥后分岔。
words.en: If one thing diverges from another similar thing, the first thing becomes different from the second or develops differently from it. You can also say that two things diverge.

words.ex: The blood began to congeal on the floor.
words.ex_cn: 血液开始在地面上凝结。
words.en: If a liquid congeals, it becomes very thick and sticky and almost solid.

words.ex: The smile on his face was illusory.
words.ex_cn: 他脸上的微笑是虚假的。
words.en: If something is illusory, it is not real or true, although it may seem to be.

words.tr: v. 报（某事）之仇；为（某人）报仇
words.ex: He wants to avenge his brother's death.
words.ex_cn: 他想为弟弟的死报仇。
words.en: To avenge someone means to harm or punish someone who has harmed them or someone they care about.

words.ex: Steve Jobs is the founder of Apple.
words.ex_cn: 史蒂夫·乔布斯是苹果公司的创办者。
words.en: A founder is someone who establishes an organization, company, or institution. As a verb, it means to fail or collapse, especially in terms of a plan or a ship sinking.

words.tr:
adj. 可怕的；恐怖的；惨白的；令人不快的
adv. 可怖地；惨白地
words.ex: The ghost looked ghastly in the dark.
words.ex_cn: 那个幽灵在黑暗中看起来吓人极了。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as ghastly, you mean that they are extremely unpleasant or shocking.

words.ex: The disease is waterborne and spreads through dirty drinking water.
words.ex_cn: 这种疾病是通过饮用水传播的。
words.en: Carried or transmitted by water.

words.ex: Don't meddle in my affairs.
words.ex_cn: 别插手我的事情。
words.en: To meddle means to interfere in something that is not one's concern.

words.ex: He can discriminating between real and fake coins.
words.ex_cn: 他能区分真币和假币。
words.en: If you describe someone as discriminating, you mean that they are able to recognize and appreciate the good qualities of something, especially things that are of high quality.

words.ex: He gave an absolute yes to the offer.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个提议给出了完全肯定的回答。
words.en: Absolute means complete and total, or not limited in any way.

words.tr: adj. 杰出的；卓越的；出类拔萃的
words.ex: He is a pre-eminent scientist in his field.
words.ex_cn: 他是该领域最杰出的科学家。
words.en: If someone or something is pre-eminent in a group, they are more important, powerful, or capable than other people or things in the group.

words.tr:
v. 含混不清地说话；诋毁；诽谤
n. 诽谤；诋毁；污辱
words.ex: He slurrs his words when he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 当他累了的时候，说话含糊不清。
words.en: If someone slurs their speech or if their speech slurs, they do not pronounce each word clearly, because they are drunk, ill, or sleepy. A slur is an insulting remark which could damage someone's reputation.

words.tr: adj. 多结节的；难以解决的；棘手的
words.ex: The old tree had a knotty trunk.
words.ex_cn: 这棵老树有一个多结节的树干。
words.en: A knotty problem or issue is very complicated and difficult to solve.

words.tr: n. 保证；保修单；保证书
words.ex: The phone comes with a one-year warranty.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机有一年的保修期。
words.en: A warranty is a written guarantee, often given to the purchaser of an article by its manufacturer, promising to repair or replace it if necessary within a specified period of time.

words.tr: v. 恳求；征求；（妓女）拉客
words.ex: He solicits donations for the charity.
words.ex_cn: 他为慈善机构募捐。
words.en: If you solicit money, help, support, or an opinion from someone, you ask them for it.

words.ex: He bought an extravagant car that cost too much money.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一辆奢侈的车，价格太贵了。
words.en: Spending much more than is necessary or wise; excessively expensive.

words.ex: He tried to reconcile his work and family life.
words.ex_cn: 他试图调和工作与家庭生活。
words.en: If you reconcile two beliefs, facts, or demands that seem to be opposed or completely different, you find a way in which they can both be true or both be successful.

words.ex: They did a collaborative project in class.
words.ex_cn: 他们在课堂上做了一个合作项目。
words.en: A collaborative piece of work is done by two or more people or groups working together.

words.ex: He blurted out the secret by accident.
words.ex_cn: 他不小心说出了秘密。
words.en: If someone blurts something, they say it suddenly, after trying hard to keep quiet or to keep it secret.

words.ex: He is methodical in organizing his work.
words.ex_cn: 他在安排工作时很有条理。
words.en: If you describe someone as methodical, you mean that they do things carefully, thoroughly, and in order.

words.ex: He glowered at the boy who broke his vase.
words.ex_cn: 他怒视着打碎他花瓶的那个男孩。
words.en: If you glower at someone or something, you look at them in an angry way.

words.ex: The machine makes a perpetual noise.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器发出持续的噪音。
words.en: Something that is perpetual continues indefinitely or for a very long time without interruption.

words.tr: adj. 即将发生的；迫在眉睫的； v. “impend”的现在分词；
words.ex: An impending storm made people stay indoors.
words.ex_cn: 一场即将发生的风暴让人们待在室内。
words.en: If an event or situation is impending, it is about to happen or is likely to happen very soon.

words.tr: v. 聚合；合并；长到一起
words.ex: The small ponds coalesce into a large lake.
words.ex_cn: 小池塘合并成一个大湖。
words.en: If two or more things coalesce, they come together and form a single group or system.

words.ex: He wears aristocratic clothes to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他穿着贵族风格的衣服去参加派对。
words.en: Belonging to or characteristic of the aristocracy.

words.ex: He resolved the problem with a simple plan.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个简单的计划解决了问题。
words.en: If you resolve to do something, you make a firm decision to do it.

words.tr: adj. 非实体的；非物质的；无形体的
words.ex: The ghost is incorporeal and cannot be touched.
words.ex_cn: 这个幽灵是无形的，无法被触碰。
words.en: Not composed of matter; having no material existence.

words.ex: The climactic scene of the movie surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 电影的高潮场景让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: Relating to the most intense, exciting, or important point of something; reaching a climax.

words.ex: The strange noise confounded the children.
words.ex_cn: 奇怪的声音让孩子们感到困惑。
words.en: To confuse and surprise someone, especially by being difficult to understand or deal with.

words.tr: adj. 相接的；相邻的；接壤的
words.ex: The two countries are contiguous.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家是相邻的。
words.en: Being in contact; touching or next to each other.

words.ex: The migrant found a new job in the city.
words.ex_cn: 这位移居者在城市里找到了一份新工作。
words.en: A migrant is a person who moves from one place to another, especially in order to find work.

words.tr:
n. 最高统治者；君主；元首
adj. 独立自主的；拥有最高统治权的
words.ex: The sovereign makes important decisions for the country.
words.ex_cn: 君主为国家做出重要决定。
words.en: A sovereign is a king, queen, or other supreme ruler.

words.tr: adj. 有阵风的；起大风的；突发的
words.ex: The gusty winds made it difficult to walk.
words.ex_cn: 阵风使得行走变得困难。
words.en: If it is gusty, the wind is blowing in strong, sudden bursts.

words.tr:
v. 闪烁；发微光
n. 微光；闪光
words.ex: The lake shimmers under the moonlight.
words.ex_cn: 湖面在月光下闪烁。
words.en: To shine with a soft, slightly wavering light.

words.ex: She implored him to stay.
words.ex_cn: 她恳求他留下。
words.en: If you implore someone to do something, you ask them to do it in a forceful, emotional way.

words.ex: He is an eminent scientist who won the Nobel Prize.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位获得诺贝尔奖的杰出科学家。
words.en: An eminent person is well-known and respected, especially because they are good at their profession.

words.tr:
adj. 微不足道的；无关紧要的
v. 闹着玩；玩弄；“trifle”的现在分词
words.ex: He ignored the trifling mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他忽略了这个微不足道的错误。
words.en: If you describe something as trifling, you mean that it is unimportant or insignificant.

words.ex: The rain necessitated staying indoors.
words.ex_cn: 下雨使待在室内成为必需。
words.en: To necessitate something means to make it necessary for something to be done or to happen.

words.ex: He gave a confrontational answer to the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他对老师给出了一个对抗性的回答。
words.en: If you describe someone as confrontational, you mean that they tend to cause or be involved in arguments or disagreements.

words.tr:
v. 轻快地掠过；突然换位；搬家
n. 掠过；迅速飞过；偷偷搬家
words.ex: The butterfly flits from flower to flower.
words.ex_cn: 蝴蝶在花朵间飞舞。
words.en: To move quickly and lightly from one place to another.

words.ex: The statue was colossal, taller than the building.
words.ex_cn: 这座雕像巨大，比大楼还高。
words.en: If you describe something as colossal, you are emphasizing that it is very large.

words.ex: The gang tried to extort money from the shop owner.
words.ex_cn: 这个帮派试图向店主敲诈钱财。
words.en: To extort is to obtain something, especially money, through force, threats, or other unfair means.

words.tr:
n. 中产阶级的人；资产阶级的人
adj. 中产阶级的；追求名利的；资产阶级的
words.ex: He lives a bourgeois life with a big house and a car.
words.ex_cn: 他过着资产阶级的生活，有一栋大房子和一辆车。
words.en: If you describe people, their way of life, or their attitudes as bourgeois, you are criticizing them for caring too much about money and possessions and for being too conventional.

words.ex: He tried to finagle his way into the event without a ticket.
words.ex_cn: 他试图没有票就混进活动。
words.en: To obtain something by deceitful or dishonest means.

words.ex: The toy store sells many novelty items for children.
words.ex_cn: 玩具店出售许多为儿童设计的新奇物品。
words.en: The quality of being new, original, or unusual; something new, original, or unusual.

words.ex: The table is made of a composite material.
words.ex_cn: 这张桌子是由一种合成材料制成的。
words.en: A composite is something that is made up of several different parts or materials.

words.ex: The stray dog wandered into the backyard.
words.ex_cn: 这只走失的狗走进了后院。
words.en: If someone or something strays, they wander away from where they are supposed to be.

words.ex: The storm sundered the old tree.
words.ex_cn: 风暴把那棵老树劈开了。
words.en: To break or split apart, especially along a natural line or grain.

words.tr:
n. 主人；主持人；
v. 主持；
words.ex: The host welcomed us with tea and cookies.
words.ex_cn: 主人用茶和饼干欢迎了我们。
words.en: A host is a person who receives or entertains guests, especially in their own home. A host is also a person who presents a television or radio program.

words.ex: The pine grows tall in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 松树在森林里长得很高。
words.en: A pine is a type of evergreen tree which has long thin leaves called needles and produces cones. As a verb, to pine means to feel a deep longing or desire for something or someone.

words.ex: His frugality helped him save money for years.
words.ex_cn: 他的节俭让他多年都存下了钱。
words.en: Frugality is the quality of being careful with money or food, so that you only spend what is necessary.

words.tr: n. 洗涤剂；洗衣粉；去垢剂；
words.ex: She uses detergent to wash the clothes.
words.ex_cn: 她用洗涤剂洗衣服。
words.en: A detergent is a substance that is used for cleaning things, especially clothes and dishes.

words.ex: The denouement of the story was surprising.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事的结局令人惊讶。
words.en: The final part of a play, movie, or narrative in which the strands of the plot are drawn together and matters are explained or resolved.

words.tr: v. 预先阻止；抢先一步
words.ex: He forestalls problems by planning ahead.
words.ex_cn: 他通过提前计划来防止问题。
words.en: To forestall something means to prevent it from happening or to act before someone else does in order to prevent them from doing something.

words.tr:
n. 皱眉蹙额；退缩
v. 皱眉蹙额；退避
words.ex: He let out a wince when he touched his sore arm.
words.ex_cn: 当他碰触到疼痛的手臂时，他皱了一下眉。
words.en: If you wince, you make a slight, sudden movement of your face, especially when you are in pain or when you see or hear something unpleasant.

words.ex: The ubiquity of smartphones makes life easier.
words.ex_cn: 智能手机的普遍存在让生活更轻松。
words.en: The state or capacity of being everywhere, especially at the same time; omnipresence.

words.ex: He entreats his friend to help him.
words.ex_cn: 他恳求朋友帮助他。
words.en: To ask someone earnestly or anxiously to do something.

words.ex: The merger of two companies created a bigger business.
words.ex_cn: 两家公司的合并创建了一家更大的企业。
words.en: A merger is the joining together of two separate companies or organizations so that they become one.

words.tr:
adj. 笨拙的；不机敏的；笨手笨脚的
n. 一个笨拙愚蠢的人
words.ex: He was maladroit when he dropped the glass.
words.ex_cn: 他不小心把玻璃杯打翻了。
words.en: If you describe someone as maladroit, you mean that they are clumsy or awkward, especially in social situations.

words.ex: The wind strews leaves on the ground.
words.ex_cn: 风把树叶吹得满地都是。
words.en: To scatter or spread things untidily over a surface or area.

words.ex: The family reduced their monthly expenditure.
words.ex_cn: 这个家庭减少了每月的开支。
words.en: Expenditure is the spending of money on something, or the money that is spent on something.

words.tr: n. 修辞学；花言巧语；华丽的文辞；
words.ex: He studied rhetoric to improve his speaking skills.
words.ex_cn: 他学习修辞学以提高自己的演讲能力。
words.en: Rhetoric is the art or study of using language effectively and persuasively.

words.tr:
n. 凿子
v. 雕；凿；欺骗
words.ex: He used a chisel to carve the stone.
words.ex_cn: 他用凿子雕刻石头。
words.en: A chisel is a tool with a long metal blade which has a sharp edge for cutting wood, stone, or metal.

words.ex: The restaurant has a calm ambience.
words.ex_cn: 这家餐厅有一种宁静的氛围。
words.en: The character and atmosphere of a place.

words.tr:
v. 乱写；乱画；涂鸦
n. 乱画；乱写；涂鸦
words.ex: He doodled on his notebook during class.
words.ex_cn: 他在上课时在笔记本上乱画。
words.en: If you doodle, you draw small, simple pictures or patterns on a piece of paper, often while you are thinking about something else.

words.ex: The bird flew aloft above the trees.
words.ex_cn: 鸟儿在树顶上方高飞。
words.en: If something is aloft, it is in the air or off the ground.

words.tr:
n. 松鸡；松鸡肉；怨言；牢骚
v. 抱怨；发牢骚
words.ex: The hunter saw a grouse in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 猎人在森林里看到一只松鸡。
words.en: A grouse is a bird with a plump body and feathered legs, belonging to the family Tetraonidae. As a verb, to grouse means to complain or grumble.

words.ex: The big company owns a subsidiary that makes phones.
words.ex_cn: 这家大公司拥有一家生产手机的附属公司。
words.en: A subsidiary is a company which is part of a larger and more important company.

words.ex: He faltered when asked his name.
words.ex_cn: 当被问到名字时，他犹豫了。
words.en: If you falter, you lose your confidence and stop doing something or start making mistakes.

words.ex: The flowers are aromatic and fill the garden with scent.
words.ex_cn: 这些花是芳香的，使花园充满香气。
words.en: Having a pleasant and distinctive smell.

words.ex: She wrote a letter to condole with him on his loss.
words.ex_cn: 她写了一封信，对他的损失表示慰问。
words.en: To express sympathy or sorrow for someone who has experienced a misfortune or loss.

words.tr:
n. 猎物；受害者；受骗者；
v. 捕食；坑害；折磨；
words.ex: The lion chased its prey across the plain.
words.ex_cn: 狮子在平原上追逐它的猎物。
words.en: An animal that is hunted and killed by another for food.

words.ex: The company hired an expert to do an audit.
words.ex_cn: 公司聘请了一位专家进行审计。
words.en: An audit is an official examination of the accounts of a business or organization to check that they are accurate and correct.

words.tr: v. 发誓放弃；断然丢弃
words.ex: He forswears lying to his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他发誓不再对朋友撒谎。
words.en: If you forswear something, you promise to stop doing it or having it, especially because you think it is bad or harmful.

words.tr: v. 猛冲；猛投；猛烈碰撞
words.ex: The car hurtled down the hill.
words.ex_cn: 汽车飞速冲下山坡。
words.en: If someone or something hurtles somewhere, they move there very quickly, often in a uncontrolled way.

words.ex: The phoenix rises from its ashes.
words.ex_cn: 凤凰从灰烬中重生。
words.en: A phoenix is a mythical bird that is said to be cyclically regenerated or reborn. Associated with the sun, a phoenix obtains new life by arising from the ashes of its predecessor.

words.tr: adj. 善于操纵的；会控制的；
words.ex: He is a manipulative person who always controls others.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个善于操纵他人的人。
words.en: If you describe someone as manipulative, you disapprove of them because they skillfully force or persuade people to act in the way that they want.

words.tr: adj. 刻板的；坚硬的；严格的；
words.ex: He has a rigid attitude toward rules.
words.ex_cn: 他对规则的态度很刻板。
words.en: not able to be changed or adapted; not able to be bent or moved; stiff

words.tr:
n. 运输；
v. 运输；
words.ex: He uses public transport to go to work.
words.ex_cn: 他乘坐公共交通去上班。
words.en: To transport something or someone is to move them from one place to another, especially over long distances.

words.ex: The temple is a divine place.
words.ex_cn: 这座寺庙是神的圣地。
words.en: Something that is divine relates to a god or goddess.

words.tr: adj. 俗艳的；花哨的；过分装饰的
words.ex: The room was decorated in a garish pink that hurt the eyes.
words.ex_cn: 房间被装饰成刺眼的粉红色，令人眼睛不适。
words.en: If you describe something as garish, you mean that it is excessively bright, colorful, or elaborate in a way that is considered tasteless or unattractive.

words.ex: The teacher chose an arbitrary number to start the game.
words.ex_cn: 老师随意选了一个数字来开始游戏。
words.en: If you describe an action, rule, or decision as arbitrary, you think that it is not based on any principle, plan, or system. It often seems unfair because of this.

words.tr: n. 冒名顶替者；冒名行骗者
words.ex: He was exposed as an impostor who had been posing as a doctor.
words.ex_cn: 他被揭露为一个冒充医生的骗子。
words.en: An impostor is someone who pretends to be someone else in order to deceive people.

words.tr:
n. 经常重复的评价（或抱怨）；叠句；
v. 克制；
words.ex: His constant refrain is that the food is too expensive.
words.ex_cn: 他经常抱怨食物太贵。
words.en: If you refrain from doing something, you deliberately do not do it.

words.tr: v. 使慌乱；打扰；使担忧
words.ex: The loud noise didn't faze the experienced speaker.
words.ex_cn: v. 大声的噪音并没有打扰到这位有经验的演讲者。
words.en: To disturb or disconcert someone.

words.ex: He made a gaffe when he called the boss by the wrong name.
words.ex_cn: 他叫错老板的名字，犯了个错误。
words.en: A gaffe is a mistake that a person makes in public, especially something embarrassing that they say or do.

words.ex: She dotes on her little grandson.
words.ex_cn: 她非常疼爱她的孙子。
words.en: If you say that someone dotes on a person or a thing, you mean that they love or care about them very much and spend a lot of time with them.

words.ex: The teacher gave an assessment of the students' work.
words.ex_cn: 老师对学生的作品进行了评估。
words.en: An assessment is a judgment about something, especially about how good or bad it is, or an amount that is calculated for something, especially for tax purposes.

words.ex: He devised a new way to solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他设计了一种解决这个问题的新方法。
words.en: To devise something means to plan or invent a new way of doing something.

words.ex: The cat has a fluffy tail.
words.ex_cn: 这只猫有一条蓬松的尾巴。
words.en: Something that is fluffy is soft and light, with many small, loose pieces or parts.

words.tr: v. 安抚；讨好；使息怒；调和
words.ex: He tried to conciliate his angry neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他试图安抚他生气的邻居。
words.en: If you conciliate someone, you try to end a disagreement with them by doing or saying things that will make them less angry or more friendly.

words.ex: Honey is a viscous liquid.
words.ex_cn: 蜂蜜是一种黏稠的液体。
words.en: A viscous liquid is thick and sticky and does not flow easily.

words.tr:
v. 为 ... 上脚镣；束缚；限制
n. 脚镣；桎梏；束缚
words.ex: The prisoner was fettered with chains.
words.ex_cn: 囚犯被锁链束缚着。
words.en: A fetter is a chain or shackle for the feet, or something that confines or restrains.

words.tr:
n. 流浪汉；漂泊者；乞丐
adj. 流浪的；漂泊的
words.ex: The vagrant slept on the park bench.
words.ex_cn: 那个流浪汉睡在公园的长椅上。
words.en: A vagrant is someone who moves from place to place and does not have a permanent home or job.

words.ex: The wind began to slacken after the storm.
words.ex_cn: 风暴过后，风速开始减缓。
words.en: If something slackens or if you slacken it, it becomes slower, less active, or less intense.

words.tr: adj. 不受个人感情影响的；没有人情味的；
words.ex: The judge gave an impersonal decision based on the law.
words.ex_cn: 法官基于法律作出了不受个人感情影响的判决。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as impersonal, you mean that they do not show any emotion about the person they are dealing with.

words.ex: The company will consolidate two departments next month.
words.ex_cn: 公司下个月将合并两个部门。
words.en: To consolidate something means to make it stronger, more secure, or more solid.

words.ex: He spoke with certitude about the answer.
words.ex_cn: 他对于这个答案说话时充满确信。
words.en: A feeling of being certain or convinced about something.

words.ex: The news roiled the financial markets.
words.ex_cn: 这个消息搅乱了金融市场。
words.en: To make (a liquid) turbid or muddy by stirring up sediment; to disturb or irritate.

words.tr: v. 使变白；（脸色）变苍白；焯
words.ex: She blanches the vegetables before freezing them.
words.ex_cn: 她在冷冻蔬菜之前先焯水。
words.en: To blanch means to make something white or pale, often by removing color or by causing it to lose color. It can also refer to the process of briefly boiling vegetables and then plunging them into cold water to halt the cooking process.

words.ex: His countenance showed surprise.
words.ex_cn: 他的面容流露出惊讶。
words.en: A person's face or facial expression; support or approval.

words.ex: He dissimulated his anger to keep the peace.
words.ex_cn: 他掩饰了自己的愤怒以维持和平。
words.en: To dissimulate means to hide your real feelings, character, or intentions.

words.ex: The passengers disembark at the port.
words.ex_cn: 乘客们在港口上岸。
words.en: To disembark means to leave a ship, aircraft, or other vehicle.

words.tr:
n. 钩；扣；紧握；紧抱
v. 抱紧；握紧；扣紧
words.ex: The necklace has a gold clasp.
words.ex_cn: 这条项链有一个金色的钩。
words.en: A clasp is a small device that fastens something, or the act of holding someone or something tightly.

words.ex: The car decelerate when it sees the red light.
words.ex_cn: 当汽车看到红灯时，它减速了。
words.en: If a vehicle or machine decelerates or if you decelerate it, it slows down.

words.ex: The basement was dank and cold.
words.ex_cn: 地下室又潮又冷。
words.en: Unpleasantly damp and cold.

words.tr:
adj. 柔和的；减弱的；郁郁不乐的
v. 征服；克制；制服；“subdue”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The room had subdued lights.
words.ex_cn: 房间里灯光柔和。
words.en: If a color or light is subdued, it is not very bright.

words.ex: He picked a random number to win the prize.
words.ex_cn: 他随意选了一个数字来赢得奖品。
words.en: If you describe something as random, you mean that it happens or is chosen without any definite plan, pattern, or purpose.

words.ex: He got compensatory pay for working overtime.
words.ex_cn: 他因加班获得了补偿性工资。
words.en: Compensatory is used to describe something that is intended to compensate for something else, especially loss or damage.

words.tr: v. 敷衍；拖延；见风驶舵
words.ex: He decided to temporize until he had more information.
words.ex_cn: 他决定拖延时间，直到获得更多信息。
words.en: To temporize means to delay making a decision or giving a definite answer in order to gain time or avoid committing oneself.

words.ex: The lush grass looked green after the rain.
words.ex_cn: 雨后，葱翠的草地显得格外绿。
words.en: A lush area has a lot of green, healthy plants, grass, and trees.

words.tr: n. 注意的焦点； 引人注目的事物；北极星
words.ex: The new museum became the cynosure of all eyes in the city.
words.ex_cn: 这座新博物馆成为全城瞩目的焦点。
words.en: A cynosure is someone or something that is the center of attention or admiration.

chapters.name: 阅读词汇 文史地理

words.tr: n. 信徒；信仰者；崇拜者
words.ex: She was a devoted votary of classical music.
words.ex_cn: 她是古典音乐的虔诚崇拜者。
words.en: A votary is someone who is devoted to a particular religion, activity, or cause.

words.tr:
n. 尖塔；尖顶；尖峰；尖岩石；顶点；顶峰
v. 造小尖塔；把...放在极高处
words.ex: The pinnacle of the church reached high into the sky.
words.ex_cn: 教堂的尖塔高耸入云。
words.en: The pinnacle of something is the highest point or level that it can reach, especially when it is very good.

words.tr: adj. 自我中心的；利己的；
words.ex: He is egocentric and only talks about himself.
words.ex_cn: 他以自我为中心，只谈论自己。
words.en: If you describe someone as egocentric, you mean that they are only concerned with their own needs and desires, and not with those of other people.

words.tr: v. 痛饮狂欢；狂饮作乐
words.ex: They carouse every weekend at the beach.
words.ex_cn: 他们每周末都在海滩上狂欢。
words.en: To engage in a noisy, lively drinking party.

words.ex: The old tree produced many progeny.
words.ex_cn: 这棵老树生了许多后代。
