words.en: The offspring or descendants considered as a group.

words.ex: The telescope showed a bright nebula in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 望远镜在夜空中显示了一个明亮的星云。
words.en: A nebula is a cloud of gas and dust in outer space, visible in the night sky either as an indistinct bright patch or as a dark silhouette against other luminous matter.

words.tr: v. 作…的摘要；成为…的缩影；概括；集中体现
words.ex: This painting epitomizes the beauty of nature.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画概括了自然的美。
words.en: If you say that something or someone epitomizes a particular thing, you mean that they are a perfect example of it.

words.ex: She had a presentiment that something bad was going to happen.
words.ex_cn: 她有一种不祥的预感，觉得会有坏事发生。
words.en: A presentiment is a feeling that something is about to happen, especially something unpleasant.

words.tr: adj. 极神圣的；神圣不可侵犯的
words.ex: The church's rules were considered sacrosanct and unchangeable.
words.ex_cn: 教堂的规定被认为是神圣不可侵犯的，不可改变的。
words.en: If you describe something as sacrosanct, you mean that it is considered to be special and should not be changed or interfered with.

words.ex: He is studying anthropology at university.
words.ex_cn: 他正在大学里学习人类学。
words.en: Anthropology is the study of human societies and cultures and their development.

words.tr: adj. 时代错误的；落伍的；过时的
words.ex: Wearing a horse-drawn carriage in modern times is anachronistic.
words.ex_cn: 在现代穿马车是过时的。
words.en: Something that is anachronistic is out of its proper time in history, or seems to belong to a different time.

words.ex: The queen was resplendent in her golden crown.
words.ex_cn: 女王戴着金色王冠，光彩夺目。
words.en: Something that is resplendent is very bright and attractive, often because it is richly decorated or very colorful.

words.ex: His visage showed deep sadness.
words.ex_cn: 他的面容流露出深深的悲伤。
words.en: The appearance of the face or facial expression of a person.

words.tr: n. （名人）雕像；（丑化的）模拟像
words.ex: They burned an effigy of the king.
words.ex_cn: 他们烧了一个国王的雕像。
words.en: An effigy is a sculpture or model of a person, often made to be destroyed as a protest or as part of a ceremony.

words.ex: The grandeur of the palace amazed everyone.
words.ex_cn: 宫殿的宏伟让每个人都感到惊讶。
words.en: The quality of being grand or splendid in appearance or style.

words.ex: The clan lived in a small village for centuries.
words.ex_cn: 这个氏族几个世纪以来一直住在一个小村庄里。
words.en: A clan is a group of families or relatives who are connected by blood or marriage and who often share the same surname.

words.ex: The archaeologist found an old pot in the ground.
words.ex_cn: 这位考古学家在地下发现了一个旧陶罐。
words.en: An archaeologist is someone who studies the societies and cultures of the past by examining the remains of their buildings, tools, and other objects.

words.tr: adj. 灰白的；须发斑白的
words.ex: The old man had a hoary beard.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人有一头灰白的胡须。
words.en: If you describe something as hoary, you mean that it is old and often repeated and therefore not interesting or original.

words.ex: He is an icon of pop music.
words.ex_cn: 他是流行音乐的偶像。
words.en: An icon is a small picture or symbol on a computer screen that represents a program or a file.

words.ex: The choir sings every Sunday in church.
words.ex_cn: 唱诗班每周日在教堂唱歌。
words.en: A choir is a group of people who sing together, especially in a church or school.

words.ex: He believes in an egalitarian society where everyone is equal.
words.ex_cn: 他相信一个人人平等的平等主义社会。
words.en: Egalitarian is used to describe something that is based on the principle that all people are equal and deserve equal rights and opportunities.

words.ex: The river has a sinuous path through the forest.
words.ex_cn: 这条河在森林中蜿蜒流淌。
words.en: Something that is sinuous has many smooth turns and curves.

words.ex: Polygamy is illegal in many countries.
words.ex_cn: 一夫多妻制在许多国家是非法的。
words.en: Polygamy is the custom or practice of having more than one wife or husband at the same time.

words.ex: She embellished the dress with flowers.
words.ex_cn: 她用花朵装饰了这条裙子。
words.en: To embellish something means to make it more attractive by adding decorative details or features.

words.ex: He believes in monogamy and stays with one partner.
words.ex_cn: 他相信一夫一妻制，并且只与一个伴侣在一起。
words.en: The practice or condition of having a single sexual partner during a period of time.

words.ex: The church has a big dome above the altar.
words.ex_cn: 教堂的祭坛上方有一个大穹顶。
words.en: A dome is a rounded vault made of either curved segments or a shell of revolution, meaning an arch rotated around its central vertical axis.

words.ex: The preamble explains the purpose of the law.
words.ex_cn: 序言解释了法律的目的。
words.en: A preamble is an introduction to a speech or piece of writing, especially one that explains what follows.

words.tr: adj. 痛切的；酸楚的；强烈的；尖刻的
words.ex: The letter was poignant and made her cry.
words.ex_cn: 这封信很感人，让她哭了。
words.en: A poignant piece of writing or music makes you feel sad or full of pity.

words.ex: The pianist played a mordent on the high note.
words.ex_cn: 钢琴家在高音上弹了一个回音装饰音。
words.en: A mordent is a musical ornament that involves the rapid alternation of a note with the one immediately below it.

words.ex: The law is retroactive and covers last year.
words.ex_cn: 这项法律具有追溯效力，适用于去年。
words.en: If a decision, action, or law is retroactive, it is intended to take effect from a date before it was actually made.

words.ex: The abridgement of the book makes it easier to read.
words.ex_cn: 这本书的缩写版更容易阅读。
words.en: An abridgement is a shortened version of a written work, which retains the main ideas or themes of the original.

words.ex: He believes in calvinism and trusts God's plan.
words.ex_cn: 他相信加尔文主义，并信任上帝的计划。
words.en: Calvinism is a major branch of Protestantism that follows the theological tradition and forms of Christian practice of John Calvin and other Reformation-era theologians.

words.tr:
n. 教皇绝对权力主义者；山那边的人或地区
adj. 山外的；阿尔卑斯山以南的；信奉教皇至上主义的
words.ex: He is an ultramontane Catholic who supports the Pope.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位支持教皇的超蒙坦派天主教徒。
words.en: Relating to or advocating the supremacy of the Pope over the Church and secular affairs, especially as formerly upheld by certain Roman Catholics.

words.tr:
v. 预言；预测
n. （古罗马）占兆官；占卜师
words.ex: The early reviews augur well for the success of the movie.
words.ex_cn: 早期的评论预示着这部电影将取得成功。
words.en: to predict or foretell, especially from signs or omens

words.tr: n. 唯物主义者；物质主义者
words.ex: He is a materialist who believes only in physical things.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个只相信物质实体的唯物主义者。
words.en: A materialist is someone who believes that only physical matter exists, and that everything, including thought and feeling, can be explained in terms of matter and physical phenomena.

words.ex: The indigenous people live in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 本土居民住在森林里。
words.en: Indigenous people or things belong to the country in which they are found, rather than coming there or being brought there from another country.

words.tr:
adj. 超自然的；神秘的；隐藏的
v. 掩蔽
n. 神秘的事物；神秘学
words.ex: He is interested in the occult.
words.ex_cn: 他对神秘学感兴趣。
words.en: Relating to mystical, supernatural, or magical powers, practices, or phenomena.

words.ex: He told ribaldry jokes at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他在派对上讲了粗俗的笑话。
words.en: Ribaldry refers to language or behavior that is vulgar, lewd, or indecent, often in a humorous context.

words.ex: The hikers got stuck in a quagmire near the river.
words.ex_cn: 徒步者在河边陷入了一片沼泽地。
words.en: A quagmire is a difficult, complicated, or unpleasant situation that is hard to escape from.

words.ex: He lives by hedonism, seeking pleasure every day.
words.ex_cn: 他奉行享乐主义，每天追求快乐。
words.en: Hedonism is the belief that gaining pleasure is the most important thing in life.

words.ex: The king walked with pomp in the parade.
words.ex_cn: 国王在游行中以隆重的气势行走。
words.en: Pomp is the use of a lot of ceremony, fine clothes, and decorations, especially on a public or official occasion.

words.ex: He uses wavelet to analyze sound signals.
words.ex_cn: 他使用小波来分析声音信号。
words.en: A wavelet is a small wave; a ripple.

words.ex: The nomadic family moves with their sheep every season.
words.ex_cn: 这个游牧家庭每季都随着羊群迁移。
words.en: A nomadic way of life is one in which people move from place to place instead of living in one place all the time.

words.tr: adj. 激起性欲的；满足感官的；撩人的
words.ex: The painting showed a voluptuous woman with flowing curves.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画描绘了一位身材性感、曲线优美的女人。
words.en: If you describe a woman as voluptuous, you mean that she has large breasts and hips and is considered sexually attractive.

words.tr: v. 说教；讲道；说大道理
words.ex: He often sermonizes about honesty at family dinners.
words.ex_cn: 他经常在家庭晚餐时讲教诲关于诚实。
words.en: To preach or deliver a sermon; to lecture someone in a tedious or pompous way.

words.tr: n. 仓库；贮藏室；存放处；智囊
words.ex: He saves his code in a GitHub repository.
words.ex_cn: 他把代码保存在 GitHub 仓库中。
words.en: A repository is a place where something is stored or can be found.

words.tr:
adj. 多汞的；含汞的；易变的；灵活的；反复无常的
n. 汞制剂；水银剂
words.ex: His mercurial mood changes from happy to angry quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他多汞的情绪很快从高兴变到生气。
words.en: If you describe someone as mercurial, you mean that they frequently change their mind or mood without warning.

words.tr: adj. 嗜酒的；好饮的；吸水的
words.ex: He is a bibulous man who drinks wine every night.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个每晚都喝酒的嗜酒者。
words.en: Bibulous means having a tendency to absorb liquids or being fond of alcoholic beverages.

words.tr: adj. 神圣化的； 受崇敬的
words.ex: The hallowed ground is where the heroes rest.
words.ex_cn: 那片神圣的土地是英雄们安息的地方。
words.en: Something that is hallowed is respected and admired, usually because it is old, important, or has a good reputation.

words.tr: n. 弟兄们；同胞；教友；会友
words.ex: The brethren gathered for prayer each morning.
words.ex_cn: 兄弟们每天早上聚集祷告。
words.en: Brethren is an old-fashioned plural form of 'brother', used especially in religious contexts to refer to male members of a group or community.

words.ex: The historian interpolated the text with his own opinions.
words.ex_cn: 这位历史学家在文本中插入了自己的观点。
words.en: To interpolate means to insert something between other things or parts, especially to insert words into a text.

words.tr: adj. 意志的；发自意志的；表示意志的
words.ex: He has a volitive nature and makes his own choices.
words.ex_cn: 他有意志坚定的天性，自己做决定。
words.en: Relating to the will or the expression of a wish or desire.

words.tr: n. 罗马教皇；主教；大祭司；教宗
words.ex: The pontiff gave a speech to the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 教皇向人群发表了演讲。
words.en: A pontiff is a high-ranking religious leader, especially the Pope in the Roman Catholic Church.

words.tr: adj. 说得过去的；站得住脚的；可防守的
words.ex: His excuse was a little weak, but still tenable.
words.ex_cn: 他的借口有点牵强，但还是说得过去的。
words.en: If an idea, argument, or plan is tenable, it is reasonable and could be successfully defended against criticism.

words.tr: adj. 平民的；卑贱的；卑鄙的；不光彩的
words.ex: He came from an ignoble family, but worked hard to succeed.
words.ex_cn: 他出身于平民家庭，但努力工作以取得成功。
words.en: If you describe something as ignoble, you mean that it is bad and something to be ashamed of.

words.ex: He lost his pecuniary support after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在事故后失去了经济支持。
words.en: Pecuniary means relating to money, especially in terms of financial gain or loss.

words.tr: n. 禁欲；独身；独身生活
words.ex: He chose celibacy to focus on his religion.
words.ex_cn: 他选择独身以专注于他的宗教。
words.en: The state of abstaining from marriage and sexual relations.

words.tr: adj. 俗丽而不值钱的；花里胡哨的
words.ex: She wore a tawdry dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿着一件俗丽的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe something as tawdry, you mean that it is showy and bright but of very poor quality.

words.ex: The jury was sequestered during the trial.
words.ex_cn: 陪审团在审判期间被隔离。
words.en: To sequester means to isolate or hide away; it can also refer to the legal process of seizing property until a debt is paid or a dispute is resolved.

words.ex: The birds fly home at gloaming.
words.ex_cn: 鸟儿在暮色中飞回家。
words.en: The gloaming is the time of day when the sun has just set and it is beginning to get dark, often considered to be a magical or mysterious time.

words.ex: He looked up the word in his lexicon.
words.ex_cn: 他在词典里查了这个词。
words.en: The vocabulary of a person, language, or branch of knowledge.

words.ex: The conductor waved the baton to start the symphony.
words.ex_cn: 指挥家挥动指挥棒，开始交响乐。
words.en: A baton is a stick that is used by conductors to direct an orchestra or choir, by a relay runner to pass on the race, or by a police officer as a weapon.

words.ex: She will beautify her garden with flowers.
words.ex_cn: 她将用花朵美化她的花园。
words.en: To make something more attractive or beautiful.

words.tr: adj. 可怕的；恐怖的；令人毛骨悚然的
words.ex: The macabre scene in the horror movie made the audience cringe.
words.ex_cn: 恐怖电影中那可怕的场景让观众不寒而栗。
words.en: If you describe something as macabre, you mean that it is strange and horrible because it is connected with death or violence.

words.ex: The general used a clever stratagem to win the battle.
words.ex_cn: 将军使用了一个巧妙的战略赢得了战斗。
words.en: A stratagem is a plan or scheme, especially one used to outwit an opponent or achieve an end.

words.tr: adj. 贪吃的；贪婪的；如饥似渴的
words.ex: He is a voracious eater who finishes all the food on his plate.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个贪吃的人，总会把盘子里的所有食物吃完。
words.en: If you describe a person or their appetite for something as voracious, you mean that they want a lot of something.

words.tr: adj. 有利的；吉祥的；吉利的
words.ex: The weather was propitious for a picnic.
words.ex_cn: 天气非常适合野餐。
words.en: If something is propitious, it is likely to lead to success, or it indicates a good chance of success.

words.ex: He wakes up at antemeridian.
words.ex_cn: 他在上午醒来。
words.en: Relating to the period of time before noon (midday).

words.ex: He tried to make atonement for his mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他试图为自己的错误赎罪。
words.en: Atonement is the act of doing something to make up for a wrong that you have done, especially in a religious context.

words.tr: adj. 诙谐的；爱开玩笑的；滑稽的
words.ex: He is jocular during breaks, making everyone laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他在休息时很幽默，让大家笑个不停。
words.en: If you say that someone has a jocular manner, you mean that they are cheerful and often make jokes or try to make people laugh.

words.ex: He was called a recreant for running away from the battle.
words.ex_cn: 他因逃离战场而被称为懦夫。
words.en: Someone who is recreant is cowardly or disloyal.

words.tr: adj. 装作圣洁的；伪善的
words.ex: He gave a sanctimonious speech about honesty.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一番关于诚实的伪善演讲。
words.en: If you describe someone as sanctimonious, you disapprove of them because you think that they are trying to appear morally better than other people.

words.tr:
adj. 本国的；地方的
n. 方言；土语
words.ex: He wrote the poem in the vernacular language.
words.ex_cn: 他用本国语言写了这首诗。
words.en: The vernacular is the language or dialect spoken by the ordinary people in a particular country or region.

words.ex: The boat sailed into the bight to avoid the storm.
words.ex_cn: 船驶入海湾以躲避风暴。
words.en: A bight is a long, gradual curve or recess in the coastline or the loop of a rope.

words.ex: The verity of his story was proven by the evidence.
words.ex_cn: 他故事的真实性被证据证明了。
words.en: Verity refers to the quality or state of being true or real.

words.ex: He tries to eschew sugar for health reasons.
words.ex_cn: 他为了健康尽量避免吃糖。
words.en: If you eschew something, you deliberately avoid doing it or becoming involved in it.

words.ex: The forest remained pristine and untouched.
words.ex_cn: 这片森林保持原始且未被破坏。
words.en: Something that is pristine is in its original condition and has not been spoiled or damaged.

words.ex: A gentle zephyr blew through the trees.
words.ex_cn: 一阵轻柔的微风吹过树林。
words.en: A zephyr is a gentle, mild breeze, traditionally from the west, and especially one of the soft, mild breezes of spring or summer.

words.ex: The engineer built a prototype of the new car.
words.ex_cn: 工程师制作了这辆新车的原型。
words.en: A prototype is the first or original example of something that has been or will be copied or developed; it is a model or preliminary version.

words.tr: adj. 空虚的；茫然的；空洞的
words.ex: His vacuous smile made no sense.
words.ex_cn: 他空洞的微笑毫无意义。
words.en: If you describe someone's mind or smile as vacuous, you are critical of them because they lack intelligence, understanding, or seriousness.

words.ex: He is a lexicographer who writes dictionaries.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位编写词典的词典编纂者。
words.en: A lexicographer is a person who writes, compiles, or edits dictionaries.

words.ex: He believes in empiricism and trusts what he can see.
words.ex_cn: 他相信经验主义，只相信自己能看见的东西。
words.en: The practice of relying on observation and experiment especially in the natural sciences.

words.tr:
n. 盎格鲁-撒克逊人；盎格鲁-撒克逊语
adj. 盎格鲁-撒克逊人的；盎格鲁-撒克逊语的
words.ex: The anglo-saxon people lived in England long ago.
words.ex_cn: 盎格鲁-撒克逊人很久以前生活在英格兰。
words.en: Relating to the Germanic inhabitants of England from the 5th century AD to the Norman Conquest.

words.ex: The dark clouds are a harbinger of storm.
words.ex_cn: 乌云是暴风雨的预兆。
words.en: A harbinger is something that shows that something is going to happen soon, especially something bad.

words.tr: adj. 难以捉摸的；难以理解的；神秘莫测的
words.ex: His expression was inscrutable.
words.ex_cn: 他的表情难以捉摸。
words.en: If someone or something is inscrutable, it is impossible to understand or know what they are thinking or feeling.

words.tr: v. 专横；跋扈；盛气凌人
words.ex: He tries to domineer over his little brother.
words.ex_cn: 他试图对弟弟发号施令。
words.en: To domineer means to rule over or control others in a harsh or arrogant way.

words.ex: The antonym of 'hot' is 'cold'.
words.ex_cn: ‘hot’的反义词是‘cold’。
words.en: An antonym is a word that means the opposite of another word.

words.ex: He lit the brazier to keep warm.
words.ex_cn: 他点燃了火盆来取暖。
words.en: A brazier is a portable heater consisting of a pan or stand for holding lighted coals.

words.tr: adj. 耻辱的；不名誉的；不光彩的
words.ex: He faced an ignominious defeat in the election.
words.ex_cn: 他在选举中遭遇了耻辱的失败。
words.en: If you describe an experience or action as ignominious, you mean it is embarrassing because it shows a great lack of success.

words.ex: He is an illustrious scientist who won many awards.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位杰出的科学家，获得过许多奖项。
words.en: If you describe someone as illustrious, you mean that they are very well known because they have a high position in society or they have done something impressive.

words.ex: He was an ingrate who never thanked anyone for their help.
words.ex_cn: 他是个忘恩负义的人，从不感谢别人的帮助。
words.en: An ingrate is a person who is not grateful for something that has been done for them.

words.ex: The aristocrat lived in a big castle.
words.ex_cn: 这位贵族住在一座大城堡里。
words.en: An aristocrat is a person of high rank in a society, especially one who inherits a title and lands.

words.ex: The movie has verisimilitude because it feels real.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影具有逼真性，因为它感觉真实。
words.en: the quality of seeming to be true or real

words.ex: The palace has a grandiose design with tall columns and golden domes.
words.ex_cn: 这座宫殿有着宏伟的设计，配有高大的柱子和金色的圆顶。
words.en: If you describe something as grandiose, you mean it is larger or more elaborate than necessary, or it is intended to seem very impressive or magnificent.

words.ex: He was punished for plagiarism in his essay.
words.ex_cn: 他因论文剽窃而受到惩罚。
words.en: Plagiarism is the practice of using or copying someone else's idea or work and pretending that you thought of it or created it.

words.tr: adj. 词藻浮华的；夸大的；做作的
words.ex: He gave a grandiloquent speech full of big words.
words.ex_cn: 他发表了一篇充满华丽辞藻的演讲。
words.en: If you describe someone's language as grandiloquent, you mean that it is extremely formal, elaborate, or exaggerated, and is used to impress people.

words.tr: n. 违反语法；文法错误；举止失礼
words.ex: He made a solecism when he said 'between you and I'.
words.ex_cn: 当他说出'between you and I'时，犯了一个语法错误。
words.en: A solecism is a grammatical mistake in speech or writing, or a breach of etiquette.

words.tr: n. 迷宫；难解的事件；错综复杂；
words.ex: The child got lost in the labyrinth.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在迷宫里迷路了。
words.en: A labyrinth is a complicated irregular network of passages or paths in which it is difficult to find one's way; a maze.

words.ex: He added an addendum to the contract.
words.ex_cn: 他在合同后加了一个附录。
words.en: An addendum is an additional section at the end of a book or document that provides further information or corrections.

words.tr: n. 女修道院院长；女庵主持
words.ex: The abbess leads the nuns in prayer.
words.ex_cn: 女修道院院长带领修女们祈祷。
words.en: An abbess is the female superior of a community of nuns, often having the same authority and responsibilities as an abbot in a male monastery.

words.ex: The speech was a panegyric to the retiring chairman.
words.ex_cn: 这场演讲是对即将退休的主席的赞颂。
words.en: A panegyric is a formal public speech, or written verse, delivered in high praise of a person or thing, a eulogy.

words.ex: He has a penchant for sweet food.
words.ex_cn: 他偏爱甜食。
words.en: A penchant is a strong liking or taste for something.

words.tr: adj. 灵活的；敏捷的；机敏的
words.ex: The cat is nimble and jumps over the fence.
words.ex_cn: 这只猫很敏捷，跳过了篱笆。
words.en: Someone who is nimble is able to move their fingers, hands, or legs quickly and easily.

words.ex: The effulgence of the sun made the sky bright.
words.ex_cn: 太阳的光辉使天空变得明亮。
words.en: Effulgence is a radiant splendor or brilliance.

words.ex: The viceroy ruled the colony for the king.
words.ex_cn: 总督为国王统治着殖民地。
words.en: A viceroy is a person who governs a country or province as the representative of a monarch.

words.ex: He was happy to get riddance of the old chair.
words.ex_cn: 他很高兴摆脱了那把旧椅子。
words.en: The act of getting rid of something or someone unwanted.

words.ex: The sun is a bright luminary in the sky.
words.ex_cn: 太阳是天空中一个明亮的发光体。
words.en: A luminary is a person who is very famous and highly respected, especially in a particular field.

words.ex: His altruism made him donate all his money to the poor.
words.ex_cn: 他的利他主义让他把所有钱捐给了穷人。
words.en: Altruism is the belief in or practice of disinterested and selfless concern for the well-being of others.

words.tr: adj. 多愁善感的；令人作呕的；自作多情的
words.ex: The movie was too mawkish with its fake tears.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影用虚假的眼泪显得过于矫情。
words.en: If you describe something as mawkish, you mean that it is sentimental in a way that you find unpleasant or silly.

words.tr: adj. 自然主义的；写实主义的；
words.ex: The painting has a naturalistic style, showing trees and animals as they really look.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画具有自然主义风格，真实地描绘了树木和动物。
words.en: Naturalistic describes something that is made or done in a way that is very similar to nature.

words.tr: n. 赋格曲；朦胧状态；神游症
words.ex: He composed a fugue for the piano.
words.ex_cn: 他为钢琴创作了一首赋格曲。
words.en: A fugue is a piece of music that begins with a theme that is then repeated and developed by different voices or instruments in a structured manner.

words.ex: His argument was full of sophisms that obscured the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他的论点充满了诡辩，掩盖了真相。
words.en: A sophism is a clever but false argument, especially one used deliberately to deceive.

words.ex: He used subterfuge to avoid answering the question.
words.ex_cn: 他用遁词来避免回答问题。
words.en: Deceit used in order to achieve one's goal.

words.ex: The gold mine became a bonanza for the town.
words.ex_cn: 这个金矿成了这个小镇的致富之源。
words.en: A bonanza is a situation or event that creates a sudden increase in wealth, good fortune, or profits.

words.tr: adj. 死后的；死后出版的；遗腹的
words.ex: He received a posthumous award for his bravery.
words.ex_cn: 他因勇敢而被追授了奖项。
words.en: Posthumous means occurring, awarded, or appearing after the death of the originator.

words.tr: adj. 预知的；有先见之明的
words.ex: His prescient warning saved many lives.
words.ex_cn: 他那有先见之明的警告挽救了许多生命。
words.en: Having or showing knowledge of events before they take place.

words.ex: He is a dogmatist who never listens to others.
words.ex_cn: 他是个从不听别人意见的教条主义者。
words.en: A dogmatist is someone who asserts their opinions in an arrogant manner, without considering the opinions of others.

words.tr: n. 年鉴编者；编年史作者
words.ex: The annalist wrote down the events of each year.
words.ex_cn: 编年史家记录了每年的事件。
words.en: An annalist is a person who writes annals, which are detailed records of events in chronological order.

words.ex: Finding my lost keys while walking in the park was pure serendipity.
words.ex_cn: 在公园散步时偶然找到了丢失的钥匙，这真是易遇奇缘的运气。
words.en: The occurrence and development of events by chance in a happy or beneficial way.

words.ex: The poem has four stanzas.
words.ex_cn: 这首诗有四节。
words.en: A stanza is a group of lines in a poem that are separated from other groups by a space.

words.tr: adj. 无所不在的；遍及各处的
words.ex: The smell of bread is omnipresent in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 早晨面包的香味无处不在。
words.en: If you describe something as omnipresent, you mean that it seems to be everywhere at the same time.

words.ex: He gave a short valediction at the graduation ceremony.
words.ex_cn: 他在毕业典礼上发表了简短的告别演说。
words.en: A valediction is a speech or statement made as a farewell, especially at a graduation ceremony.

words.ex: He spoke in the guise of a friend.
words.ex_cn: 他以朋友的伪装说话。
words.en: An external form, appearance, or manner of presentation, typically concealing the true nature of something.

words.tr: adj. 实用的；功利主义的；
words.ex: The chair is utilitarian and comfortable.
words.ex_cn: 这把椅子实用又舒适。
words.en: Utilitarian means relating to or adhering to the belief that the value of a thing or an action is determined by its utility.

words.ex: He is an equestrian rider who trains every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位每天早上训练的骑马者。
words.en: An equestrian is someone who rides horses, especially as a sport or a profession.

words.ex: He showed great temerity by challenging the expert without any preparation.
words.ex_cn: 他没有做任何准备就挑战专家，显得非常鲁莽。
words.en: If you say that someone has the temerity to do something, you are annoyed about something they have done which you think took a lot of nerve.

words.tr:
adj. 忏悔的；悔过的
n. 忏悔者；悔罪者
words.ex: He sat in the church, a penitent man seeking forgiveness.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在教堂里，一个忏悔的人寻求宽恕。
words.en: Feeling or showing sorrow and regret for having done wrong; repentant.

words.tr: adj. 邪恶的；险恶的；不祥的
words.ex: The old house looked sinister in the moonlight.
words.ex_cn: 那座老房子在月光下显得阴森可怖。
words.en: Something that is sinister seems evil or harmful.

words.ex: The miscreant was caught red-handed.
words.ex_cn: 那个恶棍被当场抓住。
words.en: A miscreant is someone who behaves badly or does not obey the law.

words.ex: The novel is epistolary, written as letters.
words.ex_cn: 这部小说是书信体的，由书信组成。
words.en: Relating to the writing of letters or literary works in the form of letters.

words.ex: She is the belle of the ball.
words.ex_cn: 她是舞会上的美女。
words.en: A belle is a beautiful and charming woman, especially the most beautiful one at a particular event or in a particular group.

words.ex: He used a colloquialism when he said 'gonna' instead of 'going to'.
words.ex_cn: 他说'gonna'而不是'going to'时，使用了一个口语词。
words.en: A colloquialism is a word or phrase that is used in informal language rather than in formal speech or writing.

words.ex: The court imposed a punitive fine for the violation.
words.ex_cn: 法院对这一违规行为处以惩罚性罚款。
words.en: Punitive actions, laws, or measures are intended to punish someone.

words.ex: The potentate ruled with an iron fist.
words.ex_cn: 这位统治者以铁腕统治。
words.en: A potentate is a ruler who has great power, especially one who rules over a large area or empire.

words.ex: His speech was full of trite phrases.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲充满了陈腐的表达。
words.en: If you say that something such as an idea, remark, or story is trite, you mean that it is dull and boring because it has been said or told too many times.

words.ex: He used guile to trick the guard.
words.ex_cn: 他用诡计骗过了守卫。
words.en: Guile is the quality of being skilled at deceiving people in order to achieve something.

words.ex: The teacher gave a lucid explanation of the math problem.
words.ex_cn: 老师对这道数学题做了一个易懂的解释。
words.en: If someone is lucid, they are able to understand things clearly and think clearly, especially when they have been very ill or confused.

words.tr: adj. 雕像般的；轮廓清晰的；体态优美的
words.ex: She is statuesque and stands tall like a model.
words.ex_cn: 她身材高挑，像模特一样挺拔。
words.en: If you describe someone, especially a woman, as statuesque, you mean that they are tall and beautiful in a way that is similar to a statue.

words.tr: adj. 诙谐的；开玩笑的；闹着玩的
words.ex: He told a jocose joke to make everyone laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他讲了一个幽默的笑话来让大家笑。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as jocose, you mean that they are playful and humorous.

words.tr: n. 亵渎；亵圣；悖理逆天的行为
words.ex: He committed sacrilege by breaking the holy statue.
words.ex_cn: 他砸了圣像，犯下了亵渎之罪。
words.en: If someone's behaviour or actions are described as sacrilege, they are considered to show a lack of respect for something that is regarded as holy or very important.

words.tr: v. 撤回声明；放弃信仰
words.ex: He recanted his statement after seeing the evidence.
words.ex_cn: 他在看到证据后撤回了他的话。
words.en: If you recant, you say publicly that you no longer hold a set of beliefs that you had in the past.

words.ex: The lecherous man made rude comments to women.
words.ex_cn: 那个好色的男人对女性说了粗俗的话。
words.en: If you describe someone as lecherous, you disapprove of them because they behave in a lustful and unpleasant way.

words.tr: n. 印刷术；排印；印刷样式
words.ex: He loves good typography in books.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢书中的好排版。
words.en: The art or process of setting and arranging types and printing from them.

words.ex: He learned about his ancestry from his grandmother.
words.ex_cn: 他从祖母那里了解了自己的血统。
words.en: Your ancestry is the series of ancestors from whom you are descended.

words.tr: adj. 莽撞的；有勇无谋的
words.ex: He made a foolhardy decision to climb the mountain alone.
words.ex_cn: 他做出了一个有勇无谋的决定，独自去爬山。
words.en: If you describe behavior or an action as foolhardy, you mean that it is very risky because it shows a lack of thought or care for the possible consequences.

words.ex: The resurrection of the dead is a key belief in Christianity.
words.ex_cn: 死者的复活是基督教的核心信仰。
words.en: The act of rising from the dead or returning to life; the revival of something that had been dormant or inactive.

words.tr: adj. 全能的；无所不能的
words.ex: The god is omnipotent.
words.ex_cn: 这个神是无所不能的。
words.en: Having unlimited power, able to do anything.

words.ex: He read an anthology of short stories last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚读了一本短篇故事选集。
words.en: An anthology is a collection of writings, such as poems or stories, that have been chosen by someone because they are considered to be the best or most interesting examples of their kind.

words.ex: The dark clouds foreshadow a storm.
words.ex_cn: 乌云预示着一场风暴。
words.en: If something foreshadows an event or situation, it suggests that it will happen.

words.ex: The battalion marched slowly through the town.
words.ex_cn: 那个营缓缓穿过小镇。
words.en: A battalion is a large group of soldiers that consists of three or more companies.

words.ex: He bought a small figurine from the market.
words.ex_cn: 他从市场上买了一个小雕像。
words.en: A figurine is a small ornamental statuette.

words.tr: adj. 好战凶猛的；寻衅的；言词刻毒的
words.ex: He gave a truculent reply to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了好斗的答复。
words.en: If you say that someone is truculent, you mean that they are bad-tempered and aggressive.

words.ex: Some people believe that their lives are predestined by fate.
words.ex_cn: 有些人认为他们的生活是由命运预先注定的。
words.en: If you say that something is predestined, you mean that it seems certain to happen, usually because it has been decided by God or by fate.

words.ex: He studied theology at a prestigious seminary.
words.ex_cn: 他在一所著名的神学院学习神学。
words.en: A seminary is a college for training people to become priests or ministers.

words.ex: It is paradoxical that he sleeps all day but stays awake at night.
words.ex_cn: 他白天睡觉却晚上醒着，这很矛盾。
words.en: If something is paradoxical, it involves two facts or qualities which seem to contradict each other.

words.tr: adj. 精力充沛的；热情洋溢的；
words.ex: The exuberant children ran around the park.
words.ex_cn: 那些精力充沛的孩子们在公园里跑来跑去。
words.en: If you are exuberant, you are full of energy, excitement, and cheerfulness.

words.ex: The stock price hit its nadir last month.
words.ex_cn: 股票价格上个月跌至最低点。
words.en: The nadir of something is the worst or lowest point that it reaches.

words.ex: The plasticity of the clay made it ideal for sculpting.
words.ex_cn: 黏土的可塑性使其非常适合雕塑。
words.en: The quality of being easily shaped or molded.

words.ex: He was a faithful disciple of the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他是老师的一名忠实弟子。
words.en: A disciple is a follower or student of a teacher, leader, or philosopher.

words.tr:
adj. 告别的
n. 告别辞；告别演说
words.ex: He gave a valedictory speech at graduation.
words.ex_cn: 他在毕业典礼上发表了告别演讲。
words.en: A valedictory speech, letter, or performance is one that is intended as a goodbye.

words.ex: The residue left in the cup was sugar.
words.ex_cn: 杯子里留下的残留物是糖。
words.en: A residue of something is a small amount that remains after the main part has gone or been taken or used.

words.tr: adj. 精神的；灵魂的；心理的；通灵的；
words.ex: He has a psychic connection with his twin brother.
words.ex_cn: 他和双胞胎兄弟有精神上的联系。
words.en: Relating to or denoting faculties or phenomena that are apparently inexplicable by natural laws, especially involving telepathy or clairvoyance.

words.ex: The sun is at its zenith at noon.
words.ex_cn: 太阳在正午时分达到最高点。
words.en: The zenith is the time at which something is most powerful or successful.

words.ex: He believes in fatalism and does not try to change his fate.
words.ex_cn: 他相信宿命论，不愿改变自己的命运。
words.en: Fatalism is the belief that all events are predetermined and therefore inevitable.

words.ex: Honesty is the main tenet of his life.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是他生活的宗旨。
words.en: A tenet is a principle or belief, especially one that is part of a larger system of beliefs.

words.ex: Her terse reply left no room for further discussion.
words.ex_cn: 她简洁的回答没有留下进一步讨论的余地。
words.en: A terse statement or comment is brief and to the point, often seeming rude or unfriendly because of its brevity.

words.tr: adj. 悦耳的；动听的；和谐的
words.ex: The singer's voice is euphonious.
words.ex_cn: 这位歌手的声音悦耳动听。
words.en: Something that is euphonious has a pleasant sound.

words.tr:
n. （文字）诽谤
v. 发表文字诽谤（某人）
words.ex: He wrote a false story about her, and it was libel.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一篇关于她的虚假文章，这是诽谤。
words.en: A libel is a published false statement that is damaging to a person's reputation; a written defamation.

words.ex: He is a maverick who always does things his own way.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个总是按自己方式做事的独行其是者。
words.en: If you describe someone as a maverick, you mean that they are unconventional and independent, and do not think or behave in the same way as other people.

words.tr:
adj. 隐姓埋名的；化名的
adv. 隐姓埋名地；匿名地
words.ex: He traveled incognito to avoid being recognized.
words.ex_cn: 他隐瞒身份旅行以避免被认出。
words.en: If someone does something incognito, they do it without letting people know who they are.

words.tr:
n. 预示；前兆；预感
v. 预示；预兆
words.ex: The dark clouds presage a storm.
words.ex_cn: 乌云预示着一场风暴。
words.en: If something presages a situation or event, it is considered to be a warning or sign of what is about to happen.

words.ex: The gods foreordain his fate.
words.ex_cn: 神早已注定他的命运。
words.en: To decide or determine (something) beforehand; to predestine.

words.ex: The recondite math problem confused most students.
words.ex_cn: 这道深奥的数学题让大多数学生感到困惑。
words.en: Recondite knowledge or information is known and understood by very few people.

words.ex: The poem uses assonance to sound musical.
words.ex_cn: 这首诗使用了近音韵来听起来悦耳。
words.en: Assonance is the repetition of vowel sounds in nearby words, used to add a musical effect to poetry or prose.

words.tr: n. 利他主义者；爱他主义者
words.ex: He was known as an altruist who always put others' needs before his own.
words.ex_cn: 他以利他主义者著称，总是把别人的需要放在自己之前。
words.en: An altruist is someone who shows unselfish concern for the welfare of others.

words.ex: He garnered food for the winter.
words.ex_cn: 他贮藏了过冬的食物。
words.en: To gather or collect something, especially information or support.

words.tr: v. 使（尤指不好的情形、体系、信仰）持续、长存；
words.ex: The system perpetuates inequality among the poor.
words.ex_cn: 这个体系使贫困人群的不平等持续存在。
words.en: To perpetuate something means to cause it to continue, especially for a long time.

words.ex: He is a bibliophile who loves reading books.
words.ex_cn: 他是个爱书之人，喜欢读书。
words.en: A bibliophile is a person who loves or collects books, especially as examples of fine or unusual printing, binding, or the like.

words.ex: His dominance in the game surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他在比赛中的支配表现让所有人感到惊讶。
words.en: Dominance is the state of being more powerful, important, or noticeable than other people or things.

words.ex: Obesity is a serious health problem in many countries.
words.ex_cn: 肥胖是许多国家的一个严重健康问题。
words.en: Obesity is a medical condition in which excess body fat has accumulated to the extent that it may have a negative effect on health.

words.tr: adj. 卑鄙的；污秽的；肮脏的
words.ex: He made a sordid deal to cheat his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一笔卑鄙的交易来欺骗他的朋友。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as sordid, you mean that it is very immoral or dishonest.

words.ex: He lives a spartan life with little food and no luxuries.
words.ex_cn: 他过着简朴的生活，食物很少，也没有奢侈品。
words.en: If you describe something as spartan, you mean that it is very simple and not at all luxurious, often because it is intended to be useful or practical rather than attractive.

words.ex: He gave a stellar performance in the play.
words.ex_cn: 他在剧中表现出色。
words.en: Of or relating to stars; outstanding or excellent.

words.ex: We visited a old chateau in the French countryside.
words.ex_cn: 我们参观了法国乡村的一座古老城堡。
words.en: A chateau is a large French country house or castle, often giving its name to wine made in its neighbourhood.

words.tr:
v. 缓慢而弯曲地流动；漫步；闲聊
n. 河流的曲折；漫步；迂回曲折的进程
words.ex: The river meanders through the forest.
words.ex_cn: 这条河蜿蜒穿过森林。
words.en: To meander means to follow a winding and turning course, often used to describe the way a river flows or the way a person walks without a clear direction.

words.tr:
adj. 教条（主义）的；空谈理论的
n. 教条主义者；空论家
words.ex: He is a doctrinaire who always follows rules strictly.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个教条主义者，总是严格遵守规则。
words.en: If you say that someone is doctrinaire, you are criticizing them for following fixed theories or principles rather than considering practical problems.

words.tr: adj. 拂晓的；黄昏的；朦胧的
words.ex: The rabbit is crepuscular, so it comes out at dawn and dusk.
words.ex_cn: 这只兔子是晨昏活动的，所以它在黎明和黄昏时出来。
words.en: Relating to or resembling twilight; dim or indistinct.

words.ex: He invented a neology to describe the new technology.
words.ex_cn: 他创造了一个新词来描述这项新技术。
words.en: The invention or use of new words or new senses of existing words.

words.tr: adj. 积满污垢的；肮脏的
words.ex: The boy's hands are grimy from playing in the dirt.
words.ex_cn: 男孩的手因为玩土变得脏兮兮的。
words.en: Something that is grimy is very dirty.

words.ex: The priest placed the offering on the altar.
words.ex_cn: 牧师把供品放在祭坛上。
words.en: An altar is a raised area in a place of worship where people can honor God with offerings.

words.tr:
v. 声称；意指；意味着
n. 意义；要旨；主要意思
words.ex: The letter purports to be from the president.
words.ex_cn: 这封信声称是总统写的。
words.en: If something purports to be a particular thing or to do a particular thing, it claims or appears to be that thing or to do that thing, even though this may not be the case.

words.ex: The overlord ruled the land with a strict hand.
words.ex_cn: 领主以严厉的方式统治着这片土地。
words.en: A person who has great power or authority over others, especially a ruler who has power over a large area or many people.

words.tr: adj. 不可剥夺（或分割）的
words.ex: Freedom is an inalienable right.
words.ex_cn: 自由是不可剥夺的权利。
words.en: An inalienable right or quality is one that cannot be taken away from you.

words.ex: It's preposterous to think cats can drive cars.
words.ex_cn: 认为猫会开车是极其荒谬的。
words.en: If you describe something as preposterous, you mean that it is extremely unreasonable and foolish.

words.tr: v. 消灭；毁掉；清除；抹除
words.ex: The bomb will obliterate the building.
words.ex_cn: 炸弹会摧毁那栋大楼。
words.en: To obliterate something means to remove all signs of it or to destroy it completely.

words.ex: He is obese because he eats too much junk food.
words.ex_cn: 他因为吃太多垃圾食品而肥胖。
words.en: If someone is obese, they are extremely fat.

words.ex: The soldier was honored for his valor in battle.
words.ex_cn: 这位士兵因在战斗中的英勇表现而受到表彰。
words.en: Valor is great courage, especially in a battle or war.

words.ex: The car got stuck in a morass after the heavy rain.
words.ex_cn: 大雨过后，汽车陷在了沼泽地里。
words.en: A morass is a complicated or confused situation that is difficult to get out of, or a stretch of low, soft, wet ground; a marsh.

words.tr: n. 高超的技艺；造诣；英勇；
words.ex: His prowess in basketball amazed everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他在篮球方面的高超技艺让所有人都惊叹。
words.en: Exceptional skill or ability in a particular field or activity.

words.ex: His misanthropy was evident in his solitary lifestyle.
words.ex_cn: 他独居的生活方式明显表现出他对人类的厌恶。
words.en: Misanthropy is a general dislike, distrust, or hatred of the human species or a disposition to dislike and/or distrust other people's silent consensus about reality.

words.tr: adj. 根深蒂固的；积习难改的
words.ex: He is an inveterate smoker who cannot quit.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个根深蒂固的吸烟者，无法戒掉。
words.en: If you describe someone as, for example, an inveterate liar or smoker, you mean that they have lied or smoked for a long time and are not likely to stop doing it.

words.tr: n. 教规；准则；真作集；精品集；大教堂教士
words.ex: The church follows the canon of its faith.
words.ex_cn: 教会遵循其信仰的教规。
words.en: A canon is a rule or principle that is considered to be established, accepted, or authoritative, especially in the fields of religion, literature, or law.

words.tr: v. 加苦味于；使怨愤；使难受
words.ex: The unfair treatment embittered him.
words.ex_cn: 不公平的对待使他变得愤恨。
words.en: To make someone feel bitter or resentful.

words.ex: The cowboy rode his horse up the butte.
words.ex_cn: 牛仔骑马上了那座平顶山。
words.en: A butte is an isolated hill with steep, often vertical sides and a small, relatively flat top; buttes are smaller than mesas, plateaus, and tablelands.

words.tr: adj. 枯燥的；乏味的；平淡无奇的
words.ex: His prosaic speech bored everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他平淡无奇的演讲让所有人都感到无聊。
words.en: If you describe something as prosaic, you mean that it is ordinary and not at all interesting or unusual.

words.ex: He writes books under a pseudonym.
words.ex_cn: 他用笔名写书。
words.en: A pseudonym is a name that someone, especially a writer, uses instead of their real name.

words.ex: The book begins with a short prologue.
words.ex_cn: 这本书以一个简短的序言开始。
words.en: A prologue is an introduction to a book, play, or other written work that sets the scene or provides background information.

words.ex: The slave worked in the fields every day.
words.ex_cn: 这个奴隶每天在田地里劳作。
words.en: A slave is someone who is the legal property of another person and is forced to obey them.

words.tr: adj. 精密复杂的；老练的；
words.ex: The phone has a sophisticated camera.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机有一个精密复杂的摄像头。
words.en: A sophisticated person is intelligent and knows a lot, so that they are able to understand complicated situations. A sophisticated machine, device, or method is more advanced or complex than others.

words.tr: n. 城市居民；市民；公民
words.ex: The burgher voted in the town meeting.
words.ex_cn: 市民在城镇会议上投票了。
words.en: A burgher is a citizen of a town or city, especially a member of the middle class.

words.tr: adj. 宫殿般的；宏伟的；富丽堂皇的
words.ex: He lives in a palatial house near the lake.
words.ex_cn: 他住在湖边一座宏伟的房子里。
words.en: If you describe a building or a place as palatial, you mean that it is very large, impressive, or luxurious, like a palace.

words.ex: She values chastity before marriage.
words.ex_cn: 她重视婚前的贞洁。
words.en: Chastity is the state of not having sex with anyone, or of only having sex with your husband or wife, especially because of your religious beliefs.

words.ex: His tenacity helped him finish the marathon despite the pain.
words.ex_cn: 他的坚韧让他即使疼痛也完成了马拉松。
words.en: The quality or fact of being able to grip something firmly; the quality or fact of being very determined and not giving up easily.

words.ex: He gave a sardonic smile when she told the truth.
words.ex_cn: 当她说出真相时，他露出了讽刺的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as sardonic, you mean they are mocking or scornful in a humorous way.

words.tr: adj. 猥亵的；淫秽的；诲淫的；好色的
words.ex: The novel was criticized for its salacious content.
words.ex_cn: 这部小说因其淫秽内容而受到批评。
words.en: If you describe something such as a book or joke as salacious, you think that it deals with sexual matters in an unnecessarily detailed way.

words.ex: The linguist parsed the sentence into its constituent parts.
words.ex_cn: 语言学家将句子分解为其组成部分。
words.en: To parse means to analyze a sentence or string of characters in a computer language into its component parts and describe their syntactic roles.

words.ex: He needs time to recuperate after surgery.
words.ex_cn: 他需要时间在手术后恢复。
words.en: To recuperate means to recover from illness or exertion, or to regain or make up for something lost or damaged.

words.tr: adj. 沉重的；笨重的；沉闷的
words.ex: He carried a ponderous box across the room.
words.ex_cn: 他搬着一个沉重的箱子穿过房间。
words.en: Something that is ponderous is very heavy or is very slow and clumsy because of its weight or size.

words.ex: The map shows the topography of the mountain area.
words.ex_cn: 这张地图显示了山区的地形。
words.en: The topography of an area is the physical features of its surface, such as hills, valleys, and rivers, especially the representation of these features on maps.

words.tr: n. 炼狱；受难的处所（或状态）；折磨
words.ex: He felt like he was in purgatory while waiting for the results.
words.ex_cn: 他在等待结果时感觉自己身处炼狱。
words.en: Purgatory is a place or state of suffering inhabited by the souls of sinners who are expiating their sins before going to heaven.

words.tr: n. 隐居者；遁世者；隐士
words.ex: He lives as a recluse in the woods.
words.ex_cn: 他住在树林里，过着隐居的生活。
words.en: A recluse is a person who lives alone and avoids other people.

words.ex: Their answers were concordant.
words.ex_cn: 他们的答案是一致的。
words.en: If two things are concordant, they are in agreement or harmony with each other.

words.ex: He lives in a monocracy where one person controls everything.
words.ex_cn: 他生活在一个由一个人掌控一切的独裁政体中。
words.en: A system of government by one person only.

words.ex: The movie is a melodrama with crying and loud arguments.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影是一部充满哭泣和激烈争吵的煽情剧。
words.en: A melodrama is a dramatic work in which the plot, typically sensational and designed to appeal strongly to the emotions, takes precedence over detailed characterization.

words.ex: She believed that their meeting was kismet.
words.ex_cn: 她相信他们的相遇是天命。
words.en: Kismet is a term used to express the concept of destiny or fate, often implying that events are predetermined.

words.ex: The temporal change of seasons affects our daily life.
words.ex_cn: 季节的时间变化影响我们的日常生活。
words.en: Relating to time as opposed to eternity; relating to worldly life as opposed to spiritual life.

words.tr:
adj. 挥霍的；丰富的；慷慨的；不吝惜的
n. 浪子
words.ex: The prodigal son returned home after years.
words.ex_cn: 那个浪子多年后回到了家。
words.en: A prodigal person spends money or resources in a way that is not careful and is too generous.

words.tr: adj. 异想天开的；古怪的；反复无常的
words.ex: The little girl wore a whimsical hat with flowers.
words.ex_cn: 小女孩戴着一顶带有花朵的古怪帽子。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as whimsical, you mean that they are unusual, playful, and unpredictable, often in a way that you find charming or amusing.

words.ex: She is pregnant and will have a baby next month.
words.ex_cn: 她怀孕了，下个月就要生宝宝了。
words.en: Having a baby developing in the uterus.

words.tr: adj. 智慧的；表现智慧的；赋予智慧的
words.ex: He reads sapiential texts to find wise advice.
words.ex_cn: 他阅读智慧文献以寻找明智的建议。
words.en: Relating to wisdom or the wise, often used to describe literature or sayings that impart wisdom.

words.ex: He will braze the metal parts together.
words.ex_cn: 他将把金属部件用钎焊连接在一起。
words.en: To join or decorate metal objects by soldering them with an alloy of brass or copper.

words.ex: The hiker stared into the dark abyss.
words.ex_cn: 徒步者凝视着黑暗的深渊。
words.en: An abyss is a very deep hole in the ground, or a very difficult or unpleasant situation that seems to have no end.

words.tr: n. 土著；（尤指澳大利亚的）土著居民
words.ex: The aborigine lived in the desert for thousands of years.
words.ex_cn: 这位土著在沙漠中生活了数千年。
words.en: An aborigine is one of the original or earliest known inhabitants of a country or region.

words.ex: The old abbey stands on a hill near the village.
words.ex_cn: 这座古老的修道院坐落在村庄附近的山上。
words.en: A complex of buildings housing a monastery or convent, typically including a church, living quarters, and other facilities.

words.ex: The river flows through a deep ravine.
words.ex_cn: 河流流经一个深谷。
words.en: A ravine is a deep, narrow gorge with steep sides, often carved by a river or stream.

words.tr: n. 同形（同音）异义词；同名异物
words.ex: The words 'bear' and 'bare' are homonyms.
words.ex_cn: “bear”和“bare”这两个词是同音异义词。
words.en: A homonym is a word that is pronounced the same as another word but differs in meaning. The words may be spelled the same, such as 'rose' (flower) and 'rose' (past tense of rise), or differently, such as 'carat', 'caret', and 'carrot'.

words.tr: adj. 宽松的；容积大的；部头大的；卷数多的
words.ex: She wore a voluminous dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条宽松的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: Something that is voluminous is very large or contains a lot of things.

words.tr: n. 新信徒；新手；初学者
words.ex: The neophyte learned the prayers from the elder.
words.ex_cn: 新信徒向长者学习祷告。
words.en: A neophyte is someone who is new to a particular activity, subject, or religion and is therefore inexperienced.

words.ex: The troubadour sang love songs in the castle.
words.ex_cn: 游吟诗人在城堡里唱情歌。
words.en: A troubadour was a composer and performer of Old Occitan lyric poetry during the High Middle Ages (1100–1350). Since the word troubadour is etymologically masculine, a female troubadour is usually called a trobairitz.

words.tr:
n. 高谈阔论；长篇大论；大声斥责的讲话
v. 作长篇大论；高谈阔论；猛烈的批评或训斥
words.ex: The politician gave a long harangue about taxes.
words.ex_cn: 这位政客就税收问题发表了一番长篇高谈阔论。
words.en: A harangue is a lengthy and aggressive speech, especially one delivered in public.

words.tr: adj. 自负的；自命不凡的；浮华的
words.ex: He gave a pompous speech with big words.
words.ex_cn: 他用华丽的词藻做了一番自大的演讲。
words.en: If you describe someone as pompous, you mean that they behave or speak in a very serious way because they think they are more important than they really are.

words.tr: v. （使）音相谐；（使）成为准押韵
words.ex: The poet tries to assonate sounds in his lines.
words.ex_cn: 这位诗人试图在诗行中使音韵和谐。
words.en: To correspond in sound, especially in vowel sound; to rhyme partially or imperfectly.

words.ex: He rebut the claim with clear evidence.
words.ex_cn: 他用清晰的证据反驳了这一说法。
words.en: If you rebut a charge or criticism that is made against you, you give reasons why it is untrue or unacceptable.

words.tr: adj. 不容亵渎的；不可侵犯的
words.ex: Her privacy is inviolable.
words.ex_cn: 她的隐私是不可侵犯的。
words.en: If a law or principle is inviolable, it must not be broken or treated without respect.

words.ex: The statue was placed on a marble pedestal.
words.ex_cn: 雕像被放置在大理石底座上。
words.en: A pedestal is the base or support on which a statue, obelisk, or column is mounted.

words.ex: He bought a replica of the ancient statue.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一件古代雕像的复制品。
words.en: A replica of something such as a statue, building, or weapon is an accurate copy of it.

words.tr: adj. 无可挑剔的；无瑕疵的；
words.ex: Her impeccable manners impressed everyone at the dinner.
words.ex_cn: 她无可挑剔的礼仪让晚宴上的每个人都印象深刻。
words.en: If you describe something as impeccable, you are emphasizing that it is perfect and has no faults.

words.ex: The choir sang in unisonous harmony.
words.ex_cn: 合唱团以一致的和谐演唱。
words.en: Sounding together in harmony; simultaneous in pitch.

words.tr:
adj. 多种语言的；通晓数种语言的
n. 通晓数种语言的人
words.ex: He is a polyglot who speaks five languages.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位会说五种语言的多语者。
words.en: A polyglot is a person who knows and is able to use several languages.

words.ex: He wrote a treatise on ancient Chinese philosophy.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一部关于中国古代哲学的专著。
words.en: A treatise is a formal and systematic written discourse on some subject, generally longer and more detailed than an essay.

words.ex: The miser saved all his money and never spent it.
words.ex_cn: 这个吝啬鬼把所有的钱都存起来，从不花掉。
words.en: A miser is a person who is extremely unwilling to spend money, often to the point of living in poverty despite having wealth.

words.ex: The gypsy played violin on the street.
words.ex_cn: 吉卜赛人在街上拉小提琴。
words.en: A gypsy is a member of a race of people who travel from place to place, especially in Europe, and who traditionally live by seasonal work, music, and fortune-telling.

words.ex: The refulgent sun illuminated the entire room.
words.ex_cn: 灿烂的阳光照亮了整个房间。
words.en: Shining brightly; radiant.

words.ex: She saw the aurora in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 她在夜空中看到了极光。
words.en: An aurora is a natural light display in the sky, predominantly seen in the high latitude (Arctic and Antarctic) regions, caused by the collision of solar wind and magnetospheric charged particles with the high altitude atmosphere.

words.ex: His bibliomania led him to spend a fortune on rare books.
words.ex_cn: 他的藏书癖让他花了一大笔钱购买珍本书。
words.en: An excessive fondness for acquiring and possessing books.

words.tr:
v. 润饰；修整
n. 润饰；修整
words.ex: The photographer spent hours retouching the photo to remove blemishes.
words.ex_cn: 摄影师花了几个小时修整照片以去除瑕疵。
words.en: To retouch a photograph or a piece of artwork means to improve its appearance by making small changes or corrections.

words.ex: The aforesaid rule applies to all students.
words.ex_cn: 上述规则适用于所有学生。
words.en: Used to refer to something that has already been mentioned.

words.tr: adj. 粗鲁辱骂的；恶语毁谤的；下流粗俗的
words.ex: The politician was criticized for making scurrilous remarks about his opponent.
words.ex_cn: 这位政客因对对手发表下流的言论而受到批评。
words.en: If you describe something as scurrilous, you mean that it is vulgar and intended to damage someone's reputation.

words.tr:
n. 诡计；花言巧语
v. 欺骗；诱骗；消磨
words.ex: He used a clever wile to deceive his enemies.
words.ex_cn: 他使用了一个巧妙的诡计来欺骗他的敌人。
words.en: If you say that someone uses wiles to achieve something, you mean that they use clever methods to persuade people to do what they want.

words.ex: He ensconced himself in the armchair with a book.
words.ex_cn: 他把自己安顿在扶手椅里看书。
words.en: If you ensconce yourself somewhere, you settle yourself there in a safe, comfortable, or secret place.

words.ex: He can describe the picture in one sentence.
words.ex_cn: 他能用一句话描述这幅画。
words.en: If you describe a person, object, event, or situation, you say what they are like or what happened.

words.tr: n. 复制本；摹本；仿制品；传真
words.ex: He sent a facsimile of the document to his office.
words.ex_cn: 他把文件的传真发到了办公室。
words.en: An exact copy of a document, picture, or piece of writing, especially one that has been made by a machine.

words.tr:
v. 断然拒绝
n. 粗暴回绝；生硬的拒绝
words.ex: He rebuffed her offer with a shake of his head.
words.ex_cn: 他摇了摇头，拒绝了她的提议。
words.en: If you rebuff someone or rebuff a suggestion that they make, you refuse to do what they suggest.

words.ex: The dark clouds looked ominous before the storm.
words.ex_cn: 暴风雨来临前，乌云显得不祥。
words.en: If you describe something as ominous, you mean that it worries you because it makes you think that something unpleasant is going to happen.

words.ex: His egregious mistake cost the team the game.
words.ex_cn: 他严重的错误让球队输掉了比赛。
words.en: An egregious error or failure is extremely bad and noticeable.

words.tr: adj. 教区的；地方范围的；思想狭隘的
words.ex: The priest served in a small parochial church.
words.ex_cn: 牧师在一座小型教区教堂服务。
words.en: If you describe someone as parochial, you are criticizing them because you think they are too concerned with their own affairs and should be thinking about more important things.

words.ex: The hiker stood at the precipice, afraid to move.
words.ex_cn: 徒步者站在悬崖边，不敢动。
words.en: A very steep or overhanging place on a cliff or mountain; a situation of great peril.

words.tr: n. 陈词滥调；老生常谈；
words.ex: His speech was full of platitudes about hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲充满了关于努力工作的陈词滥调。
words.en: A platitude is a statement that has been used so often that it is meaningless and shows a lack of original thought.

words.tr: n. 女家长制；女族长制；母权制
words.ex: In some cultures, matriarchy is the dominant social system.
words.ex_cn: 在一些文化中，母权制是主导的社会体系。
words.en: A matriarchy is a social system in which females hold the primary power positions in roles of political leadership, moral authority, social privilege, and control of property.

words.tr: adj. 天使般的；可爱的；善良的
words.ex: Her smile is angelic and calm.
words.ex_cn: 她的微笑如天使般宁静。
words.en: If you describe someone as angelic, you mean that they are very good, kind, and gentle.

words.tr: adj. 似是而非的；貌似有理的
words.ex: His argument is specious and misleading.
words.ex_cn: 他的论点看似有理但具有误导性。
words.en: Something that is specious seems to be good, sound, or correct but is actually wrong or false.

words.tr: n. 意志力；自愿选择；自行决断
words.ex: He did it of his own volition.
words.ex_cn: 他是出于自己的意愿做的。
words.en: The power to make your own decisions or choices.

words.ex: The old man gave an enigmatic smile.
words.ex_cn: 那位老人露出了一个神秘的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as enigmatic, you mean they are mysterious and difficult to understand.

words.tr: n. 隐士；隐居者；遁世者
words.ex: The hermit lives alone in a small cave.
words.ex_cn: 这位隐士独自住在一个小山洞里。
words.en: A hermit is someone who lives alone and apart from society, often for religious reasons.

words.tr: n. 工艺专科学院；理工专科学院；
words.ex: He enrolled in a polytechnic to learn engineering.
words.ex_cn: 他进入了一所工艺专科学院学习工程。
words.en: A polytechnic is an institution of higher education offering courses in many subjects, especially vocational or technical subjects.

words.ex: The internet created many new neologisms like 'selfie' and 'blog'.
words.ex_cn: 互联网创造了许多新词，比如'selfie'和'blog'。
words.en: A neologism is a newly coined word or expression that may be in the process of entering common use, but has not yet been accepted into mainstream language.

words.tr: adj. 有男子气概的；阳刚的；强有力的
words.ex: He is a virile man who works hard every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个精力充沛的男子，每天努力工作。
words.en: If you describe a man as virile, you mean that he has the qualities that a man is traditionally expected to have, such as strength and sexual power.

words.ex: His heterodox ideas shocked the traditional scholars.
words.ex_cn: 他的非正统观点让传统学者感到震惊。
words.en: Heterodox ideas, opinions, or practices are different from the accepted or official ones.

words.tr: adj. 言简意赅的；简明扼要的；凝练的
words.ex: He gave a laconic reply: 'Yes.'
words.ex_cn: 他简短地回答：‘是的。’
words.en: If you describe someone as laconic, you mean that they use very few words to say something, so that they seem casual or unfriendly.

words.ex: He gave a verbose answer to the simple question.
words.ex_cn: 他对简单的问题给出了冗长的回答。
words.en: Using or containing more words than are necessary; long-winded.

words.ex: The priest gave a short homily after the prayer.
words.ex_cn: 祷告后，牧师做了一个简短的讲道。
words.en: A homily is a religious discourse which is intended to edify a congregation, typically given by a priest or minister during a service.

words.ex: The peninsular town has narrow streets and old houses.
words.ex_cn: 这个半岛上的小镇有狭窄的街道和古老的房屋。
words.en: Relating to or characteristic of a peninsula; resembling a peninsula.

words.ex: His ribald jokes were inappropriate for a family gathering.
words.ex_cn: 他的下流笑话不适合家庭聚会。
words.en: If you describe someone's language or behavior as ribald, you mean that it refers to sex in a rude or humorous way.

words.ex: The herald announced the king's arrival.
words.ex_cn: 传令官宣布了国王的到来。
words.en: A herald is someone who carries or proclaims important news; a forerunner or harbinger.

words.ex: The mariner sailed the ship across the ocean.
words.ex_cn: 这位海员驾船横渡了海洋。
words.en: A mariner is a sailor.

words.tr: adj. 类似的；同源的；一致的；相应的
words.ex: The two animals have homologous limbs.
words.ex_cn: 这两种动物有类似的四肢。
words.en: Having the same relation, relative position, or structure, in particular.

words.ex: The words 'light' and 'night' are assonant.
words.ex_cn: 单词 'light' 和 'night' 是押元音的。
words.en: Having or producing a pleasant sound, especially through the repetition of similar vowel sounds.

words.ex: The artistry of the painting amazed everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画的艺术性让每个人都惊叹。
words.en: The skill of an artist, or the quality of being artistic.

words.tr: v. 跑在...之前；预示；胜过；为...之先驱
words.ex: He foreruns the team by running fast.
words.ex_cn: 他跑得快，走在队伍前面。
words.en: To be a sign or warning that something is going to happen.

words.ex: The fate was preordained by the gods.
words.ex_cn: 命运早已由神明注定。
words.en: If something is preordained, it is decided by God or fate in advance.

words.tr:
v. 夺取；费力取得；歪曲
n. 扭；拧
words.ex: He wrests the ball from his opponent.
words.ex_cn: 他从对手那里抢走球。
words.en: To wrest something from someone means to take it from them with a lot of effort, often because they do not want to give it to you.

words.tr: n. 游牧民；流浪者；游牧生活；流浪生活
words.ex: The nomad walks with his sheep across the desert.
words.ex_cn: 游牧民带着他的羊群穿越沙漠。
words.en: A nomad is someone who has no permanent home and moves according to the seasons from place to place in search of food, water, and grazing land.

words.ex: He showed prescience by predicting the storm.
words.ex_cn: 他通过预测风暴展现了先见之明。
words.en: The ability to know or predict what will happen in the future.

words.tr:
n. 谷歌（网络搜索引擎）；
vt. 用搜索引擎搜索（尤指用谷歌搜索引擎）；
words.ex: I use Google to find information online.
words.ex_cn: 我使用谷歌在网上查找信息。
words.en: To use the Google search engine to find information on the internet.

words.ex: The recalcitrant student refused to follow the rules.
words.ex_cn: 这个顽抗的学生拒绝遵守规则。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as recalcitrant, you mean that they are unwilling to obey orders or are difficult to deal with.

words.ex: The venerable teacher has taught for over 40 years.
words.ex_cn: 这位值得尊敬的老师已经教书40多年了。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as venerable, you mean that they are old and respected.

words.ex: His lascivious remarks made her uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 他挑逗性的言论让她感到不适。
words.en: If you describe someone as lascivious, you disapprove of them because they show a very strong interest in sex, especially in a crude or unpleasant way.

words.tr: n. 文物工作者；古文物收藏家；古玩商
words.ex: He is an antiquary who collects old coins.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位收藏古币的古物研究者。
words.en: An antiquary is a person who studies or collects antiques and ancient artifacts.

words.tr: v. （使）复活；（使）恢复知觉；（使）复兴
words.ex: The paramedics tried to resuscitate the man after he collapsed.
words.ex_cn: 当这位男子晕倒后，急救人员试图救活他。
words.en: To resuscitate someone means to bring them back to consciousness or to make them start breathing again after they have stopped.

words.tr: adj. 红润的；华丽的；过分装饰的
words.ex: Her cheeks were florid after running in the cold.
words.ex_cn: 她在寒冷中跑步后，脸颊变得红润。
words.en: If you describe something as florid, you mean that it is complicated and elaborate rather than plain and simple.

words.tr:
adj. 先锋的；前卫的
n. 先锋派；前卫
words.ex: The artist uses avant-garde styles in her paintings.
words.ex_cn: 这位艺术家在她的画作中使用前卫的风格。
words.en: Avant-garde is used to describe people or works that are experimental or innovative, particularly in the arts.

words.ex: The smoke is an indicant of fire.
words.ex_cn: 烟是火灾的迹象。
words.en: Something that serves to indicate or suggest something.

words.tr: n. 无家可归的人；流浪儿；无主的动物
words.ex: The waif was found wandering the streets alone.
words.ex_cn: 这个流浪儿被发现独自一人在街上徘徊。
words.en: A waif is a person, especially a child, who has no home or friends and is very thin and poorly dressed.

words.tr: n. 骑士精神；骑士制度；
words.ex: He showed chivalry by helping the lady carry her bags.
words.ex_cn: 他帮助那位女士提包，展现了骑士精神。
words.en: Chivalry is a set of qualities such as bravery, courtesy, honor, and gallantry toward women, associated with the medieval institution of knighthood.

words.ex: She replenished the water bottle after the hike.
words.ex_cn: 她在徒步后补充了水瓶里的水。
words.en: If you replenish something, you make it full or complete again.

words.ex: The old factory was a colossus in the town.
words.ex_cn: 那座旧工厂是镇上的庞然大物。
words.en: A colossus is a statue that is much bigger than life size. In a figurative sense, it can also refer to a person or thing of enormous size, importance, or ability.

words.tr: adj. 云雾状的；朦胧的；模糊的
words.ex: The nebulous cloud floated slowly across the sky.
words.ex_cn: 那团云雾状的云缓缓飘过天空。
words.en: If you describe something as nebulous, you mean that it is vague and not clearly defined or not easy to describe.

words.tr: adj. 明智的；有见识的；判断正确的
words.ex: He made a judicious choice about which book to buy.
words.ex_cn: 他做出了一个明智的买书决定。
words.en: If you describe an action or decision as judicious, you approve of it because you think that it shows good judgment and sense.

words.tr: n. 自明之理；不言而喻的道理；老生常谈
words.ex: It is a truism that water boils at 100 degrees Celsius.
words.ex_cn: 水在100摄氏度沸腾，这是一个不言而喻的事实。
words.en: A truism is a statement that is obviously true and says nothing new or interesting.

words.ex: The archbishop gave a speech at the church.
words.ex_cn: 大主教在教堂发表了一次演讲。
words.en: An archbishop is a bishop of the highest rank who is in charge of an archdiocese.

words.tr:
v. （把绳）拴在系绳栓上；停止
n. 栓紧绳索；绳索固定点
words.ex: He will belay the climber from the top.
words.ex_cn: 他将在顶部为攀岩者系绳保护。
words.en: To secure or fasten a rope to a rock, post, or other object, especially in climbing or sailing.

words.ex: The clear sky was an auspice of good weather.
words.ex_cn: 晴朗的天空是好天气的预兆。
words.en: An auspice is a sign or omen that is believed to predict the future, often seen as favorable or supportive. It can also refer to the protection or support provided by a person or organization.

words.tr: v. 重述要点；简要回顾
words.ex: Can you recapitulate the main points of the lecture?
words.ex_cn: 你能重述一下讲座的主要要点吗？
words.en: If you recapitulate something, you say it again briefly, or you give a summary of it.

words.ex: His dishonesty became his nemesis.
words.ex_cn: 他的不诚实成了他的天谴。
words.en: Someone's nemesis is a person or thing that is very difficult for them to defeat.

words.ex: The technology is becoming obsolescent as newer models are introduced.
words.ex_cn: 随着新模型的推出，这项技术正在变得过时。
words.en: Becoming obsolete or going out of use.

words.tr: adj. 彩虹色的；色彩斑斓的
words.ex: The soap bubble is iridescent in the sunlight.
words.ex_cn: 肥皂泡在阳光下呈现出彩虹色。
words.en: Showing luminous colors that seem to change when seen from different angles.

words.tr:
n. 颈手枷
v. 给…上颈手枷；使惹人嘲笑；示众；公开批评
words.ex: The newspaper did not hesitate to pillory the corrupt politician.
words.ex_cn: 这家报纸毫不犹豫地公开谴责那位腐败的政客。
words.en: A pillory is a wooden framework with holes for the head and hands, in which offenders were formerly locked and exposed to public abuse or ridicule. As a verb, to pillory means to expose someone to public scorn, ridicule, or abuse.

words.ex: She is the quintessence of grace.
words.ex_cn: 她是优雅的典范。
words.en: The quintessence of something is the most perfect or typical example of it.

words.tr: adj. 唐吉诃德式的；不切实际的
words.ex: He made a quixotic effort to fix the broken bridge with sticks and glue.
words.ex_cn: 他用树枝和胶水试图修复那座破桥，这真是异想天开。
words.en: If you describe someone's ideas or plans as quixotic, you mean that they are imaginative or hopeful but unrealistic.

words.tr: n. 攻击传统观念的人；
words.ex: He is an iconoclast who challenges old beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 他是个挑战传统观念的人。
words.en: An iconoclast is someone who criticizes or attacks cherished beliefs or institutions.

words.tr: adj. 全知的；无所不知的
words.ex: The omniscient narrator knows everything about the characters.
words.ex_cn: 全知的叙述者了解角色的一切。
words.en: Knowing everything; having infinite awareness, understanding, and insight.

words.tr: n. 沙文主义；侵略主义
words.ex: He shouted with jingoism during the national parade.
words.ex_cn: 他在国庆游行中带着沙文主义大喊大叫。
words.en: Jingoism is an extreme form of patriotism that often involves a belligerent foreign policy, advocating the use of threats or actual force against other countries in order to safeguard what it perceives as its country's national interests.

words.ex: His collection of virtu was the envy of many collectors.
words.ex_cn: 他收藏的古董让许多收藏家羡慕不已。
words.en: Virtu refers to a knowledge of or expertise in the fine arts, especially in relation to the appreciation or collection of art objects.

words.ex: He bought the car on a whim.
words.ex_cn: 他一时兴起买了这辆车。
words.en: A whim is a sudden desire or change of mind, especially one that is unusual or unexplained.

words.ex: He checks the almanac for the next full moon.
words.ex_cn: 他查阅历书以查找下一个满月的日期。
words.en: An almanac is a book published every year which contains information about events connected with a particular subject or activity, and facts and statistics about that subject or activity.

words.ex: The bird sang a melodious song at dawn.
words.ex_cn: 鸟儿在黎明时唱出旋律优美的歌。
words.en: If something such as a voice or a tune is melodious, it is pleasant to listen to because it has a musical quality.

words.ex: He works in meteorology and predicts the weather.
words.ex_cn: 他从事气象学工作，预测天气。
words.en: Meteorology is the scientific study of the atmosphere and of atmospheric conditions, especially as they relate to weather and weather forecasting.

words.tr: n. 年代学；年表；按年代次序的排列
words.ex: He wrote the chronology of ancient Rome.
words.ex_cn: 他写了古罗马的年代顺序。
words.en: Chronology is the arrangement of events or dates in the order of their occurrence.

words.ex: He tried to usurp the throne from his brother.
words.ex_cn: 他试图从他兄弟手中篡夺王位。
words.en: If you say that someone usurps a job, role, title, or position, they take it from someone when they have no right to do this.

words.tr: n. （古罗马的）酒神节；狂饮的闹宴
words.ex: The party turned into a bacchanalia after midnight.
words.ex_cn: 午夜过后，派对变成了一个狂欢的酒宴。
words.en: A bacchanalia is a wild and drunken celebration or orgy.

words.tr: n. 古文物研究者（或收藏家、经营者）；
words.ex: The antiquarian bought an old Roman coin at the market.
words.ex_cn: 这位古文物研究者在市场买了一枚古罗马硬币。
words.en: An antiquarian is someone who studies or collects antiques or antiquities.

words.ex: Life is full of vicissitude.
words.ex_cn: 生活充满起伏。
words.en: A change of circumstances or fortune, typically one that is unwelcome or unpleasant.

words.ex: The sheep grazed on the grassy brae.
words.ex_cn: 羊群在长满草的山坡上吃草。
words.en: A slope or hillside.

words.ex: She was accused of practicing witchcraft.
words.ex_cn: 她被指控施行巫术。
words.en: Witchcraft is the use of magical powers, especially for evil purposes.

words.tr: n. 时代精神；时代思潮
words.ex: The film captures the zeitgeist of the 1960s.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影捕捉到了20世纪60年代的时代精神。
words.en: The defining spirit or mood of a particular period of history as shown by the ideas and beliefs of the time.

words.tr:
n. 起义者；叛乱者；造反者
adj. 叛乱的；起义的
words.ex: The insurgent attacked the village at night.
words.ex_cn: 叛乱分子在夜里袭击了村庄。
words.en: An insurgent is a person who rises in active revolt against an established authority or government.

words.ex: The artist used a chromatic palette to create vibrant landscapes.
words.ex_cn: 艺术家使用彩色调色板创作出充满活力的风景画。
words.en: Relating to colors or the use of colors; also relating to or using notes not belonging to the diatonic scale of the key in which a passage is written.

words.tr: adj. 前面的；前部的；较早的
words.ex: The anterior part of the brain controls movement.
words.ex_cn: 大脑的前部控制运动。
words.en: Located before or at the front of something.

words.ex: The bicycle was a precursor to the car.
words.ex_cn: 自行车是汽车的先驱。
words.en: A precursor is something that happened or existed before another thing, especially if it either developed into it or had an influence on it.

words.tr: adj. 轻飘的；缥缈的；虚空的；精致的；
words.ex: The ethereal scarf floated gently in the wind.
words.ex_cn: 那条轻飘的围巾在风中轻轻飘动。
words.en: Something that is ethereal is extremely delicate and light in a way that seems not to be of this world.

words.ex: The epitaph on his grave says, 'Beloved father and friend.'
words.ex_cn: 他墓碑上的墓志铭写着：‘受人爱戴的父亲和朋友。’
words.en: An epitaph is a short piece of writing or a poem about a dead person, especially one written on their gravestone.

words.ex: The monk meditates every morning.
words.ex_cn: 这位僧侣每天早上冥想。
words.en: A monk is a member of a religious community of men who live by certain vows and usually wear a habit.

words.tr: adj. 尖锐的；有力的；精辟的
words.ex: His trenchant criticism left no room for doubt.
words.ex_cn: 他尖锐的批评让人没有怀疑的余地。
words.en: If you say that someone's speech or writing is trenchant, you mean that it is very clear and effective, often in criticizing something.

words.ex: The people rose up against the tyranny of the king.
words.ex_cn: 人民反抗了国王的暴虐。
words.en: Tyranny is cruel and unfair treatment by someone with power over other people, or a government in which a single ruler has absolute power.

words.tr: adj. 修辞性的；词藻华丽的；反问的
words.ex: He asked a rhetorical question to make a point.
words.ex_cn: 他问了一个修辞性的问题来阐明观点。
words.en: A rhetorical question is one which is asked in order to make a statement rather than to get an answer.

words.ex: His views were considered heretical by the religious authorities.
words.ex_cn: 他的观点被宗教权威认为是异端的。
words.en: If someone's beliefs or actions are heretical, they are contrary to the official or accepted beliefs or practices of a particular religion or group.

words.ex: The book contains esoteric ideas that only experts understand.
words.ex_cn: 这本书包含了只有专家才能理解的深奥思想。
words.en: Intended for or likely to be understood by only a small number of people with a specialized knowledge or interest.

words.ex: He gave a succinct answer.
words.ex_cn: 他给出了一个简洁的回答。
words.en: Something that is succinct expresses facts or ideas clearly and in few words.

words.tr: adj. 言简意赅的；精练的
words.ex: He gave a pithy answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了简洁有力的回答。
words.en: A pithy statement or piece of writing is short, clear, and full of meaning.

words.tr:
v. 潦草地写；匆匆地写；乱涂乱画
n. 潦草的字迹；涂鸦
words.ex: He scribbled his name on the paper.
words.ex_cn: 他在纸上潦草地写了名字。
words.en: To scribble means to write or draw something quickly or carelessly.

words.tr: adj. 游历的；游离不定的；行为不当的；出轨的
words.ex: The errant knight traveled far across the land.
words.ex_cn: 这位游历的骑士穿越了广袤的土地。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as errant, you mean that they have strayed from the proper course or standards.

words.ex: He lives in a quiet borough of New York.
words.ex_cn: 他住在纽约的一个安静的行政区。
words.en: A borough is a town, or a district within a large city, that has its own local government.

words.tr:
n. 拙劣的模仿（作品）
v. 拙劣模仿
words.ex: The film is a parody of classic horror movies.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影是对经典恐怖电影的滑稽模仿。
words.en: A parody is a humorous or satirical imitation of a serious piece of literature or writing.

words.tr:
adj. 海滨的；沿岸的
n. 沿（海）岸地区
words.ex: The littoral zone has many small fish and shells.
words.ex_cn: 滨海区有许多小鱼和贝壳。
words.en: The littoral refers to the region of the shore of a lake, sea, or ocean, especially the zone between high and low water marks. It can also describe something relating to or situated on the shore of the sea or a lake.

words.tr: adj. 遮遮掩掩的；守口如瓶的；
words.ex: He gave a secretive smile and walked away.
words.ex_cn: 他露出一个遮遮掩掩的微笑，然后走开了。
words.en: If you are secretive, you like to have secrets and to keep your knowledge, feelings, or intentions hidden.

words.ex: They enthrone the king with great ceremony.
words.ex_cn: 他们以盛大的仪式拥立国王。
words.en: To install a monarch on a throne in a ceremony.

words.tr:
adj. 截平的；截短的；被删节的；切去顶端的
v. 截短；修剪；修短；“truncate”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The truncated pyramid has a flat top.
words.ex_cn: 这个截平的金字塔有一个平坦的顶部。
words.en: If something is truncated, it is cut short or cut off.

words.ex: The precession of the equinoxes is a slow movement of the Earth's axis.
words.ex_cn: 春分点的岁差是地球自转轴的缓慢移动。
words.en: The slow movement of the axis of a spinning body around another axis due to a torque (such as gravitational influence) acting to change the direction of the first axis.

words.ex: The machinations of the rival company were uncovered.
words.ex_cn: 竞争对手公司的阴谋被揭露了。
words.en: A machination is a plot or scheme, especially one that is complex or devious.

words.tr: n. 俏皮话；妙语；诙谐语
words.ex: His speech was filled with witticisms that kept the audience laughing.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲中充满了妙语，让观众笑声不断。
words.en: A witticism is a clever and amusing remark.

words.tr: adj. 无法解释的；费解的
words.ex: His sudden silence was inexplicable.
words.ex_cn: 他突然的沉默无法解释。
words.en: If something is inexplicable, you cannot explain why it happens or why it is true.

words.ex: She had a presentient feeling that something bad was going to happen.
words.ex_cn: 她有一种预感，觉得有什么不好的事情即将发生。
words.en: Having a premonition or foreboding; able to sense something before it happens.

words.ex: He believes in nihilism and thinks nothing matters.
words.ex_cn: 他相信虚无主义，认为什么都不重要。
words.en: Nihilism is the belief that all values are baseless and that nothing can be known or communicated.

words.ex: He was raised in a family that practices catholicism.
words.ex_cn: 他在一个信奉天主教的家庭中长大。
words.en: The faith, practice, and church order of the Roman Catholic Church.

words.ex: The concept of antemundane existence is often explored in theological discussions.
words.ex_cn: 世界形成前的存在概念经常在神学讨论中被探讨。
words.en: Existing or occurring before the creation of the world.

words.ex: The vagabond sleeps under the bridge.
words.ex_cn: 这个流浪汉睡在桥下。
words.en: A vagabond is someone who wanders from place to place without a home or job.

words.ex: The phone has a simple interface.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机有一个简单的界面。
words.en: An interface is a point where two systems, subjects, organizations, etc. meet and interact.

words.ex: The city is at a latitude of 40 degrees north.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市位于北纬40度。
words.en: Latitude is the distance of a place north or south of the equator, measured in degrees.

words.tr:
v. 细述；叙述
n. 叙述；重新计票
words.ex: He tried to recount the accident to the police.
words.ex_cn: 他试图向警察重新叙述那场事故。
words.en: To recount means to tell someone about something that happened, often in detail; or to count something again to make sure the number is correct.

words.tr: n. 宣言；声明；格言；警句
words.ex: The judge's dictum was clear and final.
words.ex_cn: 法官的宣言清晰而最终。
words.en: A dictum is a formal pronouncement from an authoritative source; it can also be a short statement that expresses a general truth or principle.

words.tr: n. 即兴表演；即兴创作
words.ex: He made a song by improvisation during the concert.
words.ex_cn: 他在音乐会上即兴创作了一首歌。
words.en: Improvisation is the activity of making or doing something that you have not planned, using whatever you find.

words.ex: The old adage says, 'Slow and steady wins the race.'
words.ex_cn: 这句古老的格言说：'慢而稳者胜。'
words.en: An adage is a short, wise saying which has been used for a long time and is generally accepted as true.

words.tr: n. 山崩；塌方；压倒性的胜利
words.ex: The heavy rain caused a landslide.
words.ex_cn: 大雨引发了山体滑坡。
words.en: A landslide is a victory in an election in which a person or political party gets far more votes or seats than their opponents.

words.ex: The cows graze on the prairie.
words.ex_cn: 牛在草原上吃草。
words.en: A prairie is a large area of flat, grassy land, especially in North America.

words.ex: He works on a large ranch in Texas.
words.ex_cn: 他在德克萨斯州的一个大牧场工作。
words.en: A ranch is a large farm, especially in the western United States and Canada, where cattle or other animals are bred and raised.

words.ex: The house has a small terrace with chairs.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子有一个带椅子的小平台。
words.en: A terrace is a flat area of stone or grass next to a building where people can sit.

words.ex: Calling time a thief is a metaphor.
words.ex_cn: 把时间称为小偷是一种隐喻。
words.en: A metaphor is a figure of speech in which a word or phrase is applied to an object or action to which it is not literally applicable.

words.ex: The Industrial Revolution was a new epoch in history.
words.ex_cn: 工业革命是历史上一个新时代。
words.en: An epoch is a period of time in history or a person's life, typically one marked by notable events or particular characteristics.

words.ex: He told a long saga about his grandfather's adventures.
