words.ex: The doctor gave him an anticoagulant to prevent blood clots.
words.ex_cn: 医生给他开了抗凝剂以防止血栓。
words.en: An anticoagulant is a substance that prevents blood from clotting.

words.tr: n. [生化] 抗凝血酶（一种产生与肝脏的抗酶，能抑制血清中的凝血酶活化，从而防止纤维蛋白的形成）
words.ex: The patient has low antithrombin levels.
words.ex_cn: 这名患者的抗凝血酶水平很低。
words.en: Antithrombin is a substance in the blood that inhibits blood clotting by inactivating thrombin.

words.ex: He is pharming animals to make medicine.
words.ex_cn: 他正在给动物进行药用培育以生产药物。
words.en: Pharming is a type of cyber attack aimed at redirecting a website's traffic to another, fake site, often for the purpose of stealing personal information or installing malware.

words.ex: He tweaked the volume to make it louder.
words.ex_cn: 他微调了音量，让它更大声。
words.en: To tweak something means to make a small change to it in order to improve it or make it work better.

words.tr:
n. 曲柄；怪人；脾气坏的人
v. 用曲柄转动
adj. 古怪的；易怒的
words.ex: He turns the crank to start the old engine.
words.ex_cn: 他转动曲柄来启动旧引擎。
words.en: A crank is a device for transmitting rotary motion, consisting of a handle or arm attached at right angles to a shaft. It can also refer to a person who holds unorthodox opinions or behaves in an eccentric manner.

words.tr: n. 凝血；结块; v. 结块（clot的ing形式）
words.ex: The wound stops clotting after a few minutes.
words.ex_cn: 伤口几分钟后停止凝血。
words.en: Clotting is the process by which blood changes from a liquid to a gel, forming a clot.

words.ex: He has an autoimmune disease that affects his skin.
words.ex_cn: 他患有一种影响皮肤的自身免疫性疾病。
words.en: An autoimmune disease or condition is one in which your immune system mistakenly attacks your own body.

words.ex: The scientist created a transgenic mouse to study disease.
words.ex_cn: 科学家创造了一种转基因小鼠来研究疾病。
words.en: Relating to or denoting an organism that contains genetic material into which DNA from an unrelated organism has been artificially introduced.

words.ex: He carried a bucketful of water from the well.
words.ex_cn: 他从井里提了一桶水。
words.en: The amount that a bucket can hold.

words.tr: n. 天花乱坠的广告宣传；炒作；
words.ex: The new phone got a lot of hype before its release.
words.ex_cn: 这款新手机在发布前受到了大量天花乱坠的广告宣传。
words.en: If someone or something is hyped, they are praised or advertised a lot in newspapers, on television, etc., especially in a way that is intended to make them seem very exciting or important.

words.ex: His systolic blood pressure is 120.
words.ex_cn: 他的收缩压是120。
words.en: Relating to the phase of the heartbeat when the heart muscle contracts and pumps blood from the chambers into the arteries.

chapters.name: 阅读词汇 性格特点

words.tr: adj. 不知悔悟的；无悔意的
words.ex: The impenitent criminal continued to commit crimes despite repeated warnings.
words.ex_cn: 尽管一再警告，那个不知悔改的罪犯仍然继续犯罪。
words.en: If you describe someone as impenitent, you mean that they are not ashamed of their bad behavior or attitudes, and they do not wish to change them.

words.tr: adj. 好战的；好斗的；爱滋事的
words.ex: He is pugnacious and always argues with his classmates.
words.ex_cn: 他好斗，总是和同学争吵。
words.en: Someone who is pugnacious is eager to argue or fight.

words.ex: He criticized others for lying, but his own actions showed hypocrisy.
words.ex_cn: 他批评别人撒谎，但自己的行为却表现出虚伪。
words.en: The practice of claiming to have moral standards or beliefs to which one's own behavior does not conform; pretense.

words.tr: n. 阿谀奉承的人；谄媚者；马屁精
words.ex: He is a sycophant who always agrees with his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个总是附和老板的马屁精。
words.en: A sycophant is someone who praises powerful or rich people in an insincere way in order to get an advantage.

words.tr: adj. 抱怨的；爱发牢骚的
words.ex: She had a querulous tone when she spoke.
words.ex_cn: 她说话时带着一种爱发牢骚的语气。
words.en: If you describe someone as querulous, you mean that they complain about things in a rather bad-tempered way.

words.ex: The inexorable flow of time cannot be stopped.
words.ex_cn: 时间不可阻挡地流逝。
words.en: If you describe something as inexorable, you mean that it is impossible to stop or prevent from happening.

words.ex: The intrepid explorer climbed the high mountain.
words.ex_cn: 这位无畏的探险家爬上了高山。
words.en: If you describe someone as intrepid, you mean that they are brave, fearless, and willing to do things that might be dangerous.

words.ex: He is penurious and never tips the waiter.
words.ex_cn: 他很吝啬，从不给服务员小费。
words.en: If you describe someone as penurious, you mean that they are extremely poor or extremely unwilling to spend money.

words.tr: adj. 自负的；一本正经的
words.ex: He gave a priggish reply to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个自以为是的回答。
words.en: If you describe someone as priggish, you mean that they are very self-righteous and think that they are morally superior to other people.

words.tr: adj. 不奸猾的；厚道的；坦率的
words.ex: He is a guileless boy who always tells the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个纯真无邪的男孩，总是说真话。
words.en: If you describe someone as guileless, you mean that they behave openly and truthfully and do not try to deceive people.

words.ex: He is a hypocrite because he says he loves peace but fights often.
words.ex_cn: 他是个伪君子，因为他声称热爱和平，却经常打架。
words.en: A hypocrite is someone who pretends to have certain beliefs or opinions that they do not really have, especially in order to deceive people.

words.ex: He is irascible when he wakes up late.
words.ex_cn: 他起床晚时容易发怒。
words.en: If you describe someone as irascible, you mean that they become angry very easily.

words.tr: v. 组成；创作；“compose”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The team is composed of five players.
words.ex_cn: 这个团队由五名队员组成。
words.en: If someone is composed, they are calm and able to control their feelings.

words.tr: adj. 易怒的；坏脾气的；乖戾的
words.ex: She had a peevish tone when she spoke.
words.ex_cn: 她说话时带着一种易怒的语气。
words.en: If you describe someone as peevish, you mean that they are easily irritated by unimportant things.

words.tr: adj. 执拗的；固执的；顽固的；
words.ex: He is obstinate and won't change his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他很执拗，不肯改变主意。
words.en: If you describe someone as obstinate, you are being critical of them because they are very determined to do what they want, and refuse to change their mind or be persuaded to do something else.

words.tr: adj. 易怒的；难驾驭的；脾气不好的
words.ex: The fractious child refused to eat his vegetables.
words.ex_cn: 这个脾气暴躁的孩子拒绝吃蔬菜。
words.en: If you describe someone as fractious, you mean they are easily upset or annoyed, and often complain.

words.tr: adj. 顽固的；执拗的；冷酷无情的
words.ex: He is obdurate and refuses to change his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他固执己见，拒绝改变主意。
words.en: If you describe someone as obdurate, you mean that they are determined not to change their mind or attitude in spite of efforts to persuade them.

words.tr: n. 硬皮；老茧；胼胝；麻木；无情
words.ex: His hands showed callosity from years of hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他的双手因多年辛勤劳动而长满了老茧。
words.en: Callosity refers to the quality of being callous, which means showing or having an insensitive and cruel disregard for others. It can also refer to a thickened and hardened part of the skin or soft tissue, especially in an area that has been subjected to friction.

words.tr:
n. 平衡；姿态；镇静
v. 使平衡；保持（某种姿势）
words.ex: The dancer maintained her poise on one foot.
words.ex_cn: 舞者单脚保持平衡。
words.en: If someone has poise, they are calm, dignified, and self-controlled.

words.ex: He remained unaffected by the noise.
words.ex_cn: 他没有受到噪音的影响。
words.en: If someone or something is unaffected by an event or occurrence, they are not changed by it in any way.

words.tr: adj. 易驾驭的；温顺的；易处理的
words.ex: The dog is so tractable that it follows commands effortlessly.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗非常驯良，能轻松地服从命令。
words.en: If you say that a person, problem, or device is tractable, you mean that they can be easily controlled or dealt with.

words.ex: He was called effeminate for wearing pink.
words.ex_cn: 他因为穿粉色被说娘娘腔。
words.en: If you describe a man or his behaviour as effeminate, you mean that he behaves, looks, or sounds like a woman or girl.

words.ex: The surgeon's dexterity saved the patient's life.
words.ex_cn: 外科医生的灵巧救了病人的命。
words.en: Skill and grace in physical movement, especially in the use of the hands; adroitness.

words.tr: adj. 钝的；愚钝的；钝角的
words.ex: The angle is obtuse, so it is larger than 90 degrees.
words.ex_cn: 这个角是钝的，所以它大于90度。
words.en: If you describe someone as obtuse, you mean that they are slow to understand things.

words.tr: adj. 不守规矩的；难控制的；难管束的
words.ex: The unruly child refused to sit quietly.
words.ex_cn: 这个不守规矩的孩子不肯安静地坐着。
words.en: If you describe people, especially children, as unruly, you mean that they behave badly and are difficult to control.

words.tr: adj. 沉默寡言的；讳莫如深的
words.ex: He is reticent about his feelings.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的感受很沉默。
words.en: If you are reticent about something, you are unwilling to talk about it or make your feelings known.

words.tr: adj. 慈善的；乐善好施的；
words.ex: He made a philanthropic donation to help poor children.
words.ex_cn: 他捐赠了一笔慈善款项来帮助贫困儿童。
words.en: A philanthropic person or organization freely gives money or other help to people who need it.

words.tr: adj. 絮聒的；饶舌的；多嘴的
words.ex: He is garrulous and talks too much.
words.ex_cn: 他话很多，说个不停。
words.en: If you describe someone as garrulous, you mean that they talk a lot, especially about things that are not important.

words.ex: The turtle moves in a sluggish way.
words.ex_cn: 乌龟移动得很缓慢。
words.en: If you describe something as sluggish, you mean that it is moving or working more slowly than usual.

words.tr: adj. 郁闷的；抑郁的；孤僻的
words.ex: He was morose after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后变得忧郁。
words.en: If you describe someone as morose, you mean that they are very unhappy, bad-tempered, and unwilling to talk or be sociable.

words.tr: adj. 谨慎的；慎重的；精明的
words.ex: He is prudent with his money.
words.ex_cn: 他在花钱时很谨慎。
words.en: If you are prudent, you are careful and avoid taking unnecessary risks.

words.tr: adj. 谨慎的；细心的；深谋远虑的
words.ex: He made a prudential decision to save money.
words.ex_cn: 他做出了一个谨慎的决定来存钱。
words.en: Prudential means involving or showing care and thought for the future.

words.ex: The kleptomaniac keeps stealing small items from stores.
words.ex_cn: 这个偷窃狂不断从商店偷小东西。
words.en: A kleptomaniac is a person who has a strong, uncontrollable desire to steal, especially when they do not need the items and cannot afford them.

words.ex: He has an insatiable hunger for knowledge.
words.ex_cn: 他对知识有着无法满足的渴望。
words.en: If someone is insatiable, they always want more of something and are never satisfied.

words.tr: adj. 自命不凡的；自负的；矫饰的
words.ex: He wore a fancy hat to seem pretentious.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了一顶华丽的帽子，显得自命不凡。
words.en: If you describe something as pretentious, you mean that it is intended to seem important or significant, but you think it is not.

words.tr: adj. 紧握的；顽强的；坚决的；强的（记忆力）
words.ex: The child held the toy with tenacious hands.
words.ex_cn: 孩子用紧握的手抓住玩具。
words.en: If you describe someone as tenacious, you are admiring their determination to do something and their refusal to stop trying even when it is difficult.

words.tr: adj. 苛求的；吹毛求疵的
words.ex: He is hypercritical about small mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他对小错误非常吹毛求疵。
words.en: If you say that someone is hypercritical, you mean that they criticize things too much or too severely.

words.ex: He is known for his probity in business.
words.ex_cn: 他以商业中的正直著称。
words.en: Probity is the quality of having strong moral principles and honesty.

words.ex: His joke brought some levity to the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他的笑话为会议带来了一些轻松气氛。
words.en: Levity refers to a lack of seriousness, especially at an inappropriate time, often characterized by frivolity or lightness of manner.

words.tr: adj. 拖拉的；拖沓的；磨蹭的
words.ex: He gave a dilatory answer to the teacher's question.
words.ex_cn: 他对老师的问题回答得很拖拉。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as dilatory, you mean that they are slow and cause delay.

words.ex: He had the effrontery to lie to his teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他竟敢对老师撒谎。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as effrontery, you are emphasizing that it is very rude or disrespectful.

words.ex: The veracity of his story was questioned by the police.
words.ex_cn: 他的故事的真实性受到了警方的质疑。
words.en: Veracity refers to the quality of being true or accurate.

words.ex: The cat is agile and jumps high.
words.ex_cn: 这只猫很敏捷，跳得很高。
words.en: Someone who is agile can move quickly and easily.

words.ex: He is niggardly with his money.
words.ex_cn: 他对待钱很吝啬。
words.en: If you describe someone as niggardly, you are criticizing them for being too mean or unwilling to spend money.

words.tr: adj. 爱挑剔的；过分讲究的
words.ex: He is fastidious about keeping his room clean.
words.ex_cn: 他非常讲究保持房间整洁。
words.en: Very attentive to and concerned about accuracy and detail.

words.ex: He is timorous when speaking in front of people.
words.ex_cn: 他在众人面前说话时很胆怯。
words.en: If you describe someone as timorous, you mean that they are nervous and lack courage or confidence.

words.ex: The courageous soldier made a valorous charge.
words.ex_cn: 这位勇敢的士兵进行了英勇的冲锋。
words.en: If you describe someone as valorous, you mean that they are very brave, especially in battle.

words.tr: adj. 糟糕透顶的；恶劣的；卑鄙的
words.ex: He said a vile thing to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他对朋友说了句卑鄙的话。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is vile, you mean that they are extremely unpleasant.

words.ex: His pusillanimous behavior in the face of danger was disappointing.
words.ex_cn: 他在危险面前的懦弱行为令人失望。
words.en: If you say that someone is pusillanimous, you mean that they are timid or afraid, especially in a way that you find irritating or disappointing.

words.ex: He shows narcissism by always talking about himself.
words.ex_cn: 他总是谈论自己，表现出自恋。
words.en: Narcissism is the habit of always thinking about yourself and your appearance and abilities, and believing that you are better than other people.

words.tr: adj. 愚昧的；昏庸的；愚笨的
words.ex: His fatuous smile made everyone uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 他那愚蠢的微笑让每个人都感到不舒服。
words.en: If you describe a person, action, or remark as fatuous, you mean that they are extremely silly, showing a lack of intelligence or thought.

words.tr: adj. 淡而无味的；枯燥乏味的
words.ex: The soup was insipid and boring.
words.ex_cn: 这汤淡而无味，很无聊。
words.en: If you describe food or drink as insipid, you mean that it is very weak, tasteless, or uninteresting.

words.tr: adj. 非常自负的；自命不凡的
words.ex: He was so vainglorious that he believed his own press clippings.
words.ex_cn: 他非常自负，以至于相信了自己的新闻剪报。
words.en: If you describe someone as vainglorious, you are critical of them because they are very proud of their own status, abilities, or achievements.

words.ex: He is taciturn and rarely speaks.
words.ex_cn: 他沉默寡言，很少说话。
words.en: A taciturn person does not say very much and can seem unfriendly.

words.ex: The obstreperous crowd made it difficult to hear the speaker.
words.ex_cn: 吵闹的人群使得演讲者的话难以听清。
words.en: If you say that someone is obstreperous, you are annoyed because they are noisy and difficult to control.

words.ex: His prolix speech made everyone bored.
words.ex_cn: 他冗长的演讲让所有人都感到无聊。
words.en: Using or containing too many words; tediously lengthy.

words.tr: adj. 虔诚的；信神的；伪善的
words.ex: He is a pious man who prays every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个每天祈祷的虔诚的人。
words.en: Someone who is pious is very religious and moral.

words.tr: adj. 谨小慎微的；一丝不苟的
words.ex: He is punctilious about following every rule.
words.ex_cn: 他对遵守每一条规则都谨小慎微。
words.en: If someone is punctilious, they are very careful to behave correctly and to follow the details of rules or customs.

words.ex: He laughed at the silly joke, but she saw it as mere frivolity.
words.ex_cn: 他笑了那个愚蠢的笑话，但她认为那只是轻浮。
words.en: If you refer to an activity as frivolity, you think that it is useful and silly rather than serious and sensible.

words.tr: adj. 过分拘谨的；装正经的
words.ex: She is prudish about wearing shorts in public.
words.ex_cn: 她对在公共场合穿短裤感到拘谨。
words.en: If you describe someone as prudish, you mean that they are too easily shocked by things relating to sex.

words.tr: adj. 不动声色的；无动于衷的；不易激动的
words.ex: He remained stolid in the face of adversity.
words.ex_cn: 面对逆境，他依然冷漠。
words.en: If you describe someone as stolid, you mean that they do not show much emotion or are not very exciting or interesting.

words.tr: adj. 阴险的；潜伏的；暗中作祟的
words.ex: The insidious virus spread quietly through the town.
words.ex_cn: 这种隐蔽的病毒悄然在小镇蔓延。
words.en: Proceeding in a gradual, subtle way, but with harmful effects.

words.tr: adj. 笨重的；难处理的；臃肿的；庞大的
words.ex: The box was unwieldy and hard to carry.
words.ex_cn: 这个盒子又大又笨重，很难搬。
words.en: An unwieldy object is difficult to move or handle because of its size, shape, or weight.

words.tr: adj. 引起兴趣的；引人入胜的； v. “intrigue”的现在分词；
words.ex: The mystery story was intriguing.
words.ex_cn: 这个侦探故事很引人入胜。
words.en: If you describe something as intriguing, you mean that it is interesting or strange.

words.ex: The movie was banned for its lewd content.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影因内容猥亵而被禁播。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as lewd, you are critical of it because it is sexual in a rude and unpleasant way.

words.tr: n. 奸诈；欺骗；口是心非
words.ex: He showed duplicity by lying to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他通过对朋友撒谎表现出虚伪。
words.en: If you accuse someone of duplicity, you mean that they are deceitful.

words.ex: The despotic king ruled with fear.
words.ex_cn: 这位专制的国王用恐惧统治。
words.en: If you say that someone is despotic, you are emphasizing that they use their power over other people in a very unfair or cruel way.

words.ex: He is too faint-hearted to speak in front of the class.
words.ex_cn: 他太胆小了，不敢在全班面前说话。
words.en: Lacking courage or determination; timid.

words.tr: adj. 自恋的；自我陶醉的
words.ex: She had a narcissistic personality and always thought she was the center of attention.
words.ex_cn: 她有自恋型人格，总是认为自己就是关注的中心。
words.en: If you describe someone as narcissistic, you are critical of them because they think about themselves a lot and admire themselves too much.

words.tr: adj. 轻佻的；不可靠的；易惊慌的
words.ex: The horse is skittish around loud noises.
words.ex_cn: 这匹马对大声响很敏感。
words.en: If you describe a person or animal as skittish, you mean they are easily frightened or nervous.

words.tr: adj. 慷慨的；优厚的； 大方的
words.ex: He gave a munificent donation to the school.
words.ex_cn: 他向学校捐赠了一笔慷慨的款项。
words.en: If you describe someone as munificent, you mean that they are very generous, often in the form of giving money or gifts.

words.ex: Everyone is fallible, even teachers.
words.ex_cn: 每个人都会犯错，即使是老师。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is fallible, you mean that they are not perfect and are likely to make mistakes or to fail in what they are doing.

words.tr: adj. 做戏似的；不自然的；戏剧性的
words.ex: Her performance was too stagy to be believable.
words.ex_cn: 她的表演太过做作，令人难以相信。
words.en: If you describe something as stagy, you mean that it is artificial and exaggerated, like something in a play.

words.tr:
n. 斯多葛派人；坚忍克己之人；
adj. 斯多葛派的；坚忍克己的；
words.ex: He is a stoic who never shows his emotions.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个从不流露情感的斯多葛派人。
words.en: Someone who is stoic does not show their feelings or complain when bad things happen to them.

words.tr: adj. 愚蠢的；幼稚的；孩子气的
words.ex: His puerile jokes made everyone uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 他幼稚的笑话让每个人都感到不舒服。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as puerile, you mean that they are silly and childish.

words.ex: His hardihood in the face of danger was admired by all.
words.ex_cn: 他在危险面前表现出的刚毅受到所有人的钦佩。
words.en: Boldness or daring, especially in challenging situations.

words.tr: adj. 亲切的；和蔼的；温暖的
words.ex: He is a genial man who always smiles.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个和蔼可亲的人，总是面带微笑。
words.en: Friendly and cheerful.

words.ex: He is gullible and believes every story he hears.
words.ex_cn: 他很容易受骗，相信每一个他听到的故事。
words.en: If you describe someone as gullible, you mean they are easily tricked because they are too trusting.

words.tr: adj. 清洁的；无瑕疵的；无过失的
words.ex: The kitchen was immaculate after she cleaned it.
words.ex_cn: 她打扫后，厨房非常干净。
words.en: If you describe something as immaculate, you mean that it is extremely clean, tidy, or neat.

words.ex: The school has stringent rules about homework.
words.ex_cn: 学校对作业有严格的规定。
words.en: Stringent measures, rules, or conditions are very strict or severe.

words.tr:
adj. 挥霍无度的；行为不检点的；放荡的
n. 放荡的人；恣意挥霍的人
words.ex: His profligate lifestyle led to his financial ruin.
words.ex_cn: 他放荡的生活方式导致了他经济上的破产。
words.en: Someone who is profligate spends too much money or uses too much of something.

words.tr: adj. 傲慢的；目空一切的；自大的
words.ex: He gave a supercilious smile when she asked a simple question.
words.ex_cn: 当她问了一个简单的问题时，他露出了傲慢的微笑。
words.en: If you say that someone is supercilious, you disapprove of them because they behave in a way that shows they think they are better than other people.

words.tr: adj. 不修边幅的；邋遢的
words.ex: He wore slovenly clothes to work.
words.ex_cn: 他穿着邋遢的衣服去上班。
words.en: If you describe someone as slovenly, you disapprove of them because they are careless and untidy in their appearance or habits.

words.tr: adj. 缺乏兴趣的；漠不关心的；
words.ex: He was apathetic about the movie.
words.ex_cn: 他对这部电影缺乏兴趣。
words.en: If you describe someone as apathetic, you are criticizing them because they do not seem to be interested in or enthusiastic about doing anything.

words.tr: adj. 话多的；健谈的；喋喋不休的
words.ex: He is a loquacious man who talks all day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个整天喋喋不休的人。
words.en: If you describe someone as loquacious, you mean that they talk a lot.

words.tr: adj. 语言交际能力的（尤指用外语）；乐意沟通的；
words.ex: He is very communicative in English, even when he makes mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他用英语交流时很有能力，即使犯了错误。
words.en: Someone who is communicative talks to people, for example about their feelings, and tells people things.

words.ex: He is slothful and never does his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他懒惰，从不做作业。
words.en: If you describe someone as slothful, you mean that they are lazy.

words.ex: He is a staid man who never wears casual clothes.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个古板的人，从不穿休闲服。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as staid, you mean that they are serious, dull, and rather old-fashioned.

words.ex: He showed great fortitude during the hard times.
words.ex_cn: 他在艰难时期展现了极大的毅力。
words.en: Fortitude is the mental and emotional strength that enables a person to face difficulty, danger, or pain without fear.

words.tr: adj. 派系的；与派系相关的；好争论的
words.ex: The factious group refused to cooperate with others.
words.ex_cn: 这个分裂的团体拒绝与其他人的合作。
words.en: If you describe a group or activity as factious, you mean that it is divided into groups that have strong and unfriendly disagreements.

words.tr:
adj. 奢侈的；慷慨给予的；挥霍的；过多的
v. 浪费；挥霍；慷慨给予
words.ex: He threw a lavish party for his birthday.
words.ex_cn: 他为自己的生日举办了一场奢华的派对。
words.en: If you describe something as lavish, you mean that it is very elaborate and impressive and a lot of money has been spent on it. If you say that someone is lavish in the way they behave, you mean that they give, spend, or use a lot of something.

words.ex: The villainous man stole the money.
words.ex_cn: 那个邪恶的人偷了钱。
words.en: If you describe someone as villainous, you mean that they are very wicked and evil.

words.tr: v. 使无效；使显得愚蠢
words.ex: The boring meeting stultifies his creativity.
words.ex_cn: 这个无聊的会议扼杀了他的创造力。
words.en: To stultify someone or something means to cause them to appear foolish or to be ineffective.

words.tr: n. 宽宏大量；慷慨给与
words.ex: Her munificence in donating to charity is well known.
words.ex_cn: 她对慈善机构的慷慨捐赠是众所周知的。
words.en: Munificence is the quality of being extremely generous.

words.tr: adj. 不忠的；背信弃义的
words.ex: The perfidious traitor betrayed his comrades.
words.ex_cn: 那个背信弃义的叛徒背叛了他的同伙。
words.en: If you describe someone as perfidious, you mean that they have betrayed someone or cannot be trusted.

words.ex: The precocious child could read before age five.
words.ex_cn: 这个早熟的孩子在五岁前就会阅读了。
words.en: A precocious child shows intelligence or skill at a very young age, especially in a way that is unusual for their age.

words.tr: n. 自命不凡；自称；标榜；虚荣
words.ex: His pretension made others think he was better than them.
words.ex_cn: 他的自命不凡让别人觉得他比他们强。
words.en: If you say that someone has pretensions, you mean that they claim or pretend that they are more important, intelligent, or skilled than they really are.

words.tr: n. 顽固；执拗；坚持到底
words.ex: His pertinacity helped him finish the hard task.
words.ex_cn: 他的执着帮助他完成了这项困难的任务。
words.en: The quality of holding firmly to a purpose, belief, or action; stubbornness.

words.tr: adj. 鄙视的；不屑一顾的；轻蔑的
words.ex: He gave a disdainful look at the messy room.
words.ex_cn: 他轻蔑地看了一眼凌乱的房间。
words.en: If you are disdainful of someone or something, you dislike them because you think that they are inferior or unimportant.

words.tr: adj. 直言无讳的；坦率的；
words.ex: He is an outspoken teacher who always tells the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位直言不讳的老师，总是说真话。
words.en: Someone who is outspoken expresses their opinions frankly and honestly, even if they are likely to shock or offend people.

words.tr:
adj. 讽刺的；刻毒的；卑鄙的
n. 人造宝石；伪币
words.ex: She made a snide comment about his appearance.
words.ex_cn: 她对他的外表进行了暗讽。
words.en: A snide remark or comment is one that criticizes someone in an unkind and indirect way.

words.ex: He was courteous to everyone he met.
words.ex_cn: 他对遇到的每个人都很有礼貌。
words.en: Someone who is courteous is polite and respectful to other people.

words.tr: adj. 脾气坏的；乖戾的；傲慢的
words.ex: The surly man refused to say hello.
words.ex_cn: 那个脾气暴躁的人拒绝打招呼。
words.en: If someone is surly, they are unfriendly and bad-tempered.

words.ex: He remained imperturbable even when the storm hit.
words.ex_cn: 即使风暴来袭，他依然镇定自若。
words.en: If you describe someone as imperturbable, you mean that they remain calm, even in disturbing or dangerous situations.

words.tr: adj. 刚愎自用的；顽固的；任性的
words.ex: He is headstrong and refuses to listen.
words.ex_cn: 他很固执，不肯听别人的话。
words.en: If you refer to someone as headstrong, you are slightly critical of them because they are very determined to do what they want, and refuse to be advised by others.

words.ex: He is an optimist who believes things will get better.
words.ex_cn: 他是个乐观主义者，相信事情会好转。
words.en: An optimist is someone who always expects good things to happen or is always hopeful about the future.

words.ex: He spoke with diffidence during the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议上说话时很犹豫。
words.en: Diffidence is the quality of being shy and not confident of your abilities.

words.ex: Her insolence made everyone uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 她的傲慢让每个人都感到不适。
words.en: Insolence is rude and disrespectful behavior.

words.ex: He is introspective and often thinks about his feelings.
words.ex_cn: 他善于内省，经常思考自己的感受。
words.en: If you describe someone as introspective, you mean that they spend a lot of time examining their own thoughts, ideas, and feelings.

words.tr: adj. 傲慢的；自负的；自以为是的
words.ex: His overweening pride led to his downfall.
words.ex_cn: 他过于自信的骄傲导致了他的失败。
words.en: If you describe someone as overweening, you are criticizing them because they are too confident and think they are better than other people.

words.tr: adj. 闷热的；性感的；撩人的
words.ex: The sultry weather made everyone feel tired.
words.ex_cn: 闷热的天气让每个人都感到疲惫。
words.en: Sultry weather is hot and damp in a way that makes you feel uncomfortable.

words.ex: His obstinacy in refusing treatment led to his condition worsening.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝治疗的固执态度导致他的病情恶化。
words.en: The quality or state of being obstinate; stubbornness.

words.ex: His hubris made him lose the game.
words.ex_cn: 他的傲慢让他输掉了比赛。
words.en: Hubris is excessive pride or self-confidence, often leading to downfall or failure.

words.ex: His impetuosity made him quit his job without thinking.
words.ex_cn: 他的鲁莽让他未经思考就辞了工作。
words.en: The quality of being impetuous; rashness or impulsiveness.

words.ex: His overbearing boss always tells him what to do.
words.ex_cn: 他专横的老板总是告诉他该做什么。
words.en: If you describe someone as overbearing, you mean that they behave in a very unpleasant way because they are too confident of their own importance.

words.ex: The car took a precipitous turn on the mountain road.
words.ex_cn: 汽车在山路上急转弯。
words.en: A precipitous slope or cliff is very steep and often dangerous.

words.ex: He is a stalwart of the environmental movement.
words.ex_cn: 他是环保运动的坚定分子。
words.en: A stalwart person is someone who is very loyal and committed to a person, belief, or cause and is not likely to change their views or behavior.

words.ex: He hates bigotry and speaks up for everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他憎恨偏见，并为所有人发声。
words.en: Bigotry is the possession or expression of strong, unreasonable prejudices or opinions.

words.tr: adj. 活泼的；敏捷的；充满生气的
words.ex: The old man is still spry and walks fast.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人仍然身手敏捷，走得很慢。
words.en: Someone who is spry, especially an older person, is lively and active.

words.tr: adj. 胆汁的；患胆病的；脾气暴躁的；恶心头痛的；让人恶心的
words.ex: He had a bilious complexion due to his illness.
words.ex_cn: 由于生病，他的脸色发黄。
words.en: If someone is bilious, they are bad-tempered or irritable, often because of a problem with their liver or digestion.

words.tr:
adj. 牛的；似牛的；迟钝的
n. 牛；牛科动物
words.ex: The bovine grazed quietly in the field.
words.ex_cn: 那头牛在田野里安静地吃草。
words.en: Relating to or resembling cattle; slow or dull in manner.

words.tr: adj. 滑稽的；诙谐的；爱恶作剧的
words.ex: His waggish sense of humor often lightened the mood at serious meetings.
words.ex_cn: 他滑稽的幽默感经常在严肃的会议上活跃气氛。
words.en: If you describe someone or their behaviour as waggish, you mean that they are humorous and often make jokes or amusing remarks.

words.tr: adj. 易怒的；难以处理的；敏感的
words.ex: He is touchy about his weight.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己体重很敏感。
words.en: If you describe someone as touchy, you mean that they are easily upset, offended, or irritated.

words.ex: His voice sounds raspy after shouting all day.
words.ex_cn: 他大喊了一整天后，声音变得沙哑。
words.en: A raspy voice or sound is unpleasantly rough.

words.ex: He became testy when he was asked about his past.
words.ex_cn: 当被问及他的过去时，他变得易怒。
words.en: If someone is testy, they are easily annoyed and impatient.

words.tr: adj. 不动感情的；冷静的；平心静气的
words.ex: She remained dispassionate throughout the heated debate.
words.ex_cn: 她在激烈的辩论中始终保持冷静。
words.en: If you are dispassionate, you are able to act calmly and reasonably and not be influenced by your feelings or by personal opinions.

words.ex: He led a dissolute life after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后过着放荡的生活。
words.en: If you describe someone as dissolute, you mean they behave in a way that is considered immoral because they do things such as drink or have sex too much.

words.ex: He showed circumspection before making a decision.
words.ex_cn: 他在做决定之前表现得非常谨慎。
words.en: Circumspection is the quality of being careful and considering all the possible risks and consequences before doing something.

words.ex: Old sailors often got scurvy from lack of fresh fruit.
words.ex_cn: 老水手因缺乏新鲜水果而患上坏血病。
words.en: A disease caused by a deficiency of vitamin C, characterized by spongy and bleeding gums, bleeding under the skin, and extreme weakness.

words.tr: adj. 流泪的；爱哭的；引人落泪的
words.ex: The lachrymose melody of the violin added to the somber atmosphere.
words.ex_cn: 小提琴哀伤的旋律增添了忧郁的气氛。
words.en: If you describe someone as lachrymose, you mean that they are sad or likely to cry easily.

words.tr: n. 不慎重；轻率；言行失检
words.ex: His indiscretion caused a big problem at work.
words.ex_cn: 他的轻率行为在工作中引起了大问题。
words.en: Indiscretion refers to behavior or speech that is not discreet; it can also mean a lack of good judgment or care in what one says or does.

words.tr: adj. 无光泽的；暗淡的；无生气的；乏善可陈的
words.ex: The paint on the car looked lackluster after the storm.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴过后，车漆显得暗淡无光。
words.en: If you describe something as lackluster, you mean that it is not exciting or not very good quality.

words.ex: He was known as a skinflint who never spent a penny on anything.
words.ex_cn: 他以吝啬鬼著称，从不为任何东西花一分钱。
words.en: A skinflint is someone who is extremely unwilling to spend money.

words.ex: The poignancy of the moment was not lost on anyone.
words.ex_cn: 那一刻的辛酸没有被任何人忽略。
words.en: The quality of evoking a keen sense of sadness or regret.

words.tr:
n. 愚蠢的错误；傻瓜；蠢人
v. 犯愚蠢的错误；混；打发时间
words.ex: He made a goof when he forgot his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他忘记带作业，犯了一个愚蠢的错误。
words.en: If you call someone a goof, you mean they are silly or stupid. As a verb, to goof means to make a mistake or do something badly.

words.ex: He is a fiery man who gets angry easily.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个容易发怒的暴躁男人。
words.en: If you describe something as fiery, you mean that it is burning strongly or contains fire. It can also describe someone's temper or speech as being very passionate or intense.

words.tr: adj. 忧郁的；乖戾的；严肃的
words.ex: He has a saturnine mood and rarely smiles.
words.ex_cn: 他情绪阴郁，很少微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as saturnine, you mean that they are serious and unfriendly.

words.ex: He gave up worldly pleasures to live a simple life.
words.ex_cn: 他放弃了世俗的享乐，过着简朴的生活。
words.en: Worldly means relating to the world and the practical matters of life, rather than to spiritual or religious matters.

words.tr:
adj. 热恋着的；冲昏头脑的；入迷的
v. 使冲昏头脑；使着迷；“infatuate”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: She was infatuated with the new pop star.
words.ex_cn: 她对这位新晋流行歌手非常着迷。
words.en: If you are infatuated with someone, you have a very strong feeling of love or attraction for them, which usually does not last very long.

words.tr: v. 用喙整理羽毛；精心打扮；感觉良好
words.ex: The bird preens its feathers every morning.
words.ex_cn: 这只鸟每天早上梳理它的羽毛。
words.en: If a bird preens or preens itself, it cleans and arranges its feathers using its beak.

words.ex: His craftiness helped him win the game.
words.ex_cn: 他的狡猾帮助他赢得了比赛。
words.en: Craftiness is the quality of being clever at planning something so that you get what you want, especially by deceiving other people.

words.tr:
adj. 唯利是图的；雇佣的
n. 雇佣兵；唯利是图者
words.ex: He works as a mercenary for money.
words.ex_cn: 他为了钱当雇佣兵。
words.en: A mercenary is a professional soldier hired to serve in a foreign army.

words.tr: adj. 坐立不安的；烦躁的
words.ex: The child is fidgety during the long meeting.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在长时间的会议中坐立不安。
words.en: If someone is fidgety, they keep making small quick movements with their hands or feet, usually because they are nervous, bored, or excited.

words.tr: n. 自我陶醉者；自恋者
words.ex: He is a narcissist who only talks about himself.
words.ex_cn: 他是个只谈论自己的自恋者。
words.en: A narcissist is someone who has an excessive interest in or admiration of themselves.

words.tr:
adj. 尖刻的；刻薄的；尖锐讥讽的
n. 媒染剂
words.ex: His mordant wit made everyone laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他尖刻的幽默让大家笑了。
words.en: A mordant remark is one that is critical and sarcastic. In chemistry, a mordant is a substance used to set dyes on fabrics or tissue sections by forming a coordination complex with the dye which then attaches to the fabric or tissue.

words.ex: His paranoia made him believe that everyone was out to get him.
words.ex_cn: 他的多疑让他相信每个人都在算计他。
words.en: Paranoia is the unreasonable feeling that you are being threatened in some way, or that people are trying to harm you, without any evidence.

words.ex: The movie had prurient scenes that upset many viewers.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影有令人不适的色情场面。
words.en: Having or encouraging an excessive interest in sexual matters.

words.tr: adj. 爱讲道的；说教的；爱唠叨的
words.ex: His speech was preachy and full of moral lessons.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲充满了道德说教。
words.en: If you describe someone as preachy, you mean that they try to give people moral advice in a way that is annoying or boring.

words.tr: n. 厌恶世人者；遁世者
words.ex: He is a misanthrope who avoids people.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个避世的人，不喜欢与人交往。
words.en: A misanthrope is someone who dislikes and avoids other people.

words.tr: adj. 别致的；时髦的；小巧玲珑的；活泼的；无礼的；唐突的
words.ex: She gave a pert reply to the interviewer's question.
words.ex_cn: 她对采访者的问题给出了无礼的回答。
words.en: If you describe someone as pert, you mean that they are lively and confident, and perhaps slightly disrespectful.

words.tr: n.  浮华；虚夸；炫耀；自负
words.ex: His pomposity often alienated his colleagues.
words.ex_cn: 他的自大使他经常疏远同事。
words.en: Pomposity is the quality of being pompous; self-importance.

words.ex: He bought equity in a tech company.
words.ex_cn: 他购买了一家科技公司的股票。
words.en: Equity is the quality of being fair and impartial.

words.ex: He reads fantasy books for escapism.
words.ex_cn: 他读奇幻小说来逃避现实。
words.en: Escapism is the tendency to seek distraction and relief from unpleasant realities, especially by seeking entertainment or engaging in fantasy.

words.tr:
n. 透视者；千里眼的人；有洞察力的人
adj.  透视的；有洞察力的
words.ex: The clairvoyant claimed to foresee the future events.
words.ex_cn: 这位能预知未来的人声称可以预见未来的事件。
words.en: A clairvoyant is someone who claims to have the ability to perceive events in the future or beyond normal sensory contact.

words.tr: adj. 迟的；缓慢的；迟缓的
words.ex: He is tardy for school every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上上学都迟到。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as tardy, you think that they are later than they should be or later than expected.

words.ex: The judge showed leniency toward the first-time offender.
words.ex_cn: 法官对初犯表现出了宽大。
words.en: Leniency is the quality of being more merciful or tolerant than expected.

words.tr:
adv. 小心地；谨慎地
adj. 小心的；谨慎的
words.ex: He walked gingerly on the icy path.
words.ex_cn: 他小心翼翼地走在结冰的小路上。
words.en: If you do something gingerly, you do it in a careful manner, usually because you expect it to be dangerous, unpleasant, or painful.

words.tr: adj. 慷慨的；大方的； 豪爽的
words.ex: He is openhanded with his money, always helping friends.
words.ex_cn: 他慷慨大方，总是帮助朋友。
words.en: If you describe someone as openhanded, you mean that they give generously or freely.

words.ex: She fought gamely despite her injuries.
words.ex_cn: 尽管受了伤，她还是勇敢地战斗。
words.en: In a brave and spirited manner; with pluck.

words.tr:
adj. 不爱交际的；离群索居的；即将退休的
v. 退休；退役；“retire”的现在分词
words.ex: She was a retiring woman, preferring to spend her evenings at home.
words.ex_cn: 她是一个不爱与人交往的女人，更喜欢在家度过晚上。
words.en: If someone is retiring, they are about to leave their job permanently, usually because of age.

words.ex: He has a predilection for sweet food.
words.ex_cn: 他偏爱甜食。
words.en: If you have a predilection for something, you have a strong liking for it.

words.tr: adj. 不受约束的；无拘无束的
words.ex: He sang uninhibited at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他在聚会上毫无拘束地唱歌。
words.en: If you describe a person or their behavior as uninhibited, you mean that they express their opinions and feelings openly, and behave as they want to, without worrying what other people think.

words.ex: The company showed compliance with safety rules.
words.ex_cn: 该公司遵守了安全规定。
words.en: The act of complying with a wish, request, or demand; obedience.

words.tr: n. 变色龙；见风使舵的人
words.ex: The chameleon changes color to hide.
words.ex_cn: 变色龙改变颜色来隐藏自己。
words.en: A chameleon is a type of lizard that can change the color of its skin in order to blend in with its surroundings.

words.ex: His trustworthiness makes people want to work with him.
words.ex_cn: 他的可信度让人们愿意和他合作。
words.en: The quality of being deserving of trust or confidence.

words.tr: adj. 面有愠色的；闷闷不乐的；阴沉的
words.ex: He gave a sullen look when his mom asked him to clean his room.
words.ex_cn: 当妈妈让他打扫房间时，他一脸阴沉。
words.en: Someone who is sullen is bad-tempered and does not speak much.

words.ex: The loud noise was an annoyance to everyone.
words.ex_cn: 那阵噪音让每个人都感到烦恼。
words.en: Annoyance is the feeling of being slightly angry or impatient.

words.ex: The sandpaper feels coarse to the touch.
words.ex_cn: 这张砂纸摸起来很粗糙。
words.en: Coarse things have a rough texture because they consist of thick threads or large pieces.

words.tr: adv. 轻率地；冒失地；仓促地
words.ex: He rashly quit his job without a plan.
words.ex_cn: 他鲁莽地辞了工作，却没有计划。
words.en: If someone acts rashly, they act hastily and without thinking carefully about what they are doing.

chapters.name: 阅读词汇 情感观点

words.tr:
v. 使迷惑；使不知所措
n. 迷惑；困惑；为难
words.ex: The tricky question nonplused the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 这个棘手的问题让老师不知所措。
words.en: To cause to be at a loss as to what to say, think, or do; perplex.

words.ex: He was ravenous after running five miles.
words.ex_cn: 跑了五英里后，他饿极了。
words.en: If you are ravenous, you are extremely hungry.

words.tr: v. 歪曲；不实报道；曲解
words.ex: He misrepresents the facts to win the debate.
words.ex_cn: 他歪曲事实以赢得辩论。
words.en: To give a false or misleading account of the nature of something.

words.ex: The roller coaster exhilarates the children.
words.ex_cn: 过山车让孩子们感到兴奋。
words.en: To make someone feel very happy and excited.

words.ex: The tape has strong adhesion to the wall.
words.ex_cn: 胶带对墙壁有很强的粘性。
words.en: The process or condition of sticking or staying attached, especially the sticking together of substances.

words.tr:
v. 使不再抱幻想；使理想破灭
n. 幻灭；理想破灭
words.ex: The bad experience disillusioned him about politics.
words.ex_cn: 这次糟糕的经历让他对政治不再抱幻想。
words.en: If a person or thing disillusions you, they make you realize that something is not as good as you thought it was.

words.ex: He remained impassive when he heard the bad news.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到这个坏消息时，他依然面无表情。
words.en: If someone is impassive, they do not show any emotion.

words.ex: The music enraptured the whole audience.
words.ex_cn: 音乐让整个观众着迷。
words.en: To fill someone with great delight or joy.

words.tr: adj. 使人厌烦的；令人生气的
words.ex: The irksome noise from the construction site kept me awake all night.
words.ex_cn: 建筑工地的恼人噪音让我整晚都没睡着。
words.en: If something is irksome, it annoys you.

words.tr:
n. 争吵
v. 争吵
words.ex: The two boys squabble over toys every day.
words.ex_cn: 这两个男孩每天为玩具争吵。
words.en: A squabble is a noisy disagreement about something unimportant.

words.tr: adj. 过分虚伪而令人生厌的
words.ex: He gave her a fulsome compliment.
words.ex_cn: 他给了她一段过分的赞美。
words.en: If you describe expressions of praise, apology, or gratitude as fulsome, you disapprove of them because they are exaggerated and elaborate, so that they sound insincere.

words.ex: He shouted a malediction at the thief.
words.ex_cn: 他对着小偷咒骂了一句。
words.en: A malediction is a curse or the act of uttering a curse.

words.ex: He espouses simple ideas about justice.
words.ex_cn: 他拥护关于正义的简单理念。
words.en: If you espouse a particular policy, cause, or belief, you become very interested in it and give your support to it.

words.tr: adj. 感情脆弱的；易落泪的；多愁善感的
words.ex: She was feeling maudlin after watching the sentimental movie.
words.ex_cn: 看完那部感人的电影后，她感到非常伤感。
words.en: If you describe someone as maudlin, you mean that they are being sad and sentimental in a foolish way, perhaps because of drinking alcohol.

words.ex: The child's petulant behavior was a result of his frustration.
words.ex_cn: 孩子暴躁的行为是因他的沮丧所致。
words.en: If you describe someone as petulant, you mean that they get angry or annoyed in a childish or unreasonable way.

words.ex: The king made a proclamation about peace.
words.ex_cn: 国王发布了一项关于和平的公告。
words.en: A proclamation is a public announcement about something important, often made by a king, queen, or government.

words.ex: The loud noise caused him vexation.
words.ex_cn: 噪音让他感到烦恼。
words.en: The state of being annoyed, frustrated, or worried.

words.ex: They impute the failure to poor planning.
words.ex_cn: 他们把失败归因于计划不周。
words.en: If you impute something such as blame or a crime to someone, you say that they are responsible for it or that they caused it.

words.ex: He did not agree with the policy, but he did not want to vilify those who supported it.
words.ex_cn: 他不同意这项政策，但不想诋毁那些支持它的人。
words.en: To vilify someone means to say or write very unpleasant things about them in order to hurt their reputation.

words.tr: adj. 心照不宣的；不作声的
words.ex: They have a tacit understanding about the rules.
words.ex_cn: 他们对规则有一种心照不宣的理解。
words.en: If you refer to someone's tacit agreement or approval, you mean they are agreeing to something or approving it without actually saying so, often because they are unwilling to admit to doing so.

words.ex: The child looked at her mother with adoration.
words.ex_cn: 孩子带着崇拜的眼神看着她的母亲。
words.en: Adoration is a feeling of great love and admiration.

words.tr: adj. 恋爱的；性爱的；色情的
words.ex: He wrote amatory poems to his beloved.
words.ex_cn: 他为心爱的人写下了恋爱的诗篇。
words.en: Relating to or expressive of love, especially sexual love.

words.ex: The movie showed a gruesome accident.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影展示了一起令人毛骨悚然的事故。
words.en: Something that is gruesome is extremely unpleasant and shocking, especially because it involves death or injury.

words.ex: No one can gainsay the truth.
words.ex_cn: 没有人能否认这个事实。
words.en: If there is no gainsaying something, it is not possible to deny that it is true or that it exists.

words.tr: v. 拒绝；断绝关系；否认；驳斥
words.ex: He repudiate the false claim.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝了这个虚假的声明。
words.en: If you repudiate something or someone, you show that you strongly disagree with them and do not want to be connected with them in any way.

words.ex: He is pertinacious about finishing his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他坚持要完成作业。
words.en: Someone who is pertinacious continues trying to do something in a very determined way, even though it is difficult or other people are against it.

words.tr: adj. 有知觉的；有感觉力的；
words.ex: The robot became sentient and could feel pain.
words.ex_cn: 这个机器人变得有知觉，能够感受到疼痛。
words.en: A sentient being is capable of perception or feeling.

words.ex: The phone is expensive.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机很贵。
words.en: Costing a lot of money; having a high price.

words.tr: adj. 诚实的；说实话的；准确的
words.ex: He is a veracious person who always tells the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个诚实的人，总是说真话。
words.en: Someone who is veracious is truthful and honest.

words.ex: He is scrupulous about checking his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他检查作业时一丝不苟。
words.en: If you are scrupulous, you are careful, thorough, and extremely attentive to details.

words.tr: adj. 平静的；宁静的；安详的
words.ex: The lake is serene in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 清晨的湖面很宁静。
words.en: Calm, peaceful, and untroubled; tranquil.

words.ex: Her sagacity in business matters was widely recognized.
words.ex_cn: 她在商业事务上的睿智广为人知。
words.en: The quality of being sagacious; wisdom and good judgment.

words.ex: He gave an artful answer to the tricky question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个棘手的问题给出了一个巧妙的回答。
words.en: If you describe someone as artful, you mean that they are clever and skillful at achieving what they want, especially by deceiving people.

words.ex: She had only the faintest inkling of what he was planning.
words.ex_cn: 她对他正在策划的事情只有一点模糊的概念。
words.en: An inkling is a slight knowledge or suspicion of something.

words.ex: The speaker eulogized the bravery of the soldiers.
words.ex_cn: 演讲者颂扬了士兵们的英勇。
words.en: To speak or write in praise of someone or something highly.

words.tr: adj. 有差异的；不一致的
words.ex: The two reports are discrepant in their findings.
words.ex_cn: 这两份报告的发现存在差异。
words.en: If two or more facts, ideas, or statements are discrepant, they are different from each other and do not agree or match.

words.tr: adj. 心烦意乱的；忧心如焚的
words.ex: She was distraught when she lost her dog.
words.ex_cn: 当她丢失了她的狗时，她非常悲痛。
words.en: If someone is distraught, they are so upset and worried that they cannot think clearly.

words.ex: The teacher reprehended the student for his disruptive behavior.
words.ex_cn: 老师因学生扰乱课堂的行为而责备他。
words.en: If you reprehend someone, you criticize them severely for their actions or behavior.

words.tr: n. 尖刻的言辞；激烈的争吵
words.ex: There was acrimony between the two neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 两个邻居之间充满了敌意。
words.en: Bitterness or ill feeling.

words.ex: He tries to downplay his mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他试图淡化自己的错误。
words.en: To downplay something means to make it seem less important or less bad than it really is.

words.tr: adj. 傲慢的；无礼的；侮慢的
words.ex: The insolent boy talked back to his teacher.
words.ex_cn: 那个无礼的男孩顶撞了老师。
words.en: If you say that someone is insolent, you mean they are rude and do not show respect for people in positions of authority.

words.ex: The team was drubbed in the final game.
words.ex_cn: 这支球队在决赛中遭到了重击。
words.en: To beat someone severely or to defeat them decisively in a competition or argument.

words.ex: The magic show enthralls the children.
words.ex_cn: 魔术表演让孩子们着迷。
words.en: If you are enthralled by something, you are so interested and excited by it that you give it all your attention.

words.tr: adj. 恶臭的；有恶臭的；有臭味的
words.ex: The malodorous garbage was attracting flies.
words.ex_cn: 那堆有恶臭的垃圾招来了苍蝇。
words.en: Having a very unpleasant smell.

words.ex: He undervalues his own talent.
words.ex_cn: 他低估了自己的才华。
words.en: If you undervalue something or someone, you fail to recognize how valuable or important they are.

words.tr: v. 不赞成；反对；使羞愧；使困窘
words.ex: His parents discountenance his late-night parties.
words.ex_cn: 他的父母不赞成他熬夜聚会。
words.en: If you discountenance something, you disapprove of it and try to prevent it from happening.

words.tr:
v. 大叫；大哭；大声训斥
n. 叫骂声；放声痛哭
words.ex: The baby began to bawl when he saw the dog.
words.ex_cn: 当宝宝看到狗时，开始大哭。
words.en: To shout or cry loudly and often for a long time.

words.ex: He works on an advisory committee.
words.ex_cn: 他在一个顾问委员会工作。
words.en: An advisory is a report or announcement that gives advice or information about a particular subject.

words.tr:
v. 诋毁；诽谤；中伤
n. 诋毁；诽谤；中伤
words.ex: He spread slander about his neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他散布了关于他邻居的诽谤。
words.en: Slander is the action or crime of making a false spoken statement damaging to a person's reputation.

words.tr: adj. 不注意的；疏忽的；非故意的
words.ex: He made an inadvertent mistake while typing.
words.ex_cn: 他在打字时不小心犯了个错误。
words.en: If something bad is inadvertent, it is done without realizing that it is wrong or that it could have bad consequences.

words.tr: v. 含糊其辞；说模棱两可的话
words.ex: He equivocates when asked about the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 当被问到错误时，他含糊其辞。
words.en: If you equivocate, you use ambiguous language in order to deceive people or to avoid speaking directly about something.

words.tr: adj. 贴切的；恰当的；妥帖的
words.ex: His felicitous remark made everyone smile.
words.ex_cn: 他得体的言论让每个人都笑了。
words.en: Well chosen or suited to the circumstances.

words.tr:
adj. 卑劣的；胆小的
n. 卑劣的懦夫；胆小鬼；可怜虫；坏东西
words.ex: The caitiff ran away when the fight started.
words.ex_cn: 这个懦夫一开战就逃跑了。
words.en: A caitiff is a contemptible or cowardly person.

words.ex: He proved his innocence to vindicate his name.
words.ex_cn: 他证明了自己的清白以洗清自己的名声。
words.en: To clear someone of blame or suspicion.

words.ex: He made a venial mistake in the report.
words.ex_cn: 他在报告中犯了一个可以原谅的错误。
words.en: If you describe a wrong action as venial, you mean that it is not very serious or grave, and therefore easy to forgive.

words.tr: adj. 若无其事的；不在乎的；冷淡的
words.ex: He was nonchalant about the test result.
words.ex_cn: 他对考试结果表现得漫不经心。
words.en: If you describe someone as nonchalant, you mean that they appear not to worry or care about things and that they seem very calm.

words.tr:
v. 咬牙；（因愤怒）咬牙切齿
n. 咬牙切齿
words.ex: The dog gnashes its teeth when it is angry.
words.ex_cn: 狗生气时会咬牙。
words.en: If you gnash your teeth, you grind them together in anger or pain.

words.tr: adj. 精疲力竭的；腻烦的；无兴致的
words.ex: She felt jaded after a long day at work.
words.ex_cn: 工作了一整天后，她感到精疲力竭。
words.en: If you are jaded, you feel bored, tired, and not enthusiastic, especially because you have had too much of something.

words.tr: adj. 陈腐的；陈词滥调的；老生常谈的
words.ex: His jokes are hackneyed and boring.
words.ex_cn: 他的笑话陈腐又无聊。
words.en: If you describe something as hackneyed, you mean that it is unoriginal and has been used so often that it is no longer interesting.

words.tr: adj. 不舒适的；不方便的
words.ex: The room is incommodious and hard to move in.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间狭小，很难活动。
words.en: If you describe a place as incommodious, you mean that it is uncomfortable because it is too small or too crowded.

words.tr: adj. 荒唐的；荒谬的；可笑的
words.ex: The trial was farcical, with everyone laughing.
words.ex_cn: 这场审判很荒谬，所有人都在笑。
words.en: If you describe a situation as farcical, you mean that it is so silly or extreme that you are unable to take it seriously.

words.ex: His argument is fallacious because it ignores the facts.
words.ex_cn: 他的论点是错误的，因为它忽略了事实。
words.en: If an idea, argument, or reason is fallacious, it is wrong because it is based on a fallacy.

words.tr: adj. 冒泡的；起泡的；活泼的
words.ex: The champagne was effervescent and bubbled in the glass.
words.ex_cn: 香槟在杯中冒泡沸腾。
words.en: If you describe someone as effervescent, you mean that they are lively, entertaining, enthusiastic, and cheerful.

words.ex: The guard is vigilant at night.
words.ex_cn: 这名守卫在夜里非常警惕。
words.en: Someone who is vigilant gives careful attention to a particular problem or situation and concentrates on noticing any danger or trouble that there might be.

words.ex: He wrote a poem about amour.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一首关于爱情的诗。
words.en: An amour is a love affair, especially a secret one.

words.tr: n. 敏捷的回答；机智的回答
words.ex: The witty repartee between the two comedians kept the audience laughing.
words.ex_cn: 两位喜剧演员之间的机智对话让观众笑声不断。
words.en: A repartee is a quick, witty reply or a conversation full of such replies.

words.ex: The earthquake caused a strong tremor in the building.
words.ex_cn: 地震使大楼发生了强烈的震动。
words.en: A tremor is a small earthquake or a shaking or vibrating movement, especially one caused by fear or nervousness.

words.ex: He made an animadversion on his friend's poor choice.
words.ex_cn: 他对朋友的糟糕选择提出了批评。
words.en: A critical or censorious remark or comment.

words.ex: The crowd was exultant after their team won.
words.ex_cn: 球队赢了之后，人群欣喜若狂。
words.en: If you are exultant, you feel very happy and proud because of something that has happened.

words.ex: He gave his acquiescence to the plan.
words.ex_cn: 他默许了这个计划。
words.en: Acquiescence is the act of accepting or agreeing to something without protest.

words.tr: v. 猛烈抨击；痛骂；激烈反对
words.ex: He often inveighs against the corruption in the government.
words.ex_cn: 他经常猛烈抨击政府中的腐败现象。
words.en: If you inveigh against something, you criticize it strongly.

words.ex: His tone was one of gentle reproof.
words.ex_cn: 他的语气带着温和的责备。
words.en: An expression of blame or disapproval.

words.tr: adj. 真实的；真的；正确的；
words.ex: The story is true.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事是真实的。
words.en: in accordance with fact or reality

words.tr: adj. 歇斯底里的；异常激动的
words.ex: She became hysterical when she lost her wallet.
words.ex_cn: 她丢了钱包时变得歇斯底里。
words.en: If someone is hysterical, they are in a state of uncontrolled excitement, anger, or panic, often because of a shock or a very upsetting experience.

words.tr: v. （故意地）混淆；使混乱；使困惑
words.ex: He tries to obfuscate the truth with complicated words.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用复杂的词语混淆真相。
words.en: To obfuscate something means to deliberately make it unclear or difficult to understand.

words.tr: adj. 可觉察的；很可观的
words.ex: There is an appreciable difference in his grades.
words.ex_cn: 他的成绩有明显的差异。
words.en: If something is appreciable, it is large enough to be noticed or considered important.

words.ex: He decided to waive the fee.
words.ex_cn: 他决定放弃这笔费用。
words.en: If you waive a right, claim, or privilege, you do not insist on it or do not use it.

words.ex: The guard showed vigilance during the night shift.
words.ex_cn: 守卫在夜班期间保持警惕。
words.en: Vigilance is the action or state of keeping careful watch for possible danger or difficulties.

words.tr:
adj. 安详的；安静的；镇静的
v. 给…服镇静剂
words.ex: The sedate old man sat quietly by the window.
words.ex_cn: 那位安详的老人安静地坐在窗边。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as sedate, you mean that they are quiet, calm, and dignified.

words.ex: He is a dissentious person who always argues with others.
words.ex_cn: 他是个好争论的人，总是和别人争吵。
words.en: Inclined to or causing dissent; contentious.

words.ex: He bemoans the loss of his old car.
words.ex_cn: 他抱怨失去了他的旧车。
words.en: If you bemoan something, you express sorrow or dissatisfaction about it.

words.ex: Bravo! You did an amazing job!
words.ex_cn: 好啊！你做得太棒了！
words.en: Used to express approval when a performer or other person has done something well.

words.tr:
n. 刚毛；猪鬃
v. 大为恼怒；耸起毛发
words.ex: The brush has stiff bristles for cleaning pots.
words.ex_cn: 这把刷子有坚硬的刚毛，用来清洗锅具。
words.en: A bristle is a short, stiff hair, usually one of many on an animal or brush. As a verb, it can mean to react angrily or defensively, or (of hair or fur) to stand upright away from the skin, typically as a sign of anger or fear.

words.tr: v. 增添活力；振奋；使活跃
words.ex: The fresh air invigorates me every morning.
words.ex_cn: 每天早晨的新鲜空气让我精神焕发。
words.en: If something invigorates you, it makes you feel more energetic and alive.

words.tr: v. 使说不出话来；使目瞪口呆
words.ex: The magic trick dumbfound everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个魔术让所有人都惊呆了。
words.en: If someone or something dumbfounds you, they surprise you so much that you cannot think or speak for a moment.

words.tr: adj. 重罪的；恶毒的；凶恶的
words.ex: He committed a felonious act last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年犯下了一项重罪行为。
words.en: Involving or relating to a felony; criminal.

words.tr: v. 使恼怒；使厌烦；使烦恼
words.ex: The loud noise irks her every morning.
words.ex_cn: 每天早上，巨大的噪音都让她感到烦躁。
words.en: To irritate, annoy, or exasperate someone.

words.ex: She gave me a book.
words.ex_cn: 她给了我一本书。
words.en: To freely transfer the possession of something to someone; to cause or allow someone to have something.

words.ex: The loud noise deranges the baby.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音让婴儿烦躁不安。
words.en: To derange something is to disturb the normal arrangement or functioning of it, often causing confusion or disorder.

words.ex: He reck he can finish the work today.
words.ex_cn: 他以为他今天能完成这项工作。
words.en: To pay heed or attention to something; to care or be concerned about something.

words.ex: The priest gave a benediction at the end of the service.
words.ex_cn: 牧师在仪式结束时给予了祝福。
words.en: A benediction is a prayer asking for God's blessing, especially one at the end of a religious service.

words.ex: The bully tried to intimidate the new student.
words.ex_cn: 那个霸凌者试图恐吓新生。
words.en: If you intimidate someone, you deliberately make them frightened enough to do what you want them to do.

words.tr: adj. 再三要求的；纠缠不休的
words.ex: He was importunate in asking for money.
words.ex_cn: 他不停地要求给钱。
words.en: persistent to the point of annoyance

words.ex: He received laudation for his brave actions.
words.ex_cn: 他因勇敢的行为而受到赞扬。
words.en: The act of praising or complimenting someone or something highly.

words.tr: v. 反复地说；重申；重述
words.ex: He reiterate that he is sorry.
words.ex_cn: 他反复地说他很抱歉。
words.en: If you reiterate something, you say it again, usually in order to emphasize it.

words.ex: He prevaricates when asked about the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 当被问到错误时，他回避回答。
words.en: If you prevaricate, you avoid giving a direct answer or making a firm decision.

words.ex: He misstates the facts on purpose.
words.ex_cn: 他故意歪曲事实。
words.en: To state something incorrectly or falsely.

words.tr: adj. 后悔的；悔过的；表示悔改的
words.ex: He was repentant after lying to his mother.
words.ex_cn: 他对对母亲撒谎感到后悔。
words.en: Feeling or expressing sincere regret and remorse about one's wrongdoing or sin.

words.tr: v. 使静止不动；使停泊
words.ex: The wind helps to becalm the boat.
words.ex_cn: 风帮助船平静下来。
words.en: To becalm means to make something calm or still, especially in the context of making the sea calm so that a sailing ship cannot move because there is no wind.

words.tr:
n. 授权；任期；委任；命令
v. 授权；委任
words.ex: The government has a mandate from the people to change the law.
words.ex_cn: 政府得到了人民的授权来修改法律。
words.en: If someone is given a mandate to carry out a particular policy or task, they are given the official authority to do it.

words.tr: v. 大声叫喊着说；叫嚷
words.ex: He vociferate his anger loudly in the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议上大声喊出他的愤怒。
words.en: To shout, complain, or argue loudly or vehemently.

words.tr:
v. 激怒；使生气；激起
n. 怨恨；愤恨
words.ex: His rude comment piqued her anger.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁的评论激怒了她。
words.en: If something piques your interest or curiosity, it makes you interested or curious.

words.ex: He animadverted on his friend's careless mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他批评了朋友的粗心错误。
words.en: To express criticism or censure.

words.ex: The children were running in a frenetic way around the room.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在房间里发狂似的跑来跑去。
words.en: If you describe an activity as frenetic, you mean that it is fast and energetic, but rather uncontrolled and often not very well organized.

words.ex: The loud noise exasperates me.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音让我感到烦躁。
words.en: If someone or something exasperates you, they annoy you and make you feel frustrated or impatient.

words.tr: v. 使声音降低；压抑（声音）；蒙住；裹
words.ex: He muffled his laugh with a pillow.
words.ex_cn: 他用枕头捂住笑声。
words.en: To muffle a sound is to make it quieter or less clear, often by covering it or wrapping it in something.

words.ex: He felt listless after the long illness.
words.ex_cn: 他生病后感到无精打采。
words.en: If someone is listless, they lack energy or enthusiasm.

words.tr: v. 迷惑；使迷惑不解；使糊涂
words.ex: The magic trick will mystify the children.
words.ex_cn: 这个魔术会让孩子们感到困惑。
words.en: If you are mystified by something, you find it impossible to explain or understand.

words.ex: His voice trembled with ire.
words.ex_cn: 他的声音因愤怒而颤抖。
words.en: Anger or wrath.

words.ex: He gave her flowers to placate her.
words.ex_cn: 他送她花来安抚她。
words.en: If you placate someone, you do or say something to make them stop feeling angry.

words.tr: adj. 强制的；法定的；义务的；
words.ex: Wearing a helmet is mandatory for cyclists.
words.ex_cn: 骑自行车时戴头盔是强制的。
words.en: If something is mandatory, it is required by law or by a rule or regulation.

words.ex: Her hug gave me solace after the loss.
words.ex_cn: 在失去亲人后，她的拥抱给了我安慰。
words.en: Solace is comfort that you feel when you are consoled in times of disappointment or sadness.

words.tr:
n. 马笼头；缰绳；约束
v. 套笼头；表示恼怒；抑制
words.ex: He pulled the bridle to stop the horse.
words.ex_cn: 他拉了一下缰绳让马停下来。
words.en: A bridle is a set of straps that fits around a horse's head and is used to control the horse. As a verb, to bridle means to put a bridle on a horse or to restrain or control something.

words.tr:
n. （当众）侮辱；冒犯
v. （当众）侮辱；冒犯
words.ex: He felt an affront when they laughed at his idea.
words.ex_cn: 当他们嘲笑他的想法时，他感到受到了冒犯。
words.en: If something is an affront to you, it is an action or remark that insults or offends you.

words.tr: adj. 可恶的；令人憎恶的；令人痛恨的
words.ex: He finds lying to friends abhorrent.
words.ex_cn: 他认为对朋友撒谎是令人厌恶的。
words.en: If something is abhorrent to you, you hate it very much, often because you think it is immoral or wrong.

words.ex: His laudable effort helped the team win.
words.ex_cn: 他值得赞美的努力帮助团队赢得了比赛。
words.en: Deserving praise and commendation.

words.ex: His jocund laughter filled the room.
words.ex_cn: 他那快活的笑声充满了整个房间。
words.en: If you describe someone as jocund, you mean that they are cheerful and happy.

words.ex: The adherence of the sticker to the wall is strong.
words.ex_cn: 贴纸对墙的粘附很强。
words.en: Adherence is the act of following or sticking to a particular set of beliefs, principles, or rules.

words.tr: adj. 令人厌恶的；讨厌的；抵触的
words.ex: The smell was repugnant.
words.ex_cn: 那气味令人厌恶。
words.en: If you think that something is horrible and disgusting, you can say that it is repugnant.

words.tr: n. 憎恨；厌恶；可憎的事物
words.ex: The sight of the rotting food was an abomination.
words.ex_cn: 腐烂食物的景象令人作呕。
words.en: An abomination is something that you dislike and disapprove of very strongly.

words.ex: He had to relinquish his seat to an old man.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不把座位让给一位老人。
words.en: If you relinquish something, such as power or control, you give it up, often unwillingly.

words.ex: He bethinks himself of his mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他反思自己的错误。
words.en: To think of something or to consider something again.

words.ex: The imperious queen demanded immediate obedience.
words.ex_cn: 这位专横的女王要求立即服从。
words.en: If you describe someone as imperious, you mean that they have a proud manner and expect to be obeyed.

words.tr: adj. 赞美的；赞赏的；称赞的
words.ex: The teacher gave a laudatory remark about his effort.
words.ex_cn: 老师对他的努力给予了赞扬的评价。
words.en: If something is laudatory, it expresses praise.

words.ex: She is assertive when she speaks up for her rights.
words.ex_cn: 当她为自己权利发声时，表现得坚定自信。
words.en: Someone who is assertive behaves confidently and is not frightened to say what they want or believe.

words.ex: He faced an accusation of stealing money.
words.ex_cn: 他面临偷钱的指控。
words.en: An accusation is a statement saying that someone has done something wrong or illegal.

words.ex: He grimaced when he tasted the bitter medicine.
words.ex_cn: 他喝下苦涩的药时皱起了脸。
words.en: A grimace is an ugly, twisted expression on a person's face, usually because they are experiencing pain or strong feelings.

words.tr: adj. 不合适的；不相称的；不协调的；
words.ex: His funny hat was incongruous with the formal suit.
words.ex_cn: 他的滑稽帽子与正式西装不搭配。
words.en: Something that is incongruous is strange when considered together with other aspects of a situation.

words.ex: The boss is dictatorial and never listens to others.
words.ex_cn: 老板很专横，从不听别人的意见。
words.en: If you describe someone as dictatorial, you are criticizing them for behaving in a way that shows they expect to be obeyed without question.

words.ex: She made an earnest entreaty for forgiveness.
words.ex_cn: 她真诚地恳求原谅。
words.en: An entreaty is a serious and often emotional request for something, especially for help or mercy.

words.tr: adj. 不重要的；无关紧要的
words.ex: His comment was inconsequential to the decision.
words.ex_cn: 他的评论对决定无关紧要。
words.en: If you describe something as inconsequential, you mean that it is not important.

words.ex: He saw a beautiful panorama from the mountain top.
words.ex_cn: 他从山顶看到了美丽的全景。
words.en: A panorama is a view of a wide area, or a description or study that presents all the different parts or aspects of a particular subject.

words.tr:
adj. 贬损的；轻蔑的
n. 贬损语
words.ex: He used a pejorative word to describe his neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他用了一个贬义词来描述他的邻居。
words.en: A pejorative word or expression is one that expresses criticism or disapproval.

words.ex: He gave her a scowl when she was late.
words.ex_cn: 她迟到时，他皱了皱眉。
words.en: When someone scowls, they look at someone or something with an angry or irritated expression.

words.ex: He tried to calumniate his neighbor with false lies.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用虚假的谎言诽谤他的邻居。
words.en: If someone calumniates you, they make unpleasant and untrue statements about you in order to damage your reputation.

words.tr: adj. 令人作呕的；令人恶心的
words.ex: The smell made him feel nauseous.
words.ex_cn: 那股气味让他感到恶心。
words.en: If you feel nauseous, you feel as if you want to vomit.

words.tr: n. 漫不经心； 漠不关心；无忧无虑
words.ex: He showed insouciance when the teacher scolded him.
words.ex_cn: 老师批评他时，他表现得毫不在意。
words.en: A feeling of not worrying about anything because you do not think anything bad will happen.

words.ex: His speech was full of invective against his opponent.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲充满了对对手的辱骂。
words.en: Invective is rude and unpleasant things that people shout at someone they hate or are angry with.

words.tr: v. 强使接受；打扰；闯入
words.ex: He tried to obtrude his opinions on the group.
words.ex_cn: 他试图强使组里接受他的观点。
words.en: To force something on someone in a way that is unwelcome or intrusive.

words.tr: n. 报复；报仇；报复性劫掠
words.ex: He feared reprisal after speaking out against the boss.
words.ex_cn: 他因公开反对老板而害怕遭到报复。
words.en: An act of retaliation for a wrong or injury.

words.tr: adj. 不屈不挠的；百折不挠的
words.ex: He is indomitable in facing challenges.
words.ex_cn: 他在面对挑战时永不言败。
words.en: If you say that someone has an indomitable spirit, you admire them because they never give up or admit that they have been defeated.

words.tr:
adj. 慷慨激昂的；热烈的
v. 激起热情；使激动；“impassion”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He gave an impassioned speech about peace.
words.ex_cn: 他发表了充满激情的关于和平的演讲。
words.en: An impassioned speech or piece of writing is one that expresses very strong feelings about something.

words.ex: Behold the beautiful sunset.
words.ex_cn: 看那美丽的日落。
words.en: To see or observe (someone or something, especially something remarkable or impressive).

words.ex: He gave a vehement reply to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了激烈的回答。
words.en: If a person or their actions or comments are vehement, the person has very strong feelings or opinions and expresses them forcefully.

words.ex: Instead of apologizing, she began to recriminate.
words.ex_cn: 她没有道歉，反而开始反唇相讥。
words.en: If you recriminate, you accuse someone who has accused you of something.

words.ex: The teacher lauded the student for her hard work.
words.ex_cn: 老师称赞了这名学生努力学习。
words.en: If people laud someone, they praise and admire them.

words.tr: adj. 残酷的；无情的；持续恶化的；无休止的
words.ex: The remorseless man did not apologize.
words.ex_cn: 那个无情的人没有道歉。
words.en: If you describe someone as remorseless, you mean that they are very determined and do not give up easily, even if what they are doing is cruel or unpleasant.

words.tr:
adv. 狂暴地；狂怒地；杀气腾腾地
adj. 狂暴的；狂怒的；杀气腾腾的
words.ex: The dog ran amok in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 狗在花园里乱跑。
words.en: If someone runs amok, they behave in a wild and uncontrolled manner, often causing damage or harm.

words.tr: adj. 想复仇的；报复性的；怀恨的
words.ex: He was vindictive and refused to forgive her.
words.ex_cn: 他心怀报复，拒绝原谅她。
words.en: If you say that someone is vindictive, you are critical of them because they deliberately try to upset or cause trouble for someone who they think has done them harm.

words.tr: adj. 不留心的；不注意的
words.ex: He was heedless of the warning signs.
words.ex_cn: 他对警告信号毫不在意。
words.en: If you are heedless of someone or something, you do not take any notice of them.

words.tr: adj. 关怀的；切望的；惦记的；悬虑的
words.ex: He was solicitous about her health.
words.ex_cn: 他非常关心她的健康。
words.en: If you are solicitous, you are very concerned about someone's safety, health, or comfort.

words.ex: She was frantic to catch the last bus.
words.ex_cn: 她急忙赶着赶最后一班公交车。
words.en: If someone is frantic, they are behaving in a wild and desperate way, often because they are frightened or worried.

words.ex: The lambs gambol in the green field.
words.ex_cn: 小羊在绿地上嬉戏。
words.en: If animals or people gambol, they run or jump about in a playful way.

words.ex: He felt contrition after lying to his mother.
words.ex_cn: 他在对母亲撒谎后感到悔恨。
words.en: The state of feeling remorseful and penitent.

words.tr: n. 提出（异议）；插嘴（插入）行为
words.ex: The teacher's interposition stopped the fight.
words.ex_cn: 老师的介入阻止了这场打斗。
words.en: The act of placing or inserting between or among others; intervention.

words.ex: He disavow any connection to the crime.
words.ex_cn: 他否认与这起犯罪有任何关联。
words.en: If you disavow something, you say that you are not responsible for it or you do not agree with it.

words.ex: His comments about her appearance really riled her.
words.ex_cn: 他对她外貌的评论真的激怒了她。
words.en: To make someone annoyed or irritated.

words.ex: She was enamored with the beauty of the sunset.
words.ex_cn: 她被日落的美景迷住了。
words.en: To fill someone with love or delight; to captivate.

words.ex: He is enamoured by the beauty of the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 他被夜空的美丽迷住了。
words.en: To fill someone with love and delight; to charm or captivate.

words.ex: He detests eating broccoli.
words.ex_cn: 他讨厌吃西兰花。
words.en: If you detest something, you dislike it intensely.

words.tr: adj. 自由决定的；酌情行事的；便宜行事的
words.ex: He spent his discretionary money on a new phone.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的可自由支配的钱花在了一部新手机上。
words.en: If something is discretionary, it is available for use as someone chooses, rather than according to a set plan or rule.

words.tr: n. 做手势；做示意动作
words.ex: His animated gesticulation made it clear he was very excited about the proposal.
words.ex_cn: 他激动的示意动作表明他对这个提议非常兴奋。
words.en: Gesticulation refers to the act of making gestures, especially while speaking, to emphasize or illustrate what is being said.

words.tr: adj. 使人悲痛的；令人心碎的
words.ex: The story of the orphan's struggle was heartrending.
words.ex_cn: 这个孤儿奋斗的故事令人心碎。
words.en: Causing great sadness or distress.

words.ex: They tried to coerce him into signing the paper.
words.ex_cn: 他们试图强迫他签署那份文件。
words.en: If you coerce someone into doing something, you make them do it, even though they do not want to.

words.tr: adj. 平静的；宁静的；温和的；
words.ex: The lake was placid in the morning light.
words.ex_cn: 清晨的阳光下，湖面平静无波。
words.en: A placid person or animal is calm and does not easily become excited, angry, or upset.

words.tr: adj. 被诅咒的；可恶的；讨厌的
words.ex: He was accursed for lying to his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他因为对朋友撒谎而遭到诅咒。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as accursed, you are emphasizing that you dislike or hate them very much.

words.ex: He felt trepidation before the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他在考试前感到恐惧。
words.en: A feeling of fear or anxiety about something that may happen.

words.tr: v. 叽哩咕噜地叫；急促不清地说
words.ex: He gibbers when he is nervous.
words.ex_cn: 当他紧张时，他会胡言乱语。
words.en: To speak rapidly and unintelligibly, often in a state of panic or excitement.

words.tr: n. 误称…之名；不当之名
words.ex: Calling a tomato a vegetable is a misnomer.
words.ex_cn: 把番茄称为蔬菜是一种错误的称呼。
words.en: A misnomer is a name that is wrongly or unsuitably applied to someone or something.

words.ex: His whine about the food made everyone annoyed.
words.ex_cn: 他对食物的抱怨让所有人都感到厌烦。
words.en: If someone or something whines, they make a long, high-pitched noise, especially one which sounds sad or unpleasant.

words.tr: adj. 大声喊叫的；喧嚷的
words.ex: The vociferous crowd shouted for change.
words.ex_cn: 喧闹的人群大声要求变革。
words.en: If you describe someone as vociferous, you mean that they speak with great energy and determination, because they want their views to be heard.

words.tr: adj. 谄媚的；奉承的；阿谀的
words.ex: He gave an adulatory speech about the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他发表了对老师赞不绝口的演讲。
words.en: If someone is adulatory, they give a lot of praise and admiration, often in a way that is not sincere.

words.tr: n. 反复无常；任性；怪想
words.ex: Her decision to quit the job was a sudden caprice.
words.ex_cn: 她决定辞职是突如其来的任性之举。
words.en: A sudden and unaccountable change of mood or behavior.

words.tr: adj. 不利的；麻烦的；异常的；意外的；棘手的
words.ex: He faced untoward remarks from his classmates.
words.ex_cn: 他遭到了同学的不友好的评论。
words.en: If you say that something is untoward, you mean that it is unexpected and causes difficulties.

words.tr: adj. 奔放的；兴高采烈的；沸腾的
words.ex: He is ebullient after winning the prize.
words.ex_cn: 他赢得奖后非常兴奋。
words.en: If you describe someone as ebullient, you mean that they are lively and full of enthusiasm or excitement about something.

words.ex: His assertion was simple: the project will finish on time.
words.ex_cn: 他的断言很简单：项目会按时完成。
words.en: A statement that is made with confidence but without proof.

words.tr:
n. 重复部分；再现
v. 重演；重奏
words.ex: The song ended with a short reprise of the chorus.
words.ex_cn: 这首歌以副歌的简短重复部分结束。
words.en: A reprise is a repetition of a piece of music or a performance. It can also refer to the act of repeating something.

words.ex: He filed a grievance about the unfair treatment.
words.ex_cn: 他因不公平的对待提出了不满。
words.en: A grievance is a feeling of resentment over something believed to be wrong or unfair.

words.ex: He had a dour expression on his face.
words.ex_cn: 他脸上带着严厉的表情。
words.en: If you describe someone as dour, you mean they are very serious and unfriendly.

words.tr:
adj. 急动的；颠簸的；抽筋的
n. 肉干
words.ex: His jerky movements made the camera footage blurry.
words.ex_cn: 他急动的动作让视频画面变得模糊。
words.en: If you describe something as jerky, you mean that it moves in a way that is not smooth, but rather with sudden stops and starts.

words.ex: The country made a unilateral decision to close the border.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家单方面决定关闭边境。
words.en: Involving only one group or country.

words.ex: He tries to ingratiate himself with his boss by bringing coffee every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上送咖啡给老板，试图讨好他。
words.en: If someone tries to ingratiate themselves with you, they do things to try and make you like them.

words.tr: adj. 相关的；有联系的； v. 关联；“relate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: This book is related to science.
words.ex_cn: 这本书与科学相关。
words.en: If two or more things are related, there is a connection between them.

words.tr:
adj. 呼格的（语法）
n. 呼格（词）
words.ex: He used 'friend' as a vocative in his letter.
words.ex_cn: 他在信中用'朋友'作为呼语。
words.en: The vocative case is a grammatical case used for a noun that identifies a person (animal, object, etc.) being addressed and/or is the subject of the sentence.

words.ex: He could espy a small boat in the distance.
words.ex_cn: 他能隐约看见远处有一条小船。
words.en: If you espy something, you see or notice it, often when it is not easy to do so.

words.ex: He taunted his brother for losing the game.
words.ex_cn: 他奚落弟弟比赛输了。
words.en: If someone taunts you, they say unkind or insulting things to you, especially about your weaknesses or failures.

words.tr:
v. 大声宣布；装饰
n. 徽章
words.ex: He blazoned his name on the flag.
words.ex_cn: 他在旗帜上醒目地写下了自己的名字。
words.en: To blazon something means to describe, depict, or display it prominently or vividly, often in a heraldic context.

words.ex: He gave a licentious speech at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他在聚会上发表了一篇放荡不羁的演讲。
words.en: If you describe a person as licentious, you mean that they are very immoral in their sexual behavior.

words.tr: n. 堕落的人；不道德的人
words.ex: The townspeople shunned the reprobate, fearing his influence.
words.ex_cn: 镇上的人们都避开那个堕落的人，害怕他的影响。
words.en: A reprobate is a person who behaves in a way that is morally wrong and who shows no regret or shame for their actions.

words.ex: His actions were marked by turpitude and deceit.
words.ex_cn: 他的行为充满了卑鄙和欺骗。
words.en: Turpitude refers to depravity or wickedness, especially in a moral sense.

words.tr: adj. 温文儒雅的；彬彬有礼的
words.ex: He is an urbane man who speaks politely.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个举止文雅、说话有礼貌的人。
words.en: If you describe someone as urbane, you mean that they are polite, confident, and comfortable in social situations.

words.ex: The magic show captivates the children.
words.ex_cn: 魔术表演吸引了孩子们。
words.en: If you are captivated by someone or something, you find them fascinating and attractive.

words.tr: adj. 深沉响亮的；洪亮的
words.ex: The bell rang with a sonorous sound.
words.ex_cn: 钟发出洪亮的声音。
words.en: A sonorous sound is deep, full, and rich, often pleasing to the ear.

words.ex: The committee issued a remonstrance against the proposed changes.
words.ex_cn: 委员会对拟议的变更提出了抗议。
words.en: A remonstrance is a formal statement of protest or complaint.

words.tr: adj. 宽宏大量的；有雅量的
words.ex: He was magnanimous and forgave his enemy.
words.ex_cn: 他宽宏大量，原谅了他的敌人。
words.en: If you are magnanimous, you behave kindly and generously toward someone, especially after defeating them or being treated badly by them.

words.ex: The storm was formidable and destroyed many houses.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴很可怕，摧毁了许多房屋。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as formidable, you mean that you feel slightly frightened by them because they are very great or impressive.

words.ex: She upbraided him for his carelessness.
words.ex_cn: 她因他的粗心大意而责骂他。
words.en: To criticize or reproach severely; to scold.

words.tr: n. 意见分歧；纠纷；争执
words.ex: The team had dissension about the new plan.
words.ex_cn: 团队对新计划有分歧。
words.en: Disagreement among people or groups, especially when it leads to conflict.

words.ex: The speech embolden the protesters to speak up.
words.ex_cn: 这次演讲鼓舞了抗议者们发声。
words.en: To embolden someone means to make them feel more confident or courageous.

words.tr: v. 大声呵斥；强烈谴责
words.ex: He fulminates against unfair laws.
words.ex_cn: 他强烈谴责不公正的法律。
words.en: To fulminate means to express vehement protest. It can also mean to explode or detonate.

words.tr: n. 听人命令；受人指挥
words.ex: He gave me a beck to come closer.
words.ex_cn: 他向我招手让我靠近。
words.en: A beck is a small stream or a gesture of summoning or calling.

words.tr: adj. 感觉上的；感官的；（引起）美感的
words.ex: She wore a sensuous silk dress.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一件性感的丝绸裙子。
words.en: Relating to or affecting the senses rather than the intellect; characterized by a pleasing or luxurious quality that appeals to the senses.

words.tr: adj. 粗鲁的；生硬的；粗哑的
words.ex: The old man gave a gruff answer.
words.ex_cn: 老人粗声粗气地回答了。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as gruff, you mean that they seem rather unfriendly or bad-tempered.

words.tr: adj. 健谈的；滔滔不绝的
words.ex: He is a voluble speaker who talks all day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个健谈的人，整天说个不停。
words.en: If you describe someone as voluble, you mean that they talk a lot with great energy and enthusiasm.

words.tr: n. 告诫；忠告；告诫书；传票
words.ex: He ignored the monition from his teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他忽视了老师的警告。
